{
  
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Unary Arithmetical Operations for Vector Objects}}\logpage{[ 26, 8, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7F8CE23F7A250072}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AdditiveInverseMutable({\mdseries\slshape v})\index{AdditiveInverseMutable@\texttt{AdditiveInverseMutable}!for vector object}
\label{AdditiveInverseMutable:for vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AdditiveInverseSameMutability({\mdseries\slshape v})\index{AdditiveInverseSameMutability@\texttt{AdditiveInverseSameMutability}!for vector object}
\label{AdditiveInverseSameMutability:for vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ZeroMutable({\mdseries\slshape v})\index{ZeroMutable@\texttt{ZeroMutable}!for vector object}
\label{ZeroMutable:for vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ZeroSameMutability({\mdseries\slshape v})\index{ZeroSameMutability@\texttt{ZeroSameMutability}!for vector object}
\label{ZeroSameMutability:for vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsZero({\mdseries\slshape v})\index{IsZero@\texttt{IsZero}!for vector object}
\label{IsZero:for vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Characteristic({\mdseries\slshape v})\index{Characteristic@\texttt{Characteristic}!for vector object}
\label{Characteristic:for vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a vector object



 For a vector object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}}, the operations for computing the additive inverse with prescribed mutability
return a vector object with the same \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a vector object}) and \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a vector object}) values, such that the sum with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} is a zero vector. It is not specified what happens if the base domain does not
admit the additive inverses of the entries. 

 Analogously, the operations for computing a zero vector with prescribed
mutability return a vector object compatible with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}}. 

 \texttt{IsZero} returns \texttt{true} if all entries in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} are zero, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \texttt{Characteristic} returns the corresponding value of the \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a vector object}) value of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}}. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Binary Arithmetical Operations for Vector Objects}}\logpage{[ 26, 8, 2 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X85A815CA790094CC}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}+({\mdseries\slshape v1, v2})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}+@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}+}!for two vector objects}
\label{bSlash+:for two vector objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}({\mdseries\slshape v1, v2})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}}!for two vector objects}
\label{bSlash-:for two vector objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*({\mdseries\slshape s, v})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*}!for scalar and vector object}
\label{bSlash*:for scalar and vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*({\mdseries\slshape v, s})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*}!for vector object and scalar}
\label{bSlash*:for vector object and scalar}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*({\mdseries\slshape v1, v2})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*}!for two vector objects}
\label{bSlash*:for two vector objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ScalarProduct({\mdseries\slshape v1, v2})\index{ScalarProduct@\texttt{ScalarProduct}!for two vector objects}
\label{ScalarProduct:for two vector objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/({\mdseries\slshape v, s})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/}!for vector object and scalar}
\label{bSlash/:for vector object and scalar}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\


 The sum and the difference, respectively, of two vector objects \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v2}} is a new mutable vector object whose entries are the sums and the differences
of the entries of the arguments. 

 The product of a scalar \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} and a vector object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} (from the left or from the right) is a new mutable vector object whose entries
are the corresponding products. 

 The quotient of a vector object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} and a scalar \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} is a new mutable vector object whose entries are the corresponding quotients. 

 The product of two vector objects \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v2}} as well as the result of \texttt{ScalarProduct} is the standard scalar product of the two arguments (an element of the base
domain of the vector objects). 

 All this is defined only if the vector objects have the same length and are
defined over the same base domain and have the same representation, and if the
products with the given scalar belong to the base domain; otherwise it is not
specified what happens. If the result is a vector object then it has the same
representation and the same base domain as the given vector object(s). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AddVector (for two vector objects)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 8, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X876090A684E71C93}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AddVector({\mdseries\slshape dst, src[, mul[, from, to]]})\index{AddVector@\texttt{AddVector}!for two vector objects}
\label{AddVector:for two vector objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AddVector({\mdseries\slshape dst, mul, src[, from, to]})\index{AddVector@\texttt{AddVector}!for two vector objects and a scalar}
\label{AddVector:for two vector objects and a scalar}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
nothing



 Called with two vector objects \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dst}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape src}}, this function replaces the entries of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dst}} in\texttt{\symbol{45}}place by the entries of the sum \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dst}}\texttt{ + }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape src}}. 

 If a scalar \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mul}} is given as the third or second argument, respectively, then the entries of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dst}} get replaced by those of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dst}}\texttt{ + }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape src}}\texttt{ * }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mul}} or \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dst}}\texttt{ + }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mul}}\texttt{ * }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape src}}, respectively. 

 If the optional parameters \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}} are given then only the index range \texttt{[\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}}..\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}}]} is guaranteed to be affected. Other indices \emph{may} be affected, if it is more convenient to do so. This can be helpful if entries
of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape src}} are known to be zero. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} is bigger than \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}}, the operation does nothing. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MultVector (for a vector object)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 8, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8039D013817317C3}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MultVector({\mdseries\slshape v, mul[, from, to]})\index{MultVector@\texttt{MultVector}!for a vector object}
\label{MultVector:for a vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MultVectorLeft({\mdseries\slshape v, mul[, from, to]})\index{MultVectorLeft@\texttt{MultVectorLeft}!for a vector object}
\label{MultVectorLeft:for a vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MultVectorRight({\mdseries\slshape v, mul[, from, to]})\index{MultVectorRight@\texttt{MultVectorRight}!for a vector object}
\label{MultVectorRight:for a vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
nothing



 These operations multiply \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mul}} in\texttt{\symbol{45}}place where \texttt{MultVectorLeft} multiplies with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mul}} from the left and \texttt{MultVectorRight} does so from the right. 

 Note that \texttt{MultVector} is just a synonym for \texttt{MultVectorLeft}. This was chosen because vectors in \textsf{GAP} are by default row vectors and scalar multiplication is usually written as $a \cdot v = a \cdot [v_1, ..., v_n] = [a \cdot v_1, ..., a \cdot v_n]$ with scalars being applied from the left. 

 If the optional parameters \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}} are given then only the index range \texttt{[\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}}..\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}}]} is guaranteed to be affected. Other indices \emph{may} be affected, if it is more convenient to do so. This can be helpful if entries
of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} are known to be zero. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} is bigger than \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}}, the operation does nothing. 

 }

 }

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ConcatenationOfVectors}}\logpage{[ 26, 9, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7AC470557EC90714}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ConcatenationOfVectors({\mdseries\slshape v1, v2, ...})\index{ConcatenationOfVectors@\texttt{ConcatenationOfVectors}!for arbitrary many vector objects}
\label{ConcatenationOfVectors:for arbitrary many vector objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ConcatenationOfVectors({\mdseries\slshape vlist})\index{ConcatenationOfVectors@\texttt{ConcatenationOfVectors}!for a list of vector objects}
\label{ConcatenationOfVectors:for a list of vector objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a vector object



 Returns a new mutable vector object in the representation of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v1}} or the first entry of the nonempty list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape vlist}} of vector objects, respectively, such that the entries are the concatenation
of the given vector objects. 

 (Note that \texttt{Concatenation} (\ref{Concatenation:for several lists}) is a function for which no methods can be installed.) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ExtractSubVector}}
\logpage{[ 26, 9, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DBE956E7F9C700E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ExtractSubVector({\mdseries\slshape v, l})\index{ExtractSubVector@\texttt{ExtractSubVector}}
\label{ExtractSubVector}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a vector object



 Returns a new mutable vector object of the same vector representation as \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}}, containing the entries of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} at the positions in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape l}}. 

 This is the same as \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{123}}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape l}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{125}}}, the name \texttt{ExtractSubVector} was introduced in analogy to \texttt{ExtractSubMatrix} (\ref{ExtractSubMatrix}), for which no equivalent syntax using curly brackets is available. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CopySubVector}}
\logpage{[ 26, 9, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80EC354D78D7B5A6}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CopySubVector({\mdseries\slshape src, dst, scols, dcols})\index{CopySubVector@\texttt{CopySubVector}}
\label{CopySubVector}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
nothing



 For two row vectors or vector objects \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape src}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dst}}, such that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dst}} is mutable, and two lists \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape scols}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dcols}} of positions, \texttt{CopySubVector} assigns the entries \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape src}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{123}} }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape scols}}\texttt{ \texttt{\symbol{125}}} (see \texttt{ExtractSubVector} (\ref{ExtractSubVector})) to the positions \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dcols}} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dst}}, but without creating an intermediate object and thus {\textendash}at least
in special cases{\textendash} much more efficiently. 

 For certain objects like compressed vectors this might be significantly more
efficient if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape scols}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dcols}} are ranges with increment 1. 

 If the global option \texttt{check} is set to \texttt{false} then \texttt{CopySubVector} need not perform consistency checks. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{WeightOfVector (for a vector object)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 9, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X866366E587991171}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{WeightOfVector({\mdseries\slshape v})\index{WeightOfVector@\texttt{WeightOfVector}!for a vector object}
\label{WeightOfVector:for a vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
an integer



 returns the Hamming weight of the vector object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}}, i.e., the number of nonzero entries in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DistanceOfVectors (for two vector objects)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 9, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81ACAE017C00F782}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DistanceOfVectors({\mdseries\slshape v1, v2})\index{DistanceOfVectors@\texttt{DistanceOfVectors}!for two vector objects}
\label{DistanceOfVectors:for two vector objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
an integer



 returns the Hamming distance of the vector objects \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v2}}, i.e., the number of entries in which the vectors differ. The vectors must
have equal length. }

 }

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Unary Arithmetical Operations for Matrix Objects}}\logpage{[ 26, 10, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X819F87A07DA7E2DC}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AdditiveInverseMutable({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{AdditiveInverseMutable@\texttt{AdditiveInverseMutable}!for matrix object}
\label{AdditiveInverseMutable:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AdditiveInverseSameMutability({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{AdditiveInverseSameMutability@\texttt{AdditiveInverseSameMutability}!for matrix object}
\label{AdditiveInverseSameMutability:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ZeroMutable({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{ZeroMutable@\texttt{ZeroMutable}!for matrix object}
\label{ZeroMutable:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ZeroSameMutability({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{ZeroSameMutability@\texttt{ZeroSameMutability}!for matrix object}
\label{ZeroSameMutability:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OneMutable({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{OneMutable@\texttt{OneMutable}!for matrix object}
\label{OneMutable:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OneSameMutability({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{OneSameMutability@\texttt{OneSameMutability}!for matrix object}
\label{OneSameMutability:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InverseMutable({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{InverseMutable@\texttt{InverseMutable}!for matrix object}
\label{InverseMutable:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InverseSameMutability({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{InverseSameMutability@\texttt{InverseSameMutability}!for matrix object}
\label{InverseSameMutability:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsZero({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{IsZero@\texttt{IsZero}!for matrix object}
\label{IsZero:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsOne({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{IsOne@\texttt{IsOne}!for matrix object}
\label{IsOne:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Characteristic({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{Characteristic@\texttt{Characteristic}!for matrix object}
\label{Characteristic:for matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a matrix object



 For a vector object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, the operations for computing the additive inverse with prescribed mutability
return a matrix object with the same \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a matrix object}) and \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) values, such that the sum with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} is a zero matrix. It is not specified what happens if the base domain does not
admit the additive inverses of the entries. 

 Analogously, the operations for computing a zero matrix with prescribed
mutability return a matrix object compatible with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 

 The operations for computing an identity matrix with prescribed mutability
return a matrix object compatible with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, provided that the base domain admits this and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} is square and nonempty. 

 Analogously, the operations for computing an inverse matrix with prescribed
mutability return a matrix object compatible with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, provided that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} is invertible.  (If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} is not invertible then the operations return \texttt{fail}.) 

 \texttt{IsZero} returns \texttt{true} if all entries in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} are zero, and \texttt{false} otherwise. \texttt{IsOne} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} is nonempty and square and contains the identity of the base domain in the
diagonal, and zero in all other places. 

 \texttt{Characteristic} returns the corresponding value of the \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) value of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Binary Arithmetical Operations for Matrix Objects}}\logpage{[ 26, 10, 2 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7BBB70557A7A9591}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}+({\mdseries\slshape M1, M2})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}+@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}+}!for two matrix objects}
\label{bSlash+:for two matrix objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}({\mdseries\slshape M1, M2})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}}!for two matrix objects}
\label{bSlash-:for two matrix objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*({\mdseries\slshape s, M})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*}!for scalar and matrix object}
\label{bSlash*:for scalar and matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*({\mdseries\slshape M, s})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*}!for Matrix object and scalar}
\label{bSlash*:for Matrix object and scalar}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*({\mdseries\slshape M1, M2})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*}!for two matrix objects}
\label{bSlash*:for two matrix objects}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/({\mdseries\slshape M, s})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/}!for matrix object and scalar}
\label{bSlash/:for matrix object and scalar}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}({\mdseries\slshape M, n})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}}!for matrix object and integer}
\label{bSlash^:for matrix object and integer}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\


 The sum and the difference, respectively, of two matrix objects \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M2}} is a new fully mutable matrix object whose entries are the sums and the
differences of the entries of the arguments. 

 The product of a scalar \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} and a matrix object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} (from the left or from the right) is a new fully mutable matrix object whose
entries are the corresponding products. 

 The product of two matrix objects \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M2}} is a new fully mutable matrix object; if both \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M2}} are in the filter \texttt{IsOrdinaryMatrix} (\ref{IsOrdinaryMatrix}) then the entries of the result are those of the ordinary matrix product. 

 The quotient of a matrix object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} and a scalar \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} is a new fully mutable matrix object whose entries are the corresponding
quotients. 

 For a nonempty square matrix object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} over an associative base domain, and a positive integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{94}}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} is a fully mutable matrix object whose entries are those of the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th power of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} is zero then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{94}}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} is an identity matrix, and if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} is a negative integer and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} is invertible then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{94}}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} is the (\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{45}}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}})\texttt{\symbol{45}}th power of the inverse of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 

 All this is defined only if the matrix objects have the same dimensions and
are defined over the same base domain and have the same representation, and if
the products with the given scalar belong to the base domain; otherwise it is
not specified what happens. If the result is a matrix object then it has the
same representation and the same base domain as the given matrix object(s). }

 }

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MatElm}}
\logpage{[ 26, 11, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X870FBE817C884AB5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MatElm({\mdseries\slshape M, row, col})\index{MatElm@\texttt{MatElm}}
\label{MatElm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
an entry of the matrix object



 For a matrix object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, this operation returns the entry in row \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape row}} and column \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape col}}. 

 Also the syntax \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{[ }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape row}}\texttt{, }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape col}}\texttt{ ]} is supported. 

 Note that this is \emph{not} equivalent to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{[ }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape row}}\texttt{ ][ }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape col}}\texttt{ ]}, which would first try to access \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{[ }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape row}}\texttt{ ]}, and this is in general not possible. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SetMatElm}}
\logpage{[ 26, 11, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C33059984635480}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SetMatElm({\mdseries\slshape M, row, col, obj})\index{SetMatElm@\texttt{SetMatElm}}
\label{SetMatElm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
nothing



 For a mutable matrix object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, this operation assigns the object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} to the position in row \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape row}} and column \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape col}}, provided that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} is compatible with the \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) value of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 

 Also the syntax \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{[ }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape row}}\texttt{, }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape col}}\texttt{ ]:= }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} is supported. 

 Note that this is \emph{not} equivalent to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{[ }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape row}}\texttt{ ][ }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape col}}\texttt{ ]:= }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}}, which would first try to access \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{[ }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape row}}\texttt{ ]}, and this is in general not possible. 

 If the global option \texttt{check} is set to \texttt{false} then \texttt{SetMatElm} need not perform consistency checks. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ExtractSubMatrix}}
\logpage{[ 26, 11, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X838B45F7790E9FDF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ExtractSubMatrix({\mdseries\slshape M, rows, cols})\index{ExtractSubMatrix@\texttt{ExtractSubMatrix}}
\label{ExtractSubMatrix}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Creates a copy of the submatrix described by the two lists, which mean subsets
of row and column positions, respectively. This does \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rows}}\texttt{\symbol{125}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape cols}}\texttt{\symbol{125}} and returns the result. It preserves the representation
of the matrix. 

 If the \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a matrix object}) value of the result implies \texttt{IsCopyable} (\ref{IsCopyable}) then the result is fully mutable. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MutableCopyMatrix (for a matrix object)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 11, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X793CD4637F237915}{}

 For a matrix object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, this operation returns a fully mutable copy of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, with the same \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a matrix object}) and \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) values, }

 Does \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dst}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape drows}}\texttt{\symbol{125}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dcols}}\texttt{\symbol{125}} := \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape src}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape srows}}\texttt{\symbol{125}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape scols}}\texttt{\symbol{125}}} without creating an intermediate object and thus {\textendash}at least in

 If the global option \texttt{check} is set to \texttt{false} then \texttt{CopySubMatrix} need not perform consistency checks. }

 The idea is that there should be an efficient way to form the product $v$\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. }

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CompanionMatrix}}\logpage{[ 26, 11, 8 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7E06762479A00DF4}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CompanionMatrix({\mdseries\slshape pol, M})\index{CompanionMatrix@\texttt{CompanionMatrix}!for polynomial and matrix object}
\label{CompanionMatrix:for polynomial and matrix object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CompanionMatrix({\mdseries\slshape filt, pol, R})\index{CompanionMatrix@\texttt{CompanionMatrix}!for filter, polynomial, and semiring}
\label{CompanionMatrix:for filter, polynomial, and semiring}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CompanionMatrix({\mdseries\slshape pol, R})\index{CompanionMatrix@\texttt{CompanionMatrix}!for polynomial and semiring}
\label{CompanionMatrix:for polynomial and semiring}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a matrix object



 For a monic, univariate polynomial \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pol}} whose coefficients lie in the base domain of the matrix object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, \texttt{CompanionMatrix} returns the companion matrix of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pol}}, as a matrix object with the same \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a matrix object}) and \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) values as \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 

 We use column convention, that is, the negatives of the coefficients of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pol}} appear in the last column of the result. 

 If a filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} and a semiring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are given then the companion matrix is returned as a matrix object with \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a matrix object}) value \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} and \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) value \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 

 If only \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pol}} and a semiring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are given, the representation of the result is guessed from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 

 If the \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a matrix object}) value of the result implies \texttt{IsCopyable} (\ref{IsCopyable}) then the result is fully mutable. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x:= X( GF(5) );;  pol:= x^3 + x^2 + 2*x + 3;;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@M:= CompanionMatrix( IsPlistMatrixRep, pol, GF(25) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Display( M );|
  <3x3-matrix over GF(5^2):
  [[ 0*Z(5), 0*Z(5), Z(5) ]
   [ Z(5)^0, 0*Z(5), Z(5)^3 ]
   [ 0*Z(5), Z(5)^0, Z(5)^2 ]
  ]>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Operations for Row List Matrix Objects}}\label{Operations for Row List Matrix Objects}
\logpage{[ 26, 12, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7D40EE2084A6C976}{}
{
  In general, matrix objects are not lists in the sense of \texttt{IsList} (\ref{IsList}), and they need not behave like lists, that is, they need not obey all the
rules for lists that are stated in Chapter \ref{Lists}. There are situations where one wants to have matrix objects that can on the
one hand benefit from \textsf{GAP}'s method selection, as is explained in Section \ref{Concepts and Rules for Vector and Matrix Objects}, and do on the other hands support access to \textsf{GAP} objects that represent their rows (which are suitable vector objects). Matrix
objects whose \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a matrix object}) value implies \texttt{IsRowListMatrix} (\ref{IsRowListMatrix}) support the operations described in this section. 

 One implementation of such matrices is given by the \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a matrix object}) value \texttt{IsPlistMatrixRep} (\ref{IsPlistMatrixRep}), and any row of these matrices is a vector object in \texttt{IsPlistVectorRep} (\ref{IsPlistVectorRep}). Note that these objects do \emph{not} lie in \texttt{IsList} (\ref{IsList}) (and in particular not in \texttt{IsPlistRep} (\ref{IsPlistRep})), thus we are allowed to define the above operations only restrictively, as
follows. 

 Unbinding an entry in a row or unbinding a row in a matrix is allowed only in
the last position, that is, the vector and matrix objects insist on being
dense. All rows of a matrix must have the same length and the same base
domain. 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{List Access for a Row List Matrix}}\logpage{[ 26, 12, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X82C4FCFA808010F8}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]({\mdseries\slshape M, pos})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]}!for a row list matrix}
\label{bSlash[bSlash]:for a row list matrix}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a vector object



 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} is a row list matrix and if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}} is a positive integer not larger than the number of rows of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, this operation returns the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th row of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 

 It is not specified what happens if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}} is larger. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{List Assignment for a Row List Matrix}}\logpage{[ 26, 12, 2 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7F89BB2482D28AAE}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]\texttt{\symbol{92}}:\texttt{\symbol{92}}=({\mdseries\slshape M, pos, v})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]\texttt{\symbol{92}}:\texttt{\symbol{92}}=@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]\texttt{\symbol{92}}:\texttt{\symbol{92}}=}!for a row list matrix and a vector object}
\label{bSlash[bSlash]bSlash:bSlash=:for a row list matrix and a vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
nothing



 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} is a row list matrix, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} is a vector object that can occur as a row in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} (that is, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} has the same base domain, the right length, and the right vector
representation), and if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}} is a positive integer not larger than the number of rows of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} plus 1, this operation sets \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} as the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th row of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 

 In all other situations, it is not specified what happens. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Sublist Access for a Row List Matrix}}\logpage{[ 26, 12, 3 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X807518367C96516F}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{125}}({\mdseries\slshape M, poss})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{125}}@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{125}}}!for a row list matrix}
\label{bSlash{bSlash}:for a row list matrix}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a row list matrix



 For a row list matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} and a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape poss}} of positions, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{123}} }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape poss}}\texttt{ \texttt{\symbol{125}}} returns a new mutable row list matrix with the same representation as \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, whose rows are identical to the rows at the positions in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape poss}} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Sublist Assignment for a Row List Matrix}}\logpage{[ 26, 12, 4 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8371789181FA136B}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{125}}\texttt{\symbol{92}}:\texttt{\symbol{92}}=({\mdseries\slshape M, poss, M2})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{125}}\texttt{\symbol{92}}:\texttt{\symbol{92}}=@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{123}}\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{125}}\texttt{\symbol{92}}:\texttt{\symbol{92}}=}!for row list matrices}
\label{bSlash{bSlash}bSlash:bSlash=:for row list matrices}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
nothing



 For a mutable row list matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape poss}} of positions, and a row list matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M2}} of the same vector type and with the same base domain, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{123}} }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape poss}}\texttt{ \texttt{\symbol{125}}:= }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M2}} assigns the rows of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M2}} to the positions \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape poss}} in the list of rows of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 

 It is not specified what happens if the resulting range of row positions is
not dense. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsBound\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}] (for a row list matrix)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 12, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X872E63867803ED78}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsBound\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]({\mdseries\slshape M, pos})\index{IsBound\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]@\texttt{IsBound\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]}!for a row list matrix}
\label{IsBoundbSlash[bSlash]:for a row list matrix}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
\texttt{true} or \texttt{false}



 For a row list matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} and a positive integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}}, \texttt{IsBound( }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{[ }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}}\texttt{ ] )} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}} is at most the number of rows of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, and \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Unbind\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}] (for a row list matrix)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 12, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79328CB280C71DDB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Unbind\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]({\mdseries\slshape M, pos})\index{Unbind\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]@\texttt{Unbind\texttt{\symbol{92}}[\texttt{\symbol{92}}]}!for a row list matrix}
\label{UnbindbSlash[bSlash]:for a row list matrix}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
nothing



 For a mutable row list matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}} rows, \texttt{Unbind( }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}\texttt{[ }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}}\texttt{ ] )} removes the last row. It is not specified what happens if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}} has another value. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Add (for a row list matrix and a vector object)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 12, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BDD838579E4D2D6}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Add({\mdseries\slshape M, v[, pos]})\index{Add@\texttt{Add}!for a row list matrix and a vector object}
\label{Add:for a row list matrix and a vector object}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
nothing



 For a mutable row list matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} and a vector object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} that is compatible with the rows of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, the two argument version adds \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} at the end of the list of rows of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 

 If a positive integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}} is given then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}} is added in position \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}}, and all later rows are shifted up by one position. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Remove (for a row list matrix)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 12, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86E355D07A41C025}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Remove({\mdseries\slshape M[, pos]})\index{Remove@\texttt{Remove}!for a row list matrix}
\label{Remove:for a row list matrix}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a vector object if the removed row exists, otherwise nothing



 For a mutable row list matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, this operation removes the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th row and shifts the later rows down by one position. The
default for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}} is the number of rows of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 

 If the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pos}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th row existed in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} then it is returned, otherwise nothing is returned. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Append (for two row list matrices)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 12, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82D0359B81F8D442}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Append({\mdseries\slshape M1, M2})\index{Append@\texttt{Append}!for two row list matrices}
\label{Append:for two row list matrices}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
nothing



 For two row list matrices \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M2}} such that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M1}} is mutable and such that the \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a matrix object}) and \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) values are equal, this operation appends the rows of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M2}} to the rows of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M1}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ShallowCopy (for a row list matrix)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 12, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E234F717BE333EA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ShallowCopy({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{ShallowCopy@\texttt{ShallowCopy}!for a row list matrix}
\label{ShallowCopy:for a row list matrix}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a matrix object



 For a row list matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, this operation returns a new mutable matrix with the same \texttt{ConstructingFilter} (\ref{ConstructingFilter:for a matrix object}) and \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) values as \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, which shares its rows with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ListOp (for a row list matrix)}}
\logpage{[ 26, 12, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E9F095E85DED480}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ListOp({\mdseries\slshape M[, func]})\index{ListOp@\texttt{ListOp}!for a row list matrix}
\label{ListOp:for a row list matrix}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a plain list



 For a row list matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}, the variant with one argument returns the plain list (see \texttt{IsPlistRep} (\ref{IsPlistRep})) of its rows, and the variant with two arguments returns the plain list of
values of these rows under the function \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape func}}. }

 }

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MultMatrixRowLeft}}
\logpage{[ 26, 13, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B3997D37CC44FCA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MultMatrixRowLeft({\mdseries\slshape mat, i, elm})\index{MultMatrixRowLeft@\texttt{MultMatrixRowLeft}}
\label{MultMatrixRowLeft}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MultMatrixRow({\mdseries\slshape mat, i, elm})\index{MultMatrixRow@\texttt{MultMatrixRow}}
\label{MultMatrixRow}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
nothing



 

 Multiplies the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th row of the mutable matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mat}} with the scalar \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} from the left in\texttt{\symbol{45}}place. 

 \texttt{MultMatrixRow} is a synonym of \texttt{MultMatrixRowLeft}. This was chosen because linear combinations of rows of matrices are usually
written as $ v \cdot A = [v_1, ... ,v_n] \cdot A$ which multiplies scalars from the left. }
