\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Useful Categories for all Elements of a Family}}\label{Useful Categories for all Elements of a Family}
\logpage{[ 31, 15, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7ABEF00C870789D2}{}
{
  The following categories of elements are to be understood mainly as categories
for all objects in a family, they are usually used as third argument of \texttt{NewFamily} (\ref{NewFamily}). The purpose of each of the following categories is then to guarantee that
each collection of its elements automatically lies in its collections category
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{CategoryCollections} (\ref{CategoryCollections})). 

 For example, the multiplication of permutations is associative, and it is
stored in the family of permutations that each permutation lies in \texttt{IsAssociativeElement} (\ref{IsAssociativeElement}). As a consequence, each magma consisting of permutations (more precisely:
each collection that lies in the family \texttt{CollectionsFamily( PermutationsFamily )}, see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{CollectionsFamily} (\ref{CollectionsFamily})) automatically lies in \texttt{CategoryCollections( IsAssociativeElement )}. A magma in this category is always known to be associative, via a logical
implication (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Logical Implications}). 

 Similarly, if a family knows that all its elements are in the categories \texttt{IsJacobianElement} (\ref{IsJacobianElement}) and \texttt{IsZeroSquaredElement} (\ref{IsZeroSquaredElement}), then each algebra of these elements is automatically known to be a Lie
algebra (see Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Algebras}). 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsAssociativeElement}}
\logpage{[ 31, 15, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7979AFAA80FF795A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAssociativeElement({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsAssociativeElement@\texttt{IsAssociativeElement}}
\label{IsAssociativeElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAssociativeElementCollection({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsAssociativeElementCollection@\texttt{IsAssociativeElementCollection}}
\label{IsAssociativeElementCollection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAssociativeElementCollColl({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsAssociativeElementCollColl@\texttt{IsAssociativeElementCollColl}}
\label{IsAssociativeElementCollColl}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 An element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} in the category \texttt{IsAssociativeElement} knows that the multiplication of any elements in the family of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} is associative. For example, all permutations lie in this category, as well as
those ordinary matrices (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsOrdinaryMatrix} (\ref{IsOrdinaryMatrix})) whose entries are also in \texttt{IsAssociativeElement}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElement}}
\logpage{[ 31, 15, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78A286418205CE44}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElement({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElement@\texttt{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElement}}
\label{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElementCollection({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElementCollection@\texttt{IsAdditively}\-\texttt{Commutative}\-\texttt{Element}\-\texttt{Collection}}
\label{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElementCollection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElementCollColl({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElementCollColl@\texttt{IsAdditively}\-\texttt{Commutative}\-\texttt{Element}\-\texttt{Coll}\-\texttt{Coll}}
\label{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElementCollColl}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElementFamily({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElementFamily@\texttt{IsAdditively}\-\texttt{Commutative}\-\texttt{Element}\-\texttt{Family}}
\label{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElementFamily}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 An element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} in the category \texttt{IsAdditivelyCommutativeElement} knows that the addition of any elements in the family of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} is commutative. For example, each finite field element and each rational
number lies in this category. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsCommutativeElement}}
\logpage{[ 31, 15, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8137FA8D86714AC0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsCommutativeElement({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsCommutativeElement@\texttt{IsCommutativeElement}}
\label{IsCommutativeElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsCommutativeElementCollection({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsCommutativeElementCollection@\texttt{IsCommutativeElementCollection}}
\label{IsCommutativeElementCollection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsCommutativeElementCollColl({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsCommutativeElementCollColl@\texttt{IsCommutativeElementCollColl}}
\label{IsCommutativeElementCollColl}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 An element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} in the category \texttt{IsCommutativeElement} knows that the multiplication of any elements in the family of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} is commutative. For example, each finite field element and each rational
number lies in this category. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsFiniteOrderElement}}
\logpage{[ 31, 15, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X810D2E5E832594AA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFiniteOrderElement({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsFiniteOrderElement@\texttt{IsFiniteOrderElement}}
\label{IsFiniteOrderElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFiniteOrderElementCollection({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsFiniteOrderElementCollection@\texttt{IsFiniteOrderElementCollection}}
\label{IsFiniteOrderElementCollection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFiniteOrderElementCollColl({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsFiniteOrderElementCollColl@\texttt{IsFiniteOrderElementCollColl}}
\label{IsFiniteOrderElementCollColl}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 An element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} in the category \texttt{IsFiniteOrderElement} knows that it has finite multiplicative order. For example, each finite field
element and each permutation lies in this category. However the value may be \texttt{false} even if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} has finite order, but if this was not known when \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} was constructed. 

 Although it is legal to set this filter for any object with finite order, this
is really useful only in the case that all elements of a family are known to
have finite order. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsJacobianElement}}
\logpage{[ 31, 15, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X796957D0805A0221}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsJacobianElement({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsJacobianElement@\texttt{IsJacobianElement}}
\label{IsJacobianElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsJacobianElementCollection({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsJacobianElementCollection@\texttt{IsJacobianElementCollection}}
\label{IsJacobianElementCollection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsJacobianElementCollColl({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsJacobianElementCollColl@\texttt{IsJacobianElementCollColl}}
\label{IsJacobianElementCollColl}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRestrictedJacobianElement({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsRestrictedJacobianElement@\texttt{IsRestrictedJacobianElement}}
\label{IsRestrictedJacobianElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRestrictedJacobianElementCollection({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsRestrictedJacobianElementCollection@\texttt{IsRestricted}\-\texttt{Jacobian}\-\texttt{Element}\-\texttt{Collection}}
\label{IsRestrictedJacobianElementCollection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRestrictedJacobianElementCollColl({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsRestrictedJacobianElementCollColl@\texttt{IsRestrictedJacobianElementCollColl}}
\label{IsRestrictedJacobianElementCollColl}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 An element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} in the category \texttt{IsJacobianElement} knows that the multiplication of any elements in the family $F$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} satisfies the Jacobi identity, that is, $x * y * z + z * x * y + y * z * x$ is zero for all $x$, $y$, $z$ in $F$. 

 For example, each Lie matrix (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsLieMatrix} (\ref{IsLieMatrix})) lies in this category. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsZeroSquaredElement}}
\logpage{[ 31, 15, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7844399D7847AB24}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsZeroSquaredElement({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsZeroSquaredElement@\texttt{IsZeroSquaredElement}}
\label{IsZeroSquaredElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsZeroSquaredElementCollection({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsZeroSquaredElementCollection@\texttt{IsZeroSquaredElementCollection}}
\label{IsZeroSquaredElementCollection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsZeroSquaredElementCollColl({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsZeroSquaredElementCollColl@\texttt{IsZeroSquaredElementCollColl}}
\label{IsZeroSquaredElementCollColl}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 An element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} in the category \texttt{IsZeroSquaredElement} knows that \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}2 = Zero( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} )}. For example, each Lie matrix (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsLieMatrix} (\ref{IsLieMatrix})) lies in this category. 

 Although it is legal to set this filter for any zero squared object, this is
really useful only in the case that all elements of a family are known to have
square zero. }

 }

 }

            
\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Mappings}}\label{Mappings}
\logpage{[ 32, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7C9734B880042C73}{}
{
  \index{functions!as in mathematics} \index{relations} A \emph{mapping} in \textsf{GAP} is what is called a ``function'' in mathematics. \textsf{GAP} also implements \emph{generalized mappings} in which one element might have several images, these can be imagined as
subsets of the cartesian product and are often called ``relations''. 

 Most operations are declared for general mappings and therefore this manual
often refers to ``(general) mappings'', unless you deliberately need the generalization you can ignore the ``general'' bit and just read it as ``mappings''. 

 A \emph{general mapping} $F$ in \textsf{GAP} is described by its source $S$, its range $R$, and a subset $Rel$ of the direct product $S \times R$, which is called the underlying relation of $F$. $S$, $R$, and $Rel$ are generalized domains (see \ref{Domains}). The corresponding attributes for general mappings are \texttt{Source} (\ref{Source}), \texttt{Range} (\ref{Range:of a general mapping}), and \texttt{UnderlyingRelation} (\ref{UnderlyingRelation}).   

 Note that general mappings themselves are \emph{not} domains. One reason for this is that two general mappings with same underlying
relation are regarded as equal only if also the sources are equal and the
ranges are equal. Other, more technical, reasons are that general mappings and
domains have different basic operations, and that general mappings are
arithmetic objects (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Arithmetic Operations for General Mappings}); both should not apply to domains. 

 Each element of an underlying relation of a general mapping lies in the
category of direct product elements (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsDirectProductElement} (\ref{IsDirectProductElement})). 

 For each $s \in S$, the set $\{ r \in R | (s,r) \in Rel \}$ is called the set of \emph{images} of $s$. Analogously, for $r \in R$, the set $\{ s \in S | (s,r) \in Rel \}$ is called the set of \emph{preimages} of $r$. 

 The \emph{ordering} of general mappings via \texttt{{\textless}} is defined by the ordering of source, range, and underlying relation.
Specifically, if the source and range domains of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}} are the same, then one considers the union of the preimages of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}} as a strictly ordered set. The smaller of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}} is the one whose image is smaller on the first point of this sequence where
they differ. 

 For mappings which preserve an algebraic structure a \emph{kernel} is defined. Depending on the structure preserved the operation to compute this
kernel is called differently, see Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Mappings which are Compatible with Algebraic Structures}. 

 Some technical details of general mappings are described in
section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Technical Matters Concerning General Mappings}.   
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Direct Products and their Elements}}\label{sect:Direct Products and their Elements}
\logpage{[ 32, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X859A13548515A5D7}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsDirectProductElement}}
\logpage{[ 32, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87FD9FE787023FF0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsDirectProductElement({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsDirectProductElement@\texttt{IsDirectProductElement}}
\label{IsDirectProductElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 \texttt{IsDirectProductElement} is a subcategory of the meet of \texttt{IsDenseList} (\ref{IsDenseList}), \texttt{IsMultiplicativeElementWithInverse} (\ref{IsMultiplicativeElementWithInverse}), \texttt{IsAdditiveElementWithInverse} (\ref{IsAdditiveElementWithInverse}), and \texttt{IsCopyable} (\ref{IsCopyable}), where the arithmetic operations (addition, zero, additive inverse,
multiplication, powering, one, inverse) are defined componentwise. 

 Note that each of these operations will cause an error message if its result
for at least one component cannot be formed. 

 For an object in the filter \texttt{IsDirectProductElement}, \texttt{ShallowCopy} (\ref{ShallowCopy}) returns a mutable plain list with the same entries. The sum and the product of
a direct product element and a list in \texttt{IsListDefault} (\ref{IsListDefault}) is the list of sums and products, respectively. The sum and the product of a
direct product element and an object that is neither a list nor a collection
is the direct product element of componentwise sums and products,
respectively. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DirectProductElement}}
\logpage{[ 32, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8226334A862C5219}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DirectProductElement({\mdseries\slshape [fam, ]objlist})\index{DirectProductElement@\texttt{DirectProductElement}}
\label{DirectProductElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DirectProductElementNC({\mdseries\slshape fam, objlist})\index{DirectProductElementNC@\texttt{DirectProductElementNC}}
\label{DirectProductElementNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{DirectProductElement} returns a direct product element whose components are the entries of the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape objlist}}. If the optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} is given, it must be the family of direct product elements with the
appropriate component families; otherwise the family is determined from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape objlist}}. 

 \texttt{DirectProductElementNC} does the same but omits the checks that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} is consistent with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape objlist}}. 

 Direct product elements behave like lists: they can be indexed with \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}}[i]} to access the $i$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th component, and \texttt{Length} (\ref{Length}) returns the number of components. Arithmetic operations (multiplication,
powering, one, inverse, addition, zero, additive inverse) are performed
componentwise. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a := (1,2,3);; b := (1,2);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elm := DirectProductElement([a, b]);|
  DirectProductElement( [ (1,2,3), (1,2) ] )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elm[1];|
  (1,2,3)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elm[2];|
  (1,2)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Length(elm);|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elm2 := DirectProductElement([b, a]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elm * elm2;|
  DirectProductElement( [ (2,3), (1,3) ] )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@One(elm);|
  DirectProductElement( [ (), () ] )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Inverse(elm);|
  DirectProductElement( [ (1,3,2), (1,2) ] )
\end{Verbatim}
 

 The following example shows \texttt{DirectProductElement} in the context of a direct product $K = G \times H$ built with \texttt{DirectProduct} (\ref{DirectProduct}), where $G$ is a permutation group and $H$ is a pc group. The projections of $K$ are used to move between the direct product and its component groups. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G := DihedralGroup(IsPermGroup, 8);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@H := CyclicGroup(IsPcGroup, 4);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@K := DirectProduct(G, H);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@proj1 := Projection(K, 1);; proj2 := Projection(K, 2);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g := (1,2,3,4);; h := GeneratorsOfGroup(H)[1];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elm := DirectProductElement([g, h]);|
  DirectProductElement( [ (1,2,3,4), f1 ] )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Image(proj1, elm) = g;|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Image(proj2, elm) = h;|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DirectProductFamily}}
\logpage{[ 32, 1, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78F8A1168280E06D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DirectProductFamily({\mdseries\slshape args})\index{DirectProductFamily@\texttt{DirectProductFamily}}
\label{DirectProductFamily}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape args}} must be a dense list of \texttt{CollectionsFamily} (\ref{CollectionsFamily}) families, otherwise the function raises an error. 

 \texttt{DirectProductFamily} returns \texttt{fam}, a collections family of \texttt{IsDirectProductElement} (\ref{IsDirectProductElement}) objects. 

 \texttt{fam} is the \texttt{CollectionsFamily} (\ref{CollectionsFamily}) of \texttt{IsDirectProductElement} (\ref{IsDirectProductElement}) objects whose \texttt{i}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th component is in \texttt{ElementsFamily(args[i])}. 

 Note that a collection in \texttt{fam} may not itself be a direct product; it just is a subcollection of a direct
product. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@D8 := DihedralGroup(IsPermGroup, 8);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FamilyObj(D8) = CollectionsFamily(PermutationsFamily);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@fam := DirectProductFamily([FamilyObj(D8), FamilyObj(D8)]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ComponentsOfDirectProductElementsFamily(ElementsFamily(fam));|
  [ <Family: "PermutationsFamily">, <Family: "PermutationsFamily"> ]
\end{Verbatim}
 Also note that not all direct products in \textsf{GAP} are created via these families. For example if the arguments to \texttt{DirectProduct} (\ref{DirectProduct}) are permutation groups, then it returns a permutation group as well, whose
elements are not \texttt{IsDirectProductElement} (\ref{IsDirectProductElement}) objects. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@fam = FamilyObj(DirectProduct(D8, D8));|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@D4 := DihedralGroup(IsPcGroup, 4);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@fam2 := DirectProductFamily([FamilyObj(D8), FamilyObj(D4)]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@fam2 = FamilyObj(DirectProduct(D8, D4));|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Creating Mappings}}\label{Creating Mappings}
\logpage{[ 32, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7CF6FEFB8290D5CB}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneralMappingByElements}}
\logpage{[ 32, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79D0D2F07A14D039}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneralMappingByElements({\mdseries\slshape S, R, elms})\index{GeneralMappingByElements@\texttt{GeneralMappingByElements}}
\label{GeneralMappingByElements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 is the general mapping with source \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and range \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, and with underlying relation consisting of the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elms}} of direct product elements. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MappingByFunction}}\logpage{[ 32, 2, 2 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7D55E1977ED70E01}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MappingByFunction({\mdseries\slshape S, R, fun[, invfun]})\index{MappingByFunction@\texttt{MappingByFunction}!by function (and inverse function) between two domains}
\label{MappingByFunction:by function (and inverse function) between two domains}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MappingByFunction({\mdseries\slshape S, R, fun, false, prefun})\index{MappingByFunction@\texttt{MappingByFunction}!by function and function that computes one preimage}
\label{MappingByFunction:by function and function that computes one preimage}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{MappingByFunction} returns a mapping \texttt{map} with source \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and range \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, such that each element $s$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is mapped to the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fun}}$( s )$, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fun}} is a \textsf{GAP} function. 

 If the argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape invfun}} is bound then \texttt{map} is a bijection between \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, and the preimage of each element $r$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is given by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape invfun}}$( r )$, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape invfun}} is a \textsf{GAP} function. 

 If five arguments are given and the fourth argument is \texttt{false} then the \textsf{GAP} function \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prefun}} can be used to compute a single preimage also if \texttt{map} is not bijective.    

 The mapping returned by \texttt{MappingByFunction} lies in the filter \texttt{IsNonSPGeneralMapping} (\ref{IsNonSPGeneralMapping}), see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Technical Matters Concerning General Mappings}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{InverseGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X865FC25A87D36F3D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InverseGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{InverseGeneralMapping@\texttt{InverseGeneralMapping}}
\label{InverseGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The \emph{inverse general mapping} of a general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} is the general mapping whose underlying relation (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{UnderlyingRelation} (\ref{UnderlyingRelation})) contains a pair $(r,s)$ if and only if the underlying relation of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} contains the pair $(s,r)$. 

 Note that the inverse general mapping of a mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} is in general only a general mapping. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} knows to be bijective, then its inverse general mapping will know to be a
mapping. However, \texttt{Inverse} (\ref{Inverse}) works for a bijective general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} only if the source and range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} coincide. This behaviour agrees with the definition of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Inverse}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RestrictedInverseGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 2, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BD2D5A87CD6B213}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RestrictedInverseGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{RestrictedInverseGeneralMapping@\texttt{RestrictedInverseGeneralMapping}}
\label{RestrictedInverseGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The \emph{restricted inverse general mapping} of a general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} is the general mapping whose underlying relation (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{UnderlyingRelation} (\ref{UnderlyingRelation})) contains a pair $(r,s)$ if and only if the underlying relation of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} contains the pair $(s,r)$, and whose domain is restricted to the image of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} and whose range is the domain of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CompositionMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 2, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7ED1E4E27CCE2DCA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CompositionMapping({\mdseries\slshape map1, map2, ...})\index{CompositionMapping@\texttt{CompositionMapping}}
\label{CompositionMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{CompositionMapping} allows one to compose arbitrarily many general mappings, and delegates each
step to \texttt{CompositionMapping2} (\ref{CompositionMapping2}). The result is a map that maps an element first under the last argument, then
under the penultimate argument and so forth. 

 Additionally, the properties \texttt{IsInjective} (\ref{IsInjective}) and \texttt{IsSingleValued} (\ref{IsSingleValued}) are maintained. If the range of the $i+1$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th argument is identical to the range of the $i$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th argument, also \texttt{IsTotal} (\ref{IsTotal}) and \texttt{IsSurjective} (\ref{IsSurjective}) are maintained. (So one should not call \texttt{CompositionMapping2} (\ref{CompositionMapping2}) directly if one wants to maintain these properties.) 

 Depending on the types of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}}, the returned mapping might be constructed completely new (for example by
giving domain generators and their images, this is for example the case if
both mappings preserve the same algebraic structures and \textsf{GAP} can decompose elements of the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}} into generators) or as an (iterated) composition (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsCompositionMappingRep} (\ref{IsCompositionMappingRep})). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := GroupHomomorphismByImages(CyclicGroup(IsPermGroup, 2),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@                                  CyclicGroup(IsPermGroup, 1));|
  [ (1,2) ] -> [ () ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g := GroupHomomorphismByImages(CyclicGroup(IsPermGroup, 6),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@                                  CyclicGroup(IsPermGroup, 2));|
  [ (1,2,3,4,5,6) ] -> [ (1,2) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@CompositionMapping(f, g);|
  [ (1,2,3,4,5,6) ] -> [ () ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@CompositionMapping(g, f);|
  [ (1,2) ] -> [ () ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CompositionMapping2}}
\logpage{[ 32, 2, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86486B687B7077AC}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CompositionMapping2({\mdseries\slshape map2, map1})\index{CompositionMapping2@\texttt{CompositionMapping2}}
\label{CompositionMapping2}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CompositionMapping2General({\mdseries\slshape map2, map1})\index{CompositionMapping2General@\texttt{CompositionMapping2General}}
\label{CompositionMapping2General}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{CompositionMapping2} returns the composition of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map1}}, this is the general mapping that maps an element first under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map1}}, and then maps the images under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}}. 

 (Note the reverse ordering of arguments in the composition via the
multiplication \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*} (\ref{bSlash*}). 

 \texttt{CompositionMapping2General} is the method that forms a composite mapping with two constituent mappings.
(This is used in some algorithms.) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsCompositionMappingRep}}
\logpage{[ 32, 2, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A926D167C3155F6}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsCompositionMappingRep({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{IsCompositionMappingRep@\texttt{IsCompositionMappingRep}}
\label{IsCompositionMappingRep}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Representation)}}\\


 Mappings in this representation are stored as composition of two mappings,
(pre)images of elements are computed in a two\texttt{\symbol{45}}step process.
The constituent mappings of the composition can be obtained via \texttt{ConstituentsCompositionMapping} (\ref{ConstituentsCompositionMapping}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ConstituentsCompositionMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 2, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87775B438008DCA5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ConstituentsCompositionMapping({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{ConstituentsCompositionMapping@\texttt{ConstituentsCompositionMapping}}
\label{ConstituentsCompositionMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} is stored in the representation \texttt{IsCompositionMappingRep} (\ref{IsCompositionMappingRep}) as composition of two mappings \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}}, this function returns the two constituent mappings in a list \texttt{[ \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}} ]}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ZeroMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 2, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X795FF8DC785F110A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ZeroMapping({\mdseries\slshape S, R})\index{ZeroMapping@\texttt{ZeroMapping}}
\label{ZeroMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 A zero mapping is a total general mapping that maps each element of its source
to the zero element of its range. 

 (Each mapping with empty source is a zero mapping.) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IdentityMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 2, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EBAE0368470A603}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IdentityMapping({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{IdentityMapping@\texttt{IdentityMapping}}
\label{IdentityMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the bijective mapping with source and range equal to the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}, which maps each element of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} to itself. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Embedding}}\logpage{[ 32, 2, 11 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X86452F8587CBAEA0}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Embedding({\mdseries\slshape S, T})\index{Embedding@\texttt{Embedding}!for two domains}
\label{Embedding:for two domains}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Embedding({\mdseries\slshape S, i})\index{Embedding@\texttt{Embedding}!for a domain and a positive integer}
\label{Embedding:for a domain and a positive integer}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns the embedding of the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} in the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape T}}, or in the second form, some domain indexed by the positive integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}. The precise natures of the various methods are described elsewhere: for Lie
algebras, see \texttt{LieFamily} (\ref{LieFamily}); for group products, see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Embeddings and Projections for Group Products} for a general description, or for examples see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Direct Products} for direct products, \ref{Semidirect Products} for semidirect products, or{\nobreakspace}\ref{Wreath Products} for wreath products; or for magma rings see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Natural Embeddings related to Magma Rings}. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Projection}}\logpage{[ 32, 2, 12 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8769E8DA80BC96C1}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Projection({\mdseries\slshape S, T})\index{Projection@\texttt{Projection}!for two domains}
\label{Projection:for two domains}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Projection({\mdseries\slshape S, i})\index{Projection@\texttt{Projection}!for a domain and a positive integer}
\label{Projection:for a domain and a positive integer}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Projection({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{Projection@\texttt{Projection}!for a domain}
\label{Projection:for a domain}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns the projection of the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} onto the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape T}}, or in the second form, some domain indexed by the positive integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}, or in the third form some natural quotient domain of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. Various methods are defined for group products; see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Embeddings and Projections for Group Products} for a general description, or for examples see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Direct Products} for direct products, \ref{Semidirect Products} for semidirect products, \ref{Subdirect Products} for subdirect products, or{\nobreakspace}\ref{Wreath Products} for wreath products. }

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape subdom}} is a subdomain of the source of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, this operation returns the restriction of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape subdom}}.  }

\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Properties and Attributes of (General) Mappings}}\label{Properties and Attributes of (General) Mappings}
\logpage{[ 32, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7E5A430D7F838F1C}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsTotal}}
\logpage{[ 32, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83C7494E828CC9C8}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsTotal({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{IsTotal@\texttt{IsTotal}}
\label{IsTotal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if each element in the source $S$ of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} has images, i.e., $s^{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}} \neq \emptyset$ for all $s \in S$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSingleValued}}
\logpage{[ 32, 3, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86D44C8A78BF1981}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSingleValued({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{IsSingleValued@\texttt{IsSingleValued}}
\label{IsSingleValued}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if each element in the source $S$ of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} has at most one image, i.e., $|s^{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}}| \leq 1$ for all $s \in S$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 Equivalently, \texttt{IsSingleValued( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} )} is \texttt{true} if and only if the preimages of different elements in $R$ are disjoint. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 3, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7CC95EB282854385}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsMapping({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{IsMapping@\texttt{IsMapping}}
\label{IsMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 A \emph{mapping} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} is a general mapping that assigns to each element \texttt{elm} of its source a unique element \texttt{Image( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, elm )} of its range. 

 Equivalently, the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} is a mapping if and only if it is total and single\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsTotal} (\ref{IsTotal}), \texttt{IsSingleValued} (\ref{IsSingleValued})). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsInjective}}
\logpage{[ 32, 3, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F065FD7822C0A12}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsInjective({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{IsInjective@\texttt{IsInjective}}
\label{IsInjective}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if the images of different elements in the source $S$ of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} are disjoint, i.e., $x^{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}} \cap y^{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}} = \emptyset$ for $x \neq y \in S$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 Equivalently, \texttt{IsInjective( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} )} is \texttt{true} if and only if each element in the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} has at most one preimage in $S$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSurjective}}
\logpage{[ 32, 3, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X784ECE847E005B8F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSurjective({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{IsSurjective@\texttt{IsSurjective}}
\label{IsSurjective}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if each element in the range $R$ of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} has preimages in the source $S$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., $\{ s \in S \mid x \in s^{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}} \} \neq \emptyset$ for all $x \in R$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsBijective}}
\logpage{[ 32, 3, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X878F56AB7B342767}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsBijective({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{IsBijective@\texttt{IsBijective}}
\label{IsBijective}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} is \emph{bijective} if and only if it is an injective and surjective mapping (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsMapping} (\ref{IsMapping}), \texttt{IsInjective} (\ref{IsInjective}), \texttt{IsSurjective} (\ref{IsSurjective})). }

\logpage{[ 32, 3, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B6FD7277CDE9FCB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Range({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{Range@\texttt{Range}!of a general mapping}
\label{Range:of a general mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The range of a general mapping. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Source}}
\logpage{[ 32, 3, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DE8173F80E07AB1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Source({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{Source@\texttt{Source}}
\label{Source}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The source of a general mapping. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{UnderlyingRelation}}
\logpage{[ 32, 3, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X784F871383FB599B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{UnderlyingRelation({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{UnderlyingRelation@\texttt{UnderlyingRelation}}
\label{UnderlyingRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The \emph{underlying relation} of a general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} is the domain of pairs $(s,r)$, with $s$ in the source and $r$ in the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Source} (\ref{Source}), \texttt{Range} (\ref{Range:of a general mapping})), and $r \in$ \texttt{ImagesElm( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, }$s$\texttt{ )}. 

 Each element of the underlying relation is represented by a direct product
element (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsDirectProductElement} (\ref{IsDirectProductElement})). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{UnderlyingGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 3, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X786581DE871A47D0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{UnderlyingGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{UnderlyingGeneralMapping@\texttt{UnderlyingGeneralMapping}}
\label{UnderlyingGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 attribute for underlying relations of general mappings }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Images under Mappings}}\label{Images under Mappings}
\logpage{[ 32, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X83B4FF15847F06FC}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ImagesSource}}
\logpage{[ 32, 4, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D23C1CE863DACD8}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ImagesSource({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{ImagesSource@\texttt{ImagesSource}}
\label{ImagesSource}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the set of images of the source of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 \texttt{ImagesSource} delegates to \texttt{ImagesSet} (\ref{ImagesSet}), it is introduced only to store the image of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} as attribute value. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ImagesRepresentative}}
\logpage{[ 32, 4, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85ADB89B7C8DD7D0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ImagesRepresentative({\mdseries\slshape map, elm})\index{ImagesRepresentative@\texttt{ImagesRepresentative}}
\label{ImagesRepresentative}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is an element of the source of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} then \texttt{ImagesRepresentative} returns either a representative of the set of images of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} or \texttt{fail}, the latter if and only if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} has no images under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 Anything may happen if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is not an element of the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ImagesElm}}
\logpage{[ 32, 4, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D51184B7EE5B2CF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ImagesElm({\mdseries\slshape map, elm})\index{ImagesElm@\texttt{ImagesElm}}
\label{ImagesElm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is an element of the source of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} then \texttt{ImagesElm} returns the set of all images of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 Anything may happen if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is not an element of the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ImagesSet}}
\logpage{[ 32, 4, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8781348F7F5796A0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ImagesSet({\mdseries\slshape map, elms})\index{ImagesSet@\texttt{ImagesSet}}
\label{ImagesSet}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elms}} is a subset of the source of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} then \texttt{ImagesSet} returns the set of all images of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elms}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 The result will be either a proper set or a domain. Anything may happen if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elms}} is not a subset of the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ImageElm}}
\logpage{[ 32, 4, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7CFAB0157BFB1806}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ImageElm({\mdseries\slshape map, elm})\index{ImageElm@\texttt{ImageElm}}
\label{ImageElm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is an element of the source of the total and single\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued
mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} then \texttt{ImageElm} returns the unique image of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 Anything may happen if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is not an element of the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Image}}\logpage{[ 32, 4, 6 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X87F4D35A826599C6}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Image({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{Image@\texttt{Image}!set of images of the source of a general mapping}
\label{Image:set of images of the source of a general mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Image({\mdseries\slshape map, elm})\index{Image@\texttt{Image}!unique image of an element under a mapping}
\label{Image:unique image of an element under a mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Image({\mdseries\slshape map, coll})\index{Image@\texttt{Image}!set of images of a collection under a mapping}
\label{Image:set of images of a collection under a mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{Image( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} )} is the \emph{image} of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the subset of elements of the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} that are actually values of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. \emph{Note} that in this case the argument may also be multi\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued. 

 \texttt{Image( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} )} is the image of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} of the source of the mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the unique element of the range to which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} maps \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}}. This can also be expressed as \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{94}}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} or as \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}\texttt{( }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}}\texttt{ )}. 

 Note that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} must be total and single valued, a multi valued general mapping is not allowed
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Images} (\ref{Images:set of images of the source of a general mapping})). 

 \texttt{Image( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} )} is the image of the subset \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} of the source of the mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the subset of the range to which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} maps elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}}. 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} may be a proper set or a domain. The result will be either a proper set or a
domain. Note that in this case \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} may also be multi\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued. (If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} and the result are lists then the positions of entries do in general \emph{not} correspond.) 

 \texttt{Image( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} )} can also be expressed as \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}})} and \texttt{Image( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} )} as \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}})}. Those using this notation should remember that composition of mappings in \textsf{GAP} still follows the conventions appropriate for mapping acting from the right,
so that \texttt{(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map1}}*\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}})(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}})} is equivalent to \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map2}}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map1}}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}}))} 

 \texttt{Image} delegates to \texttt{ImagesSource} (\ref{ImagesSource}) when called with one argument, and to \texttt{ImageElm} (\ref{ImageElm}) resp. \texttt{ImagesSet} (\ref{ImagesSet}) when called with two arguments. 

 If the second argument is not an element or a subset of the source of the
first argument, an error is signalled. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Images}}\logpage{[ 32, 4, 7 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X86114B2E7E77488C}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Images({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{Images@\texttt{Images}!set of images of the source of a general mapping}
\label{Images:set of images of the source of a general mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Images({\mdseries\slshape map, elm})\index{Images@\texttt{Images}!set of images of an element under a mapping}
\label{Images:set of images of an element under a mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Images({\mdseries\slshape map, coll})\index{Images@\texttt{Images}!set of images of a collection under a mapping}
\label{Images:set of images of a collection under a mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{Images( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} )} is the \emph{image} of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the subset of elements of the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} that are actually values of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 \texttt{Images( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} )} is the set of images of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} of the source of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the set of elements of the range to which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} maps \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}}. 

 \texttt{Images( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} )} is the set of images of the subset \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} of the source of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the subset of the range to which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} maps elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}}. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} may be a proper set or a domain. The result will be either a proper set or a
domain. (If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} and the result are lists then the positions of entries do in general \emph{not} correspond.) 

 \texttt{Images} delegates to \texttt{ImagesSource} (\ref{ImagesSource}) when called with one argument, and to \texttt{ImagesElm} (\ref{ImagesElm}) resp. \texttt{ImagesSet} (\ref{ImagesSet}) when called with two arguments. 

 If the second argument is not an element or a subset of the source of the
first argument, an error is signalled. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Preimages under Mappings}}\label{Preimages under Mappings}
\logpage{[ 32, 5, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X79BB1EC07C828667}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PreImagesRange}}
\logpage{[ 32, 5, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78EF1FE77B0973C0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImagesRange({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{PreImagesRange@\texttt{PreImagesRange}}
\label{PreImagesRange}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the set of preimages of the range of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 \texttt{PreImagesRange} delegates to \texttt{PreImagesSet} (\ref{PreImagesSet}), it is introduced only to store the preimage of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} as attribute value. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PreImagesElm}}
\logpage{[ 32, 5, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7FBB830C8729E995}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImagesElm({\mdseries\slshape map, elm})\index{PreImagesElm@\texttt{PreImagesElm}}
\label{PreImagesElm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is an element of the range of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} then \texttt{PreImagesElm} returns the set of all preimages of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 Anything may happen if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is not an element of the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PreImageElm}}
\logpage{[ 32, 5, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D212F727CAE971A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImageElm({\mdseries\slshape map, elm})\index{PreImageElm@\texttt{PreImageElm}}
\label{PreImageElm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is an element of the range of the injective and surjective general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} then \texttt{PreImageElm} returns the unique preimage of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 Anything may happen if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is not an element of the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PreImagesRepresentative}}
\logpage{[ 32, 5, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AE24A1586B7DE79}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImagesRepresentative({\mdseries\slshape map, elm})\index{PreImagesRepresentative@\texttt{PreImagesRepresentative}}
\label{PreImagesRepresentative}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is an element of the range of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} then \texttt{PreImagesRepresentative} returns either a representative of the set of preimages of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} or \texttt{fail}, the latter if and only if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} has no preimages under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 Anything may happen if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is not an element of the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PreImagesSet}}
\logpage{[ 32, 5, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X856BAFC87B2D2811}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImagesSet({\mdseries\slshape map, elms})\index{PreImagesSet@\texttt{PreImagesSet}}
\label{PreImagesSet}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elms}} is a subset of the range of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} then \texttt{PreImagesSet} returns the set of all preimages of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elms}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 Anything may happen if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elms}} is not a subset of the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PreImage}}\logpage{[ 32, 5, 6 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X836FAEAC78B55BF4}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImage({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{PreImage@\texttt{PreImage}!set of preimages of the range of a general mapping}
\label{PreImage:set of preimages of the range of a general mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImage({\mdseries\slshape map, elm})\index{PreImage@\texttt{PreImage}!unique preimage of an element under a general mapping}
\label{PreImage:unique preimage of an element under a general mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImage({\mdseries\slshape map, coll})\index{PreImage@\texttt{PreImage}!set of preimages of a collection under a general mapping}
\label{PreImage:set of preimages of a collection under a general mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{PreImage( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} )} is the preimage of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the subset of elements of the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} that actually have values under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. Note that in this case the argument may also be
non\texttt{\symbol{45}}injective or non\texttt{\symbol{45}}surjective. 

 \texttt{PreImage( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} )} is the preimage of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} of the range of the injective and surjective mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the unique element of the source which is mapped under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}}. Note that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} must be injective and surjective (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{PreImages} (\ref{PreImages:set of preimages of the range of a general mapping})). 

 \texttt{PreImage( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} )} is the preimage of the subset \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} of the range of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the subset of the source which is mapped under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} to elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}}. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} may be a proper set or a domain. The result will be either a proper set or a
domain. Note that in this case \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} may also be non\texttt{\symbol{45}}injective or
non\texttt{\symbol{45}}surjective. (If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} and the result are lists then the positions of entries do in general \emph{not} correspond.) 

 \texttt{PreImage} delegates to \texttt{PreImagesRange} (\ref{PreImagesRange}) when called with one argument, and to \texttt{PreImageElm} (\ref{PreImageElm}) resp. \texttt{PreImagesSet} (\ref{PreImagesSet}) when called with two arguments. 

 If the second argument is not an element or a subset of the range of the first
argument, an error is signalled. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PreImages}}\logpage{[ 32, 5, 7 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X85C8590E832002EF}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImages({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{PreImages@\texttt{PreImages}!set of preimages of the range of a general mapping}
\label{PreImages:set of preimages of the range of a general mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImages({\mdseries\slshape map, elm})\index{PreImages@\texttt{PreImages}!set of preimages of an elm under a general mapping}
\label{PreImages:set of preimages of an elm under a general mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PreImages({\mdseries\slshape map, coll})\index{PreImages@\texttt{PreImages}!set of preimages of a collection under a general mapping}
\label{PreImages:set of preimages of a collection under a general mapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{PreImages( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} )} is the preimage of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the subset of elements of the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} that have actually values under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. 

 \texttt{PreImages( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} )} is the set of preimages of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} of the range of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the set of elements of the source which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} maps to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}}. 

 \texttt{PreImages( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} )} is the set of images of the subset \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} of the range of the general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}, i.e., the subset of the source which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} maps to elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}}. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} may be a proper set or a domain. The result will be either a proper set or a
domain. (If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} and the result are lists then the positions of entries do in general \emph{not} correspond.) 

 \texttt{PreImages} delegates to \texttt{PreImagesRange} (\ref{PreImagesRange}) when called with one argument, and to \texttt{PreImagesElm} (\ref{PreImagesElm}) resp. \texttt{PreImagesSet} (\ref{PreImagesSet}) when called with two arguments. 

 If the second argument is not an element or a subset of the range of the first
argument, an error is signalled. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Arithmetic Operations for General Mappings}}\label{Arithmetic Operations for General Mappings}
\logpage{[ 32, 6, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7E2E16277940FA0B}{}
{
  General mappings are arithmetic objects. One can form groups and vector spaces
of general mappings provided that they are invertible or can be added and
admit scalar multiplication, respectively. 

 For two general mappings with same source, range, preimage, and image, the \emph{sum} is defined pointwise, i.e., the images of a point under the sum is the set of
all sums with first summand in the images of the first general mapping and
second summand in the images of the second general mapping. 

 \emph{Scalar multiplication} of general mappings is defined likewise. 

 The \emph{product} of two general mappings is defined as the composition. This multiplication is
always associative. In addition to the composition via \texttt{*}, general mappings can be composed {\textendash}in reversed order{\textendash}
via \texttt{CompositionMapping} (\ref{CompositionMapping}). 

 General mappings are in the category of multiplicative elements with inverses.
Similar to matrices, not every general mapping has an inverse or an identity,
and we define the behaviour of \texttt{One} (\ref{One}) and \texttt{Inverse} (\ref{Inverse}) for general mappings as follows. \texttt{One} (\ref{One}) returns \texttt{fail} when called for a general mapping whose source and range differ, otherwise \texttt{One} (\ref{One}) returns the identity mapping of the source. (Note that the source may differ
from the preimage). \texttt{Inverse} (\ref{Inverse}) returns \texttt{fail} when called for a non\texttt{\symbol{45}}bijective general mapping or for a
general mapping whose source and range differ; otherwise \texttt{Inverse} (\ref{Inverse}) returns the inverse mapping. 

 Besides the usual inverse of multiplicative elements, which means that \texttt{Inverse( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} ) * \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} = \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} * Inverse( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} ) = One( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} )}, for general mappings we have the attribute \texttt{InverseGeneralMapping} (\ref{InverseGeneralMapping}). If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} is a general mapping with source $S$, range $R$, and underlying relation $Rel$ then \texttt{InverseGeneralMapping( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} )} has source $R$, range $S$, and underlying relation $\{ (r,s) \mid (s,r) \in Rel \}$. For a general mapping that has an inverse in the usual sense, i.e., for a
bijection of the source, of course both concepts coincide. 

 \texttt{Inverse} (\ref{Inverse}) may delegate to \texttt{InverseGeneralMapping} (\ref{InverseGeneralMapping}). \texttt{InverseGeneralMapping} (\ref{InverseGeneralMapping}) must not delegate to \texttt{Inverse} (\ref{Inverse}), but a known value of \texttt{Inverse} (\ref{Inverse}) may be fetched. So methods to compute the inverse of a general mapping should
be installed for \texttt{InverseGeneralMapping} (\ref{InverseGeneralMapping}). 

 (Note that in many respects, general mappings behave similar to matrices, for
example one can define left and right identities and inverses, which do not
fit into the current concepts of \textsf{GAP}.) }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Mappings which are Compatible with Algebraic Structures}}\label{Mappings which are Compatible with Algebraic Structures}
\logpage{[ 32, 7, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X834E02BB7D4B4AE5}{}
{
  From an algebraical point of view, the most important mappings are those which
are compatible with a structure. For Magmas, Groups and Rings, \textsf{GAP} supports the following four types of such mappings: 

 
\begin{enumerate}
\item  General mappings that respect multiplication 
\item  General mappings that respect addition 
\item  General mappings that respect scalar mult. 
\item  General mappings that respect multiplicative and additive structure 
\end{enumerate}
 

 (Very technical note: \textsf{GAP} defines categories \texttt{IsSPGeneralMapping} and \texttt{IsNonSPGeneralMapping}. The distinction between these is orthogonal to the structure compatibility
described here and should not be confused.) }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Magma Homomorphisms}}\label{Magma Homomorphisms}
\logpage{[ 32, 8, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8008FCCC7F4C731F}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsMagmaHomomorphism}}
\logpage{[ 32, 8, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DC72CF28539A251}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsMagmaHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{IsMagmaHomomorphism@\texttt{IsMagmaHomomorphism}}
\label{IsMagmaHomomorphism}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 A \emph{magma homomorphism} is a total single valued mapping which respects multiplication. }

\hyperdef{L}{X8181676787E760A2}{}
