}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Creates the homomorphism from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape H}} without checking that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fn}} is a homomorphism. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NaturalHomomorphismByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 32, 8, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79D0216E871B7051}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NaturalHomomorphismByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape f, s})\index{NaturalHomomorphismByGenerators@\texttt{NaturalHomomorphismByGenerators}}
\label{NaturalHomomorphismByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns a mapping from the magma \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape f}} with $n$ generators to the magma \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} with $n$ generators, which maps the $i$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th generator of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape f}} to the $i$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th generator of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Mappings that Respect Multiplication}}\label{Mappings that Respect Multiplication}
\logpage{[ 32, 9, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X806F892C862F29F9}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RespectsMultiplication}}
\logpage{[ 32, 9, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BEFF95883EAEC78}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RespectsMultiplication({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{RespectsMultiplication@\texttt{RespectsMultiplication}}
\label{RespectsMultiplication}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping with underlying relation $F \subseteq S \times R$, where $S$ and $R$ are the source and the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}, respectively. Then \texttt{RespectsMultiplication} returns \texttt{true} if $S$ and $R$ are magmas such that $(s_1,r_1), (s_2,r_2) \in F$ implies $(s_1 * s_2,r_1 * r_2) \in F$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} is single\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued then \texttt{RespectsMultiplication} returns \texttt{true} if and only if the equation \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s1}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} * \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s2}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} = (\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s1}} * \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s2}})\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}} holds for all \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s2}} in $S$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RespectsOne}}
\logpage{[ 32, 9, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EE4DA097AE9CBC1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RespectsOne({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{RespectsOne@\texttt{RespectsOne}}
\label{RespectsOne}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping with underlying relation $F \subseteq \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}$, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are the source and the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}, respectively. Then \texttt{RespectsOne} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are magmas\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one such that $( $\texttt{One(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}})}$, $\texttt{One(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}})}$ ) \in F$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} is single\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued then \texttt{RespectsOne} returns \texttt{true} if and only if the equation \texttt{One( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} )\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} = One( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} )} holds. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RespectsInverses}}
\logpage{[ 32, 9, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F27AE9C84A4DF90}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RespectsInverses({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{RespectsInverses@\texttt{RespectsInverses}}
\label{RespectsInverses}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping with underlying relation $F \subseteq \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}$, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are the source and the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}, respectively. Then \texttt{RespectsInverses} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are magmas\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}inverses such that, for $s \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}$ and $r \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}$, $(s,r) \in F$ implies $(s^{{-1}},r^{{-1}}) \in F$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} is single\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued then \texttt{RespectsInverses} returns \texttt{true} if and only if the equation \texttt{Inverse( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} )\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} = Inverse( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} )} holds for all \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} in $S$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsGroupGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 9, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X819DD174829BF3AE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsGroupGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{IsGroupGeneralMapping@\texttt{IsGroupGeneralMapping}}
\label{IsGroupGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsGroupHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{IsGroupHomomorphism@\texttt{IsGroupHomomorphism}}
\label{IsGroupHomomorphism}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 A \emph{group general mapping} is a mapping which respects multiplication and inverses. If it is total and
single valued it is called a \emph{group homomorphism}. 

 Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Group Homomorphisms} explains group homomorphisms in more detail. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{KernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 9, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81A5A5CF846E5FBF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{KernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{KernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping@\texttt{Kernel}\-\texttt{Of}\-\texttt{Multiplicative}\-\texttt{General}\-\texttt{Mapping}}
\label{KernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping. Then \texttt{KernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping} returns the set of all elements in the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} that have the identity of the range in their set of images. 

 (This is a monoid if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} respects multiplication and one, and if the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} is associative.) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CoKernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 9, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F09B6E28080DCB4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CoKernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{CoKernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping@\texttt{CoKernel}\-\texttt{Of}\-\texttt{Multiplicative}\-\texttt{General}\-\texttt{Mapping}}
\label{CoKernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping. Then \texttt{CoKernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping} returns the set of all elements in the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} that have the identity of the source in their set of preimages. 

 (This is a monoid if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} respects multiplication and one, and if the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} is associative.) }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Mappings that Respect Addition}}\label{Mappings that Respect Addition}
\logpage{[ 32, 10, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8455A5A67C35178B}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RespectsAddition}}
\logpage{[ 32, 10, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A3321E878925C3A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RespectsAddition({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{RespectsAddition@\texttt{RespectsAddition}}
\label{RespectsAddition}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping with underlying relation $F \subseteq S \times R$, where $S$ and $R$ are the source and the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}, respectively. Then \texttt{RespectsAddition} returns \texttt{true} if $S$ and $R$ are additive magmas such that $(s_1,r_1), (s_2,r_2) \in F$ implies $(s_1 + s_2,r_1 + r_2) \in F$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} is single\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued then \texttt{RespectsAddition} returns \texttt{true} if and only if the equation \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s1}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} + \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s2}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} = (\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s1}}+\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s2}})\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}} holds for all \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s2}} in $S$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RespectsAdditiveInverses}}
\logpage{[ 32, 10, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8130D8907B92F746}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RespectsAdditiveInverses({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{RespectsAdditiveInverses@\texttt{RespectsAdditiveInverses}}
\label{RespectsAdditiveInverses}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping with underlying relation $F \subseteq S \times R$, where $S$ and $R$ are the source and the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}, respectively. Then \texttt{RespectsAdditiveInverses} returns \texttt{true} if $S$ and $R$ are
additive\texttt{\symbol{45}}magmas\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}inverses
such that $(s,r) \in F$ implies $(-s,-r) \in F$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} is single\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued then \texttt{RespectsAdditiveInverses} returns \texttt{true} if and only if the equation \texttt{AdditiveInverse( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} )\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} = AdditiveInverse( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} )} holds for all \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} in $S$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RespectsZero}}
\logpage{[ 32, 10, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D342736781EB280}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RespectsZero({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{RespectsZero@\texttt{RespectsZero}}
\label{RespectsZero}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping with underlying relation $F \subseteq \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}$, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are the source and the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}, respectively. Then \texttt{RespectsZero} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are
additive\texttt{\symbol{45}}magmas\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}zero
such that $( $\texttt{Zero(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}})}$, $\texttt{Zero(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}})}$ ) \in F$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} is single\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued then \texttt{RespectsZero} returns \texttt{true} if and only if the equation \texttt{Zero( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} )\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} = Zero( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} )} holds. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 10, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B99EF287A8A0BD9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping@\texttt{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping}}
\label{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAdditiveGroupHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{IsAdditiveGroupHomomorphism@\texttt{IsAdditiveGroupHomomorphism}}
\label{IsAdditiveGroupHomomorphism}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 \texttt{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping} specifies whether a general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} respects addition (see \texttt{RespectsAddition} (\ref{RespectsAddition})) and respects additive inverses (see \texttt{RespectsAdditiveInverses} (\ref{RespectsAdditiveInverses})). 

 \texttt{IsAdditiveGroupHomomorphism} is a synonym for the meet of \texttt{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping} and \texttt{IsMapping} (\ref{IsMapping}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{KernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 10, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EC0E9907D6631D6}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{KernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{KernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping@\texttt{KernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping}}
\label{KernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping. Then \texttt{KernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping} returns the set of all elements in the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} that have the zero of the range in their set of images. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CoKernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 10, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X813C6D7980213F41}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CoKernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{CoKernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping@\texttt{CoKernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping}}
\label{CoKernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping. Then \texttt{CoKernelOfAdditiveGeneralMapping} returns the set of all elements in the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} that have the zero of the source in their set of preimages. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Linear Mappings}}\label{Linear Mappings}
\logpage{[ 32, 11, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7C24431C81532575}{}
{
  Also see Sections{\nobreakspace}\ref{Mappings that Respect Multiplication}, \ref{Mappings that Respect Addition}, and \texttt{KernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping} (\ref{KernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping}), \texttt{CoKernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping} (\ref{CoKernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping}). 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RespectsScalarMultiplication}}
\logpage{[ 32, 11, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87842ED97FA19973}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RespectsScalarMultiplication({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{RespectsScalarMultiplication@\texttt{RespectsScalarMultiplication}}
\label{RespectsScalarMultiplication}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} be a general mapping, with underlying relation $F \subseteq S \times R$, where $S$ and $R$ are the source and the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}, respectively. Then \texttt{RespectsScalarMultiplication} returns \texttt{true} if $S$ and $R$ are left modules with the left acting domain $D$ of $S$ contained in the left acting domain of $R$ and such that $(s,r) \in F$ implies $(c * s,c * r) \in F$ for all $c \in D$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} is single\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued then \texttt{RespectsScalarMultiplication} returns \texttt{true} if and only if the equation \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape c}} * \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} = (\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape c}} * \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}})\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}} holds for all \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape c}} in $D$ and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} in $S$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLeftModuleGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 11, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X780BE6307A3271A9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLeftModuleGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{IsLeftModuleGeneralMapping@\texttt{IsLeftModuleGeneralMapping}}
\label{IsLeftModuleGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLeftModuleHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{IsLeftModuleHomomorphism@\texttt{IsLeftModuleHomomorphism}}
\label{IsLeftModuleHomomorphism}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 \texttt{IsLeftModuleGeneralMapping} specifies whether a general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} satisfies the property \texttt{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping} (\ref{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping}) and respects scalar multiplication (see \texttt{RespectsScalarMultiplication} (\ref{RespectsScalarMultiplication})). 

 \texttt{IsLeftModuleHomomorphism} is a synonym for the meet of \texttt{IsLeftModuleGeneralMapping} and \texttt{IsMapping} (\ref{IsMapping}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLinearMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 11, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F6841107E59107F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLinearMapping({\mdseries\slshape F, mapp})\index{IsLinearMapping@\texttt{IsLinearMapping}}
\label{IsLinearMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 For a field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} and a general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}}, \texttt{IsLinearMapping} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} is an \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}linear mapping, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 A mapping $f$ is a linear mapping (or vector space homomorphism) if the source and range are
vector spaces over the same division ring $D$, and if $f( a + b ) = f(a) + f(b)$ and $f( s * a ) = s * f(a)$ hold for all elements $a$, $b$ in the source of $f$ and $s \in D$. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Ring Homomorphisms}}\label{Ring Homomorphisms}
\logpage{[ 32, 12, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7E88C32A82E942DA}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRingGeneralMapping}}
\logpage{[ 32, 12, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C8DA031799B79D5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRingGeneralMapping({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{IsRingGeneralMapping@\texttt{IsRingGeneralMapping}}
\label{IsRingGeneralMapping}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRingHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape mapp})\index{IsRingHomomorphism@\texttt{IsRingHomomorphism}}
\label{IsRingHomomorphism}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 \texttt{IsRingGeneralMapping} specifies whether a general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mapp}} satisfies the property \texttt{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping} (\ref{IsAdditiveGroupGeneralMapping}) and respects multiplication (see \texttt{RespectsMultiplication} (\ref{RespectsMultiplication})). 

 \texttt{IsRingHomomorphism} is a synonym for the meet of \texttt{IsRingGeneralMapping} and \texttt{IsMapping} (\ref{IsMapping}). }

\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Technical Matters Concerning General Mappings}}\label{Technical Matters Concerning General Mappings}
\logpage{[ 32, 14, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7D6F78587C00CDD0}{}
{
  \texttt{Source} (\ref{Source}) and \texttt{Range} (\ref{Range:of a general mapping}) are basic operations for general mappings. \texttt{UnderlyingRelation} (\ref{UnderlyingRelation}) is secondary, its default method sets up a domain that delegates tasks to the
general mapping. (Note that this allows one to handle also infinite relations
by generic methods if source or range of the general mapping is finite.) 

 The distinction between basic operations and secondary operations for general
mappings may be a little bit complicated. Namely, each general mapping must be
in one of the two categories \texttt{IsNonSPGeneralMapping} (\ref{IsNonSPGeneralMapping}), \texttt{IsSPGeneralMapping} (\ref{IsSPGeneralMapping}). (The category \texttt{IsGeneralMapping} (\ref{IsGeneralMapping}) is defined as the disjoint union of these two.) 

 For general mappings of the first category, \texttt{ImagesElm} (\ref{ImagesElm}) and \texttt{PreImagesElm} (\ref{PreImagesElm}) are basic operations. (Note that in principle it is possible to delegate from \texttt{PreImagesElm} (\ref{PreImagesElm}) to \texttt{ImagesElm} (\ref{ImagesElm}).) Methods for the secondary operations \texttt{ImageElm} (\ref{ImageElm}), \texttt{PreImageElm} (\ref{PreImageElm}), \texttt{ImagesSet} (\ref{ImagesSet}), \texttt{PreImagesSet} (\ref{PreImagesSet}), \texttt{ImagesRepresentative} (\ref{ImagesRepresentative}), and \texttt{PreImagesRepresentative} (\ref{PreImagesRepresentative}) may use \texttt{ImagesElm} (\ref{ImagesElm}) and \texttt{PreImagesElm} (\ref{PreImagesElm}), respectively, and methods for \texttt{ImagesElm} (\ref{ImagesElm}), \texttt{PreImagesElm} (\ref{PreImagesElm}) must \emph{not} call the secondary operations. In particular, there are no generic methods for \texttt{ImagesElm} (\ref{ImagesElm}) and \texttt{PreImagesElm} (\ref{PreImagesElm}). 

 Methods for \texttt{ImagesSet} (\ref{ImagesSet}) and \texttt{PreImagesSet} (\ref{PreImagesSet}) must \emph{not} use \texttt{PreImagesRange} (\ref{PreImagesRange}) and \texttt{ImagesSource} (\ref{ImagesSource}), e.g., compute the intersection of the set in question with the preimage of
the range resp. the image of the source. 

 For general mappings of the second category (which means structure preserving
general mappings), the situation is different. The set of preimages under a
group homomorphism, for example, is either empty or can be described as a
coset of the (multiplicative) kernel. So it is reasonable to have \texttt{ImagesRepresentative} (\ref{ImagesRepresentative}), \texttt{PreImagesRepresentative} (\ref{PreImagesRepresentative}), \texttt{KernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping} (\ref{KernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping}), and \texttt{CoKernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping} (\ref{CoKernelOfMultiplicativeGeneralMapping}) as basic operations here, and to make \texttt{ImagesElm} (\ref{ImagesElm}) and \texttt{PreImagesElm} (\ref{PreImagesElm}) secondary operations that may delegate to these. 

 In order to avoid infinite recursions, we must distinguish between the two
different types of mappings. 

 (Note that the basic domain operations such as \texttt{AsList} (\ref{AsList}) for the underlying relation of a general mapping may use either \texttt{ImagesElm} (\ref{ImagesElm}) or \texttt{ImagesRepresentative} (\ref{ImagesRepresentative}) and the appropriate cokernel. Conversely, if \texttt{AsList} (\ref{AsList}) for the underlying relation is known then \texttt{ImagesElm} (\ref{ImagesElm}) resp. \texttt{ImagesRepresentative} (\ref{ImagesRepresentative}) may delegate to it, the general mapping gets the property \texttt{IsConstantTimeAccessGeneralMapping} (\ref{IsConstantTimeAccessGeneralMapping}) for this; note that this is not allowed if only an enumerator of the
underlying relation is known.) 

 Secondary operations are \texttt{IsInjective} (\ref{IsInjective}), \texttt{IsSingleValued} (\ref{IsSingleValued}), \texttt{IsSurjective} (\ref{IsSurjective}), \texttt{IsTotal} (\ref{IsTotal}); they may use the basic operations, and must not be used by them. 

 Methods for the operations \texttt{ImagesElm} (\ref{ImagesElm}), \texttt{ImagesRepresentative} (\ref{ImagesRepresentative}), \texttt{ImagesSet} (\ref{ImagesSet}), \texttt{ImageElm} (\ref{ImageElm}), \texttt{PreImagesElm} (\ref{PreImagesElm}), \texttt{PreImagesRepresentative} (\ref{PreImagesRepresentative}), \texttt{PreImagesSet} (\ref{PreImagesSet}), and \texttt{PreImageElm} (\ref{PreImageElm}) take two arguments, a general mapping \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} and an element or collection of elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}}. These methods must \emph{not} check whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} lies in the source or the range of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}}. In the case that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} does not, \texttt{fail} may be returned as well as any other \textsf{GAP} object, and even an error message is allowed. Checks of the arguments are done
only by the functions \texttt{Image} (\ref{Image:set of images of the source of a general mapping}), \texttt{Images} (\ref{Images:set of images of the source of a general mapping}), \texttt{PreImage} (\ref{PreImage:set of preimages of the range of a general mapping}), and \texttt{PreImages} (\ref{PreImages:set of preimages of the range of a general mapping}), which then delegate to the operations listed above.

\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Relations}}\label{Relations}
\logpage{[ 33, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X838651287FCCEFD8}{}
{
  \index{binary relation} \index{IsBinaryRelation@\texttt{IsBinaryRelation}!same as IsEndoGeneralMapping} \index{IsEndoGeneralMapping@\texttt{IsEndoGeneralMapping}!same as IsBinaryRelation} A \emph{binary relation} $R$ on a set $X$ is a subset of $X \times X$. A binary relation can also be thought of as a (general) mapping from $X$ to itself or as a directed graph where each edge represents an element of $R$. 

 In \textsf{GAP}, a relation is conceptually represented as a general mapping from $X$ to itself. The category \texttt{IsBinaryRelation} (\ref{IsBinaryRelation}) is a synonym for \texttt{IsEndoGeneralMapping} (\ref{IsEndoGeneralMapping}). Attributes and properties of relations in \textsf{GAP} are supported for relations, via considering relations as a subset of $X \times X$, or as a directed graph; examples include finding the strongly connected
components of a relation, via \texttt{StronglyConnectedComponents} (\ref{StronglyConnectedComponents}), or enumerating the tuples of the relation.  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{General Binary Relations}}\label{General Binary Relations}
\logpage{[ 33, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7DED7F1F78D31785}{}
{
  This section lists general constructors of relations. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsBinaryRelation}}

\hyperdef{L}{X788D722F82165551}{}

\label{IsBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is exactly the same category as (i.e. a synonym for) \texttt{IsEndoGeneralMapping} (\ref{IsEndoGeneralMapping}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{BinaryRelationByElements}}
\logpage{[ 33, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A1D8EEF8034B0B5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{BinaryRelationByElements({\mdseries\slshape domain, elms})\index{BinaryRelationByElements@\texttt{BinaryRelationByElements}}
\label{BinaryRelationByElements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 is the binary relation on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape domain}} and with underlying relation consisting of the tuples collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elms}}. This construction is similar to \texttt{GeneralMappingByElements} (\ref{GeneralMappingByElements}) where the source and range are the same set. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@r:=BinaryRelationByElements(Domain([1..3]),[DirectProductElement([1,2]),DirectProductElement([1,3])]);|
  <general mapping: Domain([ 1 .. 3 ]) -> Domain([ 1 .. 3 ]) >
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IdentityBinaryRelation}}\logpage{[ 33, 1, 3 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X81878EEF873B34D5}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IdentityBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape degree})\index{IdentityBinaryRelation@\texttt{IdentityBinaryRelation}!for a degree}
\label{IdentityBinaryRelation:for a degree}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IdentityBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape domain})\index{IdentityBinaryRelation@\texttt{IdentityBinaryRelation}!for a domain}
\label{IdentityBinaryRelation:for a domain}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 is the binary relation which consists of diagonal pairs, i.e., pairs of the
form $(x,x)$. In the first form if a positive integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape degree}} is given then the domain is the set of the integers $\{ 1, \ldots, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape degree}} \}$. In the second form, the objects $x$ are from the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape domain}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IdentityBinaryRelation(5);|
  <equivalence relation on Domain([ 1 .. 5 ]) >
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@s4:=SymmetricGroup(4);|
  Sym( [ 1 .. 4 ] )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IdentityBinaryRelation(s4);|
  IdentityMapping( Sym( [ 1 .. 4 ] ) )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EmptyBinaryRelation (for a degree)}}
\logpage{[ 33, 1, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80DDCDD387BA23F2}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EmptyBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape degree})\index{EmptyBinaryRelation@\texttt{EmptyBinaryRelation}!for a degree}
\label{EmptyBinaryRelation:for a degree}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\

\label{EmptyBinaryRelation:for a domain}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 is the relation with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} empty. In the first form of the command with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape degree}} an integer, the domain is the set of points $\{ 1, \ldots, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape degree}} \}$. In the second form, the domain is that given by the argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape domain}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@EmptyBinaryRelation(3) = BinaryRelationOnPoints([ [], [], [] ]);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Properties and Attributes of Binary Relations}}\label{Properties and Attributes of Binary Relations}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7899E59181C46EBB}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsReflexiveBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79D69B667F5FE8FE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsReflexiveBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsReflexiveBinaryRelation@\texttt{IsReflexiveBinaryRelation}}
\label{IsReflexiveBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is reflexive, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \index{reflexive relation} A binary relation $R$ (as a set of pairs) on a set $X$ is \emph{reflexive} if for all $x \in X$, $(x,x) \in R$. Alternatively, $R$ as a mapping is reflexive if for all $x \in X$, $x$ is an element of the image set $R(x)$. 

 A reflexive binary relation is necessarily a total endomorphic mapping (tested
via \texttt{IsTotal} (\ref{IsTotal})). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReflexiveBinaryRelation(BinaryRelationOnPoints([[1,3],[2],[3]]));|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReflexiveBinaryRelation(BinaryRelationOnPoints([[2],[2]]));|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSymmetricBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X785916A181555368}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSymmetricBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsSymmetricBinaryRelation@\texttt{IsSymmetricBinaryRelation}}
\label{IsSymmetricBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is symmetric, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \index{symmetric relation} A binary relation $R$ (as a set of pairs) on a set $X$ is \emph{symmetric} if $(x,y) \in R$ then $(y,x) \in R$. Alternatively, $R$ as a mapping is symmetric if for all $x \in X$, the preimage set of $x$ under $R$ equals the image set $R(x)$. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsSymmetricBinaryRelation(BinaryRelationOnPoints([[2],[1]]));|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsSymmetricBinaryRelation(BinaryRelationOnPoints([[2],[2]]));|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsTransitiveBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7823942478124563}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsTransitiveBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsTransitiveBinaryRelation@\texttt{IsTransitiveBinaryRelation}}
\label{IsTransitiveBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is transitive, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \index{transitive relation} A binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} (as a set of pairs) on a set $X$ is \emph{transitive} if $(x,y), (y,z) \in R$ implies $(x,z) \in R$. Alternatively, $R$ as a mapping is transitive if for all $x \in X$, the image set $R(R(x))$ of the image set $R(x)$ of $x$ is a subset of $R(x)$. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsTransitiveBinaryRelation(BinaryRelationOnPoints([[1,2,3],[2,3],[]]));|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsTransitiveBinaryRelation(BinaryRelationOnPoints([[1,2],[2,3],[]]));|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsAntisymmetricBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X870F72C38550A0A4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAntisymmetricBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape rel})\index{IsAntisymmetricBinaryRelation@\texttt{IsAntisymmetricBinaryRelation}}
\label{IsAntisymmetricBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}} is antisymmetric, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \index{antisymmetric relation} A binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} (as a set of pairs) on a set $X$ is \emph{antisymmetric} if $(x,y), (y,x) \in R$ implies $x = y$. Alternatively, $R$ as a mapping is antisymmetric if for all $x \in X$, the intersection of the preimage set of $x$ under $R$ and the image set $R(x)$ is $\{ x \}$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPreOrderBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X782B7C8A8136532F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPreOrderBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape rel})\index{IsPreOrderBinaryRelation@\texttt{IsPreOrderBinaryRelation}}
\label{IsPreOrderBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}} is a preorder, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \index{preorder} A \emph{preorder} is a binary relation that is both reflexive and transitive. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPartialOrderBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A1228207AB4FBA3}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPartialOrderBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape rel})\index{IsPartialOrderBinaryRelation@\texttt{IsPartialOrderBinaryRelation}}
\label{IsPartialOrderBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}} is a partial order, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \index{partial order} A \emph{partial order} is a preorder which is also antisymmetric. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsHasseDiagram}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80D3735C84D1CDC2}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsHasseDiagram({\mdseries\slshape rel})\index{IsHasseDiagram@\texttt{IsHasseDiagram}}
\label{IsHasseDiagram}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}} is a Hasse Diagram of a partial order, i.e., was computed via \texttt{HasseDiagramBinaryRelation} (\ref{HasseDiagramBinaryRelation}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsEquivalenceRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82D6CB4B7CCE9E25}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsEquivalenceRelation({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsEquivalenceRelation@\texttt{IsEquivalenceRelation}}
\label{IsEquivalenceRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is an equivalence relation, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \index{equivalence relation} Recall, that a relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is an \emph{equivalence relation} if it is symmetric, transitive, and reflexive. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Successors}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85E2FD8B82652876}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Successors({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{Successors@\texttt{Successors}}
\label{Successors}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns the list of images of a binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. If the underlying domain of the relation is not $\{ 1, \ldots, n \}$, for some positive integer $n$, then an error is signalled. 

 The returned value of \texttt{Successors} is a list of lists where the lists are ordered as the elements according to
the sorted order of the underlying set of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. Each list consists of the images of the element whose index is the same as
the list with the underlying set in sorted order. 

 The \texttt{Successors} of a relation is the adjacency list representation of the relation. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@r1:=BinaryRelationOnPoints([[2],[3],[1]]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Successors(r1);|
  [ [ 2 ], [ 3 ], [ 1 ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DegreeOfBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B4D22A17E752A91}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DegreeOfBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{DegreeOfBinaryRelation@\texttt{DegreeOfBinaryRelation}}
\label{DegreeOfBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns the size of the underlying domain of the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. This is most natural when working with a binary relation on points. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DegreeOfBinaryRelation(r1);|
  3
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PartialOrderOfHasseDiagram}}
\logpage{[ 33, 2, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8278E4457C3C3A0D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PartialOrderOfHasseDiagram({\mdseries\slshape HD})\index{PartialOrderOfHasseDiagram@\texttt{PartialOrderOfHasseDiagram}}
\label{PartialOrderOfHasseDiagram}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the partial order associated with the Hasse Diagram \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape HD}} i.e. the partial order generated by the reflexive and transitive closure of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape HD}}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Binary Relations on Points}}\label{Binary Relations on Points}
\logpage{[ 33, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X78032F927F078E19}{}
{
  We have special construction methods when the underlying \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape X}} of our relation is the set of integers $\{ 1, \ldots, n \}$. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{BinaryRelationOnPoints}}
\logpage{[ 33, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79E40E9385274F89}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{BinaryRelationOnPoints({\mdseries\slshape list})\index{BinaryRelationOnPoints@\texttt{BinaryRelationOnPoints}}
\label{BinaryRelationOnPoints}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{BinaryRelationOnPointsNC({\mdseries\slshape list})\index{BinaryRelationOnPointsNC@\texttt{BinaryRelationOnPointsNC}}
\label{BinaryRelationOnPointsNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Given a list of $n$ lists, each containing elements from the set $\{ 1, \ldots, n \}$, this function constructs a binary relation such that $1$ is related to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}}\texttt{[1]}, $2$ to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}}\texttt{[2]} and so on. The first version checks whether the list supplied is valid. The \texttt{NC} version skips this check. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=BinaryRelationOnPoints([[1,2],[2],[3]]);|
  Binary Relation on 3 points
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RandomBinaryRelationOnPoints}}
\logpage{[ 33, 3, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D9323C283867515}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RandomBinaryRelationOnPoints({\mdseries\slshape degree})\index{RandomBinaryRelationOnPoints@\texttt{RandomBinaryRelationOnPoints}}
\label{RandomBinaryRelationOnPoints}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 creates a relation on points with degree \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape degree}}. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints}}\logpage{[ 33, 3, 3 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8315C7A47CEB6BB3}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints({\mdseries\slshape trans})\index{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints@\texttt{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints}!for a transformation}
\label{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints:for a transformation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints({\mdseries\slshape perm})\index{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints@\texttt{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints}!for a permutation}
\label{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints:for a permutation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints({\mdseries\slshape rel})\index{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints@\texttt{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints}!for a binary relation}
\label{AsBinaryRelationOnPoints:for a binary relation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 return the relation on points represented by general relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}}, transformation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape trans}} or permutation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape perm}}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}} is already a binary relation on points then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}} is returned. 

 Transformations and permutations are special general endomorphic mappings and
have a natural representation as a binary relation on points. 

 In the last form, an isomorphic relation on points is constructed where the
points are indices of the elements of the underlying domain in sorted order. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@t:=Transformation([2,3,1]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@r1:=AsBinaryRelationOnPoints(t);|
  Binary Relation on 3 points
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@r2:=AsBinaryRelationOnPoints((1,2,3));|
  Binary Relation on 3 points
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@r1=r2;|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Closure Operations and Other Constructors}}\label{Closure Operations and Other Constructors}
\logpage{[ 33, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7D9A14AE799142EF}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ReflexiveClosureBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 4, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8252B17C864A4904}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ReflexiveClosureBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{ReflexiveClosureBinaryRelation@\texttt{ReflexiveClosureBinaryRelation}}
\label{ReflexiveClosureBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 is the smallest binary relation containing the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} which is reflexive. This closure inherits the properties symmetric and
transitive from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. E.g., if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is symmetric then its reflexive closure is also. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SymmetricClosureBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 4, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X820811E9785A7274}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SymmetricClosureBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{SymmetricClosureBinaryRelation@\texttt{SymmetricClosureBinaryRelation}}
\label{SymmetricClosureBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 is the smallest binary relation containing the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} which is symmetric. This closure inherits the properties reflexive and
transitive from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. E.g., if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is reflexive then its symmetric closure is also. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TransitiveClosureBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 4, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X853BFAD9858DCDF7}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TransitiveClosureBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape rel})\index{TransitiveClosureBinaryRelation@\texttt{TransitiveClosureBinaryRelation}}
\label{TransitiveClosureBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 is the smallest binary relation containing the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} which is transitive. This closure inherits the properties reflexive and
symmetric from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. E.g., if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is symmetric then its transitive closure is also. 

 \texttt{TransitiveClosureBinaryRelation} is a modified version of the Floyd\texttt{\symbol{45}}Warshall method of
solving the all\texttt{\symbol{45}}pairs shortest\texttt{\symbol{45}}paths
problem on a directed graph. Its asymptotic runtime is $O(n^3)$ where $n$ is the size of the vertex set. It only assumes there is an arbitrary (but
fixed) ordering of the vertex set. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{HasseDiagramBinaryRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 4, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79672B3A7BCB6991}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{HasseDiagramBinaryRelation({\mdseries\slshape partial\texttt{\symbol{45}}order})\index{HasseDiagramBinaryRelation@\texttt{HasseDiagramBinaryRelation}}
\label{HasseDiagramBinaryRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 is the smallest relation contained in the partial order \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape partial\texttt{\symbol{45}}order}} whose reflexive and transitive closure is equal to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape partial\texttt{\symbol{45}}order}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{StronglyConnectedComponents}}
\logpage{[ 33, 4, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85C22B3D812957C0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StronglyConnectedComponents({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{StronglyConnectedComponents@\texttt{StronglyConnectedComponents}}
\label{StronglyConnectedComponents}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns an equivalence relation on the vertices of the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PartialOrderByOrderingFunction}}
\logpage{[ 33, 4, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86AAE6027A3AEF72}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PartialOrderByOrderingFunction({\mdseries\slshape dom, orderfunc})\index{PartialOrderByOrderingFunction@\texttt{PartialOrderByOrderingFunction}}
\label{PartialOrderByOrderingFunction}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 constructs a partial order whose elements are from the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape dom}} and are ordered using the ordering function \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape orderfunc}}. The ordering function must be a binary function returning a boolean value.
If the ordering function does not describe a partial order then \texttt{fail} is returned. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Equivalence Relations}}\label{Equivalence Relations}
\logpage{[ 33, 5, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7DAA67338458BB64}{}
{
  \index{equivalence relation} An \emph{equivalence relation} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape E}} over the set \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape X}} is a relation on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape X}} which is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. A \emph{partition} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape P}} is a set of subsets of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape X}} such that for all $R, S \in P$, $R \cap S$ is the empty set and $\cup P = X$. An equivalence relation induces a partition such that if $(x,y) \in E$ then $x, y$ are in the same element of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape P}}. 

 Like all binary relations in \textsf{GAP} equivalence relations are regarded as general endomorphic mappings (and the
operations, properties and attributes of general mappings are available).
However, partitions provide an efficient way of representing equivalence
relations. Moreover, only the non\texttt{\symbol{45}}singleton classes or
blocks are listed allowing for small equivalence relations to be represented
on infinite sets. Hence the main attribute of equivalence relations is \texttt{EquivalenceRelationPartition} (\ref{EquivalenceRelationPartition}) which provides the partition induced by the given equivalence. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EquivalenceRelationByPartition}}
\logpage{[ 33, 5, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A44D73D8150266A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByPartition({\mdseries\slshape domain, list})\index{EquivalenceRelationByPartition@\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByPartition}}
\label{EquivalenceRelationByPartition}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByPartitionNC({\mdseries\slshape domain, list})\index{EquivalenceRelationByPartitionNC@\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByPartitionNC}}
\label{EquivalenceRelationByPartitionNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 constructs the equivalence relation over the set \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape domain}} which induces the partition represented by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}}. This representation includes only the non\texttt{\symbol{45}}trivial blocks
(or equivalent classes). \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} is a list of lists, each of these lists contain elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape domain}} and are pairwise mutually exclusive. 

 The list of lists do not need to be in any order nor do the elements in the
blocks (see \texttt{EquivalenceRelationPartition} (\ref{EquivalenceRelationPartition})). a list of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape domain}} The partition \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} is a list of lists, each of these is a list of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape domain}} that makes up a block (or equivalent class). The \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape domain}} is the domain over which the relation is defined, and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} is a list of lists, each of these is a list of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape domain}} which are related to each other. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} need only contain the nontrivial blocks and singletons will be ignored. The \texttt{NC} version will not check to see if the lists are pairwise mutually exclusive or
that they contain only elements of the domain. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@er:=EquivalenceRelationByPartition(Domain([1..10]),[[1,3,5,7,9],[2,4,6,8,10]]);|
  <equivalence relation on Domain([ 1 .. 10 ]) >
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsEquivalenceRelation(er);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EquivalenceRelationByRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 5, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82CD1C00810F6042}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByRelation({\mdseries\slshape rel})\index{EquivalenceRelationByRelation@\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByRelation}}
\label{EquivalenceRelationByRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the smallest equivalence relation containing the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EquivalenceRelationByPairs}}
\logpage{[ 33, 5, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B70215E7E3F9CA4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByPairs({\mdseries\slshape D, elms})\index{EquivalenceRelationByPairs@\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByPairs}}
\label{EquivalenceRelationByPairs}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByPairsNC({\mdseries\slshape D, elms})\index{EquivalenceRelationByPairsNC@\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByPairsNC}}
\label{EquivalenceRelationByPairsNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 return the smallest equivalence relation on the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} such that every pair in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elms}} is in the relation. 

 In the \texttt{NC} form, it is not checked that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elms}} are in the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EquivalenceRelationByProperty}}
\logpage{[ 33, 5, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C5AA9B97EE42DA5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByProperty({\mdseries\slshape domain, property})\index{EquivalenceRelationByProperty@\texttt{EquivalenceRelationByProperty}}
\label{EquivalenceRelationByProperty}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 creates an equivalence relation on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape domain}} whose only defining datum is that of having the property \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape property}}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Attributes of and Operations on Equivalence Relations}}\label{Attributes of and Operations on Equivalence Relations}
\logpage{[ 33, 6, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X85A2A8E27AF52769}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EquivalenceRelationPartition}}
\logpage{[ 33, 6, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X877389B683DD8F1A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceRelationPartition({\mdseries\slshape equiv})\index{EquivalenceRelationPartition@\texttt{EquivalenceRelationPartition}}
\label{EquivalenceRelationPartition}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a list of lists of elements of the underlying set of the equivalence
relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape equiv}}. The lists are precisely the nonsingleton equivalence classes of the
equivalence. This allows us to describe ``small'' equivalences on infinite sets. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfEquivalenceRelationPartition}}
\logpage{[ 33, 6, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79DC914C82D7903B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfEquivalenceRelationPartition({\mdseries\slshape equiv})\index{GeneratorsOfEquivalenceRelationPartition@\texttt{Generators}\-\texttt{Of}\-\texttt{Equivalence}\-\texttt{Relation}\-\texttt{Partition}}
\label{GeneratorsOfEquivalenceRelationPartition}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is a set of generating pairs for the equivalence relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape equiv}}. This set is not unique. The equivalence \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape equiv}} is the smallest equivalence relation over the underlying set which contains
the generating pairs. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{JoinEquivalenceRelations}}
\logpage{[ 33, 6, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82BE360381476D92}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{JoinEquivalenceRelations({\mdseries\slshape equiv1, equiv2})\index{JoinEquivalenceRelations@\texttt{JoinEquivalenceRelations}}
\label{JoinEquivalenceRelations}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MeetEquivalenceRelations({\mdseries\slshape equiv1, equiv2})\index{MeetEquivalenceRelations@\texttt{MeetEquivalenceRelations}}
\label{MeetEquivalenceRelations}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{JoinEquivalenceRelations} returns the smallest equivalence relation containing both the equivalence
relations \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape equiv1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape equiv2}}. 

 \texttt{MeetEquivalenceRelations} returns the intersection of the two equivalence relations \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape equiv1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape equiv2}}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Equivalence Classes}}\label{Equivalence Classes}
\logpage{[ 33, 7, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X79EE13287DEB11B1}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsEquivalenceClass}}
\logpage{[ 33, 7, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8424996186DB14EA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsEquivalenceClass({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsEquivalenceClass@\texttt{IsEquivalenceClass}}
\label{IsEquivalenceClass}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if the object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} is an equivalence class, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \index{equivalence class} An \emph{equivalence class} is a collection of elements which are mutually related to each other in the
associated equivalence relation. Note, this is a special category of objects
and not just a list of elements. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EquivalenceClassRelation}}
\logpage{[ 33, 7, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78F967E77EB16386}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceClassRelation({\mdseries\slshape C})\index{EquivalenceClassRelation@\texttt{EquivalenceClassRelation}}
\label{EquivalenceClassRelation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns the equivalence relation of which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}} is a class. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EquivalenceClasses (attribute)}}
\logpage{[ 33, 7, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X879439897EF4D728}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceClasses({\mdseries\slshape rel})\index{EquivalenceClasses@\texttt{EquivalenceClasses}!attribute}
\label{EquivalenceClasses:attribute}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a list of all equivalence classes of the equivalence relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}}. Note that it is possible for different methods to yield the list in
different orders, so that for two equivalence relations $c1$ and $c2$ we may have $c1 = c2$ without having \texttt{EquivalenceClasses}$( c1 ) = $\texttt{EquivalenceClasses}$( c2 )$. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@er:=EquivalenceRelationByPartition(Domain([1..10]),[[1,3,5,7,9],[2,4,6,8,10]]);|
  <equivalence relation on Domain([ 1 .. 10 ]) >
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@classes := EquivalenceClasses(er);|
  [ {1}, {2} ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EquivalenceClassOfElement}}
\logpage{[ 33, 7, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BB985BA7FD7A82E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceClassOfElement({\mdseries\slshape rel, elt})\index{EquivalenceClassOfElement@\texttt{EquivalenceClassOfElement}}
\label{EquivalenceClassOfElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EquivalenceClassOfElementNC({\mdseries\slshape rel, elt})\index{EquivalenceClassOfElementNC@\texttt{EquivalenceClassOfElementNC}}
\label{EquivalenceClassOfElementNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 return the equivalence class of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elt}} in the binary relation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}}, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elt}} is an element (i.e. a pair) of the domain of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}}. In the \texttt{NC} form, it is not checked that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elt}} is in the domain over which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rel}} is defined. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@EquivalenceClassOfElement(er,3);|
  {3}
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

 }

            
\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Orderings}}\label{Orderings}
\logpage{[ 34, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7E4AAA7382D42361}{}
{
  In \textsf{GAP} an ordering is a relation defined on a family, which is reflexive,
anti\texttt{\symbol{45}}symmetric and transitive.  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsOrdering (Filter)}}\label{sect:IsOrdering}
\logpage{[ 34, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X79B1262585CE5427}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsOrdering}}
\logpage{[ 34, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EFDF115780934AF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsOrdering({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsOrdering@\texttt{IsOrdering}}
\label{IsOrdering}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if and only if the object \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} is an ordering. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OrderingsFamily}}
\logpage{[ 34, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85E6445C87283BEC}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrderingsFamily({\mdseries\slshape fam})\index{OrderingsFamily@\texttt{OrderingsFamily}}
\label{OrderingsFamily}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 for a family \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}}, returns the family of all orderings on elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Building new orderings}}\label{Building new orderings}
\logpage{[ 34, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X85C4CAA784BD7F01}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OrderingByLessThanFunctionNC}}
\logpage{[ 34, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78B5D91278EFAFC9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrderingByLessThanFunctionNC({\mdseries\slshape fam, lt[, l]})\index{OrderingByLessThanFunctionNC@\texttt{OrderingByLessThanFunctionNC}}
\label{OrderingByLessThanFunctionNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Called with two arguments, \texttt{OrderingByLessThanFunctionNC} returns the ordering on the elements of the elements of the family \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}}, according to the \texttt{LessThanFunction} (\ref{LessThanFunction}) value given by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lt}}, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lt}} is a function that takes two arguments in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} and returns \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}. 

 Called with three arguments, for a family \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}}, a function \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lt}} that takes two arguments in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} and returns \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}, and a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape l}} of properties of orderings, \texttt{OrderingByLessThanFunctionNC} returns the ordering on the elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} with \texttt{LessThanFunction} (\ref{LessThanFunction}) value given by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lt}} and with the properties from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape l}} set to \texttt{true}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OrderingByLessThanOrEqualFunctionNC}}
\logpage{[ 34, 2, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X813D5BEB80506CE4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrderingByLessThanOrEqualFunctionNC({\mdseries\slshape fam, lteq[, l]})\index{OrderingByLessThanOrEqualFunctionNC@\texttt{OrderingByLessThanOrEqualFunctionNC}}
\label{OrderingByLessThanOrEqualFunctionNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Called with two arguments, \texttt{OrderingByLessThanOrEqualFunctionNC} returns the ordering on the elements of the elements of the family \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} according to the \texttt{LessThanOrEqualFunction} (\ref{LessThanOrEqualFunction}) value given by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lteq}}, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lteq}} is a function that takes two arguments in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} and returns \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}. 

 Called with three arguments, for a family \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}}, a function \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lteq}} that takes two arguments in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} and returns \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}, and a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape l}} of properties of orderings, \texttt{OrderingByLessThanOrEqualFunctionNC} returns the ordering on the elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} with \texttt{LessThanOrEqualFunction} (\ref{LessThanOrEqualFunction}) value given by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lteq}} and with the properties from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape l}} set to \texttt{true}. 

 Notice that these functions do not check whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lt}} or \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lteq}} are compatible, and whether the properties listed in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape l}} are indeed satisfied. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := FreeSemigroup("a","b");;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a := GeneratorsOfSemigroup(f)[1];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@b := GeneratorsOfSemigroup(f)[2];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@lt := function(x,y) return Length(x)<Length(y); end;|
  function( x, y ) ... end
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@fam := FamilyObj(a);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ord := OrderingByLessThanFunctionNC(fam,lt);|
  Ordering
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Properties and basic functionality}}\label{Properties and basic functionality}
\logpage{[ 34, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7F62235B87C20A54}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsWellFoundedOrdering}}
\logpage{[ 34, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X84FA448B7B4DDFDC}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsWellFoundedOrdering({\mdseries\slshape ord})\index{IsWellFoundedOrdering@\texttt{IsWellFoundedOrdering}}
\label{IsWellFoundedOrdering}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, returns \texttt{true} if and only if the ordering is well founded. An ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} is well founded if it admits no infinite descending chains. Normally this
property is set at the time of creation of the ordering and there is no
general method to check whether a certain ordering is well founded. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsTotalOrdering}}
\logpage{[ 34, 3, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X867AC932843AD921}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsTotalOrdering({\mdseries\slshape ord})\index{IsTotalOrdering@\texttt{IsTotalOrdering}}
\label{IsTotalOrdering}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, returns true if and only if the ordering is total. An ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} is total if any two elements of the family are comparable under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}. Normally this property is set at the time of creation of the ordering and
there is no general method to check whether a certain ordering is total. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsIncomparableUnder}}
\logpage{[ 34, 3, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X814E5E7D85EDCAC7}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsIncomparableUnder({\mdseries\slshape ord, el1, el2})\index{IsIncomparableUnder@\texttt{IsIncomparableUnder}}
\label{IsIncomparableUnder}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} on the elements of the family of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el2}}, returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el1}} $\neq$ \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el2}} and \texttt{IsLessThanUnder}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}},\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el1}},\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el2}}), \texttt{IsLessThanUnder}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}},\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el2}},\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el1}}) are both \texttt{false}; and returns \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FamilyForOrdering}}
\logpage{[ 34, 3, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X872497B9782B97B4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FamilyForOrdering({\mdseries\slshape ord})\index{FamilyForOrdering@\texttt{FamilyForOrdering}}
\label{FamilyForOrdering}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, returns the family of elements that the ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} compares. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LessThanFunction}}
\logpage{[ 34, 3, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D08ED6882015BFB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LessThanFunction({\mdseries\slshape ord})\index{LessThanFunction@\texttt{LessThanFunction}}
\label{LessThanFunction}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, returns a function $f$ which takes two elements $el1$, $el2$ in \texttt{FamilyForOrdering}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}) and returns \texttt{true} if $el1$ is strictly less than $el2$ (with respect to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}), and returns \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LessThanOrEqualFunction}}
\logpage{[ 34, 3, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X857E800583E9026D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LessThanOrEqualFunction({\mdseries\slshape ord})\index{LessThanOrEqualFunction@\texttt{LessThanOrEqualFunction}}
\label{LessThanOrEqualFunction}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, returns a function that takes two elements $el1$, $el2$ in \texttt{FamilyForOrdering}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}) and returns \texttt{true} if $el1$ is less than \emph{or equal to} $el2$ (with respect to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}), and returns \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLessThanUnder}}
\logpage{[ 34, 3, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87F51D737C695D41}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLessThanUnder({\mdseries\slshape ord, el1, el2})\index{IsLessThanUnder@\texttt{IsLessThanUnder}}
\label{IsLessThanUnder}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} on the elements of the family of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el2}}, returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el1}} is (strictly) less than \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el2}} with respect to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, and \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLessThanOrEqualUnder}}
\logpage{[ 34, 3, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8308B7DF7AAF6D9C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLessThanOrEqualUnder({\mdseries\slshape ord, el1, el2})\index{IsLessThanOrEqualUnder@\texttt{IsLessThanOrEqualUnder}}
\label{IsLessThanOrEqualUnder}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} on the elements of the family of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el2}}, returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el1}} is less than or equal to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape el2}} with respect to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsLessThanUnder(ord,a,a*b);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsLessThanOrEqualUnder(ord,a*b,a*b);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsIncomparableUnder(ord,a,b);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FamilyForOrdering(ord) = FamilyObj(a);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Orderings on families of associative words}}\label{Orderings on families of associative words}
\logpage{[ 34, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X834CD021878745BC}{}
{
  We now consider orderings on families of associative words. 

 Examples of families of associative words are the families of elements of a
free semigroup or a free monoid; these are the two cases that we consider
mostly. Associated with those families is an alphabet, which is the semigroup
(resp. monoid) generating set of the correspondent free semigroup (resp. free
monoid). For definitions of the orderings considered, see Sims \cite{Sims94}. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsOrderingOnFamilyOfAssocWords}}
\logpage{[ 34, 4, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C1808AE84B989AE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsOrderingOnFamilyOfAssocWords({\mdseries\slshape ord})\index{IsOrderingOnFamilyOfAssocWords@\texttt{IsOrderingOnFamilyOfAssocWords}}
\label{IsOrderingOnFamilyOfAssocWords}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, returns true if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} is an ordering over a family of associative words. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsTranslationInvariantOrdering}}
\logpage{[ 34, 4, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8175B8887868F29A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsTranslationInvariantOrdering({\mdseries\slshape ord})\index{IsTranslationInvariantOrdering@\texttt{IsTranslationInvariantOrdering}}
\label{IsTranslationInvariantOrdering}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} on a family of associative words, returns \texttt{true} if and only if the ordering is translation invariant. 

 This is a property of orderings on families of associative words. An ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} over a family $F$, with alphabet $X$ is translation invariant if \texttt{IsLessThanUnder(} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, $u$, $v$ \texttt{)} implies that for any $a, b \in X^*$, \texttt{IsLessThanUnder(} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, $a*u*b$, $a*v*b$ \texttt{)}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsReductionOrdering}}
\logpage{[ 34, 4, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X816CD4BD82D41ED0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsReductionOrdering({\mdseries\slshape ord})\index{IsReductionOrdering@\texttt{IsReductionOrdering}}
\label{IsReductionOrdering}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} on a family of associative words, returns \texttt{true} if and only if the ordering is a reduction ordering. An ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} is a reduction ordering if it is well founded and translation invariant. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OrderingOnGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 34, 4, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B6051C282EA88D5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrderingOnGenerators({\mdseries\slshape ord})\index{OrderingOnGenerators@\texttt{OrderingOnGenerators}}
\label{OrderingOnGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} on a family of associative words, returns a list in which the generators are
considered. This could be indeed the ordering of the generators in the
ordering, but, for example, if a weight is associated to each generator then
this is not true anymore. See the example for \texttt{WeightLexOrdering} (\ref{WeightLexOrdering}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LexicographicOrdering}}
\logpage{[ 34, 4, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79B2DEB786680F51}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LexicographicOrdering({\mdseries\slshape D[, gens]})\index{LexicographicOrdering@\texttt{LexicographicOrdering}}
\label{LexicographicOrdering}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} be a free semigroup, a free monoid, or the elements family of such a domain.
Called with only argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}, \texttt{LexicographicOrdering} returns the lexicographic ordering on the elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}. 

 The optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} can be either the list of free generators of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}, in the desired order, or a list of the positions of these generators, in the
desired order, and \texttt{LexicographicOrdering} returns the lexicographic ordering on the elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} with the ordering on the generators as given. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := FreeSemigroup(3);|
  <free semigroup on the generators [ s1, s2, s3 ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@lex := LexicographicOrdering(f,[2,3,1]);|
  Ordering
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsLessThanUnder(lex,f.2*f.3,f.3);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsLessThanUnder(lex,f.3,f.2);|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ShortLexOrdering}}
\logpage{[ 34, 4, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X802EB44B7E7B1F57}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ShortLexOrdering({\mdseries\slshape D[, gens]})\index{ShortLexOrdering@\texttt{ShortLexOrdering}}
\label{ShortLexOrdering}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} be a free semigroup, a free monoid, or the elements family of such a domain.
Called with only argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}, \texttt{ShortLexOrdering} returns the shortlex ordering on the elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}. 

 The optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} can be either the list of free generators of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}, in the desired order, or a list of the positions of these generators, in the
desired order, and \texttt{ShortLexOrdering} returns the shortlex ordering on the elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} with the ordering on the generators as given. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsShortLexOrdering}}
\logpage{[ 34, 4, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B6ED9327E0A2099}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsShortLexOrdering({\mdseries\slshape ord})\index{IsShortLexOrdering@\texttt{IsShortLexOrdering}}
\label{IsShortLexOrdering}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 for an ordering \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} of a family of associative words, returns \texttt{true} if and only if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} is a shortlex ordering. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := FreeSemigroup(3);|
  <free semigroup on the generators [ s1, s2, s3 ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@sl := ShortLexOrdering(f,[2,3,1]);|
  Ordering
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsLessThanUnder(sl,f.1,f.2);|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsLessThanUnder(sl,f.3,f.2);|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsLessThanUnder(sl,f.3,f.1);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{WeightLexOrdering}}
\logpage{[ 34, 4, 8 ]}\nobreak
