\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FreeGroup({\mdseries\slshape [wfilt, ]rank[, name]})\index{FreeGroup@\texttt{FreeGroup}!for given rank}
\label{FreeGroup:for given rank}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FreeGroup({\mdseries\slshape [wfilt][,] [name1[, name2[, ...]]]})\index{FreeGroup@\texttt{FreeGroup}!for various names}
\label{FreeGroup:for various names}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FreeGroup({\mdseries\slshape [wfilt, ]names})\index{FreeGroup@\texttt{FreeGroup}!for a list of names}
\label{FreeGroup:for a list of names}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FreeGroup({\mdseries\slshape [wfilt, ]infinity[, name][, init]})\index{FreeGroup@\texttt{FreeGroup}!for infinitely many generators}
\label{FreeGroup:for infinitely many generators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{FreeGroup} returns a free group. The number of generators, and the labels given to the
generators, can be specified in several different ways. Warning: the labels of
generators are only an aid for printing, and do not necessarily distinguish
generators; see the examples at the end of \texttt{FreeSemigroup} (\ref{FreeSemigroup:for given rank}) for more information. 
\begin{description}
\item[{ 1: For a given rank, and an optional generator name prefix }]  Called with a nonnegative integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rank}}, \texttt{FreeGroup} returns a free group on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rank}} generators. The optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} must be a string; its default value is \texttt{"f"}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is not given but the \texttt{generatorNames} option is, then this option is respected as described in
Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Generator Names}. 

 Otherwise, the generators of the returned free group are labelled \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}\texttt{1}, ..., \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}\texttt{k}, where \texttt{k} is the value of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rank}}. 

 
\item[{2: For given generator names}]  Called with various nonempty strings, \texttt{FreeGroup} returns a free group on as many generators as arguments, which are labelled \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name2}}, etc. 
\item[{3: For a given list of generator names}]  Called with a finite list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape names}} of nonempty strings, \texttt{FreeGroup} returns a free group on \texttt{Length(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape names}})} generators, whose \texttt{i}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th generator is labelled \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape names}}\texttt{[i]}. 
\item[{ 4: For the rank \texttt{infinity}, an optional default generator name prefix, and an optional finite list of
generator names }]  Called in the fourth form, \texttt{FreeGroup} returns a free group on infinitely many generators. The optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} must be a string; its default value is \texttt{"f"}, and the optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape init}} must be a finite list of nonempty strings; its default value is an empty list.
The generators are initially labelled according to the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape init}}, followed by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}\texttt{i} for each \texttt{i} in the range from \texttt{Length(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape init}})+1} to \texttt{infinity}. 
\end{description}
 If the optional first argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape wfilt}} is given, then it must be either \texttt{IsSyllableWordsFamily}, \texttt{IsLetterWordsFamily}, \texttt{IsWLetterWordsFamily}, or \texttt{IsBLetterWordsFamily}. This filter specifies the representation used for the elements of the free
group (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Representations for Associative Words}). If no such filter is given, a letter representation is used. 

 (For interfacing to old code that omits the representation flag, use of the
syllable representation is also triggered by setting the option \texttt{FreeGroupFamilyType} to the string \texttt{"syllable"}; this is overwritten by the optional first argument if it is given.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeGroup(5);|
  <free group on the generators [ f1, f2, f3, f4, f5 ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeGroup(4, "gen");|
  <free group on the generators [ gen1, gen2, gen3, gen4 ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeGroup(3 : generatorNames := "ack");|
  <free group on the generators [ ack1, ack2, ack3 ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeGroup(2 : generatorNames := ["u", "v", "w"]);|
  <free group on the generators [ u, v ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeGroup();|
  <free group of rank zero>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeGroup("a", "b", "c");|
  <free group on the generators [ a, b, c ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeGroup(["x", "y"]);|
  <free group on the generators [ x, y ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeGroup(infinity);|
  <free group with infinity generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@F := FreeGroup(infinity, "g", ["a", "b"]);|
  <free group with infinity generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfGroup(F){[1..4]};|
  [ a, b, g3, g4 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfGroup(FreeGroup(infinity, "gen")){[1..3]};|
  [ gen1, gen2, gen3 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeGroup(IsSyllableWordsFamily, 50);|
  <free group with 50 generators>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsFreeGroup}}
\logpage{[ 37, 2, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8601654A7C4AF1E7}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFreeGroup({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsFreeGroup@\texttt{IsFreeGroup}}
\label{IsFreeGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 Any group consisting of elements in \texttt{IsAssocWordWithInverse} (\ref{IsAssocWordWithInverse}) lies in the filter \texttt{IsFreeGroup}; this holds in particular for any group created with \texttt{FreeGroup} (\ref{FreeGroup:for given rank}), or any subgroup of such a group. 

     Also see Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Finitely Presented Groups}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AssignGeneratorVariables}}
\logpage{[ 37, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X814203E281F3272E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AssignGeneratorVariables({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{AssignGeneratorVariables@\texttt{AssignGeneratorVariables}}
\label{AssignGeneratorVariables}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is a group, whose generators are represented by symbols (for example a free
group, a finitely presented group or a pc group) this function assigns these
generators to global variables with the same names. 

 The aim of this function is to make it easy in interactive use to work with
(for example) a free group. It is a shorthand for a sequence of assignments of
the form 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  var1:=GeneratorsOfGroup(G)[1];
  var2:=GeneratorsOfGroup(G)[2];
  ...
  varn:=GeneratorsOfGroup(G)[n];
\end{Verbatim}
 

 However, since overwriting global variables can be very dangerous, \emph{it is not permitted to use this function within a function}. (If {\textendash}despite this warning{\textendash} this is done, the result
is undefined.) 

 If the assignment overwrites existing variables a warning is given, if any of
the variables is write protected, or any of the generator names would not be a
proper variable name, an error is raised. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Comparison of Associative Words}}\label{Comparison of Associative Words}
\logpage{[ 37, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8405BECB7AC4EB61}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{\texttt{\symbol{92}}= (for associative words)}}
\logpage{[ 37, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8206153078E97B90}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}=({\mdseries\slshape w1, w2})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}=@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}=}!for associative words}
\label{bSlash=:for associative words}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \index{equality!associative words} Two associative words are equal if they are words over the same alphabet and
if they are sequences of the same letters. This is equivalent to saying that
the external representations of the words are equal, see{\nobreakspace}\ref{The External Representation for Associative Words} and \ref{Comparison of Words}. 

 There is no ``universal'' empty word, every alphabet (that is, every family of words) has its own empty
word. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f:= FreeGroup( "a", "b", "b" );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@gens:= GeneratorsOfGroup(f);|
  [ a, b, b ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@gens[2] = gens[3];|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x:= gens[1]*gens[2];|
  a*b
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@y:= gens[2]/gens[2]*gens[1]*gens[2];|
  a*b
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x = y;|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@z:= gens[2]/gens[2]*gens[1]*gens[3];|
  a*b
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x = z;|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{\texttt{\symbol{92}}{\textless} (for associative words)}}
\logpage{[ 37, 3, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BB12B9D7F990899}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}{\textless}({\mdseries\slshape w1, w2})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}{\textless}@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}{\textless}}!for associative words}
\label{bSlash<:for associative words}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \index{smaller!associative words} The ordering of associative words is defined by length and lexicography (this
ordering is called \emph{short\texttt{\symbol{45}}lex} ordering), that is, shorter words are smaller than longer words, and words of
the same length are compared w.r.t.{\nobreakspace}the lexicographical ordering
induced by the ordering of generators. Generators are sorted according to the
order in which they were created. If the generators are invertible then each
generator \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} is larger than its inverse \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{94}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}1}, and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{94}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}1} is larger than every generator that is smaller than \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f:= FreeGroup( 2 );;  gens:= GeneratorsOfGroup( f );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a:= gens[1];;  b:= gens[2];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@One(f) < a^-1;  a^-1 < a;  a < b^-1;  b^-1 < b; b < a^2;  a^2 < a*b;|
  true
  true
  true
  true
  true
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsShortLexLessThanOrEqual}}
\logpage{[ 37, 3, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X805C519682B0A7ED}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsShortLexLessThanOrEqual({\mdseries\slshape u, v})\index{IsShortLexLessThanOrEqual@\texttt{IsShortLexLessThanOrEqual}}
\label{IsShortLexLessThanOrEqual}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns \texttt{IsLessThanOrEqualUnder(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape u}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}})} where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} is the short less ordering for the family of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape u}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}}. (This is here for compatibility with \textsf{GAP}{\nobreakspace}4.2.) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsBasicWreathLessThanOrEqual}}
\logpage{[ 37, 3, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X84875E08847B39E1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsBasicWreathLessThanOrEqual({\mdseries\slshape u, v})\index{IsBasicWreathLessThanOrEqual@\texttt{IsBasicWreathLessThanOrEqual}}
\label{IsBasicWreathLessThanOrEqual}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns \texttt{IsLessThanOrEqualUnder(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape u}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}})} where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ord}} is the basic wreath product ordering for the family of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape u}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape v}}. (This is here for compatibility with \textsf{GAP}{\nobreakspace}4.2.) }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Operations for Associative Words}}\label{Operations for Associative Words}
\logpage{[ 37, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X79AF6C757A3547BD}{}
{
  The product of two given associative words is defined as the freely reduced
concatenation of the words. \index{product!of words} \index{quotient!of words} \index{power!of words} \index{conjugate!of a word} Besides the multiplication \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}*} (\ref{bSlash*}), the arithmetical operators \texttt{One} (\ref{One}) (if the word lies in a family with identity) and (if the generators are
invertible) \texttt{Inverse} (\ref{Inverse}), \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/} (\ref{bSlash/}),\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}} (\ref{bSlash^}), \index{Comm@\texttt{Comm}!for words} \texttt{Comm} (\ref{Comm}), and \index{LeftQuotient@\texttt{LeftQuotient}!for words} \texttt{LeftQuotient} (\ref{LeftQuotient}) are applicable to associative words, see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Arithmetic Operations for Elements}. 

 See also \texttt{MappedWord} (\ref{MappedWord}), an operation that is applicable to arbitrary words. 

 See Section \ref{Representations for Associative Words} for a discussion of the internal representations of associative words that are
supported by \textsf{GAP}. Note that operations to extract or act on parts of words (letter or
syllables) can carry substantially different costs, depending on the
representation the words are in. 

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Length (for an associative word)}}
\logpage{[ 37, 4, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87CD4C6978A7936A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Length({\mdseries\slshape w})\index{Length@\texttt{Length}!for an associative word}
\label{Length:for an associative word}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 \index{length!of a word} For an associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}, \texttt{Length} returns the number of letters in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := FreeGroup("a","b");; gens := GeneratorsOfGroup(f);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a := gens[1];; b := gens[2];;w := a^5*b*a^2*b^-4*a;;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ w; Length( w );  Length( a^17 );  Length( w^0 );|
  a^5*b*a^2*b^-4*a
  13
  17
  0
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ExponentSumWord}}
\logpage{[ 37, 4, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F5ED4357A9C12E6}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ExponentSumWord({\mdseries\slshape w, gen})\index{ExponentSumWord@\texttt{ExponentSumWord}}
\label{ExponentSumWord}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 For an associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} and a generator \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gen}}, \texttt{ExponentSumWord} returns the number of times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gen}} appears in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} minus the number of times its inverse appears in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}. If both \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gen}} and its inverse do not occur in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} then $0$ is returned. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gen}} may also be the inverse of a generator. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@w;  ExponentSumWord( w, a );  ExponentSumWord( w, b );|
  a^5*b*a^2*b^-4*a
  8
  -3
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ExponentSumWord( (a*b*a^-1)^3, a );  ExponentSumWord( w, b^-1 );|
  0
  3
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Subword}}
\logpage{[ 37, 4, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82CC92C17AF6FFA0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Subword({\mdseries\slshape w, from, to})\index{Subword@\texttt{Subword}}
\label{Subword}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 For an associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} and two positive integers \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}}, \texttt{Subword} returns the subword of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} that begins at position \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} and ends at position \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}}. Indexing is done with origin 1. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@w;  Subword( w, 3, 7 );|
  a^5*b*a^2*b^-4*a
  a^3*b*a
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PositionWord}}
\logpage{[ 37, 4, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8509A0A4851981BB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PositionWord({\mdseries\slshape w, sub, from})\index{PositionWord@\texttt{PositionWord}}
\label{PositionWord}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape sub}} be associative words, and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} a positive integer. \texttt{PositionWord} returns the position of the first occurrence of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape sub}} as a subword of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}, starting at position \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}}. If there is no such occurrence, \texttt{fail} is returned. Indexing is done with origin 1. 

 In other words, \texttt{PositionWord( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape sub}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} )} is the smallest integer $i$ larger than or equal to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} such that \texttt{Subword( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}, }$i$\texttt{,} $i$\texttt{+Length( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape sub}} )\texttt{\symbol{45}}1 ) =} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape sub}}, see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Subword} (\ref{Subword}). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@w;  PositionWord( w, a/b, 1 );|
  a^5*b*a^2*b^-4*a
  8
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Subword( w, 8, 9 );|
  a*b^-1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PositionWord( w, a^2, 1 );|
  1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PositionWord( w, a^2, 2 );|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PositionWord( w, a^2, 6 );|
  7
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PositionWord( w, a^2, 8 );|
  fail
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SubstitutedWord}}\logpage{[ 37, 4, 5 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X79186218787C224A}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SubstitutedWord({\mdseries\slshape w, from, to, by})\index{SubstitutedWord@\texttt{SubstitutedWord}!replace an interval by a given word}
\label{SubstitutedWord:replace an interval by a given word}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SubstitutedWord({\mdseries\slshape w, sub, from, by})\index{SubstitutedWord@\texttt{SubstitutedWord}!replace a subword by a given word}
\label{SubstitutedWord:replace a subword by a given word}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} be an associative word. 

 In the first form, \texttt{SubstitutedWord} returns the associative word obtained by replacing the subword of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} that begins at position \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} and ends at position \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}} by the associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape by}}. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}} must be positive integers, indexing is done with origin 1. In other words, \texttt{SubstitutedWord( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape by}} )} is the product of the three words \texttt{Subword( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}, 1, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}1 )}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape by}}, and \texttt{Subword( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}}+1, Length( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} ) )}, see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Subword} (\ref{Subword}). 

 In the second form, \texttt{SubstitutedWord} returns the associative word obtained by replacing the first occurrence of the
associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape sub}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}, starting at position \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}}, by the associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape by}}; if there is no such occurrence, \texttt{fail} is returned. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@w;  SubstitutedWord( w, 3, 7, a^19 );|
  a^5*b*a^2*b^-4*a
  a^22*b^-4*a
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SubstitutedWord( w, a, 6, b^7 );|
  a^5*b^8*a*b^-4*a
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SubstitutedWord( w, a*b, 6, b^7 );|
  fail
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EliminatedWord}}
\logpage{[ 37, 4, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8486BFE1844CFE59}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EliminatedWord({\mdseries\slshape w, gen, by})\index{EliminatedWord@\texttt{EliminatedWord}}
\label{EliminatedWord}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 For an associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}, a generator \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gen}}, and an associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape by}}, \texttt{EliminatedWord} returns the associative word obtained by replacing each occurrence of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gen}} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape by}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@w;  EliminatedWord( w, a, a^2 );  EliminatedWord( w, a, b^-1 );|
  a^5*b*a^2*b^-4*a
  a^10*b*a^4*b^-4*a^2
  b^-11
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Operations for Associative Words by their Syllables}}\label{Operations for Associative Words by their Syllables}
\logpage{[ 37, 5, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7D357E047ABD2C6B}{}
{
  For an associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} $= x_1^{{n_1}} x_2^{{n_2}} \cdots x_k^{{n_k}}$ over an alphabet containing $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_k$, such that $x_i \neq x_{{i+1}}^{{\pm 1}}$ for $1 \leq i \leq k-1$, the subwords $x_i^{{e_i}}$ are uniquely determined; these powers of generators are called the \emph{syllables} of $w$. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NumberSyllables}}
\logpage{[ 37, 5, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X842D0B547CE93CF2}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NumberSyllables({\mdseries\slshape w})\index{NumberSyllables@\texttt{NumberSyllables}}
\label{NumberSyllables}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 \texttt{NumberSyllables} returns the number of syllables of the associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ExponentSyllable}}
\logpage{[ 37, 5, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E91575F848F4526}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ExponentSyllable({\mdseries\slshape w, i})\index{ExponentSyllable@\texttt{ExponentSyllable}}
\label{ExponentSyllable}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{ExponentSyllable} returns the exponent of the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th syllable of the associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorSyllable}}
\logpage{[ 37, 5, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F2A8CFD811C73B1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorSyllable({\mdseries\slshape w, i})\index{GeneratorSyllable@\texttt{GeneratorSyllable}}
\label{GeneratorSyllable}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{GeneratorSyllable} returns the number of the generator that is involved in the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th syllable of the associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SubSyllables}}
\logpage{[ 37, 5, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B4F7A167E844FA5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SubSyllables({\mdseries\slshape w, from, to})\index{SubSyllables@\texttt{SubSyllables}}
\label{SubSyllables}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{SubSyllables} returns the subword of the associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}} that consists of the syllables from positions \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}}, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape from}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape to}} must be positive integers, and indexing is done with origin 1. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@w;  NumberSyllables( w );|
  a^5*b*a^2*b^-4*a
  5
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ExponentSyllable( w, 3 );|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorSyllable( w, 3 );|
  1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SubSyllables( w, 2, 3 );|
  b*a^2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Representations for Associative Words}}\label{Representations for Associative Words}
\logpage{[ 37, 6, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X80A9F39582ED296E}{}
{
  \textsf{GAP} provides two different internal kinds of representations of associative words.
The first one are ``syllable representations'' in which words are stored in syllable (i.e. generator,exponent) form. (Older
versions of \textsf{GAP} only used this representation.) The second kind are ``letter representations'' in which each letter in a word is represented by its index number. Negative
numbers are used for inverses. Unless the syllable representation is specified
explicitly when creating the free group/monoid or semigroup, a letter
representation is used by default. 

 Depending on the task in mind, either of these two representations will
perform better in time or in memory use and algorithms that are syllable or
letter based (for example \texttt{GeneratorSyllable} (\ref{GeneratorSyllable}) and \texttt{Subword} (\ref{Subword})) perform substantially better in the corresponding representation. For
example when creating pc groups (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Pc Groups}), it is advantageous to use a syllable representation while calculations in
free groups usually benefit from using a letter representation. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLetterAssocWordRep}}
\logpage{[ 37, 6, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E3612247B3E241B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLetterAssocWordRep({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsLetterAssocWordRep@\texttt{IsLetterAssocWordRep}}
\label{IsLetterAssocWordRep}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Representation)}}\\


 A word in letter representation stores a list of generator/inverses numbers
(as given by \texttt{LetterRepAssocWord} (\ref{LetterRepAssocWord})). Letter access is fast, syllable access is slow for such words. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLetterWordsFamily}}
\logpage{[ 37, 6, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E36F7897D82417F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLetterWordsFamily({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsLetterWordsFamily@\texttt{IsLetterWordsFamily}}
\label{IsLetterWordsFamily}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 A letter word family stores words by default in letter form. 

 Internally, there are letter representations that use integers (4 Byte) to
represent a generator and letter representations that use single bytes to
represent a character. The latter are more memory efficient, but can only be
used if there are less than 128 generators (in which case they are used by
default). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsBLetterAssocWordRep}}
\logpage{[ 37, 6, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C84789D7BB161E9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsBLetterAssocWordRep({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsBLetterAssocWordRep@\texttt{IsBLetterAssocWordRep}}
\label{IsBLetterAssocWordRep}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Representation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsWLetterAssocWordRep({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsWLetterAssocWordRep@\texttt{IsWLetterAssocWordRep}}
\label{IsWLetterAssocWordRep}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Representation)}}\\


 these two subrepresentations of \texttt{IsLetterAssocWordRep} (\ref{IsLetterAssocWordRep}) indicate whether the word is stored as a list of bytes (in a string) or as a
list of integers). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsBLetterWordsFamily}}
\logpage{[ 37, 6, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8719E7F27CDA1995}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsBLetterWordsFamily({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsBLetterWordsFamily@\texttt{IsBLetterWordsFamily}}
\label{IsBLetterWordsFamily}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsWLetterWordsFamily({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsWLetterWordsFamily@\texttt{IsWLetterWordsFamily}}
\label{IsWLetterWordsFamily}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 These two subcategories of \texttt{IsLetterWordsFamily} (\ref{IsLetterWordsFamily}) specify the type of letter representation to be used. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSyllableAssocWordRep}}
\logpage{[ 37, 6, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7886F8BD83CD8081}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSyllableAssocWordRep({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsSyllableAssocWordRep@\texttt{IsSyllableAssocWordRep}}
\label{IsSyllableAssocWordRep}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Representation)}}\\


 A word in syllable representation stores generator/exponents pairs (as given
by \texttt{ExtRepOfObj} (\ref{ExtRepOfObj}). Syllable access is fast, letter access is slow for such words. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSyllableWordsFamily}}
\logpage{[ 37, 6, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7869716C84EA9D81}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSyllableWordsFamily({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsSyllableWordsFamily@\texttt{IsSyllableWordsFamily}}
\label{IsSyllableWordsFamily}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 A syllable word family stores words by default in syllable form. There are
also different versions of syllable representations, which compress a
generator exponent pair in 8, 16 or 32 bits or use a pair of integers.
Internal mechanisms try to make this as memory efficient as possible. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Is16BitsFamily}}
\logpage{[ 37, 6, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83F669828481FC32}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Is16BitsFamily({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{Is16BitsFamily@\texttt{Is16BitsFamily}}
\label{Is16BitsFamily}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Is32BitsFamily({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{Is32BitsFamily@\texttt{Is32BitsFamily}}
\label{Is32BitsFamily}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsInfBitsFamily({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsInfBitsFamily@\texttt{IsInfBitsFamily}}
\label{IsInfBitsFamily}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 Regardless of the internal representation used, it is possible to convert a
word in a list of numbers in letter or syllable representation and vice versa. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LetterRepAssocWord}}
\logpage{[ 37, 6, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BD7647C7B088389}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LetterRepAssocWord({\mdseries\slshape w[, gens]})\index{LetterRepAssocWord@\texttt{LetterRepAssocWord}}
\label{LetterRepAssocWord}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 The \emph{letter representation} of an associated word is as a list of integers, each entry corresponding to a
group generator. Inverses of the generators are represented by negative
numbers. The generator numbers are as associated to the family. 

 This operation returns the letter representation of the associative word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape w}}. 

 In the call with two arguments, the generator numbers correspond to the
generator order given in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. 

 (For words stored in syllable form the letter representation has to be
computed.) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AssocWordByLetterRep}}
\logpage{[ 37, 6, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AC8EC757CFB9A51}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AssocWordByLetterRep({\mdseries\slshape Fam, lrep[, gens]})\index{AssocWordByLetterRep@\texttt{AssocWordByLetterRep}}
\label{AssocWordByLetterRep}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 takes a letter representation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lrep}} (see \texttt{LetterRepAssocWord} (\ref{LetterRepAssocWord})) and returns an associative word in family \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} corresponding to this letter representation. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} is given, the numbers in the letter representation correspond to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@w:=AssocWordByLetterRep( FamilyObj(a), [-1,2,1,-2,-2,-2,1,1,1,1]);|
  a^-1*b*a*b^-3*a^4
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@LetterRepAssocWord( w^2 );|
  [ -1, 2, 1, -2, -2, -2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, -2, -2, -2, 1, 1, 1, 1 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

 The external representation (see section{\nobreakspace}\ref{The External Representation for Associative Words}) can be used if a syllable representation is needed. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{The External Representation for Associative Words}}\label{The External Representation for Associative Words}
\logpage{[ 37, 7, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7934D3D5797102EC}{}
{
  The external representation of the associative word $w$ is defined as follows. If $w = g_{{i_1}}^{{e_1}} * g_{{i_2}}^{{e_2}} * \cdots * g_{{i_k}}^{{e_k}}$ is a word over the alphabet $g_1, g_2, \ldots$, i.e., $g_i$ denotes the $i$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th generator of the family of $w$, then $w$ has external representation $[ i_1, e_1, i_2, e_2, \ldots, i_k, e_k ]$. The empty list describes the identity element (if exists) of the family.
Exponents may be negative if the family allows inverses. The external
representation of an associative word is guaranteed to be freely reduced; for
example, $g_1 * g_2 * g_2^{{-1}} * g_1$ has the external representation \texttt{[ 1, 2 ]}. 

 Regardless of the family preference for letter or syllable representations
(see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Representations for Associative Words}), \texttt{ExtRepOfObj} and \texttt{ObjByExtRep} can be used and interface to this ``syllable''\texttt{\symbol{45}}like representation. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@w:= ObjByExtRep( FamilyObj(a), [1,5,2,-7,1,3,2,4,1,-2] );|
  a^5*b^-7*a^3*b^4*a^-2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ExtRepOfObj( w^2 );|
  [ 1, 5, 2, -7, 1, 3, 2, 4, 1, 3, 2, -7, 1, 3, 2, 4, 1, -2 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Straight Line Programs}}\label{Straight Line Programs}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7DC99E4284093FBB}{}
{
  \emph{Straight line programs} describe an efficient way for evaluating an abstract word at concrete
generators, in a more efficient way than with \texttt{MappedWord} (\ref{MappedWord}). For example, the associative word $ababbab$ of length $7$ can be computed from the generators $a$, $b$ with only four multiplications, by first computing $c = ab$, then $d = cb$, and then $cdc$; Alternatively, one can compute $c = ab$, $e = bc$, and $aee$. In each step of these computations, one forms words in terms of the words
computed in the previous steps. 

 A straight line program in \textsf{GAP} is represented by an object in the category \texttt{IsStraightLineProgram} (\ref{IsStraightLineProgram})) that stores a list of ``lines'' each of which has one of the following three forms. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item  a nonempty dense list $l$ of integers, 
\item  a pair $[ l, i ]$ where $l$ is a list of form 1. and $i$ is a positive integer, 
\item  a list $[ l_1, l_2, \ldots, l_k ]$ where each $l_i$ is a list of form 1.; this may occur only for the last line of the program. 
\end{enumerate}
 

 The lists of integers that occur are interpreted as external representations
of associative words (see Section{\nobreakspace} \ref{The External Representation for Associative Words}); for example, the list $[ 1, 3, 2, -1 ]$ represents the word $g_1^3 g_2^{{-1}}$, with $g_1$ and $g_2$ the first and second abstract generator, respectively. 

 For the meaning of the list of lines, see \texttt{ResultOfStraightLineProgram} (\ref{ResultOfStraightLineProgram}). 

 Straight line programs can be constructed using \texttt{StraightLineProgram} (\ref{StraightLineProgram:for a list of lines (and the number of generators)}). 

 Defining attributes for straight line programs are \texttt{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram} (\ref{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram}) and \texttt{LinesOfStraightLineProgram} (\ref{LinesOfStraightLineProgram}). Another operation for straight line programs is \texttt{ResultOfStraightLineProgram} (\ref{ResultOfStraightLineProgram}). 

 Special methods applicable to straight line programs are installed for the
operations \texttt{Display} (\ref{Display}), \texttt{IsInternallyConsistent} (\ref{IsInternallyConsistent}), \texttt{PrintObj} (\ref{PrintObj}), and \texttt{ViewObj} (\ref{ViewObj}). 

 For a straight line program \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}}, the default \texttt{Display} (\ref{Display}) method prints the interpretation of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}} as a sequence of assignments of associative words; a record with components \texttt{gensnames} (with value a list of strings) and \texttt{listname} (a string) may be entered as second argument of \texttt{Display} (\ref{Display}), in this case these names are used, the default for \texttt{gensnames} is \texttt{[ g1, g2, }$\ldots$\texttt{ ]}, the default for \texttt{listname} is $r$. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsStraightLineProgram}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F69FF3F7C6694CB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsStraightLineProgram({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsStraightLineProgram@\texttt{IsStraightLineProgram}}
\label{IsStraightLineProgram}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 Each straight line program in \textsf{GAP} lies in the category \texttt{IsStraightLineProgram}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{StraightLineProgram (for a list of lines (and the number of generators))}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AECA57280DA3195}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StraightLineProgram({\mdseries\slshape lines[, nrgens]})\index{StraightLineProgram@\texttt{StraightLineProgram}!for a list of lines (and the number of generators)}
\label{StraightLineProgram:for a list of lines (and the number of generators)}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StraightLineProgram({\mdseries\slshape string, gens})\index{StraightLineProgram@\texttt{StraightLineProgram}!for a string and a list of generators names}
\label{StraightLineProgram:for a string and a list of generators names}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StraightLineProgramNC({\mdseries\slshape lines[, nrgens]})\index{StraightLineProgramNC@\texttt{StraightLineProgramNC}!for a list of lines (and the number of generators)}
\label{StraightLineProgramNC:for a list of lines (and the number of generators)}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StraightLineProgramNC({\mdseries\slshape string, gens})\index{StraightLineProgramNC@\texttt{StraightLineProgramNC}!for a string and a list of generators names}
\label{StraightLineProgramNC:for a string and a list of generators names}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 In the first form, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lines}} must be a nonempty list of lists that defines a unique straight line program
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsStraightLineProgram} (\ref{IsStraightLineProgram})); in this case \texttt{StraightLineProgram} returns this program, otherwise an error is signalled. The optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape nrgens}} specifies the number of input generators of the program; if a line of form 1.
(that is, a list of integers) occurs in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lines}} except in the last position, this number is not determined by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lines}} and therefore \emph{must} be specified by the argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape nrgens}}; if not then \texttt{StraightLineProgram} returns \texttt{fail}. 

 In the second form, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape string}} must be a nonempty string describing an arithmetic expression in terms of the
strings in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}, where multiplication is denoted by concatenation, powering is denoted by \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{94}}}, and round brackets \texttt{(}, \texttt{)} may be used. Each entry in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} must consist only of uppercase or lowercase letters (i.e., letters in \texttt{IsAlphaChar} (\ref{IsAlphaChar})) such that no entry is an initial part of another one. Called with this
input, \texttt{StraightLineProgram} returns a straight line program that evaluates to the word corresponding to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape string}} when called with generators corresponding to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. 

 The \texttt{NC} variant does the same, except that the internal consistency of the program is
not checked. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LinesOfStraightLineProgram}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81A8AFC47F8E4B91}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LinesOfStraightLineProgram({\mdseries\slshape prog})\index{LinesOfStraightLineProgram@\texttt{LinesOfStraightLineProgram}}
\label{LinesOfStraightLineProgram}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 For a straight line program \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}}, \texttt{LinesOfStraightLineProgram} returns the list of program lines. There is no default method to compute these
lines if they are not stored. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X820A592881D57802}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram({\mdseries\slshape prog})\index{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram@\texttt{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram}}
\label{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 For a straight line program \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}}, \texttt{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram} returns the number of generators that are needed as input. 

 If a line of form 1. (that is, a list of integers) occurs in the lines of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}} except the last line then the number of generators is not determined by the
lines, and must be set in the construction of the straight line program
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{StraightLineProgram} (\ref{StraightLineProgram:for a list of lines (and the number of generators)})). So if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}} contains a line of form 1. other than the last line and does \emph{not} store the number of generators then \texttt{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram} signals an error. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ResultOfStraightLineProgram}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7847D32B863E822F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ResultOfStraightLineProgram({\mdseries\slshape prog, gens})\index{ResultOfStraightLineProgram@\texttt{ResultOfStraightLineProgram}}
\label{ResultOfStraightLineProgram}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{ResultOfStraightLineProgram} evaluates the straight line program (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsStraightLineProgram} (\ref{IsStraightLineProgram})) \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}} at the group elements in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. 

 The \emph{result} of a straight line program with lines $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k$ when applied to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} is defined as follows. 
\begin{description}
\item[{(a)}]  First a list $r$ of intermediate results is initialized with a shallow copy of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. 
\item[{(b)}]  For $i < k$, before the $i$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th step, let $r$ be of length $n$. If $p_i$ is the external representation of an associative word in the first $n$ generators then the image of this word under the homomorphism that is given by
mapping $r$ to these first $n$ generators is added to $r$; if $p_i$ is a pair $[ l, j ]$, for a list $l$, then the same element is computed, but instead of being added to $r$, it replaces the $j$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th entry of $r$. 
\item[{(c)}]  For $i = k$, if $p_k$ is the external representation of an associative word then the element
described in (b) is the result of the program, if $p_k$ is a pair $[ l, j ]$, for a list $l$, then the result is the element described by $l$, and if $p_k$ is a list $[ l_1, l_2, \ldots, l_k ]$ of lists then the result is a list of group elements, where each $l_i$ is treated as in (b). 
\end{description}
 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f:= FreeGroup( "x", "y" );;  gens:= GeneratorsOfGroup( f );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x:= gens[1];;  y:= gens[2];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg:= StraightLineProgram( [ [] ] );|
  <straight line program>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg, [] );|
  [  ]
\end{Verbatim}
 The above straight line program \texttt{prg} returns {\textendash}for \emph{any} list of input generators{\textendash} an empty list. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StraightLineProgram( [ [1,2,2,3], [3,-1] ] );|
  fail
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg:= StraightLineProgram( [ [1,2,2,3], [3,-1] ], 2 );|
  <straight line program>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@LinesOfStraightLineProgram( prg );|
  [ [ 1, 2, 2, 3 ], [ 3, -1 ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg:= StraightLineProgram( "(a^2b^3)^-1", [ "a", "b" ] );|
  <straight line program>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@LinesOfStraightLineProgram( prg );|
  [ [ [ 1, 2, 2, 3 ], 3 ], [ [ 3, -1 ], 4 ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@res:= ResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg, gens );|
  y^-3*x^-2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@res = (x^2 * y^3)^-1;|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram( prg );|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Print( prg, "\n" );|
  StraightLineProgram( [ [ [ 1, 2, 2, 3 ], 3 ], [ [ 3, -1 ], 4 ] ], 2 )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Display( prg );|
  # input:
  r:= [ g1, g2 ];
  # program:
  r[3]:= r[1]^2*r[2]^3;
  r[4]:= r[3]^-1;
  # return value:
  r[4]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsInternallyConsistent( StraightLineProgramNC( [ [1,2] ] ) );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsInternallyConsistent( StraightLineProgramNC( [ [1,2,3] ] ) );|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg1:= StraightLineProgram( [ [1,1,2,2], [3,3,1,1] ], 2 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg2:= StraightLineProgram( [ [ [1,1,2,2], 2 ], [2,3,1,1] ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@res1:= ResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg1, gens );|
  (x*y^2)^3*x
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@res1 = (x*y^2)^3*x;|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@res2:= ResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg2, gens );|
  (x*y^2)^3*x
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@res2 = (x*y^2)^3*x;|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg:= StraightLineProgram( [ [2,3], [ [3,1,1,4], [1,2,3,1] ] ], 2 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@res:= ResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg, gens );|
  [ y^3*x^4, x^2*y^3 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 \index{LaTeX!for the result of a straight line program} 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8098EAAF7D344466}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram({\mdseries\slshape prog, gensnames[, "LaTeX"]})\index{StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram@\texttt{StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram}}
\label{StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram} returns a string that describes the result of the straight line program
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsStraightLineProgram} (\ref{IsStraightLineProgram})) \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}} as word(s) in terms of the strings in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gensnames}}. If the result of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}} is a single element then the return value of \texttt{StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram} is a string consisting of the entries of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gensnames}}, opening and closing brackets \texttt{(} and \texttt{)}, and powering by integers via \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{94}}}. If the result of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}} is a list of elements then the return value of \texttt{StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram} is a comma separated concatenation of the strings of the single elements,
enclosed in square brackets \texttt{[}, \texttt{]}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg:= StraightLineProgram( [ [ 1, 2, 2, 3 ], [ 3, -1 ] ], 2 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg, [ "a", "b" ] );|
  "(a^2b^3)^-1"
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg, [ "a", "b" ], "LaTeX" );|
  "(a^{2}b^{3})^{-1}"
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CompositionOfStraightLinePrograms}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8274C7948248C053}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CompositionOfStraightLinePrograms({\mdseries\slshape prog2, prog1})\index{CompositionOfStraightLinePrograms@\texttt{CompositionOfStraightLinePrograms}}
\label{CompositionOfStraightLinePrograms}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For two straight line programs \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog2}}, \texttt{CompositionOfStraightLinePrograms} returns a straight line program \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}} with the properties that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}} have the same number of inputs, and the result of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}} when applied to given generators \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} equals the result of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog2}} when this is applied to the output of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog1}} applied to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. 

 (Of course the number of outputs of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog1}} must be the same as the number of inputs of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog2}}.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg1:= StraightLineProgram( "a^2b", [ "a","b" ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg2:= StraightLineProgram( "c^5", [ "c" ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@comp:= CompositionOfStraightLinePrograms( prg2, prg1 );|
  <straight line program>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram( comp, [ "a", "b" ] );|
  "(a^2b)^5"
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg:= StraightLineProgram( [ [2,3], [ [3,1,1,4], [1,2,3,1] ] ], 2 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg, [ "a", "b" ] );|
  "[ b^3a^4, a^2b^3 ]"
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@comp:= CompositionOfStraightLinePrograms( prg, prg );|
  <straight line program>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StringOfResultOfStraightLineProgram( comp, [ "a", "b" ] );|
  "[ (a^2b^3)^3(b^3a^4)^4, (b^3a^4)^2(a^2b^3)^3 ]"
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IntegratedStraightLineProgram}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A582FA97C786640}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IntegratedStraightLineProgram({\mdseries\slshape listofprogs})\index{IntegratedStraightLineProgram@\texttt{IntegratedStraightLineProgram}}
\label{IntegratedStraightLineProgram}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For a nonempty dense list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape listofprogs}} of straight line programs $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_m$ that have the same number $n$ of inputs (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram} (\ref{NrInputsOfStraightLineProgram})), \texttt{IntegratedStraightLineProgram} returns a straight line program $prog$ with $n$ inputs such that for each $n$\texttt{\symbol{45}}tuple $gens$ of generators, \texttt{ResultOfStraightLineProgram( }$prog, gens$\texttt{ )} is the concatenation of the lists $r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_m$, where $r_i$ is equal to \texttt{ResultOfStraightLineProgram( }$p_i, gens$\texttt{ )} if this result is a list of elements, and otherwise $r_i$ is equal to the list of length one that contains this result. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f:= FreeGroup( "x", "y" );;  gens:= GeneratorsOfGroup( f );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg1:= StraightLineProgram([ [ [ 1, 2 ], 1 ], [ 1, 2, 2, -1 ] ], 2);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg2:= StraightLineProgram([ [ [ 2, 2 ], 3 ], [ 1, 3, 3, 2 ] ], 2);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg3:= StraightLineProgram([ [ 2, 2 ], [ 1, 3, 3, 2 ] ], 2);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg:= IntegratedStraightLineProgram( [ prg1, prg2, prg3 ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg, gens );|
  [ x^4*y^-1, x^3*y^4, x^3*y^4 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg:= IntegratedStraightLineProgram( [ prg2, prg3, prg1 ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg, gens );|
  [ x^3*y^4, x^3*y^4, x^4*y^-1 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg:= IntegratedStraightLineProgram( [ prg3, prg1, prg2 ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg, gens );|
  [ x^3*y^4, x^4*y^-1, x^3*y^4 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@prg:= IntegratedStraightLineProgram( [ prg, prg ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ResultOfStraightLineProgram( prg, gens );|
  [ x^3*y^4, x^4*y^-1, x^3*y^4, x^3*y^4, x^4*y^-1, x^3*y^4 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RestrictOutputsOfSLP}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C9CABD17BE4850F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RestrictOutputsOfSLP({\mdseries\slshape slp, k})\index{RestrictOutputsOfSLP@\texttt{RestrictOutputsOfSLP}}
\label{RestrictOutputsOfSLP}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape slp}} must be a straight line program returning a tuple of values. This function
returns a new slp that calculates only those outputs specified by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}}. The argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}} may be an integer or a list of integers. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}} is an integer, the resulting slp calculates only the result with that number
in the original output tuple. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}} is a list of integers, the resulting slp calculates those results with indices \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}} in the original output tuple. In both cases the resulting slp does only what
is necessary. Obviously, the slp must have a line with enough expressions
(lists) for the supplied \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}} as its last line. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape slp}} is either an slp or a pair where the first entry are the lines of the slp and
the second is the number of inputs. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IntermediateResultOfSLP}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EF202F17DCA5D1C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IntermediateResultOfSLP({\mdseries\slshape slp, k})\index{IntermediateResultOfSLP@\texttt{IntermediateResultOfSLP}}
\label{IntermediateResultOfSLP}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Returns a new slp that calculates only the value of slot \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}} at the end of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape slp}} doing only what is necessary. slp is either an slp or a pair where the first
entry are the lines of the slp and the second is the number of inputs. Note
that this assumes a general SLP with possible overwriting. If you know that
your SLP does not overwrite slots, please use \texttt{IntermediateResultOfSLPWithoutOverwrite} (\ref{IntermediateResultOfSLPWithoutOverwrite}), which is much faster in this case. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IntermediateResultOfSLPWithoutOverwrite}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8085CF79856B2889}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IntermediateResultOfSLPWithoutOverwrite({\mdseries\slshape slp, k})\index{IntermediateResultOfSLPWithoutOverwrite@\texttt{Intermediate}\-\texttt{Result}\-\texttt{Of}\-\texttt{S}\-\texttt{L}\-\texttt{P}\-\texttt{Without}\-\texttt{Overwrite}}
\label{IntermediateResultOfSLPWithoutOverwrite}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Returns a new slp that calculates only the value of slot \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}}, which must be an integer. Note that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape slp}} must not overwrite slots but only append!!! Use \texttt{IntermediateResultOfSLP} (\ref{IntermediateResultOfSLP}) in the other case! \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape slp}} is either an slp or a pair where the first entry is the list of lines of the
slp and the second is the number of its inputs. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IntermediateResultsOfSLPWithoutOverwrite}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 12 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X873244F37FAA717A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IntermediateResultsOfSLPWithoutOverwrite({\mdseries\slshape slp, k})\index{IntermediateResultsOfSLPWithoutOverwrite@\texttt{Intermediate}\-\texttt{Results}\-\texttt{Of}\-\texttt{S}\-\texttt{L}\-\texttt{P}\-\texttt{Without}\-\texttt{Overwrite}}
\label{IntermediateResultsOfSLPWithoutOverwrite}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Returns a new slp that calculates only the values of slots contained in the
list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape k}}. Note that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape slp}} must not overwrite slots but only append!!! Use \texttt{IntermediateResultOfSLP} (\ref{IntermediateResultOfSLP}) in the other case! \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape slp}} is either a slp or a pair where the first entry is the list of lines of the
slp and the second is the number of its inputs. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ProductOfStraightLinePrograms}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 13 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X837101F982C35035}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ProductOfStraightLinePrograms({\mdseries\slshape s1, s2})\index{ProductOfStraightLinePrograms@\texttt{ProductOfStraightLinePrograms}}
\label{ProductOfStraightLinePrograms}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s2}} must be two slps that return a single element with the same number of inputs.
This function constructs an slp that returns the product of the two results
the slps \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s2}} would produce with the same input. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SlotUsagePattern}}
\logpage{[ 37, 8, 14 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X84C83CE98194FD03}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SlotUsagePattern({\mdseries\slshape s})\index{SlotUsagePattern@\texttt{SlotUsagePattern}}
\label{SlotUsagePattern}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 Analyses the straight line program \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} for more efficient evaluation. This means in particular two things, when this
attribute is known: First of all, intermediate results which are not actually
needed later on are not computed at all, and once an intermediate result is
used for the last time in this SLP, it is discarded. The latter leads to the
fact that the evaluation of the SLP needs less memory. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Straight Line Program Elements}}\label{Straight Line Program Elements}
\logpage{[ 37, 9, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8188799182D82A92}{}
{
  When computing with very large (in terms of memory) elements, for example
permutations of degree a few hundred thousands, it can be helpful (in terms of
memory usage) to represent them via straight line programs in terms of an
original generator set. (So every element takes only small extra storage for
the straight line program.) 

 A straight line program element has a \emph{seed} (a list of group elements) and a straight line program on the same number of
generators as the length of this seed, its value is the value of the evaluated
straight line program. 

 At the moment, the entries of the straight line program have to be simple
lists (i.e. of the first form). 

 Straight line program elements are in the same categories and families as the
elements of the seed, so they should work together with existing algorithms. 

 Note however, that due to the different way of storage some normally very
cheap operations (such as testing for element equality) can become more
expensive when dealing with straight line program elements. This is
essentially the tradeoff for using less memory. 

 See also Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Working with large degree permutation groups}. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsStraightLineProgElm}}
\logpage{[ 37, 9, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85A5838482944FA5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsStraightLineProgElm({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsStraightLineProgElm@\texttt{IsStraightLineProgElm}}
\label{IsStraightLineProgElm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Representation)}}\\


 A straight line program element is a group element given (for memory reasons)
as a straight line program. Straight line program elements are positional
objects, the first component is a record with a component \texttt{seeds}, the second component the straight line program. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{StraightLineProgElm}}
\logpage{[ 37, 9, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78889E5B7E1B3BFF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StraightLineProgElm({\mdseries\slshape seed, prog})\index{StraightLineProgElm@\texttt{StraightLineProgElm}}
\label{StraightLineProgElm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Creates a straight line program element for seed \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape seed}} and program \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape prog}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{StraightLineProgGens}}
\logpage{[ 37, 9, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81BC263A7E45E775}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StraightLineProgGens({\mdseries\slshape gens[, base]})\index{StraightLineProgGens@\texttt{StraightLineProgGens}}
\label{StraightLineProgGens}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns a set of straight line program elements corresponding to the
generators in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} is a set of permutations then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape base}} can be given which must be a base for the group generated by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. (Such a base will be used to speed up equality tests.) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EvalStraightLineProgElm}}
\logpage{[ 37, 9, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BEAE8AC809B27DC}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EvalStraightLineProgElm({\mdseries\slshape slpel})\index{EvalStraightLineProgElm@\texttt{EvalStraightLineProgElm}}
\label{EvalStraightLineProgElm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 evaluates a straight line program element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape slpel}} from its seeds. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{StretchImportantSLPElement}}
\logpage{[ 37, 9, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D85D1DF84DC68E3}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StretchImportantSLPElement({\mdseries\slshape elm})\index{StretchImportantSLPElement@\texttt{StretchImportantSLPElement}}
\label{StretchImportantSLPElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is a straight line program element whose straight line representation is very
long, this operation changes the representation of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} to a straight line program element, equal to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}}, whose seed contains the evaluation of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} and whose straight line program has length 1. 

 For other objects nothing happens. 

 This operation permits to designate ``important'' elements within an algorithm (elements that will be referred to often), which
will be represented by guaranteed short straight line program elements. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@A,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>A !gapinput@gens:=StraightLineProgGens([(1,2,3,4),(1,2)]);A
  [ <[ [ 2, 1 ] ]|(1,2,3,4)>, <[ [ 1, 1 ] ]|(1,2)> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>A !gapinput@g:=Group(gens);;A
  !gapprompt@gap>A !gapinput@(gens[1]^3)^gens[2];A
  <[ [ 1, -1, 2, 3, 1, 1 ] ]|(1,2,4,3)>
  !gapprompt@gap>A !gapinput@Size(g);A
  24
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Objects with Memory}}\label{Objects with Memory}
\logpage{[ 37, 10, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X877AAF977A6C1F09}{}
{
  The idea behind objects with memory is as follows. One starts with a list of
seed objects and creates corresponding new objects for them that store how
they arise from the seed objects (see \texttt{GeneratorsWithMemory} (\ref{GeneratorsWithMemory})). Each product, inverse, commutator etc. of the new objects then also stores
how it was obtained from the seed objects. One can use \texttt{SLPOfElm} (\ref{SLPOfElm}) to create a straight line program for a given element $x$ such that evaluating this program in the seed objects yields $x$. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@seeds:= [ (1,2,3), (1,2) ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elms:= GeneratorsWithMemory( seeds );|
  [ <(1,2,3) with mem>, <(1,2) with mem> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x:= (elms[1] * elms[2])^-1;|
  <(2,3) with mem>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@xslp:= SLPOfElm( x );|
  <straight line program>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Display( xslp );|
  # input:
  r:= [ g1, g2 ];
  # program:
  r[3]:= r[1]*r[2];
  r[4]:= r[3]^-1;
  # return value:
  r[4]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ResultOfStraightLineProgram( xslp, seeds );|
  (2,3)
\end{Verbatim}
 

 The objects with memory are intended to behave equally to the underlying
objects without memory, apart from the behaviour concerning the memory
information. In particular, the tests for equality and ordering are delegated
to the underlying objects. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@seeds = elms;|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@( seeds[1] < seeds[2] ) = ( elms[1] < elms[2] );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 

 It may, however, happen that some \textsf{GAP} function runs into an error when it is called with elements with memory. In
such cases, probably a method for elements with memory is missing, and perhaps
some existing methods are installed with too weak requirements. As a solution,
one can then add the missing method, or ask \textsf{GAP} support for help. 

 An overview of the currently supported functionality for objects with memory
can be computed with \texttt{MethodsForObjWithMemory} (\ref{MethodsForObjWithMemory}), this may be helpful for finding code that can be adapted. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsObjWithMemory}}
\logpage{[ 37, 10, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E39534E826C6A8E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsObjWithMemory({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsObjWithMemory@\texttt{IsObjWithMemory}}
\label{IsObjWithMemory}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Representation)}}\\


 The filter \texttt{IsObjWithMemory} describes objects that can be multiplied and store information how they arise
from seed objects via arithmetic operations. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@seeds:= [ (1,2,3), (1,2) ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elms:= GeneratorsWithMemory( seeds );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsObjWithMemory( elms[1] );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsObjWithMemory( seeds[1] );|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsWithMemory}}
\logpage{[ 37, 10, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8310FFAC82CD7652}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsWithMemory({\mdseries\slshape list})\index{GeneratorsWithMemory@\texttt{GeneratorsWithMemory}}
\label{GeneratorsWithMemory}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
a list of objects with memory



 For a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} of multiplicative elements, \texttt{GeneratorsWithMemory} returns a list of corresponding objects with memory. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@seeds:= [ (1,2,3), (1,2) ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elms:= GeneratorsWithMemory( seeds );|
  [ <(1,2,3) with mem>, <(1,2) with mem> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@seeds = elms;|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ForAll( elms, IsObjWithMemory );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GroupWithMemory}}\logpage{[ 37, 10, 3 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7A73055D83FFB54A}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GroupWithMemory({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{GroupWithMemory@\texttt{GroupWithMemory}!for a group}
\label{GroupWithMemory:for a group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GroupWithMemory({\mdseries\slshape gens})\index{GroupWithMemory@\texttt{GroupWithMemory}!for a list of generators}
\label{GroupWithMemory:for a list of generators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Return a group whose \texttt{GeneratorsOfGroup} (\ref{GeneratorsOfGroup}) value is the \texttt{GeneratorsWithMemory} (\ref{GeneratorsWithMemory}) value of \texttt{GeneratorsOfGroup( }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}\texttt{ )} or of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}, respectively. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:= GroupWithMemory( SymmetricGroup( 3 ) );|
  Group([ (1,2,3), (1,2) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsObjWithMemory( One( G ) );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:= GroupWithMemory( [ (1,2,3) ] );|
  Group([ (1,2,3) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsObjWithMemory( One( G ) );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SLPOfElm}}
\logpage{[ 37, 10, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86EE81217C438D32}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SLPOfElm({\mdseries\slshape g})\index{SLPOfElm@\texttt{SLPOfElm}}
\label{SLPOfElm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} in the filter \texttt{IsObjWithMemory} (\ref{IsObjWithMemory}), return a straight line program that describes \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} in terms of the generators that were used to initialize the memory. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@seeds:= [ (1,2,3), (1,2) ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elms:= GeneratorsWithMemory( seeds );|
  [ <(1,2,3) with mem>, <(1,2) with mem> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:= (elms[2] * elms[1] * elms[2])^-1;|
  <(1,2,3) with mem>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@slp:= SLPOfElm( g );|
  <straight line program>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g = ResultOfStraightLineProgram( slp, seeds );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SLPOfElms}}
\logpage{[ 37, 10, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D3B81CE87D6D429}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SLPOfElms({\mdseries\slshape list})\index{SLPOfElms@\texttt{SLPOfElms}}
\label{SLPOfElms}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} of elements in the filter \texttt{IsObjWithMemory} (\ref{IsObjWithMemory}), return a straight line program that describes \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} in terms of the generators that were used to initialize the memory. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@seeds:= [ (1,2,3), (1,2) ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elms:= GeneratorsWithMemory( seeds );|
  [ <(1,2,3) with mem>, <(1,2) with mem> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@list:= [ elms[2] * elms[1], elms[1] * elms[2] ];|
  [ <(1,3) with mem>, <(2,3) with mem> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@slp:= SLPOfElms( list );|
  <straight line program>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@list = ResultOfStraightLineProgram( slp, seeds );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{StripMemory}}
\logpage{[ 37, 10, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X783FCE658057D273}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StripMemory({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{StripMemory@\texttt{StripMemory}}
\label{StripMemory}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 For a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}}, \texttt{StripMemory} returns a new list of the \texttt{StripMemory} results for the entries of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} is not a list and in the filter \texttt{IsObjWithMemory} (\ref{IsObjWithMemory}), \texttt{StripMemory} returns the underlying object without memory. 

 Otherwise \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj}} is returned. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@seeds:= [ (1,2,3), (1,2) ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@elms:= GeneratorsWithMemory( seeds );|
  [ <(1,2,3) with mem>, <(1,2) with mem> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StripMemory( elms );|
  [ (1,2,3), (1,2) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StripMemory( elms[1] );|
  (1,2,3)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsIdenticalObj( seeds[1], StripMemory( seeds[1] ) );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MethodsForObjWithMemory}}
\logpage{[ 37, 10, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81A6A0FB7FEBCCC4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MethodsForObjWithMemory({\mdseries\slshape })\index{MethodsForObjWithMemory@\texttt{MethodsForObjWithMemory}}
\label{MethodsForObjWithMemory}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 This function is intended to give an overview of those methods in the current \textsf{GAP} session for which at least one argument is required to be in the filter \texttt{IsObjWithMemory} (\ref{IsObjWithMemory}). 

 The return value is a list of records, with the same components as the ones
returned by \texttt{MethodsOperation} (\ref{MethodsOperation}). In particular, the \texttt{func} component of each record is the method itself, and the \texttt{info} component is a string that describes its requirements. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@res:= MethodsForObjWithMemory();;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@for r in res{ [ 1 .. 10 ] } do|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@     Print( r.info, "\n" );|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@   od;|
  ViewObj: [ IsObjWithMemory ]
  =: [ IsObjWithMemory, IsObjWithMemory ]
  =: [ IsMultiplicativeElement, IsObjWithMemory ]
  =: [ IsObjWithMemory, IsMultiplicativeElement ]
  <: [ IsObjWithMemory, IsObjWithMemory ]
  <: [ IsMultiplicativeElement, IsObjWithMemory ]
  <: [ IsObjWithMemory, IsMultiplicativeElement ]
  PrintObj: [ IsObjWithMemory ]
  Length: [ IsMatrix and IsObjWithMemory ]
  Length: [ IsObjWithMemory and IsWord ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

 Note that some functions may provide a special treatment for objects in \texttt{IsObjWithMemory} (\ref{IsObjWithMemory}) but no arguments of the function are objects with memory. For example, there
is a \texttt{One} (\ref{One}) method for a group that checks whether the generators are objects with memory,
and if yes returns an identity element with memory. Such functions do not
occur in the output of \texttt{MethodsForObjWithMemory}. }

 }

 }

            
\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Rewriting Systems}}\label{Rewriting Systems}
\logpage{[ 38, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7CA8FCFD81AA1890}{}
{
  Rewriting systems in \textsf{GAP} are a framework for dealing with the very general task of rewriting elements
of a free (or \emph{term}) algebra in some normal form. Although most rewriting systems currently in
use are \emph{string rewriting systems} (where the algebra has only one binary operation which is associative) the
framework in \textsf{GAP} is general enough to encompass the task of rewriting algebras of any signature
from groups to semirings. 

 Rewriting systems are already implemented in \textsf{GAP} for finitely presented semigroups and for pc groups. The use of these
particular rewriting systems is described in the corresponding chapters. We
describe here only the general framework of rewriting systems with a
particular emphasis on material which would be helpful for a developer
implementing a rewriting system. 

 We fix some definitions and terminology for the rest of this chapter. Let $T$ be a term algebra in some signature. A \emph{term rewriting system} for $T$ is a set of ordered pairs of elements of $T$ of the form $(l, r)$. Viewed as a set of relations, the rewriting system determines a presentation
for a quotient algebra $A$ of $T$. 

 When we take into account the fact that the relations are expressed as \emph{ordered} pairs, we have a way of \emph{reducing} the elements of $T$. Suppose an element $u$ of $T$ has a subword $l$ and $(l, r)$ is a rule of the rewriting system, then we can replace the subterm $l$ of $u$ by the term $r$ and obtain a new word $v$. We say that we have \emph{rewritten} $u$ as $v$. Note that $u$ and $v$ represent the same element of $A$. If $u$ cannot be rewritten using any rule of the rewriting system we sat that $u$ is \emph{reduced}.  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Operations on rewriting systems}}\label{Operations on rewriting systems}
\logpage{[ 38, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8287CBE183EBE5D7}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRewritingSystem}}

\hyperdef{L}{X842C0ED87986F7AA}{}

\label{IsRewritingSystem}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 This is the category in which all rewriting systems lie. }

\hyperdef{L}{X833EAA8C86356F42}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Rules({\mdseries\slshape rws})\index{Rules@\texttt{Rules}}
\label{Rules}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The rules comprising the rewriting system. Note that these may change through
the life of the rewriting system, however they will always be a set of

\logpage{[ 38, 1, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C38C2EF817F9E0A}{}
