{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RationalClasses({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{RationalClasses@\texttt{RationalClasses}}
\label{RationalClasses}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a list of the rational classes of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. (See \texttt{RationalClass} (\ref{RationalClass}).) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RationalClasses(DerivedSubgroup(g));|
  [ RationalClass( AlternatingGroup( [ 1 .. 4 ] ), () ),
    RationalClass( AlternatingGroup( [ 1 .. 4 ] ), (1,2)(3,4) ),
    RationalClass( AlternatingGroup( [ 1 .. 4 ] ), (1,2,3) ) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GaloisGroup (of rational class of a group)}}
\logpage{[ 39, 10, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X877691247DE23386}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GaloisGroup({\mdseries\slshape ratcl})\index{GaloisGroup@\texttt{GaloisGroup}!of rational class of a group}
\label{GaloisGroup:of rational class of a group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 Suppose that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ratcl}} is a rational class of a group $G$ with representative $g$. The exponents $i$ for which $g^i$ lies already in the ordinary conjugacy class of $g$, form a subgroup of the \emph{prime residue class group} $P_n$ (see \texttt{PrimitiveRootMod} (\ref{PrimitiveRootMod})), the so\texttt{\symbol{45}}called \emph{Galois group} of the rational class. The prime residue class group $P_n$ is obtained in \textsf{GAP} as \texttt{Units( Integers mod \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} )}, the unit group of a residue class ring. The Galois group of a rational class \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ratcl}} is stored in the attribute \texttt{GaloisGroup} as a subgroup of this group. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsConjugate}}\logpage{[ 39, 10, 9 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X83DD148D7DA2ABA9}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsConjugate({\mdseries\slshape G, x, y})\index{IsConjugate@\texttt{IsConjugate}!for a group and two elements}
\label{IsConjugate:for a group and two elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsConjugate({\mdseries\slshape G, U, V})\index{IsConjugate@\texttt{IsConjugate}!for a group and two groups}
\label{IsConjugate:for a group and two groups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 tests whether the elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape y}} or the subgroups \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape V}} are conjugate under the action of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. (They do not need to be \emph{contained in} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}.) This command is only a shortcut to \texttt{RepresentativeAction} (\ref{RepresentativeAction}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsConjugate(g,Group((1,2,3,4),(1,3)),Group((1,3,2,4),(1,2)));|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 

 \texttt{RepresentativeAction} (\ref{RepresentativeAction}) can be used to obtain conjugating elements. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RepresentativeAction(g,(1,2),(3,4));|
  (1,3)(2,4)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NthRootsInGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 10, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81A92F828400FC8A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NthRootsInGroup({\mdseries\slshape G, e, n})\index{NthRootsInGroup@\texttt{NthRootsInGroup}}
\label{NthRootsInGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} be an element in the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. This function returns a list of all those elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} whose \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th power is \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NthRootsInGroup(g,(1,2)(3,4),2);|
  [ (1,3,2,4), (1,4,2,3) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Normal Structure}}\label{Normal Structure}
\logpage{[ 39, 11, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X804F0F037F06E25E}{}
{
  For the operations \texttt{Centralizer} (\ref{Centralizer:for a magma and a submagma}) and \texttt{Centre} (\ref{Centre}), see Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Magmas}. \index{normalizer} 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Normalizer}}\logpage{[ 39, 11, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X87B5370C7DFD401D}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Normalizer({\mdseries\slshape G, U})\index{Normalizer@\texttt{Normalizer}!for two groups}
\label{Normalizer:for two groups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Normalizer({\mdseries\slshape G, g})\index{Normalizer@\texttt{Normalizer}!for a group and a group element}
\label{Normalizer:for a group and a group element}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 For two groups \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}}, \texttt{Normalizer} computes the normalizer $N_{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}})$, that is, the stabilizer of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}} under the conjugation action of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 

 For a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} and a group element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}, \texttt{Normalizer} computes $N_{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}}(\langle \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} \rangle)$. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Normalizer(g,Subgroup(g,[(1,2,3)]));|
  Group([ (1,2,3), (2,3) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Core}}
\logpage{[ 39, 11, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C4E00297E37AA44}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Core({\mdseries\slshape S, U})\index{Core@\texttt{Core}}
\label{Core}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}} are groups of elements in the same family, this operation returns the core of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}, that is the intersection of all \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}conjugates of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3,4),(1,2));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Core(g,Subgroup(g,[(1,2,3,4)]));|
  Group(())
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PCore}}
\logpage{[ 39, 11, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7CF497C77B1E8938}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PCore({\mdseries\slshape G, p})\index{PCore@\texttt{PCore}}
\label{PCore}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \index{Op(G)@$O_p(G)$!see PCore} The \emph{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}core} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the largest normal \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. It is the core of a Sylow \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, see \texttt{Core} (\ref{Core}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=DicyclicGroup(12);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PCore(g,2);|
  Group([ y3 ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PCore(g,2) = Core(g,SylowSubgroup(g,2));|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PCore(g,3);|
  Group([ y*y3 ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PCore(g,5);|
  Group([  ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=SymmetricGroup(4);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PCore(g,2);|
  Group([ (1,4)(2,3), (1,2)(3,4) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PCore(g,2) = Core(g,SylowSubgroup(g,2));|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NormalClosure}}
\logpage{[ 39, 11, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BDEA0A98720D1BB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NormalClosure({\mdseries\slshape G, U})\index{NormalClosure@\texttt{NormalClosure}}
\label{NormalClosure}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NormalClosure({\mdseries\slshape G, list})\index{NormalClosure@\texttt{NormalClosure}!for group and a list}
\label{NormalClosure:for group and a list}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 The normal closure of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the smallest normal subgroup of the closure of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}} which contains \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}}. 

 The second argument may also be a list of group elements, in which case the
normal closure of the group generated by these elements is computed. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NormalClosure(g,Subgroup(g,[(1,2,3)])) = Group([ (1,2,3), (2,3,4) ]);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NormalClosure(g,[(1,2,3)]) = Group([ (1,2,3), (2,3,4) ]);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NormalClosure(g,Group((3,4,5))) = Group([ (3,4,5), (1,5,4), (1,2,5) ]);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NormalIntersection}}
\logpage{[ 39, 11, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D25E7DC7834A703}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NormalIntersection({\mdseries\slshape G, U})\index{NormalIntersection@\texttt{NormalIntersection}}
\label{NormalIntersection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 computes the intersection of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}}, assuming that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is normalized by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}}. This works faster than \texttt{Intersection}, but will not produce the intersection if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is not normalized by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NormalIntersection(Group((1,2)(3,4),(1,3)(2,4)),Group((1,2,3,4)));|
  Group([ (1,3)(2,4) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ComplementClassesRepresentatives}}
\logpage{[ 39, 11, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X811B8A4683DDE1F9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ComplementClassesRepresentatives({\mdseries\slshape G, N})\index{ComplementClassesRepresentatives@\texttt{ComplementClassesRepresentatives}}
\label{ComplementClassesRepresentatives}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} be a normal subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. This command returns a set of representatives for the conjugacy classes of
complements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. Complements are subgroups of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} which intersect trivially with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} and together with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} generate \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 

 At the moment methods are available only for the case that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} or \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}\texttt{/}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} is solvable. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ComplementClassesRepresentatives(g,Group((1,2)(3,4),(1,3)(2,4)));|
  [ Group([ (3,4), (2,4,3) ]) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{InfoComplement}}
\logpage{[ 39, 11, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8581F4E77B11C610}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InfoComplement\index{InfoComplement@\texttt{InfoComplement}}
\label{InfoComplement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (info class)}}\\


 Info class for the complement routines. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Specific and Parametrized Subgroups}}\label{Specific and Parametrized Subgroups}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7C39EE3E836D6BC6}{}
{
  The centre of a group (the subgroup of those elements that commute with all
other elements of the group) can be computed by the operation \texttt{Centre} (\ref{Centre}). 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TrivialSubgroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X829759F67D4247CA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TrivialSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{TrivialSubgroup@\texttt{TrivialSubgroup}}
\label{TrivialSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TrivialSubgroup(g);|
  Group(())
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CommutatorSubgroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A9A3D5578CE33A0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CommutatorSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape G, H})\index{CommutatorSubgroup@\texttt{CommutatorSubgroup}}
\label{CommutatorSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape H}} are two groups of elements in the same family, this operation returns the
group generated by all commutators $[ g, h ] = g^{{-1}} h^{{-1}} g h$ (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Comm} (\ref{Comm})) of elements $g \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}$ and $h \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape H}}$, that is the group $\left \langle [ g, h ] \mid g \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, h \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape H}} \right \rangle$. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@CommutatorSubgroup(Group((1,2,3),(1,2)),Group((2,3,4),(3,4)));|
  Group([ (1,4)(2,3), (1,3,4) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(last);|
  12
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DerivedSubgroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7CC17CF179ED7EF2}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DerivedSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{DerivedSubgroup@\texttt{DerivedSubgroup}}
\label{DerivedSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The derived subgroup $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}'$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the subgroup generated by all commutators of pairs of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. It is normal in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} and the factor group $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}/\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}'$ is the largest abelian factor group of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3,4),(1,2));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DerivedSubgroup(g) = Group([ (1,3,2), (2,4,3) ]);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CommutatorLength}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B10B58F83DDE56E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CommutatorLength({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{CommutatorLength@\texttt{CommutatorLength}}
\label{CommutatorLength}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns the minimal number $n$ such that each element in the derived subgroup (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{DerivedSubgroup} (\ref{DerivedSubgroup})) of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} can be written as a product of (at most) $n$ commutators of elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@CommutatorLength( g );|
  1
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FittingSubgroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X780552B57C30DD8F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FittingSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{FittingSubgroup@\texttt{FittingSubgroup}}
\label{FittingSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The Fitting subgroup of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is its largest nilpotent normal subgroup. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FittingSubgroup(g);|
  Group([ (1,2)(3,4), (1,4)(2,3) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FrattiniSubgroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X788C856C82243274}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FrattiniSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{FrattiniSubgroup@\texttt{FrattiniSubgroup}}
\label{FrattiniSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The Frattini subgroup of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the intersection of all maximal subgroups of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FrattiniSubgroup(g);|
  Group(())
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PrefrattiniSubgroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81D86CCE84193E4F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PrefrattiniSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{PrefrattiniSubgroup@\texttt{PrefrattiniSubgroup}}
\label{PrefrattiniSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a Prefrattini subgroup of the finite solvable group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 

 A factor $M/N$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is called a Frattini factor if $M/N$ is contained in the Frattini subgroup of $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}/N$. A subgroup $P$ is a Prefrattini subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} if $P$ covers each Frattini chief factor of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, and if for each maximal subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} there exists a conjugate maximal subgroup, which contains $P$. In a finite solvable group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} the Prefrattini subgroups form a characteristic conjugacy class of subgroups
and the intersection of all these subgroups is the Frattini subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G := SmallGroup( 60, 7 );|
  <pc group of size 60 with 4 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@P := PrefrattiniSubgroup(G);|
  Group([ f2 ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(P);|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsNilpotent(P);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Core(G,P);|
  Group([  ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FrattiniSubgroup(G);|
  Group([  ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PerfectResiduum}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83D5C8B8865C85F1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PerfectResiduum({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{PerfectResiduum@\texttt{PerfectResiduum}}
\label{PerfectResiduum}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the smallest normal subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} that has a solvable factor group. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PerfectResiduum(SymmetricGroup(5));|
  Alt( [ 1 .. 5 ] )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SolvableRadical}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8250D99A830DA832}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SolvableRadical({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{SolvableRadical@\texttt{SolvableRadical}}
\label{SolvableRadical}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the solvable radical of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, i.e., the largest solvable normal subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@rad:= SolvableRadical( SL(2,5) );|
  <group of 2x2 matrices of size 2 over GF(5)>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size( rad );|
  2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Socle}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81F647FA83D8854F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Socle({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{Socle@\texttt{Socle}}
\label{Socle}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The socle of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the subgroup generated by all minimal normal subgroups. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Socle(g);|
  Group([ (1,4)(2,3), (1,2)(3,4) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SupersolvableResiduum}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8440C61080CDAA14}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SupersolvableResiduum({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{SupersolvableResiduum@\texttt{SupersolvableResiduum}}
\label{SupersolvableResiduum}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the supersolvable residuum of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, that is, its smallest normal subgroup $N$ such that the factor group $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} / N$ is supersolvable. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SupersolvableResiduum(g) = Group([ (1,3)(2,4), (1,4)(2,3) ]);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PRump}}
\logpage{[ 39, 12, 12 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X796DA805853FAC90}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PRump({\mdseries\slshape G, p})\index{PRump@\texttt{PRump}}
\label{PRump}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 For a prime $p$, the \emph{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}rump} of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the subgroup $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}' \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}^{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}}$. Unless it equals \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} itself (which is the e.g. the case if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is perfect), it is equal to the second term of the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}central series of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, see \texttt{PCentralSeries} (\ref{PCentralSeries}). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=DicyclicGroup(12);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PRump(g,2) = PCentralSeries(g,2)[2];|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=SymmetricGroup(4);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PRump(g,2) = AlternatingGroup(4);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Sylow Subgroups and Hall Subgroups}}\label{Sylow Subgroups and Hall Subgroups}
\logpage{[ 39, 13, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7FF0BBDD80E8F6BF}{}
{
  With respect to the following \textsf{GAP} functions, please note that by theorems of P.{\nobreakspace}Hall, a group $G$ is solvable if and only if one of the following conditions holds. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item  For each prime $p$ dividing the order of $G$, there exists a $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}complement (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{SylowComplement} (\ref{SylowComplement})). 
\item  For each set $P$ of primes dividing the order of $G$, there exists a $P$\texttt{\symbol{45}}Hall subgroup (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{HallSubgroup} (\ref{HallSubgroup})). 
\item  $G$ has a Sylow system (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{SylowSystem} (\ref{SylowSystem})). 
\item  $G$ has a complement system (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{ComplementSystem} (\ref{ComplementSystem})). 
\end{enumerate}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SylowSubgroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 13, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AA351308787544C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SylowSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape G, p})\index{SylowSubgroup@\texttt{SylowSubgroup}}
\label{SylowSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns a Sylow \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}subgroup of the finite group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. This is a \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} whose index in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is coprime to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}. \texttt{SylowSubgroup} computes Sylow subgroups via the operation \texttt{SylowSubgroupOp}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=SymmetricGroup(4);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SylowSubgroup(g,2);|
  Group([ (1,2), (3,4), (1,3)(2,4) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SylowComplement}}
\logpage{[ 39, 13, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8605F3FE7A3B8E12}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SylowComplement({\mdseries\slshape G, p})\index{SylowComplement@\texttt{SylowComplement}}
\label{SylowComplement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns a Sylow \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}complement of the finite group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. This is a subgroup $U$ of order coprime to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}} such that the index $[\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}:U]$ is a \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}power. 

 At the moment methods exist only if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is solvable and \textsf{GAP} will issue an error if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is not solvable. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SylowComplement(g,3);|
  Group([ (1,2), (3,4), (1,3)(2,4) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{HallSubgroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 13, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EDBA19E828CD584}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{HallSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape G, P})\index{HallSubgroup@\texttt{HallSubgroup}}
\label{HallSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 computes a \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape P}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}Hall subgroup for a set \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape P}} of primes. This is a subgroup the order of which is only divisible by primes
in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape P}} and whose index is coprime to all primes in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape P}}. Such a subgroup is unique up to conjugacy if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is solvable. The function computes Hall subgroups via the operation \texttt{HallSubgroupOp}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is solvable this function always returns a subgroup. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is not solvable this function might return a subgroup (if it is unique up to
conjugacy), a list of subgroups (which are representatives of the conjugacy
classes in case there are several such classes) or \texttt{fail} if no such subgroup exists. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:=SmallGroup(60,10);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@u:=HallSubgroup(h,[2,3]);|
  Group([ f1, f2, f3 ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(u);|
  12
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:=PSL(3,5);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@HallSubgroup(h,[2,3]);|
  [ <permutation group of size 96 with 6 generators>,
    <permutation group of size 96 with 6 generators> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@u := HallSubgroup(h,[3,31]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(u); StructureDescription(u);|
  93
  "C31 : C3"
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@HallSubgroup(h,[5,31]);|
  fail
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SylowSystem}}
\logpage{[ 39, 13, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X832E8E6B8347B13F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SylowSystem({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{SylowSystem@\texttt{SylowSystem}}
\label{SylowSystem}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 A Sylow system of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is a set of Sylow subgroups of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} such that every pair of subgroups from this set commutes as subgroups. Sylow
systems exist only for solvable groups. The operation returns \texttt{fail} if the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is not solvable. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:=SmallGroup(60,10);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SylowSystem(h);|
  [ Group([ f1, f2 ]), Group([ f3 ]), Group([ f4 ]) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List(last,Size);|
  [ 4, 3, 5 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ComplementSystem}}
\logpage{[ 39, 13, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87A245E180D27147}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ComplementSystem({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{ComplementSystem@\texttt{ComplementSystem}}
\label{ComplementSystem}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 A complement system of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is a set of Hall $p'$\texttt{\symbol{45}}subgroups of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, where $p'$ runs through the subsets of prime factors of $|\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}|$ that omit exactly one prime. Every pair of subgroups from this set commutes as
subgroups. Complement systems exist only for solvable groups, therefore \texttt{ComplementSystem} returns \texttt{fail} if the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is not solvable. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ComplementSystem(h);|
  [ Group([ f3, f4 ]), Group([ f1, f2, f4 ]), Group([ f1, f2, f3 ]) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List(last,Size);|
  [ 15, 20, 12 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{HallSystem}}
\logpage{[ 39, 13, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82FE5DFD84F8A3C6}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{HallSystem({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{HallSystem@\texttt{HallSystem}}
\label{HallSystem}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a list containing one Hall $P$\texttt{\symbol{45}}subgroup for each set $P$ of prime divisors of the order of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. Hall systems exist only for solvable groups. The operation returns \texttt{fail} if the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is not solvable. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@HallSystem(h);|
  [ Group([  ]), Group([ f1, f2 ]), Group([ f1, f2, f3 ]),
    Group([ f1, f2, f3, f4 ]), Group([ f1, f2, f4 ]), Group([ f3 ]),
    Group([ f3, f4 ]), Group([ f4 ]) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List(last,Size);|
  [ 1, 4, 12, 60, 20, 3, 15, 5 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

   }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Subgroups characterized by prime powers}}\label{Subgroups characterized by prime powers}
\logpage{[ 39, 14, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X87AF37E980382499}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Omega}}
\logpage{[ 39, 14, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F069ACC83DB3374}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Omega({\mdseries\slshape G, p[, n]})\index{Omega@\texttt{Omega}}
\label{Omega}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 For a \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, one defines $\Omega_{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}) = \langle g \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} \mid g^{{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}^{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}}}} = 1 \rangle$. The default value for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} is \texttt{1}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:=SmallGroup(16,10);|
  <pc group of size 16 with 4 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Omega(h,2);|
  Group([ f2, f3, f4 ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Agemo}}
\logpage{[ 39, 14, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83DB33747F069ACC}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Agemo({\mdseries\slshape G, p[, n]})\index{Agemo@\texttt{Agemo}}
\label{Agemo}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For a \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, one defines $\mho_{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}}(G) = \langle g^{{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}^{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}}}} \mid g \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} \rangle$. The default value for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} is \texttt{1}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Agemo(h,2);Agemo(h,2,2);|
  Group([ f4 ])
  Group([  ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Group Properties}}\label{Group Properties}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7B75879B8085120A}{}
{
  Some properties of groups can be defined not only for groups but also for
other structures. For example, nilpotency and solvability make sense also for
algebras. Note that these names refer to different definitions for groups and
algebras, contrary to the situation with finiteness or commutativity. In such
cases, the name of the function for groups got a suffix \texttt{Group} to distinguish different meanings for different structures. 

 Some functions, such as \texttt{IsPSolvable} (\ref{IsPSolvable}) and \texttt{IsPNilpotent} (\ref{IsPNilpotent}), although they are mathematical properties, are not properties in the sense
of \textsf{GAP} (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Attributes} and \ref{Properties}), as they depend on a parameter. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsCyclic}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DA27D338374FD28}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsCyclic({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsCyclic@\texttt{IsCyclic}}
\label{IsCyclic}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group is \emph{cyclic} if it can be generated by one element. For a cyclic group, one can compute a
generating set consisting of only one element using \texttt{MinimalGeneratingSet} (\ref{MinimalGeneratingSet}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsElementaryAbelian}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X813C952F80E775D4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsElementaryAbelian({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsElementaryAbelian@\texttt{IsElementaryAbelian}}
\label{IsElementaryAbelian}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is elementary abelian if it is commutative and if there is a prime $p$ such that the order of each element in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} divides $p$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsNilpotentGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87D062608719F2CD}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsNilpotentGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsNilpotentGroup@\texttt{IsNilpotentGroup}}
\label{IsNilpotentGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group is \emph{nilpotent} if the lower central series (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup} (\ref{LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup}) for a definition) reaches the trivial subgroup in a finite number of steps. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NilpotencyClassOfGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E3056237C6A5D43}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NilpotencyClassOfGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{NilpotencyClassOfGroup@\texttt{NilpotencyClassOfGroup}}
\label{NilpotencyClassOfGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The nilpotency class of a nilpotent group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the number of steps in the lower central series of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} (see \texttt{LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup} (\ref{LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup})); 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is not nilpotent an error is issued. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPerfectGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8755147280C84DBB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPerfectGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsPerfectGroup@\texttt{IsPerfectGroup}}
\label{IsPerfectGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group is \emph{perfect} if it equals its derived subgroup (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{DerivedSubgroup} (\ref{DerivedSubgroup})). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSolvableGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X809C78D5877D31DF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSolvableGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsSolvableGroup@\texttt{IsSolvableGroup}}
\label{IsSolvableGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group is \emph{solvable} if the derived series (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{DerivedSeriesOfGroup} (\ref{DerivedSeriesOfGroup}) for a definition) reaches the trivial subgroup in a finite number of steps. 

 For finite groups this is the same as being polycyclic (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsPolycyclicGroup} (\ref{IsPolycyclicGroup})), and each polycyclic group is solvable, but there are infinite solvable
groups that are not polycyclic. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPolycyclicGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D7456077D3D1B86}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPolycyclicGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsPolycyclicGroup@\texttt{IsPolycyclicGroup}}
\label{IsPolycyclicGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group is polycyclic if it has a subnormal series with cyclic factors. For
finite groups this is the same as if the group is solvable (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsSolvableGroup} (\ref{IsSolvableGroup})). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSupersolvableGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AADF2E88501B9FF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSupersolvableGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsSupersolvableGroup@\texttt{IsSupersolvableGroup}}
\label{IsSupersolvableGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A finite group is \emph{supersolvable} if it has a normal series with cyclic factors. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsMonomialGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83977EB97A8E2290}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsMonomialGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsMonomialGroup@\texttt{IsMonomialGroup}}
\label{IsMonomialGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A finite group is \emph{monomial} if every irreducible complex character is induced from a linear character of a
subgroup. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSimpleGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A6685D7819AEC32}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSimpleGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsSimpleGroup@\texttt{IsSimpleGroup}}
\label{IsSimpleGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsNonabelianSimpleGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsNonabelianSimpleGroup@\texttt{IsNonabelianSimpleGroup}}
\label{IsNonabelianSimpleGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group is \emph{simple} if it is nontrivial and has no nontrivial normal subgroups. A \emph{nonabelian simple} group is simple and not abelian. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsAlmostSimpleGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78CC9764803601E7}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAlmostSimpleGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsAlmostSimpleGroup@\texttt{IsAlmostSimpleGroup}}
\label{IsAlmostSimpleGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is \emph{almost simple} if a nonabelian simple group $S$ exists such that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is isomorphic to a subgroup of the automorphism group of $S$ that contains all inner automorphisms of $S$. 

 Equivalently, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is almost simple if and only if it has a unique minimal normal subgroup $N$ and if $N$ is a nonabelian simple group. 

  Note that an almost simple group is \emph{not} defined as an extension of a simple group by outer automorphisms, since we
want to exclude extensions of groups of prime order. In particular, a \emph{simple} group is \emph{almost simple} if and only if it is nonabelian. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsAlmostSimpleGroup( AlternatingGroup( 5 ) );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsAlmostSimpleGroup( SymmetricGroup( 5 ) );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsAlmostSimpleGroup( SymmetricGroup( 3 ) );|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsAlmostSimpleGroup( SL( 2, 5 ) );|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsQuasisimpleGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 12 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C1709A986B00F97}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsQuasisimpleGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsQuasisimpleGroup@\texttt{IsQuasisimpleGroup}}
\label{IsQuasisimpleGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is \emph{quasisimple} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is perfect (see \texttt{IsPerfectGroup} (\ref{IsPerfectGroup})) and if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}$/Z($\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}$)$ is simple (see \texttt{IsSimpleGroup} (\ref{IsSimpleGroup})), where $Z($\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}$)$ is the centre of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} (see \texttt{Centre} (\ref{Centre})). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsQuasisimpleGroup( AlternatingGroup( 5 ) );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsQuasisimpleGroup( SymmetricGroup( 5 ) );|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsQuasisimpleGroup( SL( 2, 5 ) );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup}}\logpage{[ 39, 15, 13 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7C6AA6897C4409AC}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup@\texttt{Isomorphism}\-\texttt{Type}\-\texttt{Info}\-\texttt{Finite}\-\texttt{Simple}\-\texttt{Group}!for a group}
\label{IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup:for a group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup({\mdseries\slshape n})\index{IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup@\texttt{Isomorphism}\-\texttt{Type}\-\texttt{Info}\-\texttt{Finite}\-\texttt{Simple}\-\texttt{Group}!for a group order}
\label{IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup:for a group order}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 For a finite simple group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, \texttt{IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup} returns a record with the components \texttt{name}, \texttt{shortname}, \texttt{series}, and possibly \texttt{parameter}, describing the isomorphism type of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 

 The values of the components \texttt{name}, \texttt{shortname}, and \texttt{series} are strings, \texttt{name} gives name(s) for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, \texttt{shortname} gives one name for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} that is compatible with the naming scheme used in the \textsf{GAP} packages \textsf{CTblLib} and \textsf{AtlasRep} (and in the \textsf{Atlas} of Finite Groups{\nobreakspace}\cite{CCN85}), and \texttt{series} describes the following series. 

 (If different characterizations of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} are possible only one is given by \texttt{series} and \texttt{parameter}, while \texttt{name} may give several names.) 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{"A"}}]  Alternating groups, \texttt{parameter} gives the natural degree. 
\item[{\texttt{"L"}}]  Linear groups (Chevalley type $A$), \texttt{parameter} is a list $[ n, q ]$ that indicates $L(n,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"2A"}}]  Twisted Chevalley type ${}^2A$, \texttt{parameter} is a list $[ n, q ]$ that indicates ${}^2A(n,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"B"}}]  Chevalley type $B$, \texttt{parameter} is a list $[n, q ]$ that indicates $B(n,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"2B"}}]  Twisted Chevalley type ${}^2B$, \texttt{parameter} is a value $q$ that indicates ${}^2B(2,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"C"}}]  Chevalley type $C$, \texttt{parameter} is a list $[ n, q ]$ that indicates $C(n,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"D"}}]  Chevalley type $D$, \texttt{parameter} is a list $[ n, q ]$ that indicates $D(n,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"2D"}}]  Twisted Chevalley type ${}^2D$, \texttt{parameter} is a list $[ n, q ]$ that indicates ${}^2D(n,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"3D"}}]  Twisted Chevalley type ${}^3D$, \texttt{parameter} is a value $q$ that indicates ${}^3D(4,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"E"}}]  Exceptional Chevalley type $E$, \texttt{parameter} is a list $[ n, q ]$ that indicates $E_n(q)$. The value of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} is 6, 7, or 8. 
\item[{\texttt{"2E"}}]  Twisted exceptional Chevalley type $E_6$, \texttt{parameter} is a value $q$ that indicates ${}^2E_6(q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"F"}}]  Exceptional Chevalley type $F$, \texttt{parameter} is a value $q$ that indicates $F(4,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"2F"}}]  Twisted exceptional Chevalley type ${}^2F$ (Ree groups), \texttt{parameter} is a value $q$ that indicates ${}^2F(4,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"G"}}]  Exceptional Chevalley type $G$, \texttt{parameter} is a value $q$ that indicates $G(2,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"2G"}}]  Twisted exceptional Chevalley type ${}^2G$ (Ree groups), \texttt{parameter} is a value $q$ that indicates ${}^2G(2,q)$. 
\item[{\texttt{"Spor"}}]  Sporadic simple groups, \texttt{name} gives the name. 
\item[{\texttt{"Z"}}]  Cyclic groups of prime size, \texttt{parameter} gives the size. 
\end{description}
 

 An equal sign in the name denotes different naming schemes for the same group,
a tilde sign abstract isomorphisms between groups constructed in a different
way. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup(|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@                            Group((4,5)(6,7),(1,2,4)(3,5,6)));|
  rec(
    name := "A(1,7) = L(2,7) ~ B(1,7) = O(3,7) ~ C(1,7) = S(2,7) ~ 2A(1,\
  7) = U(2,7) ~ A(2,2) = L(3,2)", parameter := [ 2, 7 ], series := "L",
    shortname := "L3(2)" )
\end{Verbatim}
 

 For a positive integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \texttt{IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup} returns \texttt{fail} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} is not the order of a finite simple group, and a record as described for the
case of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} otherwise. If more than one simple group of order \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} exists then the result record contains only the \texttt{name} component, a string that lists the two possible isomorphism types of simple
groups of this order. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup( 5 );|
  rec( name := "Z(5)", parameter := 5, series := "Z", shortname := "C5"
   )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup( 6 );|
  fail
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup(Size(SymplecticGroup(6,3))/2);|
  rec(
    name := "cannot decide from size alone between B(3,3) = O(7,3) and C\
  (3,3) = S(6,3)", parameter := [ 3, 3 ] )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SimpleGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 14 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8492B05B822AC58C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SimpleGroup({\mdseries\slshape id[, param]})\index{SimpleGroup@\texttt{SimpleGroup}}
\label{SimpleGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 This function will construct \textsc{an} instance of the specified nonabelian simple group. Groups are specified via
their name in ATLAS style notation, with parameters added if necessary. The
intelligence applied to parsing the name is limited, and at the moment no
proper extensions can be constructed. For groups which do not have a
permutation representation of small degree the \textsf{AtlasRep} package might need to be installed to construct these groups. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=SimpleGroup("M(23)");|
  M23
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(g);|
  10200960
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=SimpleGroup("PSL",3,5);|
  PSL(3,5)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(g);|
  372000
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=SimpleGroup("PSp6",2);|
  PSp(6,2)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SimpleGroupsIterator}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 15 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X839CDD8C7AE39FD6}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SimpleGroupsIterator({\mdseries\slshape [start[, end]]})\index{SimpleGroupsIterator@\texttt{SimpleGroupsIterator}}
\label{SimpleGroupsIterator}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 This function returns an iterator that will run over all nonabelian simple
groups, starting at order \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape start}} if specified, up to order $10^{27}$ (or \texttt{\symbol{45}}\texttt{\symbol{45}} if specified
\texttt{\symbol{45}}\texttt{\symbol{45}} order \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape end}}). If the option \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape NOPSL2}} is given, groups of type $PSL_2(q)$ are omitted. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@it:=SimpleGroupsIterator(20000);|
  <iterator>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List([1..8],x->NextIterator(it));|
  [ A8, PSL(3,4), PSL(2,37), PSp(4,3), Sz(8), PSL(2,32), PSL(2,41),
    PSL(2,43) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@it:=SimpleGroupsIterator(1,2000);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@l:=[];;for i in it do Add(l,i);od;l;|
  [ A5, PSL(2,7), A6, PSL(2,8), PSL(2,11), PSL(2,13) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@it:=SimpleGroupsIterator(20000,100000:NOPSL2);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@l:=[];;for i in it do Add(l,i);od;l;|
  [ A8, PSL(3,4), PSp(4,3), Sz(8), PSU(3,4), M12 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SmallSimpleGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 16 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X872E93F586F54FCE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SmallSimpleGroup({\mdseries\slshape order[, i]})\index{SmallSimpleGroup@\texttt{SmallSimpleGroup}}
\label{SmallSimpleGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
 The \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}th simple group of order \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape order}} in the stored list, given in a small\texttt{\symbol{45}}degree permutation
representation, or \texttt{fail} (\ref{fail}) if no such simple group exists. 



 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}} is not given, it defaults to{\nobreakspace}1. Currently, all simple groups of
order less than $10^6$ are available via this function. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SmallSimpleGroup(60);|
  A5
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SmallSimpleGroup(20160,1);|
  A8
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SmallSimpleGroup(20160,2);|
  PSL(3,4)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AllSmallNonabelianSimpleGroups}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 17 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EB47BF27D8CBF72}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AllSmallNonabelianSimpleGroups({\mdseries\slshape orders})\index{AllSmallNonabelianSimpleGroups@\texttt{AllSmallNonabelianSimpleGroups}}
\label{AllSmallNonabelianSimpleGroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
 A list of all nonabelian simple groups whose order lies in the range \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape orders}}. 



 The groups are given in small\texttt{\symbol{45}}degree permutation
representations. The returned list is sorted by ascending group order.
Currently, all simple groups of order less than $10^6$ are available via this function. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List(AllSmallNonabelianSimpleGroups([1..1000000]),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@        StructureDescription);|
  [ "A5", "PSL(3,2)", "A6", "PSL(2,8)", "PSL(2,11)", "PSL(2,13)",
    "PSL(2,17)", "A7", "PSL(2,19)", "PSL(2,16)", "PSL(3,3)",
    "PSU(3,3)", "PSL(2,23)", "PSL(2,25)", "M11", "PSL(2,27)",
    "PSL(2,29)", "PSL(2,31)", "A8", "PSL(3,4)", "PSL(2,37)", "O(5,3)",
    "Sz(8)", "PSL(2,32)", "PSL(2,41)", "PSL(2,43)", "PSL(2,47)",
    "PSL(2,49)", "PSU(3,4)", "PSL(2,53)", "M12", "PSL(2,59)",
    "PSL(2,61)", "PSU(3,5)", "PSL(2,67)", "J1", "PSL(2,71)", "A9",
    "PSL(2,73)", "PSL(2,79)", "PSL(2,64)", "PSL(2,81)", "PSL(2,83)",
    "PSL(2,89)", "PSL(3,5)", "M22", "PSL(2,97)", "PSL(2,101)",
    "PSL(2,103)", "HJ", "PSL(2,107)", "PSL(2,109)", "PSL(2,113)",
    "PSL(2,121)", "PSL(2,125)", "O(5,4)" ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsFinitelyGeneratedGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 18 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81E22D07871DF37E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFinitelyGeneratedGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsFinitelyGeneratedGroup@\texttt{IsFinitelyGeneratedGroup}}
\label{IsFinitelyGeneratedGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 tests whether the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} can be generated by a finite number of generators. (This property is mainly
used to obtain finiteness conditions.) 

 Note that this is a pure existence statement. Even if a group is known to be
generated by a finite number of elements, it can be very hard or even
impossible to obtain such a generating set if it is not known. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSubsetLocallyFiniteGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 19 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8648EDA287829755}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSubsetLocallyFiniteGroup({\mdseries\slshape U})\index{IsSubsetLocallyFiniteGroup@\texttt{IsSubsetLocallyFiniteGroup}}
\label{IsSubsetLocallyFiniteGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group is called locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup is
finite. This property checks whether the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}} is a subset of a locally finite group. This is used to check whether finite
generation will imply finiteness, as it does for example for permutation
groups. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 20 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8089F18C810B7E3E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsPGroup@\texttt{IsPGroup}}
\label{IsPGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 \index{p-group@$p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group} A \emph{$p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group} is a group in which the order (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Order} (\ref{Order})) of every element is of the form $p^n$ for a prime integer $p$ and a nonnegative integer $n$. \texttt{IsPGroup} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is a $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 Finite $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}groups are precisely those groups whose order
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Size} (\ref{Size})) is $1$ or a prime power (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsPrimePowerInt} (\ref{IsPrimePowerInt}), and are always nilpotent. 

 Note that $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}groups can also be infinite, and in that case, need not be
nilpotent. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsPGroup( DihedralGroup( 8 ) );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsPGroup( TrivialGroup() );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsPGroup( DihedralGroup( 10 ) );|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPowerfulPGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 21 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F232B3F8261CE25}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPowerfulPGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsPowerfulPGroup@\texttt{IsPowerfulPGroup}}
\label{IsPowerfulPGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 \index{PowerfulPGroup@Powerful $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group} A finite $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is said to be a \emph{powerful $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group} if the commutator subgroup $[\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}},\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}]$ is contained in $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}^{p}$ if the prime $p$ is odd, or if $[\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}},\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}]$ is contained in $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}^{4}$ if $p = 2$. The subgroup $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}^{p}$ is called the first Agemo subgroup, (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Agemo} (\ref{Agemo})). \texttt{IsPowerfulPGroup} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is a powerful $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group, and \texttt{false} otherwise. \emph{Note: }This function returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the trivial group. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRegularPGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 22 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7ED4A14F7A235617}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRegularPGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsRegularPGroup@\texttt{IsRegularPGroup}}
\label{IsRegularPGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 \index{RegularPGroup@Regular $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group} A finite $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is a \emph{regular $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group} if for all $a,b$ in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, one has $a^p b^p = (a b)^p c^p$ where $c$ is an element of the derived subgroup of the group generated by $a$ and $b$ (see{\nobreakspace}\cite{Hal34}). \texttt{IsRegularPGroup} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is a regular $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group, and \texttt{false} otherwise. \emph{Note: }This function returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the trivial group. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PrimePGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 23 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87356BAA7E9E2142}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PrimePGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{PrimePGroup@\texttt{PrimePGroup}}
\label{PrimePGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is a nontrivial $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsPGroup} (\ref{IsPGroup})), \texttt{PrimePGroup} returns the prime integer $p$; if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is trivial then \texttt{PrimePGroup} returns \texttt{fail}. Otherwise an error is issued. 

 (One should avoid a common error of writing \texttt{if IsPGroup(g) then ... PrimePGroup(g) ...} where the code represented by dots assumes that \texttt{PrimePGroup(g)} is an integer.) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PClassPGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 24 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X863434AD7DDE514B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PClassPGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{PClassPGroup@\texttt{PClassPGroup}}
\label{PClassPGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}class of a $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsPGroup} (\ref{IsPGroup})) is the number of steps in the lower $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}central series (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{PCentralSeries} (\ref{PCentralSeries})) of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is not a $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group then an error is issued. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RankPGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 25 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X840A4F937ABF15E1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RankPGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{RankPGroup@\texttt{RankPGroup}}
\label{RankPGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 For a $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsPGroup} (\ref{IsPGroup})), \texttt{RankPGroup} returns the \emph{rank} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, which is defined as the minimal size of a generating system of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is not a $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group then an error is issued. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:= Group((1,2,3,4), (1,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Length(PCentralSeries(h));|
  3
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PClassPGroup(h);|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RankPGroup(h);|
  2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPSolvable}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 26 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81130F9A7CFCF6BF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPSolvable({\mdseries\slshape G, p})\index{IsPSolvable@\texttt{IsPSolvable}}
\label{IsPSolvable}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 A finite group is $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}solvable if every chief factor either has order not
divisible by $p$, or is solvable. 

 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPNilpotent}}
\logpage{[ 39, 15, 27 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87415A8485FCF510}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPNilpotent({\mdseries\slshape G, p})\index{IsPNilpotent@\texttt{IsPNilpotent}}
\label{IsPNilpotent}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 A group is $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}nilpotent if it possesses a normal $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}complement. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Numerical Group Attributes}}\label{Numerical Group Attributes}
\logpage{[ 39, 16, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7F8264FA796B2B7D}{}
{
  This section gives only some examples of numerical group attributes, so it
should not serve as a collection of all numerical group attributes. The manual
contains more such attributes documented in this manual, for example, \texttt{NrConjugacyClasses} (\ref{NrConjugacyClasses}), \texttt{NilpotencyClassOfGroup} (\ref{NilpotencyClassOfGroup}) and others. 

 Note also that some functions, such as \texttt{EulerianFunction} (\ref{EulerianFunction}), are mathematical attributes, but not \textsf{GAP} attributes (see \ref{Attributes}) as they are depending on a parameter. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AbelianInvariants}}
\logpage{[ 39, 16, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X812827937F403300}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AbelianInvariants({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{AbelianInvariants@\texttt{AbelianInvariants}}
\label{AbelianInvariants}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 \index{AbelianInvariants@\texttt{AbelianInvariants}!for groups} returns the abelian invariants (also sometimes called primary decomposition)
of the commutator factor group of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. These are given as a list of prime\texttt{\symbol{45}}powers or zeroes and
describe the structure of $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}/\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}'$ as a direct product of cyclic groups of prime power (or infinite) order. 

 (See \texttt{IndependentGeneratorsOfAbelianGroup} (\ref{IndependentGeneratorsOfAbelianGroup}) to obtain actual generators). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3,4),(1,2),(5,6));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AbelianInvariants(g);|
  [ 2, 2 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:=FreeGroup(2);;h:=h/[h.1^3];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AbelianInvariants(h);|
  [ 0, 3 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Exponent}}
\logpage{[ 39, 16, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D44470C7DA59C1C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Exponent({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{Exponent@\texttt{Exponent}}
\label{Exponent}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The exponent $e$ of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the lcm of the orders of its elements, that is, $e$ is the smallest integer such that $g^e = 1$ for all $g \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}$. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Exponent(g);|
  12
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EulerianFunction}}
\logpage{[ 39, 16, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X843E0CCA8351FDF4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EulerianFunction({\mdseries\slshape G, n})\index{EulerianFunction@\texttt{EulerianFunction}}
\label{EulerianFunction}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns the number of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}tuples $(g_1, g_2, \ldots, g_n)$ of elements of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} that generate the whole group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. The elements of such an \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}tuple need not be different. 

 In \cite{Hal36}, the notation $\phi_{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}})$ is used for the value returned by \texttt{EulerianFunction}, and the quotient of $\phi_{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}})$ by the order of the automorphism group of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is called $d_{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}})$. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is a nonabelian simple group then $d_{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}}(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}})$ is the greatest number $d$ for which the direct product of $d$ groups isomorphic with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} can be generated by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} elements. 

 If the Library of Tables of Marks (see Chapter \ref{Tables of Marks}) covers the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, you may also use \texttt{EulerianFunctionByTom} (\ref{EulerianFunctionByTom}). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@EulerianFunction( g, 2 );|
  432
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Subgroup Series}}\label{Subgroup Series}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7AEDEDF67CFED672}{}
{
  In group theory many subgroup series are considered, and \textsf{GAP} provides commands to compute them. In the following sections, there is always
a series $G = U_1 > U_2 > \cdots > U_m = \langle 1 \rangle$ of subgroups considered. A series also may stop without reaching $G$ or $\langle 1 \rangle$. 

 A series is called \emph{subnormal} if every $U_{{i+1}}$ is normal in $U_i$. 

 A series is called \emph{normal} if every $U_i$ is normal in $G$. 

 A series of normal subgroups is called \emph{central} if $U_i/U_{{i+1}}$ is central in $G / U_{{i+1}}$. 

 We call a series \emph{refinable} if intermediate subgroups can be added to the series without destroying the
properties of the series. 

 Unless explicitly declared otherwise, all subgroup series are descending. That
is they are stored in decreasing order. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ChiefSeries}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BDD116F7833800F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ChiefSeries({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{ChiefSeries@\texttt{ChiefSeries}}
\label{ChiefSeries}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is a series of normal subgroups of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} which cannot be refined further. That is there is no normal subgroup $N$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} with $U_i > N > U_{{i+1}}$. This attribute returns \emph{one} chief series (of potentially many possibilities). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3,4),(1,2));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ChiefSeries(g);|
  [ Group([ (1,2,3,4), (1,2) ]),
    Group([ (2,4,3), (1,4)(2,3), (1,3)(2,4) ]),
    Group([ (1,4)(2,3), (1,3)(2,4) ]), Group(()) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ChiefSeriesThrough}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AC93E977AC9ED58}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ChiefSeriesThrough({\mdseries\slshape G, l})\index{ChiefSeriesThrough@\texttt{ChiefSeriesThrough}}
\label{ChiefSeriesThrough}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 is a chief series of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} going through the normal subgroups in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape l}}, which must be a list of normal subgroups of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} contained in each other, sorted by descending size. This attribute returns \emph{one} chief series (of potentially many possibilities). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ChiefSeriesUnderAction}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8724E15F81B51173}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ChiefSeriesUnderAction({\mdseries\slshape H, G})\index{ChiefSeriesUnderAction@\texttt{ChiefSeriesUnderAction}}
\label{ChiefSeriesUnderAction}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns a series of normal subgroups of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} which are invariant under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape H}} such that the series cannot be refined any further. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} must be a subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape H}}. This attribute returns \emph{one} such series (of potentially many possibilities). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SubnormalSeries}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A0E7A8B8495B79D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SubnormalSeries({\mdseries\slshape G, U})\index{SubnormalSeries@\texttt{SubnormalSeries}}
\label{SubnormalSeries}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}} is a subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} this operation returns a subnormal series that descends from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} to a subnormal subgroup $V \geq $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}} is subnormal, $V =$ \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@s:=SubnormalSeries(g,Group((1,2)(3,4))) =|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@[ Group([ (1,2,3,4), (1,2) ]),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@  Group([ (1,2)(3,4), (1,3)(2,4) ]),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@  Group([ (1,2)(3,4) ]) ];|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CompositionSeries}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81CDCBD67BC98A5A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CompositionSeries({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{CompositionSeries@\texttt{CompositionSeries}}
\label{CompositionSeries}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CompositionSeriesThrough({\mdseries\slshape G, normals})\index{CompositionSeriesThrough@\texttt{CompositionSeriesThrough}}
\label{CompositionSeriesThrough}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 A composition series is a subnormal series which cannot be refined. This
attribute returns \emph{one} composition series (of potentially many possibilities). The variant \texttt{CompositionSeriesThrough} takes as second argument a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape normals}} of normal subgroups of the group, and returns a composition series that
incorporates these normal subgroups. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DisplayCompositionSeries}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82C0D0217ACB2042}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DisplayCompositionSeries({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{DisplayCompositionSeries@\texttt{DisplayCompositionSeries}}
\label{DisplayCompositionSeries}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Displays a composition series of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} in a nice way, identifying the simple factors. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@B,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>B !gapinput@CompositionSeries(g);B
  [ Group([ (3,4), (2,4,3), (1,4)(2,3), (1,3)(2,4) ]),
    Group([ (2,4,3), (1,4)(2,3), (1,3)(2,4) ]),
    Group([ (1,4)(2,3), (1,3)(2,4) ]), Group([ (1,3)(2,4) ]), Group(())
   ]
  !gapprompt@gap>B !gapinput@DisplayCompositionSeries(Group((1,2,3,4,5,6,7),(1,2)));B
  G (2 gens, size 5040)
   | C2
  S (5 gens, size 2520)
   | A7
  1 (0 gens, size 1)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DerivedSeriesOfGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A879948834BD889}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DerivedSeriesOfGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{DerivedSeriesOfGroup@\texttt{DerivedSeriesOfGroup}}
\label{DerivedSeriesOfGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The derived series of a group is obtained by $U_{{i+1}} = U_i'$. It stops if $U_i$ is perfect. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DerivedLength}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A9AA1577CEC891F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DerivedLength({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{DerivedLength@\texttt{DerivedLength}}
\label{DerivedLength}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The derived length of a group is the number of steps in the derived series.
(As there is always the group, it is the series length minus 1.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List(DerivedSeriesOfGroup(g),Size);|
  [ 24, 12, 4, 1 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DerivedLength(g);|
  3
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ElementaryAbelianSeries}}\logpage{[ 39, 17, 9 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X83F057E5791944D6}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ElementaryAbelianSeries({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{ElementaryAbelianSeries@\texttt{ElementaryAbelianSeries}!for a group}
\label{ElementaryAbelianSeries:for a group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ElementaryAbelianSeriesLargeSteps({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{ElementaryAbelianSeriesLargeSteps@\texttt{ElementaryAbelianSeriesLargeSteps}}
\label{ElementaryAbelianSeriesLargeSteps}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ElementaryAbelianSeries({\mdseries\slshape list})\index{ElementaryAbelianSeries@\texttt{ElementaryAbelianSeries}!for a list}
\label{ElementaryAbelianSeries:for a list}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a series of normal subgroups of $G$ such that all factors are elementary abelian. If the group is not solvable
(and thus no such series exists) it returns \texttt{fail}. 

 The variant \texttt{ElementaryAbelianSeriesLargeSteps} tries to make the steps in this series large (by eliminating intermediate
subgroups if possible) at a small additional cost. 

 In the third variant, an elementary abelian series through the given series of
normal subgroups in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} is constructed. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List(ElementaryAbelianSeries(g),Size);|
  [ 24, 12, 4, 1 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{InvariantElementaryAbelianSeries}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X782BD7A47D6B6503}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InvariantElementaryAbelianSeries({\mdseries\slshape G, morph[, N[, fine]]})\index{InvariantElementaryAbelianSeries@\texttt{InvariantElementaryAbelianSeries}}
\label{InvariantElementaryAbelianSeries}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For a (solvable) group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} and a list of automorphisms \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape morph}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, this command finds a normal series of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} with elementary abelian factors such that every group in this series is
invariant under every automorphism in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape morph}}. 

 If a normal subgroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} which is invariant under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape morph}} is given, this series is chosen to contain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}}. No tests are performed to check the validity of the arguments. 

 The series obtained will be constructed to prefer large steps unless \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fine}} is given as \texttt{true}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3,4),(1,3));|
  Group([ (1,2,3,4), (1,3) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@hom:=GroupHomomorphismByImages(g,g,GeneratorsOfGroup(g),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@[(1,4,3,2),(1,4)(2,3)]);|
  [ (1,2,3,4), (1,3) ] -> [ (1,4,3,2), (1,4)(2,3) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@InvariantElementaryAbelianSeries(g,[hom]);|
  [ Group([ (1,2,3,4), (1,3) ]), Group([ (1,3)(2,4) ]), Group(()) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X879D55A67DB42676}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup@\texttt{LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup}}
\label{LowerCentralSeriesOfGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The lower central series of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is defined as $U_{{i+1}}:= [\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, U_i]$. It is a central series of normal subgroups. The name derives from the fact
that $U_i$ is contained in the $i$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th step subgroup of any central series. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{UpperCentralSeriesOfGroup}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 12 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8428592E8773CD7B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{UpperCentralSeriesOfGroup({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{UpperCentralSeriesOfGroup@\texttt{UpperCentralSeriesOfGroup}}
\label{UpperCentralSeriesOfGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The upper central series of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is defined as an ending series $U_i / U_{{i+1}}:= Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}/U_{{i+1}})$. It is a central series of normal subgroups. The name derives from the fact
that $U_i$ contains every $i$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th step subgroup of a central series. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PCentralSeries}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 13 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7809B7ED792669F3}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PCentralSeries({\mdseries\slshape G, p})\index{PCentralSeries@\texttt{PCentralSeries}}
\label{PCentralSeries}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 The \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}central series of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is defined by $U_1:= \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}$, $U_i:= [\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, U_{{i-1}}] U_{{i-1}}^{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}}$. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=DicyclicGroup(12);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PCentralSeries(g,2);|
  [ <pc group of size 12 with 3 generators>, Group([ y3, y*y3 ]), Group([ y*y3 ]) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=SymmetricGroup(4);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List(PCentralSeries(g,2), StructureDescription);|
  [ "S4", "A4" ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{JenningsSeries}}
\logpage{[ 39, 17, 14 ]}\nobreak
