  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3,4),(1,2));|
  Group([ (1,2,3,4), (1,2) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:=Group((1,2,3),(1,2));|
  Group([ (1,2,3), (1,2) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@quo:=GQuotients(g,h);|
  [ [ (2,4), (1,4,3) ] -> [ (2,3), (1,2,3) ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsomorphicSubgroups}}
\logpage{[ 40, 9, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83B417BE7C508DC4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsomorphicSubgroups({\mdseries\slshape G, H})\index{IsomorphicSubgroups@\texttt{IsomorphicSubgroups}}
\label{IsomorphicSubgroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 computes all monomorphisms from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape H}} into \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} up to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}conjugacy of the image groups. This classifies all \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}classes of subgroups of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} which are isomorphic to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape H}}. 

 With the existing methods, the amount of time needed grows with the size of a
generating system of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. (Thus in particular for $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}groups calculations can be slow.) A main use of \texttt{IsomorphicSubgroups} therefore is to find nonsolvable subgroups (which often can be generated by 2
elements). 

 (To find $p$\texttt{\symbol{45}}subgroups it is often faster to compute the subgroup
lattice of the Sylow subgroup and to use \texttt{IdGroup} (\textbf{smallgrp: IdGroup}) to identify the type of the subgroups.) 

 If the \texttt{findall} option is set to \texttt{false}, the algorithm will stop once one homomorphism has been found (this can be
faster and might be sufficient if not all homomorphisms are needed). 

 \index{embeddings!find all} \index{monomorphisms!find all} 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3,4),(1,2));|
  Group([ (1,2,3,4), (1,2) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:=Group((3,4),(1,2));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@emb:=IsomorphicSubgroups(g,h);|
  [ [ (3,4), (1,2) ] -> [ (1,2), (3,4) ],
    [ (3,4), (1,2) ] -> [ (1,3)(2,4), (1,2)(3,4) ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g1:=PSO(-1,8,2);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Length(IsomorphicSubgroups(g1,PSL(2,7)));|
  3
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Length(IsomorphicSubgroups(g1,PSL(2,7):findall:=false));|
  1
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MorClassLoop}}
\logpage{[ 40, 9, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AABA9A27E30BF2B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MorClassLoop({\mdseries\slshape range, classes, params, action})\index{MorClassLoop@\texttt{MorClassLoop}}
\label{MorClassLoop}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 This function loops over element tuples taken from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape classes}} and checks these for properties such as generating a given group, or
fulfilling relations. This can be used to find small generating sets or all
types of Morphisms. The element tuples are used only up to inner automorphisms
as all images can be obtained easily from them by conjugation while running
through all of them usually would take too long. 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape range}} is a group from which these elements are taken. The classes are given in a
list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape classes}} which is a list of records with the following components. 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{classes}}]  list of conjugacy classes 
\item[{\texttt{representative}}]  One element in the union of these classes 
\item[{\texttt{size}}]  The sum of the sizes of these classes 
\end{description}
 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape params}} is a record containing the following optional components. 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{gens}}]  generators that are to be mapped (for testing morphisms). The length of this
list determines the length of element tuples considered. 
\item[{\texttt{from}}]  a preimage group (that contains \texttt{gens}) 
\item[{\texttt{to}}]  image group (which might be smaller than \texttt{range}) 
\item[{\texttt{free}}]  free generators, a list of the same length than the generators \texttt{gens}. 
\item[{\texttt{rels}}]  some relations that hold among the generators \texttt{gens}. They are given as a list \texttt{[ word, order ]} where \texttt{word} is a word in the free generators \texttt{free}. 
\item[{\texttt{dom}}]  a set of elements on which automorphisms act faithfully (used to do element
tests in partial automorphism groups). 
\item[{\texttt{aut}}]  Subgroup of already known automorphisms. 
\item[{\texttt{condition}}]  A function that will be applied to the homomorphism and must return \texttt{true} for the homomorphism to be accepted. 
\end{description}
 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape action}} is a number whose bit\texttt{\symbol{45}}representation indicates the
requirements which are enforced on the element tuples found, as follows. 
\begin{description}
\item[{1}]  homomorphism 
\item[{2}]  injective 
\item[{4}]  surjective 
\item[{8}]  find all (otherwise stops after the first find) 
\end{description}
 If the search is for homomorphisms, the function returns homomorphisms
obtained by mapping the given generators \texttt{gens} instead of element tuples. 

 The ``Morpheus'' algorithm used to find homomorphisms is described in \cite[Section V.5]{Hulpke96}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Representations for Group Homomorphisms}}\label{Representations for Group Homomorphisms}
\logpage{[ 40, 10, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X81FC3CEF85CED3DC}{}
{
  The different representations of group homomorphisms are used to indicate from
what type of group to what type of group they map and thus determine which
methods are used to compute images and preimages. 

 The information in this section is mainly relevant for implementing new
methods and not for using homomorphisms. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsGroupGeneralMappingByImages}}
\logpage{[ 40, 10, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82B77A5F7F9EDBC7}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsGroupGeneralMappingByImages({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{IsGroupGeneralMappingByImages@\texttt{IsGroupGeneralMappingByImages}}
\label{IsGroupGeneralMappingByImages}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Representation)}}\\


 Representation for mappings from one group to another that are defined by
extending a mapping of group generators homomorphically. Instead of record
components, the attribute \texttt{MappingGeneratorsImages} (\ref{MappingGeneratorsImages}) is used to store generators and their images. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MappingGeneratorsImages}}
\logpage{[ 40, 10, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X863805187A24B5E3}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MappingGeneratorsImages({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{MappingGeneratorsImages@\texttt{MappingGeneratorsImages}}
\label{MappingGeneratorsImages}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 This attribute contains a list of length 2, the first entry being a list of
generators of the source of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape map}} and the second entry a list of their images. This attribute is used, for
example, by \texttt{GroupHomomorphismByImages} (\ref{GroupHomomorphismByImages}) to store generators and images.   }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsGroupGeneralMappingByAsGroupGeneralMappingByImages}}
\logpage{[ 40, 10, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DFBBAB18126B4D9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsGroupGeneralMappingByAsGroupGeneralMappingByImages({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{IsGroupGeneralMappingByAsGroupGeneralMappingByImages@\texttt{IsGroup}\-\texttt{General}\-\texttt{Mapping}\-\texttt{By}\-\texttt{As}\-\texttt{Group}\-\texttt{General}\-\texttt{Mapping}\-\texttt{By}\-\texttt{Images}}
\label{IsGroupGeneralMappingByAsGroupGeneralMappingByImages}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Representation)}}\\


 Representation for mappings that delegate work on a \texttt{GroupHomomorphismByImages} (\ref{GroupHomomorphismByImages}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPreimagesByAsGroupGeneralMappingByImages}}
\logpage{[ 40, 10, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78707DF57C3927EB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPreimagesByAsGroupGeneralMappingByImages({\mdseries\slshape map})\index{IsPreimagesByAsGroupGeneralMappingByImages@\texttt{IsPreimages}\-\texttt{By}\-\texttt{As}\-\texttt{Group}\-\texttt{General}\-\texttt{Mapping}\-\texttt{By}\-\texttt{Images}}
\label{IsPreimagesByAsGroupGeneralMappingByImages}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Representation)}}\\


 Representation for mappings that delegate work for preimages to a mapping
created with \texttt{GroupHomomorphismByImages} (\ref{GroupHomomorphismByImages}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPermGroupGeneralMapping}}

\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Group Actions}}\label{Group Actions}
\logpage{[ 41, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X87115591851FB7F4}{}
{
  \index{group actions} A \emph{group action} is a triple $(G, \Omega, \mu)$, where $G$ is a group, $\Omega$ a set and $\mu \colon \Omega \times G \rightarrow \Omega$ a function that is compatible with the group arithmetic. We call $\Omega$ the \emph{domain} of the action. 

 In \textsf{GAP}, $\Omega$ can be a duplicate\texttt{\symbol{45}}free collection (an object that permits
access to its elements via the $\Omega[n]$ operation, for example a list), it does not need to be sorted
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsSet} (\ref{IsSet})). 

 The acting function $\mu$ is a binary \textsf{GAP} function that returns the image $\mu( x, g )$ for a point $x \in \Omega$ and a group element $g \in G$. 

 In \textsf{GAP}, groups always act from the right, that is $\mu( \mu( x, g ), h ) = \mu( x, gh )$. 

 \textsf{GAP} does not test whether the acting function $\mu$ satisfies the conditions for a group operation but silently assumes that is
does. (If it does not, results are unpredictable.) 

 The first section of this chapter, \ref{About Group Actions}, describes the various ways how operations for group actions can be called. 

 Functions for several commonly used action are already built into \textsf{GAP}. These are listed in section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Basic Actions}. 

 The sections \ref{The Permutation Image of an Action} and \ref{Action of a group on itself} describe homomorphisms and mappings associated to group actions as well as the
permutation group image of an action. 

 The other sections then describe operations to compute orbits, stabilizers, as
well as properties of actions. 

 Finally section{\nobreakspace}\ref{External Sets} describes the concept of ``external sets'' which represent the concept of a \emph{$G$\texttt{\symbol{45}}set} and underly the actions mechanism.  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{About Group Actions}}\label{About Group Actions}
\logpage{[ 41, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X83661AFD7B7BD1D9}{}
{
  \index{group actions!operations syntax} The syntax which is used by the operations for group actions is quite
flexible. For example we can call the operation \texttt{OrbitsDomain} (\ref{OrbitsDomain:for a group and an action domain}) for the orbits of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} on the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} in the following ways: 

 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{OrbitsDomain}$( G, \Omega[, \mu] )$}]  The acting function $\mu$ is optional. If it is not given, the built\texttt{\symbol{45}}in action \texttt{OnPoints} (\ref{OnPoints}) (which defines an action via the caret operator \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{94}}}) is used as a default. 
\item[{\texttt{OrbitsDomain}$( G, \Omega, gens, acts[, \mu] )$}]  This second version of \texttt{OrbitsDomain} (\ref{OrbitsDomain:for a group and an action domain}) permits one to implement an action induced by a homomorphism: If the group $H$ acts on $\Omega$ via $\mu$ and $\varphi \colon G \rightarrow H$ is a homomorphism, $G$ acts on $\Omega$ via the induced action $\mu'( x, g ) = \mu( x, g^{\varphi} )$. 

 Here $gens$ must be a set of generators of $G$ and $acts$ the images of $gens$ under $\varphi$. $\mu$ is the acting function for $H$. Again, the function $\mu$ is optional and \texttt{OnPoints} (\ref{OnPoints}) is used as a default. 

 The advantage of this notation is that \textsf{GAP} does not need to construct this homomorphism $\varphi$ and the range group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape H}} as \textsf{GAP} objects. (If a small group $G$ acts via complicated objects $acts$ this otherwise could lead to performance problems.) 

 \textsf{GAP} does not test whether the mapping $gens \mapsto acts$ actually induces a homomorphism and the results are unpredictable if this is
not the case. 
\item[{\texttt{OrbitsDomain}$( xset )$}]  A third variant is to call the operation with an external set, which then
provides $G$, $\Omega$ and $\mu$. You will find more about external sets in Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{External Sets}. 
\end{description}
 

 For operations like \texttt{Stabilizer} (\ref{Stabilizer}) of course the domain must be replaced by an element of the domain of the
action. }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Basic Actions}}\label{Basic Actions}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X81B8F9CD868CD953}{}
{
  \index{group actions} \index{actions} \index{group operations} \textsf{GAP} already provides acting functions for the more common actions of a group. For
built\texttt{\symbol{45}}in operations such as \texttt{Stabilizer} (\ref{Stabilizer}) special methods are available for many of these actions. 

 If one needs an action for which no acting function is provided by the library
it can be implemented via a \textsf{GAP} function that conforms to the syntax 

 \texttt{actfun( omega, g )} 

 where \texttt{omega} is an element of the action domain, \texttt{g} is an element of the acting group, and the return value is the image of \texttt{omega} under \texttt{g}. 

 For example one could define the following function that acts on pairs of
polynomials via \texttt{OnIndeterminates} (\ref{OnIndeterminates:as a permutation action}): 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  OnIndeterminatesPairs:= function( polypair, g )
    return [ OnIndeterminates( polypair[1], g ),
             OnIndeterminates( polypair[2], g ) ];
  end;
\end{Verbatim}
 

 Note that this function \emph{must} implement a group action from the \emph{right}. This is not verified by \textsf{GAP} and results are unpredictable otherwise. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnPoints}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7FE417DD837987B4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnPoints({\mdseries\slshape pnt, g})\index{OnPoints@\texttt{OnPoints}}
\label{OnPoints}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \index{conjugation} \index{action!by conjugation} returns \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} \texttt{\symbol{94}} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}}. This is for example the action of a permutation group on points, or the
action of a group on its elements via conjugation, that is, if both \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} are elements from a common group then \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} \texttt{\symbol{94}} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}} is equal to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}$^{{-1}}$\texttt{*}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}}\texttt{*}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}. The action of a matrix group on vectors from the right is described by both \texttt{OnPoints} and \texttt{OnRight} (\ref{OnRight}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnPoints( 1, (1,2,3) );|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnPoints( (1,2), (1,2,3) );|
  (2,3)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:= Group( (1,2,3), (2,3,4) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit( g, 1, OnPoints );|
  [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnRight}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7960924D84B5B18F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnRight({\mdseries\slshape pnt, g})\index{OnRight@\texttt{OnRight}}
\label{OnRight}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} * \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}}. This is for example the action of a group on its elements via right
multiplication, or the action of a group on the cosets of a subgroup. The
action of a matrix group on vectors from the right is described by both \texttt{OnPoints} (\ref{OnPoints}) and \texttt{OnRight}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnRight( [ 1, 2 ], [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ] );|
  [ 7, 10 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnRight( (1,2,3), (2,3,4) );|
  (1,3)(2,4)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:= Group( (1,2,3), (2,3,4) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit( g, (), OnRight );|
  [ (), (1,2,3), (2,3,4), (1,3,2), (1,3)(2,4), (1,2)(3,4), (2,4,3),
    (1,4,2), (1,4,3), (1,3,4), (1,2,4), (1,4)(2,3) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnLeftInverse}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X832DF5327ECA0E44}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnLeftInverse({\mdseries\slshape pnt, g})\index{OnLeftInverse@\texttt{OnLeftInverse}}
\label{OnLeftInverse}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}^{{-1}}$ \texttt{* \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}}}. Forming the inverse is necessary to make this a proper action, as in \textsf{GAP} groups always act from the right. 

 \texttt{OnLeftInverse} is used for example in the representation of a right coset as an external set
(see{\nobreakspace}\ref{External Sets}), that is, a right coset $Ug$ is an external set for the group $U$ acting on it via \texttt{OnLeftInverse}.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnLeftInverse( [ 1, 2 ], [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ] );|
  [ 0, 1/2 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnLeftInverse( (1,2,3), (2,3,4) );|
  (1,2,4)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:= Group( (1,2,3), (2,3,4) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit( g, (), OnLeftInverse );|
  [ (), (1,3,2), (2,4,3), (1,2,3), (1,3)(2,4), (1,2)(3,4), (2,3,4),
    (1,2,4), (1,3,4), (1,4,3), (1,4,2), (1,4)(2,3) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnSets}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85AA04347CD117F9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnSets({\mdseries\slshape set, g})\index{OnSets@\texttt{OnSets}}
\label{OnSets}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \index{action!on sets} \index{action!on blocks} Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape set}} be a proper set (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Sorted Lists and Sets}). \texttt{OnSets} returns the proper set formed by the images of all points $x$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape set}} via the action function \texttt{OnPoints} (\ref{OnPoints}), applied to $x$ and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}. 

 \texttt{OnSets} is for example used to compute the action of a permutation group on blocks. 

 (\texttt{OnTuples} (\ref{OnTuples}) is an action on lists that preserves the ordering of entries.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnSets( [ 1, 3 ], (1,2,3) );|
  [ 1, 2 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnSets( [ (2,3), (1,2) ], (1,2,3) );|
  [ (2,3), (1,3) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:= Group( (1,2,3), (2,3,4) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit( g, [ 1, 2 ], OnSets );|
  [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 2, 3 ], [ 1, 3 ], [ 3, 4 ], [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 4 ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnTuples}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X832CC5F87EEA4A7E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnTuples({\mdseries\slshape tup, g})\index{OnTuples@\texttt{OnTuples}}
\label{OnTuples}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape tup}} be a list. \texttt{OnTuples} returns the list formed by the images of all points $x$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape tup}} via the action function \texttt{OnPoints} (\ref{OnPoints}), applied to $x$ and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}. 

 (\texttt{OnSets} (\ref{OnSets}) is an action on lists that additionally sorts the entries of the result.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnTuples( [ 1, 3 ], (1,2,3) );|
  [ 2, 1 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnTuples( [ (2,3), (1,2) ], (1,2,3) );|
  [ (1,3), (2,3) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:= Group( (1,2,3), (2,3,4) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit( g, [ 1, 2 ], OnTuples );|
  [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 2, 3 ], [ 1, 3 ], [ 3, 1 ], [ 3, 4 ], [ 2, 1 ],
    [ 1, 4 ], [ 4, 1 ], [ 4, 2 ], [ 3, 2 ], [ 2, 4 ], [ 4, 3 ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnPairs}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80DAA1D2855B1456}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnPairs({\mdseries\slshape tup, g})\index{OnPairs@\texttt{OnPairs}}
\label{OnPairs}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 is a special case of \texttt{OnTuples} (\ref{OnTuples}) for lists \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape tup}} of length 2. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnSetsSets}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C10492081D72376}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnSetsSets({\mdseries\slshape set, g})\index{OnSetsSets@\texttt{OnSetsSets}}
\label{OnSetsSets}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 implements the action on sets of sets. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape set}} must be a proper set whose entries are again proper sets (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Sorted Lists and Sets}). 

 \texttt{OnSetsSets} returns the proper set whose elements are the images obtained by applying the
action function \texttt{OnSets} (\ref{OnSets}) to $x$ and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}, for each element $x$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape set}}. 

 For the special case that the elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape set}} are pairwise disjoint, it is possible to use \texttt{OnSetsDisjointSets} (\ref{OnSetsDisjointSets}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnSetsSets( [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], (1,2,3) );|
  [ [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 3 ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:= Group( (1,2,3), (2,3,4) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit( g, [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], OnSetsSets );|
  [ [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], [ [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 3 ] ],
    [ [ 1, 3 ], [ 2, 4 ] ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnSetsDisjointSets}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E23686E7A9D3A20}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnSetsDisjointSets({\mdseries\slshape set, g})\index{OnSetsDisjointSets@\texttt{OnSetsDisjointSets}}
\label{OnSetsDisjointSets}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 implements the action on sets of pairwise disjoint sets (see
also{\nobreakspace}\texttt{OnSetsSets} (\ref{OnSetsSets})). \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape set}} must be a proper set whose entries are pairwise disjoint proper sets. However,
it is \emph{not} checked that the entries of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape set}} are indeed pairwise disjoint. 

 \texttt{OnSetsDisjointSets} returns the proper set whose elements are the images obtained by applying the
action function \texttt{OnSets} (\ref{OnSets}) to $x$ and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}, for each element $x$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape set}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnSetsTuples}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7ADE244E819035FF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnSetsTuples({\mdseries\slshape set, g})\index{OnSetsTuples@\texttt{OnSetsTuples}}
\label{OnSetsTuples}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 implements the action on sets of tuples. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape set}} must be a proper set of lists without holes (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Sorted Lists and Sets}). 

 \texttt{OnSetsTuples} returns the proper set whose elements are the images obtained by applying the
action function \texttt{OnTuples} (\ref{OnTuples}) to $x$ and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}, for each element $x$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape set}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnSetsTuples( [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], (1,2,3) );|
  [ [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 3 ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:= Group( (1,2,3), (2,3,4) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit( g, [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], OnSetsTuples );|
  [ [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], [ [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 3 ] ],
    [ [ 1, 3 ], [ 4, 2 ] ], [ [ 2, 4 ], [ 3, 1 ] ],
    [ [ 2, 1 ], [ 4, 3 ] ], [ [ 3, 2 ], [ 4, 1 ] ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnTuplesSets}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7FF556CD7E6739A9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnTuplesSets({\mdseries\slshape tup, g})\index{OnTuplesSets@\texttt{OnTuplesSets}}
\label{OnTuplesSets}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 implements the action on tuples of sets. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape tup}} must be a list without holes whose entries are proper sets (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Sorted Lists and Sets}). 

 \texttt{OnTuplesSets} returns the list of the corresponding images obtained by applying the action
function \texttt{OnSets} (\ref{OnSets}) to $x$ and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}, for each entry $x$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape tup}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnTuplesSets( [ [ 2, 3 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], (1,2,3) );|
  [ [ 1, 3 ], [ 1, 4 ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:= Group( (1,2,3), (2,3,4) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit( g, [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], OnTuplesSets );|
  [ [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], [ [ 2, 3 ], [ 1, 4 ] ],
    [ [ 1, 3 ], [ 2, 4 ] ], [ [ 3, 4 ], [ 1, 2 ] ],
    [ [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 3 ] ], [ [ 2, 4 ], [ 1, 3 ] ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnTuplesTuples}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X844E902382EB4151}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnTuplesTuples({\mdseries\slshape tup, g})\index{OnTuplesTuples@\texttt{OnTuplesTuples}}
\label{OnTuplesTuples}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 implements the action on tuples of tuples. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape tup}} must be a list without holes whose entries are again lists without holes. 

 \texttt{OnTuplesTuples} returns the list of the corresponding images obtained by applying the action
function \texttt{OnTuples} (\ref{OnTuples}) to $x$ and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}, for each entry $x$ of the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape tup}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnTuplesTuples( [ [ 2, 3 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], (1,2,3) );|
  [ [ 3, 1 ], [ 1, 4 ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3),(2,3,4));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit(g,[[1,2],[3,4]],OnTuplesTuples);|
  [ [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ], [ [ 2, 3 ], [ 1, 4 ] ],
    [ [ 1, 3 ], [ 4, 2 ] ], [ [ 3, 1 ], [ 2, 4 ] ],
    [ [ 3, 4 ], [ 1, 2 ] ], [ [ 2, 1 ], [ 4, 3 ] ],
    [ [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 3 ] ], [ [ 4, 1 ], [ 3, 2 ] ],
    [ [ 4, 2 ], [ 1, 3 ] ], [ [ 3, 2 ], [ 4, 1 ] ],
    [ [ 2, 4 ], [ 3, 1 ] ], [ [ 4, 3 ], [ 2, 1 ] ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnLines}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 12 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86DC2DD5829CAD9A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnLines({\mdseries\slshape vec, g})\index{OnLines@\texttt{OnLines}}
\label{OnLines}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape vec}} be a \emph{normed} row vector, that is, its first nonzero entry is normed to the identity of the
relevant field, see \texttt{NormedRowVector} (\ref{NormedRowVector}). The function \texttt{OnLines} returns the row vector obtained from first multiplying \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape vec}} from the right with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} (via \texttt{OnRight} (\ref{OnRight})) and then normalizing the resulting row vector by scalar multiplication from
the left. 

 This action corresponds to the projective action of a matrix group on
one\texttt{\symbol{45}}dimensional subspaces. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape vec}} is a zero vector or is not normed then an error is triggered
(see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Action on canonical representatives}). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnLines( [ 1, 2 ], [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3, 4 ] ] );|
  [ 1, 10/7 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@gl:=GL(2,5);;v:=[1,0]*Z(5)^0;|
  [ Z(5)^0, 0*Z(5) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:=Action(gl,Orbit(gl,v,OnLines),OnLines);|
  Group([ (2,3,5,6), (1,2,4)(3,6,5) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnIndeterminates (as a permutation action)}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 13 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7FA394D27E721E2B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnIndeterminates({\mdseries\slshape poly, perm})\index{OnIndeterminates@\texttt{OnIndeterminates}!as a permutation action}
\label{OnIndeterminates:as a permutation action}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 A permutation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape perm}} acts on the multivariate polynomial \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape poly}} by permuting the indeterminates as it permutes points. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x:=Indeterminate(Rationals,1);; y:=Indeterminate(Rationals,2);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OnIndeterminates(x^7*y+x*y^4,(1,17)(2,28));|
  x_17^7*x_28+x_17*x_28^4
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Stabilizer(Group((1,2,3,4),(1,2)),x*y,OnIndeterminates);|
  Group([ (1,2), (3,4) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Permuted (as a permutation action)}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 14 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BA8D76586F1F06E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Permuted({\mdseries\slshape list, perm})\index{Permuted@\texttt{Permuted}!as a permutation action}
\label{Permuted:as a permutation action}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\


 The following example demonstrates \texttt{Permuted} (\ref{Permuted}) being used to implement a permutation action on a domain: 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3),(1,2));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@dom:=[ "a", "b", "c" ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit(g,dom,Permuted);|
  [ [ "a", "b", "c" ], [ "c", "a", "b" ], [ "b", "a", "c" ],
    [ "b", "c", "a" ], [ "a", "c", "b" ], [ "c", "b", "a" ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OnSubspacesByCanonicalBasis}}
\logpage{[ 41, 2, 15 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85124D197F0F9C4D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnSubspacesByCanonicalBasis({\mdseries\slshape bas, mat})\index{OnSubspacesByCanonicalBasis@\texttt{OnSubspacesByCanonicalBasis}}
\label{OnSubspacesByCanonicalBasis}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OnSubspacesByCanonicalBasisConcatenations({\mdseries\slshape basvec, mat})\index{OnSubspacesByCanonicalBasisConcatenations@\texttt{OnSubspaces}\-\texttt{By}\-\texttt{Canonical}\-\texttt{Basis}\-\texttt{Concatenations}}
\label{OnSubspacesByCanonicalBasisConcatenations}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 implements the operation of a matrix group on subspaces of a vector space. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape bas}} must be a list of (linearly independent) vectors which forms a basis of the
subspace in Hermite normal form. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mat}} is an element of the acting matrix group. The function returns a mutable
matrix which gives the basis of the image of the subspace in Hermite normal
form. (In other words: it triangulizes the product of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape bas}} with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mat}}.) 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape bas}} must be given in Hermite normal form, otherwise an error is triggered
(see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Action on canonical representatives}). }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Action on canonical representatives}}\label{Action on canonical representatives}
\logpage{[ 41, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X82181CA07A5B2056}{}
{
  A variety of action functions assumes that the objects on which it acts are
given in a particular form, for example canonical representatives. Affected
actions are for example \texttt{OnSetsSets} (\ref{OnSetsSets}), \texttt{OnSetsDisjointSets} (\ref{OnSetsDisjointSets}), \texttt{OnSetsTuples} (\ref{OnSetsTuples}), \texttt{OnTuplesSets} (\ref{OnTuplesSets}), \texttt{OnLines} (\ref{OnLines}) and \texttt{OnSubspacesByCanonicalBasis} (\ref{OnSubspacesByCanonicalBasis}). 

 If orbit seeds or domain elements are not given in the required form \textsf{GAP} will issue an error message: 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit(SymmetricGroup(5),[[2,4],[1,3]],OnSetsSets);|
  Error, Action not well-defined. See the manual section
  ``Action on canonical representatives''.
\end{Verbatim}
 In this case the affected domain elements have to be brought in canonical
form, as documented for the respective action function. For interactive use
this is most easily done by acting with the identity element of the group. 

 (A similar error could arise if a user\texttt{\symbol{45}}defined action
function is used which actually does not implement an action from the right.) }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Orbits}}\label{Orbits}
\logpage{[ 41, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X81E0FF0587C54543}{}
{
  If a group $G$ acts on a set $\Omega$, the set of all images of $x \in \Omega$ under elements of $G$ is called the \emph{orbit} of $x$. The set of orbits of $G$ is a partition of $\Omega$. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Orbit}}
\logpage{[ 41, 4, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80E0234E7BD79409}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Orbit({\mdseries\slshape G[, Omega], pnt[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{Orbit@\texttt{Orbit}}
\label{Orbit}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 The orbit of the point \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} is the list of all images of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} under the action of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} w.r.t. the action function \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape act}} or \texttt{OnPoints} (\ref{OnPoints}) if no action function is given. 

 (Note that the arrangement of points in this list is not defined by the
operation.) 

 The orbit of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} will always contain one element that is \emph{equal} to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}}, however for performance reasons this element is not necessarily \emph{identical} to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}}, in particular if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} is mutable. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,3,2),(2,4,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit(g,1);|
  [ 1, 3, 2, 4 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbit(g,[1,2],OnSets);|
  [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 1, 3 ], [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 3 ], [ 3, 4 ], [ 2, 4 ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

 (See Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Basic Actions} for information about specific actions.) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Orbits (operation)}}
\logpage{[ 41, 4, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86BCAE17869BBEAA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Orbits({\mdseries\slshape G, seeds[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{Orbits@\texttt{Orbits}!operation}
\label{Orbits:operation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Orbits({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{Orbits@\texttt{Orbits}!for a permutation group}
\label{Orbits:for a permutation group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Orbits({\mdseries\slshape xset})\index{Orbits@\texttt{Orbits}!attribute}
\label{Orbits:attribute}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a duplicate\texttt{\symbol{45}}free list of the orbits of the elements
in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape seeds}} under the action \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape act}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} or under \texttt{OnPoints} (\ref{OnPoints}) if no action function is given. 

 For a permutation group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, one may also invoke this as \texttt{Orbits(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}})}, which returns all the orbits of its natural action on the set of points
moved by it. For example the group $\langle (1,2,3), (4,5) \rangle$ has the orbits $\{1,2,3\}$ and $\{4,5\}$. 

 (Note that the arrangement of orbits or of points within one orbit is not
defined by the operation.) }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OrbitsDomain}}\logpage{[ 41, 4, 3 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X86BC8B958123F953}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitsDomain({\mdseries\slshape G, Omega[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{OrbitsDomain@\texttt{OrbitsDomain}!for a group and an action domain}
\label{OrbitsDomain:for a group and an action domain}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitsDomain({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{OrbitsDomain@\texttt{OrbitsDomain}!for a permutation group}
\label{OrbitsDomain:for a permutation group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitsDomain({\mdseries\slshape xset})\index{OrbitsDomain@\texttt{OrbitsDomain}!of an external set}
\label{OrbitsDomain:of an external set}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a list of the orbits of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} on the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} (given as lists) under the action \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape act}} or under \texttt{OnPoints} (\ref{OnPoints}) if no action function is given. 

 This operation is often faster than \texttt{Orbits} (\ref{Orbits:operation}). The domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} must be closed under the action of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, otherwise an error can occur. 

 For a permutation group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, one may also invoke this as \texttt{OrbitsDomain(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}})}, which returns all the orbits of its natural action on the set of points
moved by it. 

 (Note that the arrangement of orbits or of points within one orbit is not
defined by the operation.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,3,2),(2,4,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Orbits(g,[1..5]);|
  [ [ 1, 3, 2, 4 ], [ 5 ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OrbitsDomain(g,Arrangements([1..4],3),OnTuples);|
  [ [ [ 1, 2, 3 ], [ 3, 1, 2 ], [ 1, 4, 2 ], [ 2, 3, 1 ], [ 2, 1, 4 ],
        [ 3, 4, 1 ], [ 1, 3, 4 ], [ 4, 2, 1 ], [ 4, 1, 3 ],
        [ 2, 4, 3 ], [ 3, 2, 4 ], [ 4, 3, 2 ] ],
    [ [ 1, 2, 4 ], [ 3, 1, 4 ], [ 1, 4, 3 ], [ 2, 3, 4 ], [ 2, 1, 3 ],
        [ 3, 4, 2 ], [ 1, 3, 2 ], [ 4, 2, 3 ], [ 4, 1, 2 ],
        [ 2, 4, 1 ], [ 3, 2, 1 ], [ 4, 3, 1 ] ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OrbitsDomain(g,GF(2)^2,[(1,2,3),(1,4)(2,3)],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@[[[Z(2)^0,Z(2)^0],[Z(2)^0,0*Z(2)]],[[Z(2)^0,0*Z(2)],[0*Z(2),Z(2)^0]]]);|
  [ [ <an immutable GF2 vector of length 2> ],
    [ <an immutable GF2 vector of length 2>,
        <an immutable GF2 vector of length 2>,
        <an immutable GF2 vector of length 2> ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

 (See Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Basic Actions} for information about specific actions.) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OrbitLength}}
\logpage{[ 41, 4, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X799910CF832EDC45}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitLength({\mdseries\slshape G[, Omega], pnt[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{OrbitLength@\texttt{OrbitLength}}
\label{OrbitLength}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 computes the length of the orbit of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} under the action function \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape act}} or \texttt{OnPoints} (\ref{OnPoints}) if no action function is given. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OrbitLengths}}\logpage{[ 41, 4, 5 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8032F73078DF2DDB}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitLengths({\mdseries\slshape G, seeds[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{OrbitLengths@\texttt{OrbitLengths}!for a group, a set of seeds, etc.}
\label{OrbitLengths:for a group, a set of seeds, etc.}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitLengths({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{OrbitLengths@\texttt{OrbitLengths}!for a permutation group}
\label{OrbitLengths:for a permutation group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitLengths({\mdseries\slshape xset})\index{OrbitLengths@\texttt{OrbitLengths}!for an external set}
\label{OrbitLengths:for an external set}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 computes the lengths of all the orbits of the elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape seeds}} under the action \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape act}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 

 For a permutation group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, one may also invoke this as \texttt{OrbitLengths(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}})}, which returns the lengths of all the orbits of its natural action on the set
of points moved by it. For example the group $\langle (1,2,3), (5,6) \rangle$ has the orbit lengths 2 and 3. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OrbitLengthsDomain}}\logpage{[ 41, 4, 6 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8520E2487F7E98AF}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitLengthsDomain({\mdseries\slshape G, Omega[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{OrbitLengthsDomain@\texttt{OrbitLengthsDomain}!for a group and a set of seeds}
\label{OrbitLengthsDomain:for a group and a set of seeds}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitLengthsDomain({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{OrbitLengthsDomain@\texttt{OrbitLengthsDomain}!for a permutation group}
\label{OrbitLengthsDomain:for a permutation group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitLengthsDomain({\mdseries\slshape xset})\index{OrbitLengthsDomain@\texttt{OrbitLengthsDomain}!of an external set}
\label{OrbitLengthsDomain:of an external set}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 computes the lengths of all the orbits of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}}. 

 This operation is often faster than \texttt{OrbitLengths} (\ref{OrbitLengths:for a group, a set of seeds, etc.}). The domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} must be closed under the action of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, otherwise an error can occur. 

 For a permutation group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, one may also invoke this as \texttt{OrbitLengthsDomain(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}})}, which returns the length of all the orbits of its natural action on the set
of points moved by it. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,3,2),(2,4,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OrbitLength(g,[1,2,3,4],OnTuples);|
  12
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OrbitLengths(g,Arrangements([1..4],4),OnTuples);|
  [ 12, 12 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3),(5,6,7));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OrbitLengthsDomain(g,[1,2,3]);|
  [ 3 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OrbitLengthsDomain(g);|
  [ 3, 3 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Stabilizers}}\label{Stabilizers}
\logpage{[ 41, 5, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X797BD60E7ACEF1B1}{}
{
  \index{point stabilizer}\index{set stabilizer} \index{tuple stabilizer} The \emph{stabilizer} of a point $x$ under the action of a group $G$ is the set of all those elements in $G$ which fix $x$. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OrbitStabilizer}}
\logpage{[ 41, 5, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C34EC437EF598BF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitStabilizer({\mdseries\slshape G[, Omega], pnt[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{OrbitStabilizer@\texttt{OrbitStabilizer}}
\label{OrbitStabilizer}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 computes the orbit and the stabilizer of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} simultaneously in a single orbit\texttt{\symbol{45}}stabilizer algorithm.
Returns an immutable record with components \texttt{orbit} (the orbit as a list) and \texttt{stabilizer} (the point stabilizer, a subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}). 

 The stabilizer will have \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} as its parent. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,3,2),(2,4,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@orbstab:=OrbitStabilizer(g,[1,2],OnSets);|
  rec(
    orbit := [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 1, 3 ], [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 3 ], [ 3, 4 ],
        [ 2, 4 ] ], stabilizer := Group([ (1,2)(3,4) ]) )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@orbstab.orbit;|
  [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 1, 3 ], [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 3 ], [ 3, 4 ], [ 2, 4 ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@orbstab.stabilizer;|
  Group([ (1,2)(3,4) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Stabilizer}}
\logpage{[ 41, 5, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86FB962786397E02}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Stabilizer({\mdseries\slshape G[, Omega], pnt[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{Stabilizer@\texttt{Stabilizer}}
\label{Stabilizer}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 computes the stabilizer in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} of the point \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}}, that is the subgroup of those elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} that fix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}}. The stabilizer will have \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} as its parent. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,3,2),(2,4,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@stab:=Stabilizer(g,4);|
  Group([ (1,3,2) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Parent(stab);|
  Group([ (1,3,2), (2,4,3) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 

 The stabilizer of a set or tuple of points can be computed by specifying an
action of sets or tuples of points. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Stabilizer(g,[1,2],OnSets);|
  Group([ (1,2)(3,4) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Stabilizer(g,[1,2],OnTuples);|
  Group(())
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@orbstab:=OrbitStabilizer(g,[1,2],OnSets);|
  rec(
    orbit := [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 1, 3 ], [ 1, 4 ], [ 2, 3 ], [ 3, 4 ],
        [ 2, 4 ] ], stabilizer := Group([ (1,2)(3,4) ]) )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Parent(orbstab.stabilizer);|
  Group([ (1,3,2), (2,4,3) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 

 (See Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Basic Actions} for information about specific actions.) 

 The standard methods for all these actions are an
orbit\texttt{\symbol{45}}stabilizer algorithm. For permutation groups
backtrack algorithms are used. For solvable groups an
orbit\texttt{\symbol{45}}stabilizer algorithm for solvable groups, which uses
the fact that the orbits of a normal subgroup form a block system (see \cite{SOGOS}) is used. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{OrbitStabilizerAlgorithm}}
\logpage{[ 41, 5, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78C3A8568414BC44}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{OrbitStabilizerAlgorithm({\mdseries\slshape G, Omega, blist, gens, acts, pntact})\index{OrbitStabilizerAlgorithm@\texttt{OrbitStabilizerAlgorithm}}
\label{OrbitStabilizerAlgorithm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 This operation should not be called by a user. It is documented however for
purposes to extend or maintain the group actions package (the word ``package'' here refers to the \textsf{GAP} functionality for group actions, not to a \textsf{GAP} package). 

 \texttt{OrbitStabilizerAlgorithm} performs an orbit stabilizer algorithm for the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} acting with the generators \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} via the generator images \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} and the group action \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape act}} on the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}}. (For technical reasons \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape act}} are put in one record with components \texttt{pnt} and \texttt{act} respectively.) 

 The \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pntact}} record may carry a component \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape stabsub}}. If given, this must be a subgroup stabilizing \emph{all} points in the domain and can be used to abbreviate stabilizer calculations. 

 The \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pntact}} component also may contain the boolean entry \texttt{onlystab} set to \texttt{true}. In this case the \texttt{orbit} component may be omitted from the result. 

 The argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} (which may be replaced by \texttt{false} to be ignored) is the set within which the orbit is computed (once the orbit
is the full domain, the orbit calculation may stop). If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape blist}} is given it must be a bit list corresponding to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} in which elements which have been found already will be ``ticked off'' with \texttt{true}. (In particular, the entries for the orbit of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} still must be all set to \texttt{false}). Again the remaining action domain (the bits set initially to \texttt{false}) can be used to stop if the orbit cannot grow any longer. Another use of the
bit list is if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} is an enumerator which can determine \texttt{PositionCanonical} (\ref{PositionCanonical}) values very quickly. In this situation it can be worth to search images not in
the orbit found so far, but via their position in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} and use a the bit list to keep track whether the element is in the orbit found
so far. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Elements with Prescribed Images}}\label{Elements with Prescribed Images}
\logpage{[ 41, 6, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7A9389097BAF670D}{}
{
  \index{transporter} 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RepresentativeAction}}
\logpage{[ 41, 6, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X857DC7B085EB0539}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RepresentativeAction({\mdseries\slshape G[, Omega], d, e[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{RepresentativeAction@\texttt{RepresentativeAction}}
\label{RepresentativeAction}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 computes an element of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} that maps \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} under the given action and returns \texttt{fail} if no such element exists. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,3,2),(2,4,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RepresentativeAction(g,1,3);|
  (1,3)(2,4)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RepresentativeAction(g,1,3,OnPoints);|
  (1,3)(2,4)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RepresentativeAction(g,(1,2,3),(2,4,3));|
  (1,2,4)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RepresentativeAction(g,(1,2,3),(2,3,4));|
  fail
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RepresentativeAction(g,Group((1,2,3)),Group((2,3,4)));|
  (1,2,4)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ RepresentativeAction(g,[1,2,3],[1,2,4],OnSets);|
  (2,4,3)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ RepresentativeAction(g,[1,2,3],[1,2,4],OnTuples);|
  fail
\end{Verbatim}
 

 (See Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Basic Actions} for information about specific actions.) 

 Again the standard method for \texttt{RepresentativeAction} is an orbit\texttt{\symbol{45}}stabilizer algorithm, for permutation groups
and standard actions a backtrack algorithm is used. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{The Permutation Image of an Action}}\label{The Permutation Image of an Action}
\logpage{[ 41, 7, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X87F73CCA7921DE65}{}
{
  When a group $G$ acts on a domain $\Omega$, an enumeration of $Omega$ yields a homomorphism from $G$ into the symmetric group on $\{ 1, \ldots, |\Omega| \}$. In \textsf{GAP}, the enumeration of $\Omega$ is provided by the \texttt{Enumerator} (\ref{Enumerator}) value of $\Omega$ which of course is $\Omega$ itself if it is a list. 

 For an action homomorphism, the operation \texttt{UnderlyingExternalSet} (\ref{UnderlyingExternalSet}) will return the external set on $\Omega$ which affords the action. 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ActionHomomorphism}}\logpage{[ 41, 7, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X78E6A002835288A4}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ActionHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape G, Omega[, gens, acts][, act][, "surjective"]})\index{ActionHomomorphism@\texttt{ActionHomomorphism}!for a group, an action domain, etc.}
\label{ActionHomomorphism:for a group, an action domain, etc.}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ActionHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape xset[, "surjective"]})\index{ActionHomomorphism@\texttt{ActionHomomorphism}!for an external set}
\label{ActionHomomorphism:for an external set}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ActionHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape action})\index{ActionHomomorphism@\texttt{ActionHomomorphism}!for an action image}
\label{ActionHomomorphism:for an action image}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 computes a homomorphism from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} into the symmetric group on $|\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}}|$ points that gives the permutation action of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}}. (In particular, this homomorphism is a permutation equivalence, that is the
permutation image of a group element is given by the positions of points in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}}.) 

 The result is undefined if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} does not act on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}}. 

 By default the homomorphism returned by \texttt{ActionHomomorphism} is not necessarily surjective (its \texttt{Range} (\ref{Range:of a general mapping}) value is the full symmetric group) to avoid unnecessary computation of the
image. If the optional string argument \texttt{"surjective"} is given, a surjective homomorphism is created. 

 The third version (which is supported only for \textsf{GAP}3 compatibility) returns the action homomorphism that belongs to the image
obtained via \texttt{Action} (\ref{Action:for a group, an action domain, etc.}). 

 (See Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Basic Actions} for information about specific actions.) 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3),(1,2));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@hom:=ActionHomomorphism(g,Arrangements([1..4],3),OnTuples);|
  <action homomorphism>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Image(hom);|
  Group(
  [ (1,9,13)(2,10,14)(3,7,15)(4,8,16)(5,12,17)(6,11,18)(19,22,23)(20,21,
      24), (1,7)(2,8)(3,9)(4,10)(5,11)(6,12)(13,15)(14,16)(17,18)(19,
      21)(20,22)(23,24) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(Range(hom));Size(Image(hom));|
  620448401733239439360000
  6
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@hom:=ActionHomomorphism(g,Arrangements([1..4],3),OnTuples,|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@"surjective");;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(Range(hom));|
  6
\end{Verbatim}
 

 When acting on a domain, the operation \texttt{PositionCanonical} (\ref{PositionCanonical}) is used to determine the position of elements in the domain. This can be used
to act on a domain given by a list of representatives for which \texttt{PositionCanonical} (\ref{PositionCanonical}) is implemented, for example the return value of \texttt{RightTransversal} (\ref{RightTransversal}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Action (for a group, an action domain, etc.)}}
\logpage{[ 41, 7, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85A8E93D786C3C9C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Action({\mdseries\slshape G, Omega[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{Action@\texttt{Action}!for a group, an action domain, etc.}
\label{Action:for a group, an action domain, etc.}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Action({\mdseries\slshape xset})\index{Action@\texttt{Action}!for an external set}
\label{Action:for an external set}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the image group of \texttt{ActionHomomorphism} (\ref{ActionHomomorphism:for a group, an action domain, etc.}) called with the same parameters. 

 Note that (for compatibility reasons to be able to get the action
homomorphism) this image group internally stores the action homomorphism. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} or \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} are extremely big, this can cause memory problems. In this case compute only
generator images and form the image group yourself. 

 (See Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Basic Actions} for information about specific actions.) 

 \index{regular action} The following code shows for example how to create the regular action of a
group. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3),(1,2));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Action(g,AsList(g),OnRight);|
  Group([ (1,5,3)(2,6,4), (1,6)(2,5)(3,4) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SparseActionHomomorphism}}
\logpage{[ 41, 7, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86FF54A383B73967}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SparseActionHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape G, start[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{SparseActionHomomorphism@\texttt{SparseActionHomomorphism}}
\label{SparseActionHomomorphism}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SortedSparseActionHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape G, start[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{SortedSparseActionHomomorphism@\texttt{SortedSparseActionHomomorphism}}
\label{SortedSparseActionHomomorphism}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{SparseActionHomomorphism} computes the action homomorphism (see \texttt{ActionHomomorphism} (\ref{ActionHomomorphism:for a group, an action domain, etc.})) with arguments \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, $D$, and the optional arguments given, where $D$ is the union of the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}orbits of all points in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape start}}. In the \texttt{Orbit} (\ref{Orbit}) calls that are used to create $D$, again the optional arguments given are entered.) 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} acts on a very large domain not surjectively this may yield a permutation
image of substantially smaller degree than by action on the whole domain. 

 The operation \texttt{SparseActionHomomorphism} will only use \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}=} (\ref{bSlash=}) comparisons of points in the orbit. Therefore it can be used even if no good \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}{\textless}} (\ref{bSlash<}) comparison method for these points is available. However the image group will
depend on the generators \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 

 The operation \texttt{SortedSparseActionHomomorphism} in contrast will sort the orbit and thus produce an image group which does not
depend on these generators. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:=Group(Z(3)*[[[1,1],[0,1]]]);|
  Group([ [ [ Z(3), Z(3) ], [ 0*Z(3), Z(3) ] ] ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@hom:=ActionHomomorphism(h,GF(3)^2,OnRight);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Image(hom);|
  Group([ (2,3)(4,9,6,7,5,8) ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@hom:=SparseActionHomomorphism(h,[Z(3)*[1,0]],OnRight);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Image(hom);|
  Group([ (1,2,3,4,5,6) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Action of a group on itself}}\label{Action of a group on itself}
\logpage{[ 41, 8, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7FED50ED7ACA5FB2}{}
{
  Of particular importance is the action of a group on its elements or cosets of
a subgroup. These actions can be obtained by using \texttt{ActionHomomorphism} (\ref{ActionHomomorphism:for a group, an action domain, etc.}) for a suitable domain (for example a list of subgroups). For the following
(frequently used) types of actions however special (often particularly
efficient) functions are provided. A special case is the regular action on all
elements. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FactorCosetAction (for a group and subgroup)}}
\logpage{[ 41, 8, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X784D417D87F4E58D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FactorCosetAction({\mdseries\slshape G, U[, N]})\index{FactorCosetAction@\texttt{FactorCosetAction}!for a group and subgroup}
\label{FactorCosetAction:for a group and subgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FactorCosetAction({\mdseries\slshape G, L})\index{FactorCosetAction@\texttt{FactorCosetAction}!for a group and list of subgroups}
\label{FactorCosetAction:for a group and list of subgroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 This command computes the action of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} on the right cosets of the subgroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}}. If a normal subgroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is given, it is stored as kernel of this action. When calling \texttt{FactorCosetAction} with a list of subgroups as the second argument, an action with image
isomorphic to the subdirect product of the coset actions of all subgroups is
computed. (However a degree reduction may take place if some of the actions
are redundant, i.e. there is no guarantee that every subgroup in the list is
represented by an orbit.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,2,3,4,5),(1,2));;u:=SylowSubgroup(g,2);;Index(g,u);|
  15
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FactorCosetAction(g,u);|
  [ (1,2,3,4,5), (1,2) ] -> [ (1,4,7,10,13)(2,5,8,11,14)(3,6,9,12,15),\
    (1,4)(2,6)(3,5)(7,8)(10,12)(13,14) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StructureDescription(Range(last));|
  "S5"
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FactorCosetAction(g,[u,SylowSubgroup(g,3)]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(Image(last));|
  120
\end{Verbatim}
 The correspondence of points with cosets will, for performance reasons, depend
on the method used. It is not guaranteed that it will be the same as used by \texttt{RightTransversal} or \texttt{RightCosets}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RegularActionHomomorphism}}
\logpage{[ 41, 8, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8561DEBA79E01ABD}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RegularActionHomomorphism({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{RegularActionHomomorphism@\texttt{RegularActionHomomorphism}}
\label{RegularActionHomomorphism}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns an isomorphism from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} onto the regular permutation representation of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AbelianSubfactorAction}}
\logpage{[ 41, 8, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X835317A7847477D4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AbelianSubfactorAction({\mdseries\slshape G, M, N})\index{AbelianSubfactorAction@\texttt{AbelianSubfactorAction}}
\label{AbelianSubfactorAction}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} be a group and $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} \geq \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}}$ be subgroups of a common parent that are normal under \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, such that the subfactor $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}/\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}}$ is elementary abelian. The operation \texttt{AbelianSubfactorAction} returns a list \texttt{[ \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape phi}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape alpha}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape bas}} ]} where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape bas}} is a list of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} which are representatives for a basis of $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}/\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}}$, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape alpha}} is a map from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} into a $n$\texttt{\symbol{45}}dimensional row space over $GF(p)$ where $[\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}:\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}}] = p^n$ that is the natural homomorphism of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} with the quotient represented as an additive group. Finally \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape phi}} is a homomorphism from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} into $GL_n(p)$ that represents the action of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} on the factor $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}/\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}}$. 

 Note: If only matrices for the action are needed, \texttt{LinearActionLayer} (\ref{LinearActionLayer}) might be faster. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,8,10,7,3,5)(2,4,12,9,11,6),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@            (1,9,5,6,3,10)(2,11,12,8,4,7));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@c:=ChiefSeries(g);;List(c,Size);|
  [ 96, 48, 16, 4, 1 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@HasElementaryAbelianFactorGroup(c[3],c[4]);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SetName(c[3],"my_group");;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a:=AbelianSubfactorAction(g,c[3],c[4]);|
  [ [ (1,8,10,7,3,5)(2,4,12,9,11,6), (1,9,5,6,3,10)(2,11,12,8,4,7) ] ->
      [ <an immutable 2x2 matrix over GF2>,
        <an immutable 2x2 matrix over GF2> ],
    MappingByFunction( my_group, ( GF(2)^
      2 ), function( e ) ... end, function( r ) ... end ),
    Pcgs([ (2,9,3,8)(4,11,5,10), (1,6,12,7)(4,10,5,11) ]) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=Image(a[1],g);|
  Group([ <an immutable 2x2 matrix over GF2>,
    <an immutable 2x2 matrix over GF2> ])
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(mat);|
  3
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@e:=PreImagesRepresentative(a[2],[Z(2),0*Z(2)]);|
  (2,9,3,8)(4,11,5,10)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@e in c[3];e in c[4];|
  true
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Permutations Induced by Elements and Cycles}}\label{Permutations Induced by Elements and Cycles}
\logpage{[ 41, 9, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X807AA91E841D132B}{}
{
  If only the permutation image of a single element is needed, it might not be
worth to create the action homomorphism, the following operations yield the
permutation image and cycles of a single element. 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Permutation}}\logpage{[ 41, 9, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7807A33381DCAB26}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Permutation({\mdseries\slshape g, Omega[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{Permutation@\texttt{Permutation}!for a group, an action domain, etc.}
\label{Permutation:for a group, an action domain, etc.}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Permutation({\mdseries\slshape g, xset})\index{Permutation@\texttt{Permutation}!for an external set}
\label{Permutation:for an external set}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 computes the permutation that corresponds to the action of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} on the permutation domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} (a list of objects that are permuted). If an external set \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape xset}} is given, the permutation domain is the \texttt{HomeEnumerator} (\ref{HomeEnumerator}) value of this external set (see Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{External Sets}). Note that the points of the returned permutation refer to the positions in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}}, even if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} itself consists of integers. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} does not leave the domain invariant, or does not map the domain injectively
then \texttt{fail} is returned. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PermutationCycle}}
\logpage{[ 41, 9, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81D4EA42810974A0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PermutationCycle({\mdseries\slshape g, Omega, pnt[, act]})\index{PermutationCycle@\texttt{PermutationCycle}}
\label{PermutationCycle}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 computes the permutation that represents the cycle of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} under the action of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Permutation([[Z(3),-Z(3)],[Z(3),0*Z(3)]],AsList(GF(3)^2));|
  (2,7,6)(3,4,8)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Permutation((1,2,3)(4,5)(6,7),[4..7]);|
  (1,2)(3,4)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PermutationCycle((1,2,3)(4,5)(6,7),[4..7],4);|
  (1,2)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Cycle}}
\logpage{[ 41, 9, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80AF6E0683CA7F14}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Cycle({\mdseries\slshape g, Omega, pnt[, act]})\index{Cycle@\texttt{Cycle}}
\label{Cycle}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns a list of the points in the cycle of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} under the action of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CycleLength}}
\logpage{[ 41, 9, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F559E897B333758}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CycleLength({\mdseries\slshape g, Omega, pnt[, act]})\index{CycleLength@\texttt{CycleLength}}
\label{CycleLength}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the length of the cycle of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pnt}} under the action of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Cycles}}
\logpage{[ 41, 9, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F3B387A7FD8AE5E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Cycles({\mdseries\slshape g, Omega[, act]})\index{Cycles@\texttt{Cycles}}
\label{Cycles}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns a list of the cycles (as lists of points) of the action of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CycleLengths}}
\logpage{[ 41, 9, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83040A6080C2C6C6}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CycleLengths({\mdseries\slshape g, Omega[, act]})\index{CycleLengths@\texttt{CycleLengths}}
\label{CycleLengths}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns the lengths of all the cycles under the action of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Cycle((1,2,3)(4,5)(6,7),[4..7],4);|
  [ 4, 5 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@CycleLength((1,2,3)(4,5)(6,7),[4..7],4);|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Cycles((1,2,3)(4,5)(6,7),[4..7]);|
  [ [ 4, 5 ], [ 6, 7 ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@CycleLengths((1,2,3)(4,5)(6,7),[4..7]);|
  [ 2, 2 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CycleIndex}}\logpage{[ 41, 9, 7 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X87FDA6838065CDCB}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CycleIndex({\mdseries\slshape g, Omega[, act]})\index{CycleIndex@\texttt{CycleIndex}!for a permutation and an action domain}
\label{CycleIndex:for a permutation and an action domain}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CycleIndex({\mdseries\slshape G, Omega[, act]})\index{CycleIndex@\texttt{CycleIndex}!for a permutation group and an action domain}
\label{CycleIndex:for a permutation group and an action domain}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 The \emph{cycle index} of a permutation \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} acting on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}} is defined as 
\[ z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}) = s_1^{{c_1}} s_2^{{c_2}} \cdots s_n^{{c_n}} \]
 where $c_k$ is the number of $k$\texttt{\symbol{45}}cycles in the cycle decomposition of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} and the $s_i$ are indeterminates. 

 The \emph{cycle index} of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is defined as 
\[ Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}) = \left( \sum_{{g \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}}} z(g) \right) / |\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}| . \]
 

 The indeterminates used by \texttt{CycleIndex} are the indeterminates $1$ to $n$ over the rationals (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Indeterminate} (\ref{Indeterminate:for a ring (and a number)})). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=TransitiveGroup(6,8);|
  S_4(6c) = 1/2[2^3]S(3)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@CycleIndex(g);|
  1/24*x_1^6+1/8*x_1^2*x_2^2+1/4*x_1^2*x_4+1/4*x_2^3+1/3*x_3^2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Tests for Actions}}\label{Tests for Actions}
\logpage{[ 41, 10, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X850A84618421392A}{}
{
  
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsTransitive}}\logpage{[ 41, 10, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X79B15750851828CB}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsTransitive({\mdseries\slshape G, Omega[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{IsTransitive@\texttt{IsTransitive}!for a group, an action domain, etc.}
\label{IsTransitive:for a group, an action domain, etc.}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsTransitive({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsTransitive@\texttt{IsTransitive}!for a permutation group}
\label{IsTransitive:for a permutation group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsTransitive({\mdseries\slshape xset})\index{IsTransitive@\texttt{IsTransitive}!for an external set}
\label{IsTransitive:for an external set}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if the action implied by the arguments is transitive, or \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \index{transitive} We say that a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} acts \emph{transitively} on a domain $D$ if and only if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} acts on $D$ and for every pair of points $d, e \in D$ there is an element $g$ in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} such that $d^g = e$. 

 For a permutation group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, one may also invoke this as \texttt{IsTransitive(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}})}, which tests whether the group is transitive with respect to its natural
action on the set of points moved by it. For example the group $\langle (2,3,4),(2,3) \rangle$ is transitive on the set $\{2, 3, 4\}$. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:= Group( (2,3,4), (2,3) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsTransitive( G, [ 2 .. 4 ] );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsTransitive( G, [ 2, 3 ] );   # G does not act on [ 2, 3 ]|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsTransitive( G, [ 1 .. 4 ] );  # G has two orbits on [ 1 .. 4 ]|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsTransitive( G );  # G is transitive on [ 2 .. 4 ]|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsTransitive( SL(2, 3), NormedRowVectors( GF(3)^2 ) );|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsTransitive( SL(2, 3), NormedRowVectors( GF(3)^2 ), OnLines );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Transitivity}}\logpage{[ 41, 10, 2 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8295D733796B7A37}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Transitivity({\mdseries\slshape G, Omega[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{Transitivity@\texttt{Transitivity}!for a group and an action domain}
\label{Transitivity:for a group and an action domain}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Transitivity({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{Transitivity@\texttt{Transitivity}!for a permutation group}
\label{Transitivity:for a permutation group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Transitivity({\mdseries\slshape xset})\index{Transitivity@\texttt{Transitivity}!for an external set}
\label{Transitivity:for an external set}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns the degree $k$ (a non\texttt{\symbol{45}}negative integer) of transitivity of the action
implied by the arguments, i.e. the largest integer $k$ such that the action is $k$\texttt{\symbol{45}}transitive. If the action is not transitive \texttt{0} is returned. 

 An action is \emph{$k$\texttt{\symbol{45}}transitive} if every $k$\texttt{\symbol{45}}tuple of points can be mapped simultaneously to every
other $k$\texttt{\symbol{45}}tuple. 

 For a permutation group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, one may also invoke this as \texttt{Transitivity(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}})}, which returns the degree of transitivity of the group with respect to its
natural action on the set of points moved by it. For example the group $\langle (2,3,4),(2,3) \rangle$ is 3\texttt{\symbol{45}}transitive on the set $\{2, 3, 4\}$. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=Group((1,3,2),(2,4,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsTransitive(g,[1..5]);|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Transitivity(g,[1..4]);|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Transitivity(g);|
  2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RankAction}}\logpage{[ 41, 10, 3 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8166A6A17C8D6E73}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RankAction({\mdseries\slshape G, Omega[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{RankAction@\texttt{RankAction}!for a group, an action domain, etc.}
\label{RankAction:for a group, an action domain, etc.}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RankAction({\mdseries\slshape xset})\index{RankAction@\texttt{RankAction}!for an external set}
\label{RankAction:for an external set}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns the rank of the transitive (see \texttt{IsTransitive} (\ref{IsTransitive:for a group, an action domain, etc.})) action of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Omega}}, i. e., the number of orbits of any point stabilizer. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RankAction(g,Combinations([1..4],2),OnSets);|
  4
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSemiRegular}}\logpage{[ 41, 10, 4 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7B77040F8543CD6E}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSemiRegular({\mdseries\slshape G, Omega[, gens, acts][, act]})\index{IsSemiRegular@\texttt{IsSemiRegular}!for a group, an action domain, etc.}
\label{IsSemiRegular:for a group, an action domain, etc.}
