}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Constructs a group isomorphic to the Ree group $^2G_2(q)$ where $q = 3^{{1+2m}}$ for $m$ a non\texttt{\symbol{45}}negative integer. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}) and the generating matrices are based on{\nobreakspace}\cite{KLM01}. (No particular choice of a generating set is guaranteed.) For more
information on possible values of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} see section (\ref{Basic Groups}). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ReeGroup( 27 );|
  Ree(27)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Generator Names}}\label{Generator Names}
\logpage{[ 50, 1, 16 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7D0FFDA4793995FC}{}
{
  For groups created as finitely presented groups, including polycyclic groups,
the generators are labelled, by default, with a letter and a number. It is
possible to influence this naming with the option \texttt{generatorNames}, see Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Function Call With Options}. If this option holds a string, then the generators are named with this
string and sequential numbers starting with \texttt{1}. If this option holds a list of sufficient length consisting of nonempty
strings, then the generator names are taken from this list, in order. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfGroup(AbelianGroup([5,7]));|
  [ f1, f2 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfGroup(AbelianGroup([5,7]:generatorNames:="a"));|
  [ a1, a2 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfGroup(AbelianGroup([5,7]:generatorNames:=["u","v","w"]));|
  [ u, v ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AsSSortedList(DihedralGroup(12:generatorNames:="a"));|
  [ <identity> of ..., a1, a2, a3, a1*a2, a1*a3, a2*a3, a3^2, a1*a2*a3,
    a1*a3^2, a2*a3^2, a1*a2*a3^2 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AsSSortedList(DihedralGroup(12:generatorNames:=["a","b","c"]));|
  [ <identity> of ..., a, b, c, a*b, a*c, b*c, c^2, a*b*c, a*c^2, b*c^2,
    a*b*c^2 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Classical Groups}}\label{Classical Groups}
\logpage{[ 50, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8674AAA578FE4AEE}{}
{
  The following functions return classical groups. 

 \emph{Generators} 

 
\begin{itemize}
\item  For the linear, symplectic, and unitary groups (the latter in dimension at
least $3$), the generators are taken from{\nobreakspace}\cite{Tay87}. 
\item  For the unitary groups in dimension $2$, the isomorphism of SU$(2,q)$ and SL$(2,q)$ is used, see for example{\nobreakspace}\cite{Hup67}. 
\item  The generators of the general and special orthogonal groups are taken
from{\nobreakspace}\cite{IshibashiEarnest94} and \cite{KleidmanLiebeck90}, except that the generators of the groups in odd dimension in even
characteristic are constructed via the isomorphism to a symplectic group, see
for example{\nobreakspace}\cite{Car72a}. 
\item  The generators of the groups $\Omega^\epsilon(d, q)$ are taken from{\nobreakspace}\cite{RylandsTalor98}, except that in odd dimension and even characteristic, the generators of SO$(d, q)$ are taken for $\Omega(d, q)$. Note that the generators claimed in{\nobreakspace}\cite[Section 4.5 and 4.6]{RylandsTalor98} do not describe orthogonal groups, one would have to transpose these matrices
in order to get groups that respect the required forms. The matrices
from{\nobreakspace}\cite{RylandsTalor98} generate groups of the right isomorphism types but not orthogonal groups,
except in the case $(d,q) = (5,2)$, where the matrices from{\nobreakspace}\cite{RylandsTalor98} generate the simple group $S_4(2)'$ and not the group $S_4(2)$. 
\item  The generators for the semilinear groups are constructed from the generators
of the corresponding linear groups plus one additional generator that
describes the action of the group of field automorphisms; for prime integers $p$ and positive integers $f$, this yields the matrix groups $Gamma$L$(d, p^f)$ and $Sigma$L$(d, p^f)$ as groups of $d f \times df$ matrices over the field with $p$ elements. 
\item  The generators for the conformal symplectic groups are taken
from{\nobreakspace}\cite{Tay21}. 
\end{itemize}
 

 \emph{Invariant forms} 

 
\begin{itemize}
\item  For symplectic and orthogonal matrix groups returned by the functions
described below, the invariant bilinear form is stored as the value of the
attribute \texttt{InvariantBilinearForm} (\ref{InvariantBilinearForm}). 
\item  The invariant sesquilinear form defining the unitary groups is stored as the
value of the attribute \texttt{InvariantSesquilinearForm} (\ref{InvariantSesquilinearForm})). 
\item  The defining quadratic form of orthogonal groups is stored as the value of the
attribute \texttt{InvariantQuadraticForm} (\ref{InvariantQuadraticForm}). 
\item  The bilinear form that is invariant up to scalars under the conformal
symplectic group is stored as the value of the attribute \texttt{InvariantBilinearFormUpToScalars} (\ref{InvariantBilinearFormUpToScalars}). 
\end{itemize}
 

 Note that due to the different sources for the generators, the invariant forms
for the groups $\Omega(e,d,q)$ are in general different from the forms for SO$(e,d,q)$ and GO$(e,d,q)$. If version at least 1.2.6 of the \textsf{Forms} package is loaded then compatible groups can be created by specifying the
desired form, see the sections below. 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneralLinearGroup}}\logpage{[ 50, 2, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X85D607DD82AF3E27}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneralLinearGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, R})\index{GeneralLinearGroup@\texttt{GeneralLinearGroup}!for dimension and a ring}
\label{GeneralLinearGroup:for dimension and a ring}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GL({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, R})\index{GL@\texttt{GL}!for dimension and a ring}
\label{GL:for dimension and a ring}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneralLinearGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{GeneralLinearGroup@\texttt{GeneralLinearGroup}!for dimension and field size}
\label{GeneralLinearGroup:for dimension and field size}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GL({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{GL@\texttt{GL}!for dimension and field size}
\label{GL:for dimension and field size}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 The first two forms construct a group isomorphic to the general linear group
GL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} ) of all $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}$ matrices that are invertible over the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, in the category given by the filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}}. 

 The third and the fourth form construct the general linear group over the
finite field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} elements. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}), and the returned group is the general linear group as a matrix group in its
natural action (see also{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsNaturalGL} (\ref{IsNaturalGL}), \texttt{IsNaturalGLnZ} (\ref{IsNaturalGLnZ})). 

 Currently supported rings \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are finite fields, the ring \texttt{Integers} (\ref{Integers:global variable}), and residue class rings \texttt{Integers mod \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}}}, see \ref{Residue Class Rings}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GL(4,3);|
  GL(4,3)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GL(2,Integers);|
  GL(2,Integers)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GL(3,Integers mod 12);|
  GL(3,Z/12Z)
\end{Verbatim}
 

 \index{OnLines@\texttt{OnLines}!example} Using the \texttt{OnLines} (\ref{OnLines}) operation it is possible to obtain the corresponding projective groups in a
permutation action: 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=GL(4,3);;Size(g);|
  24261120
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@pgl:=Action(g,Orbit(g,Z(3)^0*[1,0,0,0],OnLines),OnLines);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(pgl);|
  12130560
\end{Verbatim}
 

 If you are interested only in the projective group as a permutation group and
not in the correspondence between its moved points and the points in the
projective space, you can also use \texttt{PGL} (\ref{PGL}). }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SpecialLinearGroup}}\logpage{[ 50, 2, 2 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7CA3F7BF83992C6B}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SpecialLinearGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, R})\index{SpecialLinearGroup@\texttt{SpecialLinearGroup}!for dimension and a ring}
\label{SpecialLinearGroup:for dimension and a ring}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SL({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, R})\index{SL@\texttt{SL}!for dimension and a ring}
\label{SL:for dimension and a ring}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SpecialLinearGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{SpecialLinearGroup@\texttt{SpecialLinearGroup}!for dimension and a field size}
\label{SpecialLinearGroup:for dimension and a field size}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SL({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{SL@\texttt{SL}!for dimension and a field size}
\label{SL:for dimension and a field size}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 The first two forms construct a group isomorphic to the special linear group
SL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} ) of all those $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}$ matrices over the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} whose determinant is the identity of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, in the category given by the filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}}. 

 The third and the fourth form construct the special linear group over the
finite field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} elements. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}), and the returned group is the special linear group as a matrix group in its
natural action (see also{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsNaturalSL} (\ref{IsNaturalSL}), \texttt{IsNaturalSLnZ} (\ref{IsNaturalSLnZ})). 

 Currently supported rings \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are finite fields, the ring \texttt{Integers} (\ref{Integers}), and residue class rings \texttt{Integers mod \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}}}, see \ref{Residue Class Rings}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SpecialLinearGroup(2,2);|
  SL(2,2)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SL(3,Integers);|
  SL(3,Integers)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SL(4,Integers mod 4);|
  SL(4,Z/4Z)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneralUnitaryGroup}}
\logpage{[ 50, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X866D4E2B816BDFA5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneralUnitaryGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q[, form]})\index{GeneralUnitaryGroup@\texttt{GeneralUnitaryGroup}}
\label{GeneralUnitaryGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneralUnitaryGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{GeneralUnitaryGroup@\texttt{GeneralUnitaryGroup}!for a form}
\label{GeneralUnitaryGroup:for a form}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GU({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q[, form]})\index{GU@\texttt{GU}}
\label{GU}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GU({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{GU@\texttt{GU}!for a form}
\label{GU:for a form}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 constructs a group isomorphic to the general unitary group GU( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) of those $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}$ matrices over the field with $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}}^2$ elements that respect a fixed nondegenerate sesquilinear form, in the category
given by the filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}), and the returned group is the general unitary group itself. 

 If version at least 1.2.6 of the \textsf{Forms} package is loaded then the desired sesquilinear form can be specified via \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}, which can be either a matrix or a form object in \texttt{IsHermitianForm} (\textbf{Forms: IsHermitianForm}) or a group with stored \texttt{InvariantSesquilinearForm} (\ref{InvariantSesquilinearForm}) value (and then this form is taken). 

 A given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} determines \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, and also \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} except if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is a matrix that does not store its \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) value. These parameters can be entered, and an error is signalled if they do
not fit to the given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is not given then a default is chosen as described in the introduction to
Section \ref{Classical Groups}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneralUnitaryGroup( 3, 5 );|
  GU(3,5)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneralUnitaryGroup( IsPermGroup, 3, 5 );|
  Perm_GU(3,5)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SpecialUnitaryGroup}}
\logpage{[ 50, 2, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82A2AADE805DCDE9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SpecialUnitaryGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q[, form]})\index{SpecialUnitaryGroup@\texttt{SpecialUnitaryGroup}}
\label{SpecialUnitaryGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SpecialUnitaryGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{SpecialUnitaryGroup@\texttt{SpecialUnitaryGroup}!for a form}
\label{SpecialUnitaryGroup:for a form}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SU({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q[, form]})\index{SU@\texttt{SU}}
\label{SU}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SU({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{SU@\texttt{SU}!for a form}

}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 constructs a group isomorphic to the special unitary group SU( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) of those $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}$ matrices over the field with $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}}^2$ elements whose determinant is the identity of the field and that respect a
fixed nondegenerate sesquilinear form, in the category given by the filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}), and the returned group is the special unitary group itself. 

 If version at least 1.2.6 of the \textsf{Forms} package is loaded then the desired sesquilinear form can be specified via \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}, which can be either a matrix or a form object in \texttt{IsHermitianForm} (\textbf{Forms: IsHermitianForm}) or a group with stored \texttt{InvariantSesquilinearForm} (\ref{InvariantSesquilinearForm}) value (and then this form is taken). 

 A given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} determines \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, and also \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} except if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is a matrix that does not store its \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) value. These parameters can be entered, and an error is signalled if they do
not fit to the given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is not given then a default is chosen as described in the introduction to
Section \ref{Classical Groups}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SpecialUnitaryGroup( 3, 5 );|
  SU(3,5)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SpecialUnitaryGroup( IsPermGroup, 3, 5 );|
  Perm_SU(3,5)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SymplecticGroup}}\logpage{[ 50, 2, 5 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8142A8B07811CA90}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SymplecticGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, R[, form]})\index{SymplecticGroup@\texttt{SymplecticGroup}!for dimension and a ring}

}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SymplecticGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q[, form]})\index{SymplecticGroup@\texttt{SymplecticGroup}!for dimension and field size}

}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SymplecticGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{SymplecticGroup@\texttt{SymplecticGroup}!for form}
\label{SymplecticGroup:for form}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Sp({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, R[, form]})\index{Sp@\texttt{Sp}!for dimension and a ring}

}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Sp({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q[, form]})\index{Sp@\texttt{Sp}!for dimension and field size}
\label{Sp:for dimension and field size}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Sp({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{Sp@\texttt{Sp}!for form}
\label{Sp:for form}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SP({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, R[, form]})\index{SP@\texttt{SP}!for dimension and a ring}
\label{SP:for dimension and a ring}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SP({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q[, form]})\index{SP@\texttt{SP}!for dimension and field size}
\label{SP:for dimension and field size}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SP({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{SP@\texttt{SP}!for form}
\label{SP:for form}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 constructs a group isomorphic to the symplectic group Sp( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} ) of those $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}$ matrices over the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} or the field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} elements, respectively, that respect a fixed nondegenerate symplectic form, in
the category given by the filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}), and the returned group is the symplectic group itself. Other supported
values for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} are \texttt{IsPermGroup} (\ref{IsPermGroup}) (in this case, the argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is not supported) and the entries of \texttt{ConstructingFiltersForMatrixGroupElements} (\ref{ConstructingFiltersForMatrixGroupElements}). 

 At the moment finite fields or residue class rings \texttt{Integers mod \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}}}, with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} an odd prime power, are supported. 

 If version at least 1.2.6 of the \textsf{Forms} package is loaded and the arguments describe a matrix group over a finite
field then the desired bilinear form can be specified via \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}, which can be either a matrix or a form object in \texttt{IsBilinearForm} (\textbf{Forms: IsBilinearForm}) or a group with stored \texttt{InvariantBilinearForm} (\ref{InvariantBilinearForm}) value (and then this form is taken). 

 A given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} determines \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, and also \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} except if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is a matrix that does not store its \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) value. These parameters can be entered, and an error is signalled if they do
not fit to the given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is not given then a default is chosen as described in the introduction to
Section \ref{Classical Groups}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SymplecticGroup( 4, 2 );|
  Sp(4,2)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:=SymplecticGroup(6,Integers mod 9);|
  Sp(6,Z/9Z)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(g);|
  95928796265538862080
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SymplecticGroup( IsPermGroup, 4, 2 );|
  Perm_Sp(4,2)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneralOrthogonalGroup}}
\logpage{[ 50, 2, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C2051CB7B94CEB1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneralOrthogonalGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ][e, ]d, q[, form]})\index{GeneralOrthogonalGroup@\texttt{GeneralOrthogonalGroup}}
\label{GeneralOrthogonalGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneralOrthogonalGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{GeneralOrthogonalGroup@\texttt{GeneralOrthogonalGroup}!for a form}

\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GO({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ][e, ]d, q[, form]})\index{GO@\texttt{GO}}
\label{GO}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GO({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{GO@\texttt{GO}!for a form}
\label{GO:for a form}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 constructs a group isomorphic to the general orthogonal group GO( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) of those $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}$ matrices over the field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} elements that respect a non\texttt{\symbol{45}}singular quadratic form
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{InvariantQuadraticForm} (\ref{InvariantQuadraticForm})) specified by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, in the category given by the filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}}. 

 The value of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} must be $0$ for odd \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} (and can optionally be omitted in this case), respectively one of $1$ or $-1$ for even \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}), and the returned group is the general orthogonal group itself. 

 If version at least 1.2.6 of the \textsf{Forms} package is loaded then the desired quadratic form can be specified via \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}, which can be either a matrix or a form object in \texttt{IsQuadraticForm} (\textbf{Forms: IsQuadraticForm}) or a group with stored \texttt{InvariantQuadraticForm} (\ref{InvariantQuadraticForm}) value (and then this form is taken). 

 A given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} determines \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, and also \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} except if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is a matrix that does not store its \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) value. These parameters can be entered, and an error is signalled if they do
not fit to the given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is not given then a default is chosen as described in the introduction to
Section \ref{Classical Groups}. 

 Note that in{\nobreakspace}\cite{KleidmanLiebeck90}, GO is defined as the stabilizer $\Delta(V, F, \kappa)$ of the quadratic form, up to scalars, whereas our GO is called $I(V, F, \kappa)$ there. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneralOrthogonalGroup( 5, 3 );|
  GO(0,5,3)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneralOrthogonalGroup( -1, 8, 2 );|
  GO(-1,8,2)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneralOrthogonalGroup( IsPermGroup, -1, 8, 2 );|
  Perm_GO(-1,8,2)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SpecialOrthogonalGroup}}
\logpage{[ 50, 2, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78D4EEF27AA2DCFD}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SpecialOrthogonalGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ][e, ]d, q[, form]})\index{SpecialOrthogonalGroup@\texttt{SpecialOrthogonalGroup}}
\label{SpecialOrthogonalGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SpecialOrthogonalGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{SpecialOrthogonalGroup@\texttt{SpecialOrthogonalGroup}!for a form}
\label{SpecialOrthogonalGroup:for a form}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SO({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ][e, ]d, q[, form]})\index{SO@\texttt{SO}}
\label{SO}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SO({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{SO@\texttt{SO}!for a form}
\label{SO:for a form}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 constructs a group isomorphic to the special orthogonal group SO( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), which is the subgroup of all those matrices in the general orthogonal group
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{GeneralOrthogonalGroup} (\ref{GeneralOrthogonalGroup})) that have determinant one, in the category given by the filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}}. (The index of SO( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) in GO( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) is $2$ if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} is odd, and $1$ if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} is even.) Also interesting is the group Omega( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), see \texttt{Omega} (\ref{Omega:construct an orthogonal group}), which is of index $2$ in SO( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), except in the case $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} = 1$. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}), and the returned group is the special orthogonal group itself. 

 If version at least 1.2.6 of the \textsf{Forms} package is loaded then the desired quadratic form can be specified via \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}, which can be either a matrix or a form object in \texttt{IsQuadraticForm} (\textbf{Forms: IsQuadraticForm}) or a group with stored \texttt{InvariantQuadraticForm} (\ref{InvariantQuadraticForm}) value (and then this form is taken). 

 A given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} determines \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, and also \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} except if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is a matrix that does not store its \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) value. These parameters can be entered, and an error is signalled if they do
not fit to the given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is not given then a default is chosen as described in the introduction to
Section \ref{Classical Groups}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SpecialOrthogonalGroup( 5, 3 );|
  SO(0,5,3)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SpecialOrthogonalGroup( -1, 8, 2 );  # here SO and GO coincide|
  GO(-1,8,2)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SpecialOrthogonalGroup( IsPermGroup, 5, 3 );|
  Perm_SO(0,5,3)
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Omega (construct an orthogonal group)}}
\logpage{[ 50, 2, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8365E0AB8338DA3F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Omega({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ][e, ]d, q[, form]})\index{Omega@\texttt{Omega}!construct an orthogonal group}
\label{Omega:construct an orthogonal group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Omega({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]form})\index{Omega@\texttt{Omega}!construct an orthogonal group for a given quadratic form}
\label{Omega:construct an orthogonal group for a given quadratic form}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 constructs a group isomorphic to the group $\Omega$( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) of those $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}$ matrices over the field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} elements that respect a non\texttt{\symbol{45}}singular quadratic form
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{InvariantQuadraticForm} (\ref{InvariantQuadraticForm})) specified by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, and that have square spinor norm in odd characteristic or Dickson invariant $0$ in even characteristic, respectively, in the category given by the filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}}. 

 For odd \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} and $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} \geq 2$, this group has always index two in the corresponding special orthogonal
group, which will be conjugate in $GL(d,q)$ to the group returned by SO( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), see \texttt{SpecialOrthogonalGroup} (\ref{SpecialOrthogonalGroup}), but may fix a different form (see \ref{Classical Groups}). 

 The value of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} must be $0$ for odd \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} (and can optionally be omitted in this case), respectively one of $1$ or $-1$ for even \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}), and the returned group is the group $\Omega$( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) itself. 

 If version at least 1.2.6 of the \textsf{Forms} package is loaded then the desired quadratic form can be specified via \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}, which can be either a matrix or a form object in \texttt{IsQuadraticForm} (\textbf{Forms: IsQuadraticForm}) or a group with stored \texttt{InvariantQuadraticForm} (\ref{InvariantQuadraticForm}) value (and then this form is taken). 

 A given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} determines \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, and also \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} except if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is a matrix that does not store its \texttt{BaseDomain} (\ref{BaseDomain:for a matrix object}) value. These parameters can be entered, and an error is signalled if they do
not fit to the given \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape form}} is not given then a default is chosen as described in the introduction to
Section \ref{Classical Groups}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=@|B,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  @gapprompt|gap>B @gapinput|g:= Omega( 3, 5 );  StructureDescription( g );B
  Omega(0,3,5)
  "A5"
  @gapprompt|gap>B @gapinput|g:= Omega( 1, 4, 4 );  StructureDescription( g );B
  Omega(+1,4,4)
  "A5 x A5"
  @gapprompt|gap>B @gapinput|g:= Omega( -1, 4, 3 );  StructureDescription( g );B
  Omega(-1,4,3)
  "A6"
  @gapprompt|gap>B @gapinput|g:= Omega( IsPermGroup, 1, 6, 2 );  StructureDescription( g );B
  Perm_Omega(+1,6,2)
  "A8"
  @gapprompt|gap>B @gapinput|IsSubset( GO( 3, 5 ), Omega( 3, 5 ) );  # different forms!B
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneralSemilinearGroup}}
\logpage{[ 50, 2, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79C3C61A7D83A6D0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneralSemilinearGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{GeneralSemilinearGroup@\texttt{GeneralSemilinearGroup}}
\label{GeneralSemilinearGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GammaL({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{GammaL@\texttt{GammaL}}
\label{GammaL}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{GeneralSemilinearGroup} returns a group isomorphic to the general semilinear group $\Gamma$L( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) of semilinear mappings of the vector space \texttt{GF( }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}}\texttt{ )\texttt{\symbol{94}}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}), and the returned group consists of matrices of dimension \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} $f$ over the field with $p$ elements, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} $= p^f$, for a prime integer $p$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SpecialSemilinearGroup}}
\logpage{[ 50, 2, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D3779237CB5B49C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SpecialSemilinearGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{SpecialSemilinearGroup@\texttt{SpecialSemilinearGroup}}
\label{SpecialSemilinearGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SigmaL({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{SigmaL@\texttt{SigmaL}}
\label{SigmaL}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{SpecialSemilinearGroup} returns a group isomorphic to the special semilinear group $\Sigma$L( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) of those semilinear mappings of the vector space \texttt{GF( }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}}\texttt{ )\texttt{\symbol{94}}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} (see \texttt{GeneralSemilinearGroup} (\ref{GeneralSemilinearGroup})) whose linear part has determinant one. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsMatrixGroup} (\ref{IsMatrixGroup}), and the returned group consists of matrices of dimension \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} $f$ over the field with $p$ elements, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} $= p^f$, for a prime integer $p$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ProjectiveGeneralLinearGroup}}
\logpage{[ 50, 2, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F0DBEB880D2D574}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ProjectiveGeneralLinearGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{ProjectiveGeneralLinearGroup@\texttt{ProjectiveGeneralLinearGroup}}
\label{ProjectiveGeneralLinearGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PGL({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{PGL@\texttt{PGL}}
\label{PGL}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 constructs a group isomorphic to the projective general linear group PGL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) of those $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}$ matrices over the field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} elements, modulo the centre, in the category given by the filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsPermGroup} (\ref{IsPermGroup}), and the returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector
space. 

 }

}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\

}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 constructs a group isomorphic to the projective special linear group PSL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) of those $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} \times \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}$ matrices over the field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} elements whose determinant is the identity of the field, modulo the centre, in
the category given by the filter \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsPermGroup} (\ref{IsPermGroup}), and the returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector
space. }

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ProjectiveSpecialSemilinearGroup}}
\logpage{[ 50, 2, 20 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86BD9AE27CCAB1A6}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ProjectiveSpecialSemilinearGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{ProjectiveSpecialSemilinearGroup@\texttt{ProjectiveSpecialSemilinearGroup}}
\label{ProjectiveSpecialSemilinearGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PSigmaL({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]d, q})\index{PSigmaL@\texttt{PSigmaL}}
\label{PSigmaL}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{ProjectiveSpecialSemilinearGroup} returns a group isomorphic to the factor group of the special semilinear group \texttt{SigmaL(} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} \texttt{)} modulo the center of its normal subgroup \texttt{SL(} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} \texttt{)}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} is not given it defaults to \texttt{IsPermGroup} (\ref{IsPermGroup}), and the returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector space \texttt{GF(}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}}\texttt{)\texttt{\symbol{94}}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Conjugacy Classes in Classical Groups}}\label{Conjugacy Classes in Classical Groups}
\logpage{[ 50, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X85B9F2D379616C35}{}
{
  \index{ConjugacyClasses@\texttt{ConjugacyClasses}!for linear groups} For general and special linear groups (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{GeneralLinearGroup} (\ref{GeneralLinearGroup:for dimension and a ring}) and{\nobreakspace}\texttt{SpecialLinearGroup} (\ref{SpecialLinearGroup:for dimension and a ring})) \textsf{GAP} has an efficient method to generate representatives of the conjugacy classes.
This uses results from linear algebra on normal forms of matrices. If you know
how to do this for other types of classical groups, please, tell us. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g := SL(4,9);|
  SL(4,9)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrConjugacyClasses(g);|
  861
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@cl := ConjugacyClasses(g);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Length(cl);|
  861
\end{Verbatim}
 

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NrConjugacyClassesGL}}
\logpage{[ 50, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X831789117E93171E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesGL({\mdseries\slshape n, q})\index{NrConjugacyClassesGL@\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesGL}}
\label{NrConjugacyClassesGL}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesGU({\mdseries\slshape n, q})\index{NrConjugacyClassesGU@\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesGU}}
\label{NrConjugacyClassesGU}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesSL({\mdseries\slshape n, q})\index{NrConjugacyClassesSL@\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesSL}}
\label{NrConjugacyClassesSL}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesSU({\mdseries\slshape n, q})\index{NrConjugacyClassesSU@\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesSU}}
\label{NrConjugacyClassesSU}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesPGL({\mdseries\slshape n, q})\index{NrConjugacyClassesPGL@\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesPGL}}
\label{NrConjugacyClassesPGL}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesPGU({\mdseries\slshape n, q})\index{NrConjugacyClassesPGU@\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesPGU}}
\label{NrConjugacyClassesPGU}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesPSL({\mdseries\slshape n, q})\index{NrConjugacyClassesPSL@\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesPSL}}
\label{NrConjugacyClassesPSL}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesPSU({\mdseries\slshape n, q})\index{NrConjugacyClassesPSU@\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesPSU}}
\label{NrConjugacyClassesPSU}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesSLIsogeneous({\mdseries\slshape n, q, f})\index{NrConjugacyClassesSLIsogeneous@\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesSLIsogeneous}}
\label{NrConjugacyClassesSLIsogeneous}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesSUIsogeneous({\mdseries\slshape n, q, f})\index{NrConjugacyClassesSUIsogeneous@\texttt{NrConjugacyClassesSUIsogeneous}}
\label{NrConjugacyClassesSUIsogeneous}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 The first of these functions compute for given positive integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} and prime power \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} the number of conjugacy classes in the classical groups GL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), GU( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), SL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), SU( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), PGL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), PGU( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), PSL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), PSL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), respectively. (See also \texttt{ConjugacyClasses} (\ref{ConjugacyClasses:attribute}) and Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Classical Groups}.) 

 For each divisor \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape f}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} there is a group of Lie type with the same order as SL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), such that its derived subgroup modulo its center is isomorphic to PSL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ). The various such groups with fixed \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} are called \emph{isogeneous}. (Depending on congruence conditions on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} several of these groups may actually be isomorphic.) The function \texttt{NrConjugacyClassesSLIsogeneous} computes the number of conjugacy classes in this group. The extreme cases \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape f}} $= 1$ and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape f}} $= n$ lead to the groups SL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ) and PGL( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape q}} ), respectively. 

 The function \texttt{NrConjugacyClassesSUIsogeneous} is the analogous one for the corresponding unitary groups. 

 The formulae for the number of conjugacy classes are taken from{\nobreakspace}\cite{Mac81}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrConjugacyClassesGL(24,27);|
  22528399544939174406067288580609952
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrConjugacyClassesPSU(19,17);|
  15052300411163848367708
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrConjugacyClasses(SL(16,16));|
  1229782938228219920
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Constructors for Basic Groups}}\label{Constructors for Basic Groups}
\logpage{[ 50, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X817EBD6E841285CD}{}
{
  All functions described in the previous sections call constructor operations
to do the work. The names of the constructors are obtained from the names of
the functions by appending \texttt{"Cons"}, so for example \texttt{CyclicGroup} (\ref{CyclicGroup}) calls the constructor 

 \texttt{CyclicGroupCons( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape cat}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} )} 

 The first argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape cat}} for each method of this constructor must be the category for which the method
is installed. For example the method for constructing a cyclic permutation
group is installed as follows (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{InstallMethod} (\ref{InstallMethod}) for the meaning of the arguments. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  InstallMethod( CyclicGroupCons,
      "regular perm group",
      true,
      [ IsPermGroup and IsRegularProp and IsFinite, IsInt and IsPosRat ], 0,
      function( filter, n )
  
      ...
  
      end );
\end{Verbatim}
 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Selection Functions}}\label{Selection Functions}
\logpage{[ 50, 5, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X82676ED5826E9E2E}{}
{
  \index{AllPrimitiveGroups@\texttt{AllPrimitiveGroups}} \index{AllTransitiveGroups@\texttt{AllTransitiveGroups}} \index{AllLibraryGroups@\texttt{All\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Library}}Groups}} \texttt{All\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Library}}Groups( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fun1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape val1}}, ... )} 

 For a number of the group libraries two \emph{selection functions} are provided. Each \texttt{All\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Library}}Groups} selection function permits one to select \emph{all} groups from the library \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Library}} that have a given set of properties.    Currently, the library selection functions provided, of this type, are \texttt{AllSmallGroups} (\textbf{smallgrp: AllSmallGroups}), \texttt{AllIrreducibleSolvableGroups} (\textbf{primgrp: AllIrreducibleSolvableGroups}), \texttt{AllTransitiveGroups} (\textbf{transgrp: AllTransitiveGroups}), and \texttt{AllPrimitiveGroups} (\textbf{primgrp: AllPrimitiveGroups}). Corresponding to each of these there is a \texttt{One\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Library}}Group} function (see below) which returns at most one group. 

 These functions take an arbitrary number of pairs (but at least one pair) of
arguments. The first argument in such a pair is a function that can be applied
to the groups in the library, and the second argument is either a single value
that this function must return in order to have this group included in the
selection, or a list of such values. For the function \texttt{AllSmallGroups} (\textbf{smallgrp: AllSmallGroups}) the first such function must be \texttt{Size} (\ref{Size}), and, unlike the other library selection functions, it supports an
alternative syntax where \texttt{Size} (\ref{Size}) is omitted (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{AllSmallGroups} (\textbf{smallgrp: AllSmallGroups})). Also, see \texttt{AllIrreducibleSolvableGroups} (\textbf{primgrp: AllIrreducibleSolvableGroups}), for details pertaining to this function. 

 For an example, let us consider the selection function for the library of
transitive groups (also see{\nobreakspace} (\textbf{transgrp: Transitive Permutation Groups})). The command 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AllTransitiveGroups(NrMovedPoints,[10..15],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@                       Size,         [1..100],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@                       IsAbelian,    false    );|
\end{Verbatim}
 

 returns a list of all transitive groups with degree between 10 and 15 and size
less than 100 that are not abelian. 

 Thus \texttt{AllTransitiveGroups} behaves as if it was implemented by a function similar to the one defined
below, where \texttt{TransitiveGroupsList} is a list of all transitive groups. (Note that in the definition below we
assume for simplicity that \texttt{AllTransitiveGroups} accepts exactly 4 arguments. It is of course obvious how to change this
definition so that the function would accept a variable number of arguments.) 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  AllTransitiveGroups := function( fun1, val1, fun2, val2 )
  local    groups, g, i;
    groups := [];
    for i  in [ 1 .. Length( TransitiveGroupsList ) ] do
      g := TransitiveGroupsList[i];
      if      fun1(g) = val1  or IsList(val1) and fun1(g) in val1
          and fun2(g) = val2  or IsList(val2) and fun2(g) in val2
       then
        Add( groups, g );
      fi;
    od;
    return groups;
  end;
\end{Verbatim}
 

 Note that the real selection functions are considerably more difficult, to
improve the efficiency. Most important, each recognizes a certain set of
properties which are precomputed for the library without having to compute
them anew for each group. This will substantially speed up the selection
process. In the description of each library we will list the properties that
are stored for this library. 

 \index{OnePrimitiveGroup@\texttt{OnePrimitiveGroup}} \index{OneTransitiveGroup@\texttt{OneTransitiveGroup}} \index{OneLibraryGroup@\texttt{One\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Library}}Group}} \texttt{One\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Library}}Group( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fun1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape val1}}, ... )} 

 For each \texttt{All\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Library}}Groups} function (see above) there is a corresponding function \texttt{One\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape Library}}Group} on exactly the same arguments, i.e., there are \texttt{OneSmallGroup} (\textbf{smallgrp: OneSmallGroup}), \texttt{OneIrreducibleSolvableGroup} (\textbf{primgrp: OneIrreducibleSolvableGroup}), \texttt{OneTransitiveGroup} (\textbf{transgrp: OneTransitiveGroup}), and \texttt{OnePrimitiveGroup} (\textbf{primgrp: OnePrimitiveGroup}). Each function simply returns \emph{one} group in the library that has the prescribed properties, instead of \emph{all} such groups. It returns \texttt{fail} if no such group exists in the library. }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Finite Perfect Groups}}\label{Finite Perfect Groups}
\logpage{[ 50, 6, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7A884ECF813C2026}{}
{
  \index{perfect groups} The \textsf{GAP} library of finite perfect groups provides, up to isomorphism, a list of all
perfect groups whose sizes are less than $2\cdot 10^6$. The groups of orders up to $10^6$ have been enumerated by Derek{\nobreakspace}F. Holt and Wilhelm Plesken and
published in their book ``Perfect Groups'' \cite{HP89}. For orders $n = 86016$, 368640, or 737280 this work only counted the groups (but did not explicitly
list them), the groups of orders $n = 61440$, 122880, 172032, 245760, 344064, 491520, 688128, or 983040 were omitted. 

 We are grateful to Derek Holt and Wilhelm Plesken for making their groups
available to the \textsf{GAP} community by contributing their files. It should be noted that their book
contains a lot of further information for many of the library groups. So we
would like to recommend it to any \textsf{GAP} user who is interested in the groups. The library of these has been brought
into \textsf{GAP} format by Volkmar Felsch. 

 Several additional groups omitted from the book ``Perfect Groups'' have also been included. Two groups \texttt{\symbol{45}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}
one of order 450000 with a factor group of type $A_6$ and the one of order 962280 \texttt{\symbol{45}}\texttt{\symbol{45}} were
found by Jack Schmidt in 2005. Two groups of order 243000 and one each of
orders 729000, 871200, 878460 were found in 2020 by Alexander Hulpke. 

 The perfect groups of size less than $2\cdot 10^6$ which had not been classified in the work of Holt and Plesken have been
enumerated by Alexander Hulpke. They are stored directly and provide less
construction information in their names. 

 

 As all groups are stored by presentations, a permutation representation is
obtained by coset enumeration. Note that some of the library groups do not
have a faithful permutation representation of small degree. Computations in
these groups may be rather time consuming. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SizesPerfectGroups}}
\logpage{[ 50, 6, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X866A25F882A4E97B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SizesPerfectGroups({\mdseries\slshape })\index{SizesPerfectGroups@\texttt{SizesPerfectGroups}}
\label{SizesPerfectGroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 This is the ordered list of all numbers up to $2\cdot 10^6$ that occur as sizes of perfect groups. One can iterate over part of the
perfect groups library with: 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@for n in Intersection([100..500],SizesPerfectGroups()) do|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@     for k in [1..NrPerfectGroups(n)] do|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@       pg := PerfectGroup(n,k);|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@     od;|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@   od;|
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PerfectGroup}}\logpage{[ 50, 6, 2 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7906BBA7818E9415}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PerfectGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]size[, n]})\index{PerfectGroup@\texttt{PerfectGroup}!for group order (and index)}
\label{PerfectGroup:for group order (and index)}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PerfectGroup({\mdseries\slshape [filt, ]sizenumberpair})\index{PerfectGroup@\texttt{PerfectGroup}!for a pair [ order, index ]}
\label{PerfectGroup:for a pair [ order, index ]}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns a group which is isomorphic to the library group specified by the size
number \texttt{[ \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape size}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} ]} or by the two separate arguments \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape size}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, assuming a default value of $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} = 1$. The optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filt}} defines the filter in which the group is returned. Possible filters so far are \texttt{IsPermGroup} (\ref{IsPermGroup}) and \texttt{IsSubgroupFpGroup} (\ref{IsSubgroupFpGroup}). In the latter case, the generators and relators used coincide with those
given in{\nobreakspace}\cite{HP89}. The default filter is \texttt{IsPermGroup} (\ref{IsPermGroup}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G := PerfectGroup(IsPermGroup,6048,1);|
  U3(3)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:=PerfectGroup(IsPermGroup,823080,2);|
  A5 2^1 19^2 C 19^1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrMovedPoints(G);|
  6859
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:=PerfectGroup(1866240,12);|
  PG1866240.12
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NrMovedPoints(G);|
  270
\end{Verbatim}
 }

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NumberPerfectGroups}}
\logpage{[ 50, 6, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D68BE547FE5C0F5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NumberPerfectGroups({\mdseries\slshape size})\index{NumberPerfectGroups@\texttt{NumberPerfectGroups}}
\label{NumberPerfectGroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrPerfectGroups({\mdseries\slshape size})\index{NrPerfectGroups@\texttt{NrPerfectGroups}}
\label{NrPerfectGroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\

}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NrPerfectLibraryGroups({\mdseries\slshape size})\index{NrPerfectLibraryGroups@\texttt{NrPerfectLibraryGroups}}
\label{NrPerfectLibraryGroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the number of non\texttt{\symbol{45}}isomorphic perfect groups of size \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape size}} for each positive integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape size}} up to $2\cdot10^6$. Additionally, for odd \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape size}} an answer is returned (odd order groups are solvable). For any other argument
out of range it returns \texttt{fail}. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape NrPerfectGroups}} is a synonym for \texttt{NumberPerfectGroups}.
