\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FreeMonoid}}\logpage{[ 51, 2, 9 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X79FA3FA978CA2E43}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FreeMonoid({\mdseries\slshape [wfilt, ]rank[, name]})\index{FreeMonoid@\texttt{FreeMonoid}!for given rank}
\label{FreeMonoid:for given rank}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FreeMonoid({\mdseries\slshape [wfilt][,] [name1[, name2[, ...]]]})\index{FreeMonoid@\texttt{FreeMonoid}!for various names}
\label{FreeMonoid:for various names}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FreeMonoid({\mdseries\slshape [wfilt, ]names})\index{FreeMonoid@\texttt{FreeMonoid}!for a list of names}
\label{FreeMonoid:for a list of names}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FreeMonoid({\mdseries\slshape [wfilt, ]infinity[, name][, init]})\index{FreeMonoid@\texttt{FreeMonoid}!for infinitely many generators}
\label{FreeMonoid:for infinitely many generators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{FreeMonoid} returns a free monoid. The number of generators, and the labels given to the
generators, can be specified in several different ways. Warning: the labels of
generators are only an aid for printing, and do not necessarily distinguish
generators; see the examples at the end of \texttt{FreeSemigroup} (\ref{FreeSemigroup:for given rank}) for more information. 
\begin{description}
\item[{ 1: For a given rank, and an optional generator name prefix }]  Called with a nonnegative integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rank}}, \texttt{FreeMonoid} returns a free monoid on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rank}} generators. The optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} must be a string; its default value is \texttt{"m"}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is not given but the \texttt{generatorNames} option is, then this option is respected as described in
Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Generator Names}. 

 Otherwise, the generators of the returned free monoid are labelled \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}\texttt{1}, ..., \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}\texttt{k}, where \texttt{k} is the value of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rank}}. 

 
\item[{2: For given generator names}]  Called with various nonempty strings, \texttt{FreeMonoid} returns a free monoid on as many generators as arguments, which are labelled \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name2}}, etc. 
\item[{3: For a given list of generator names}]  Called with a finite list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape names}} of nonempty strings, \texttt{FreeMonoid} returns a free monoid on \texttt{Length(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape names}})} generators, whose \texttt{i}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th generator is labelled \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape names}}\texttt{[i]}. 
\item[{ 4: For the rank \texttt{infinity}, an optional default generator name prefix, and an optional finite list of
generator names }]  Called in the fourth form, \texttt{FreeMonoid} returns a free monoid on infinitely many generators. The optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} must be a string; its default value is \texttt{"m"}, and the optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape init}} must be a finite list of nonempty strings; its default value is an empty list.
The generators are initially labelled according to the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape init}}, followed by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}\texttt{i} for each \texttt{i} in the range from \texttt{Length(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape init}})+1} to \texttt{infinity}. 
\end{description}
 If the optional first argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape wfilt}} is given, then it must be either \texttt{IsSyllableWordsFamily}, \texttt{IsLetterWordsFamily}, \texttt{IsWLetterWordsFamily}, or \texttt{IsBLetterWordsFamily}. This filter specifies the representation used for the elements of the free
monoid (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Representations for Associative Words}). If no such filter is given, a letter representation is used. 

 For more on associative words see Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Associative Words}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeMonoid(5);|
  <free monoid on the generators [ m1, m2, m3, m4, m5 ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeMonoid(4, "gen");|
  <free monoid on the generators [ gen1, gen2, gen3, gen4 ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeMonoid(3 : generatorNames := "turbo");|
  <free monoid on the generators [ turbo1, turbo2, turbo3 ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeMonoid(2 : generatorNames := ["u", "v", "w"]);|
  <free monoid on the generators [ u, v ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeMonoid(); FreeMonoid(0); FreeMonoid([]);|
  <free monoid of rank zero>
  <free monoid of rank zero>
  <free monoid of rank zero>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeMonoid("a", "b", "c");|
  <free monoid on the generators [ a, b, c ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeMonoid(["x", "y"]);|
  <free monoid on the generators [ x, y ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeMonoid(infinity);|
  <free monoid with infinity generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@F := FreeMonoid(infinity, "g", ["a", "b"]);|
  <free monoid with infinity generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfMonoid(F){[1..4]};|
  [ a, b, g3, g4 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfMonoid(FreeMonoid(infinity, "gen")){[1..3]};|
  [ gen1, gen2, gen3 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfMonoid(FreeMonoid(infinity, [ "f", "g" ])){[1..3]};|
  [ f, g, m3 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FreeMonoid(IsSyllableWordsFamily, 50);|
  <free monoid with 50 generators>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MonoidByMultiplicationTable}}
\logpage{[ 51, 2, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BFE938E857CA27D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MonoidByMultiplicationTable({\mdseries\slshape A})\index{MonoidByMultiplicationTable@\texttt{MonoidByMultiplicationTable}}
\label{MonoidByMultiplicationTable}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the monoid whose multiplication is defined by the square matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{MagmaByMultiplicationTable} (\ref{MagmaByMultiplicationTable})) if such a monoid exists. Otherwise \texttt{fail} is returned. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MonoidByMultiplicationTable([[1,2,3],[2,3,1],[3,1,2]]);|
  <monoid of size 3, with 3 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MonoidByMultiplicationTable([[1,2,3],[2,3,1],[1,3,2]]);|
  fail
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Inverse semigroups and monoids}}\label{sect:IsInverseSemigroup}
\logpage{[ 51, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X840847B6810BD0E1}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{InverseSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78B13FED7AFB4326}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InverseSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape obj1, obj2, ...})\index{InverseSemigroup@\texttt{InverseSemigroup}}
\label{InverseSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
An inverse semigroup.



 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj2}}, ... are (any combination) of associative elements with unique semigroup
inverses, semigroups of such elements, or collections of such elements, then \texttt{InverseSemigroup} returns the inverse semigroup generated by the union of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj2}}, .... This equals the semigroup generated by the union of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj2}}, ... and their inverses.

 For example if \texttt{S} and \texttt{T} are inverse semigroups, then \texttt{InverseSemigroup(S, f, Idempotents(T));} is the inverse semigroup generated by \texttt{Union(GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup(S), [f], Idempotents(T)));}.

 As present, the only associative elements with unique semigroup inverses,
which do not always generate a group, are partial permutations; see Chapter \ref{Partial permutations}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := InverseSemigroup(|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@PartialPerm( [ 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 10 ], [ 2, 6, 7, 9, 1, 5 ] ) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := PartialPerm( [ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 10 ],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@[ 7, 1, 4, 3, 2, 6, 5 ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := InverseSemigroup(S, f, Idempotents(SymmetricInverseSemigroup(5)));|
  <inverse partial perm semigroup of rank 10 with 34 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(S);|
  1233
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{InverseMonoid}}
\logpage{[ 51, 3, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80D9B9A98736051B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InverseMonoid({\mdseries\slshape obj1, obj2, ...})\index{InverseMonoid@\texttt{InverseMonoid}}
\label{InverseMonoid}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
An inverse monoid.



 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj2}}, ... are (any combination) of associative elements with unique semigroup
inverses, semigroups of such elements, or collections of such elements, then \texttt{InverseMonoid} returns the inverse monoid generated by the union of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj2}}, .... This equals the monoid generated by the union of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape obj2}}, ... and their inverses.

 As present, the only associative elements with unique semigroup inverses are
partial permutations; see Chapter \ref{Partial permutations}.

 For example if \texttt{S} and \texttt{T} are inverse monoids, then \texttt{InverseMonoid(S, f, Idempotents(T));} is the inverse monoid generated by \texttt{Union(GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid(S), [f], Idempotents(T)));}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := InverseMonoid(|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@PartialPerm( [ 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 10 ], [ 2, 6, 7, 9, 1, 5 ] ) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := PartialPerm( [ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 10 ],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@[ 7, 1, 4, 3, 2, 6, 5 ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := InverseMonoid(S, f, Idempotents(SymmetricInverseSemigroup(5)));|
  <inverse partial perm monoid of rank 10 with 35 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size(S);|
  1243
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 3, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87C373597F787250}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup@\texttt{GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup}}
\label{GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
The generators of an inverse semigroup.



 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is an inverse semigroup, then \texttt{GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup} returns the generators used to define \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}, i.e. an inverse semigroup generating set for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. 

 The value of \texttt{GeneratorsOfSemigroup(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}})}, for an inverse semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}, is the union of inverse semigroup generator and their inverses. So, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is the semigroup, as opposed to inverse semigroup, generated by the elements
of \texttt{GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}})} and their inverses. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is an inverse monoid, then \texttt{GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup} returns the generators used to define \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}, as described above, and the identity of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S:=InverseMonoid(|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ PartialPerm( [ 1, 2 ], [ 1, 4 ] ),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ PartialPerm( [ 1, 2, 4 ], [ 3, 4, 1 ] ) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfSemigroup(S);|
  [ <identity partial perm on [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ]>, [2,4](1), [2,4,1,3],
    [4,2](1), [3,1,4,2] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup(S);|
  [ [2,4](1), [2,4,1,3], <identity partial perm on [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ]> ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfMonoid(S);|
  [ [2,4](1), [2,4,1,3], [4,2](1), [3,1,4,2] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid}}
\logpage{[ 51, 3, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A3B262C85B6D475}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid@\texttt{GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid}}
\label{GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
The generators of an inverse monoid.



 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is an inverse monoid, then \texttt{GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid} returns the generators used to define \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}, i.e. an inverse monoid generating set for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. 

 There are four different possible generating sets which define an inverse
monoid. More precisely, an inverse monoid can be generated as an inverse
monoid, inverse semigroup, monoid, or semigroup. The different generating sets
in each case can be obtained using \texttt{GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid}, \texttt{GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup} (\ref{GeneratorsOfInverseSemigroup}), \texttt{GeneratorsOfMonoid} (\ref{GeneratorsOfMonoid}), and \texttt{GeneratorsOfSemigroup} (\ref{GeneratorsOfSemigroup}), respectively. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S:=InverseMonoid(|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ PartialPerm( [ 1, 2 ], [ 1, 4 ] ),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ PartialPerm( [ 1, 2, 4 ], [ 3, 4, 1 ] ) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfInverseMonoid(S);|
  [ [2,4](1), [2,4,1,3] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsInverseSubsemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 3, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C4C6EE681E7A57E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsInverseSubsemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S, T})\index{IsInverseSubsemigroup@\texttt{IsInverseSubsemigroup}}
\label{IsInverseSubsemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
\texttt{true} or \texttt{false}.



 If the semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape T}} is an inverse subsemigroup of the semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}, then this operation returns \texttt{true}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@T:=InverseSemigroup(RandomPartialPerm(4));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsInverseSubsemigroup(SymmetricInverseSemigroup(4), T);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@T:=Semigroup(Transformation( [ 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 3, 7, 8 ] ),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@Transformation( [ 3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 2, 7, 8 ] ),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@Transformation([ 1, 2, 5, 3, 6, 8, 4, 4 ] ));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsInverseSubsemigroup(FullTransformationSemigroup(8), T);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Properties of Semigroups}}\label{Properties of Semigroups}
\logpage{[ 51, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X78274024827F306D}{}
{
  The following functions determine information about semigroups. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRegularSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 4, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C4663827C5ACEF1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRegularSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{IsRegularSemigroup@\texttt{IsRegularSemigroup}}
\label{IsRegularSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is regular, i.e., if every $\mathcal{D}$\texttt{\symbol{45}}class of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is regular. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRegularSemigroupElement}}
\logpage{[ 51, 4, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87532A76854347E0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRegularSemigroupElement({\mdseries\slshape S, x})\index{IsRegularSemigroupElement@\texttt{IsRegularSemigroupElement}}
\label{IsRegularSemigroupElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} has a general inverse in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}, i.e., there is an element $y \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}$ such that $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} y \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} = \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}}$ and $y \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} y = y$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{InversesOfSemigroupElement}}
\logpage{[ 51, 4, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AFDE0F17AE516C5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InversesOfSemigroupElement({\mdseries\slshape S, x})\index{InversesOfSemigroupElement@\texttt{InversesOfSemigroupElement}}
\label{InversesOfSemigroupElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A list of the inverses of an element of a semigroup.



 \texttt{InversesOfSemigroupElement} returns a list of the inverses of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} in the semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}.

 An element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape y}} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is an \emph{inverse} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} if \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}}*y*\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}}=\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}}} and \texttt{y*\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}}*y=y}. The element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} has an inverse if and only if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} is a regular element of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := Semigroup([|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ Transformation([3, 1, 4, 2, 5, 2, 1, 6, 1]),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ Transformation([5, 7, 8, 8, 7, 5, 9, 1, 9]),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ Transformation([7, 6, 2, 8, 4, 7, 5, 8, 3])]);|
  <transformation semigroup of degree 9 with 3 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x := Transformation([3, 1, 4, 2, 5, 2, 1, 6, 1]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@InversesOfSemigroupElement(S, x);|
  [  ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsRegularSemigroupElement(S, x);|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x := Transformation([1, 9, 7, 5, 5, 1, 9, 5, 1]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Set(InversesOfSemigroupElement(S, x));|
  [ Transformation( [ 1, 2, 3, 5, 5, 1, 3, 5, 2 ] ),
    Transformation( [ 1, 5, 1, 1, 5, 1, 3, 1, 2 ] ),
    Transformation( [ 1, 5, 1, 2, 5, 1, 3, 2, 2 ] ) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsRegularSemigroupElement(S, x);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(Group((1,2,3)),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ [[(), ()], [(), 0], [(), (1,2,3)]]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x := ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement(S, 2, (1,2,3), 3);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@InversesOfSemigroupElement(S, x);|
  [ (1,(1,2,3),3), (1,(1,3,2),1), (2,(),3), (2,(1,2,3),1) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSimpleSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 4, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X836F4692839F4874}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSimpleSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{IsSimpleSemigroup@\texttt{IsSimpleSemigroup}}
\label{IsSimpleSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if and only if the semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} has no proper ideals. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsZeroSimpleSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 4, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8193A60F839C064E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsZeroSimpleSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{IsZeroSimpleSemigroup@\texttt{IsZeroSimpleSemigroup}}
\label{IsZeroSimpleSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if and only if the semigroup has no proper ideals except for 0, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is a semigroup with zero. If the semigroup does not find its zero, then a
break\texttt{\symbol{45}}loop is entered. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsZeroGroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 4, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85F7E5CD86F0643B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsZeroGroup({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{IsZeroGroup@\texttt{IsZeroGroup}}
\label{IsZeroGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if and only if the semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is a group with zero adjoined. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsReesCongruenceSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 4, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7FFEC81F7F2C4EAA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsReesCongruenceSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{IsReesCongruenceSemigroup@\texttt{IsReesCongruenceSemigroup}}
\label{IsReesCongruenceSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is a Rees Congruence semigroup, that is, if all congruences of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} are Rees Congruences. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsInverseSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 4, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83F1529479D56665}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsInverseSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{IsInverseSemigroup@\texttt{IsInverseSemigroup}}
\label{IsInverseSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsInverseMonoid({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{IsInverseMonoid@\texttt{IsInverseMonoid}}
\label{IsInverseMonoid}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
\texttt{true} or \texttt{false}.



 A semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is an \emph{inverse semigroup} if every element \texttt{x} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} has a unique semigroup inverse, that is, a unique element \texttt{y} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} such that \texttt{x*y*x=x} and \texttt{y*x*y=y}.

 A monoid that happens to be an inverse semigroup is called an \emph{inverse monoid}; see \texttt{IsMonoid} (\ref{IsMonoid}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := Semigroup([|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ Transformation([1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 3, 7, 8]),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ Transformation([3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 2, 7, 8]),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ Transformation([1, 2, 5, 3, 6, 8, 4, 4])]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsInverseSemigroup(S);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Ideals of semigroups}}\label{Ideals of semigroups}
\logpage{[ 51, 5, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7BB32D508183C0F1}{}
{
  Ideals of semigroups are the same as ideals of the semigroup when considered
as a magma. For documentation on ideals for magmas, see \texttt{Magma} (\ref{Magma}). 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SemigroupIdealByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 51, 5, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D5CEE4D7D4318ED}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SemigroupIdealByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape S, gens})\index{SemigroupIdealByGenerators@\texttt{SemigroupIdealByGenerators}}
\label{SemigroupIdealByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is a semigroup, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} is a list of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. Returns the two\texttt{\symbol{45}}sided ideal of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} generated by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ReesCongruenceOfSemigroupIdeal}}
\logpage{[ 51, 5, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F01FFB18125DED5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ReesCongruenceOfSemigroupIdeal({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{ReesCongruenceOfSemigroupIdeal@\texttt{ReesCongruenceOfSemigroupIdeal}}
\label{ReesCongruenceOfSemigroupIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 A two sided ideal \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape I}} of a semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} defines a congruence on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} given by $\Delta \cup I \times I$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLeftSemigroupIdeal}}
\logpage{[ 51, 5, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A3FF85984345540}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLeftSemigroupIdeal({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{IsLeftSemigroupIdeal@\texttt{IsLeftSemigroupIdeal}}
\label{IsLeftSemigroupIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRightSemigroupIdeal({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{IsRightSemigroupIdeal@\texttt{IsRightSemigroupIdeal}}
\label{IsRightSemigroupIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSemigroupIdeal({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{IsSemigroupIdeal@\texttt{IsSemigroupIdeal}}
\label{IsSemigroupIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 Categories of semigroup ideals. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Congruences on semigroups}}\label{Congruences on semigroups}
\logpage{[ 51, 6, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7914691E7DFFE27A}{}
{
  An equivalence or a congruence on a semigroup is the equivalence or congruence
on the semigroup considered as a magma. So, to deal with equivalences and
congruences on semigroups, magma functions are used. For documentation on
equivalences and congruences on magmas, see \texttt{Magma} (\ref{Magma}). 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSemigroupCongruence}}
\logpage{[ 51, 6, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78E34B737F0E009F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSemigroupCongruence({\mdseries\slshape c})\index{IsSemigroupCongruence@\texttt{IsSemigroupCongruence}}
\label{IsSemigroupCongruence}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 a magma congruence \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape c}} on a semigroup. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsReesCongruence}}
\logpage{[ 51, 6, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X822DB78579BCB7B5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsReesCongruence({\mdseries\slshape c})\index{IsReesCongruence@\texttt{IsReesCongruence}}
\label{IsReesCongruence}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 returns \texttt{true} if and only if the congruence \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape c}} has at most one nonsingleton congruence class. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Quotients}}\label{Quotients}
\logpage{[ 51, 7, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X87CE9EAB7EE3A128}{}
{
  Given a semigroup and a congruence on the semigroup, one can construct a new
semigroup: the quotient semigroup. The following functions deal with quotient
semigroups in \textsf{GAP}. For a semigroup $S$, elements of a quotient semigroup are equivalence classes of elements of the \texttt{QuotientSemigroupPreimage} (\ref{QuotientSemigroupPreimage}) value under the congruence given by the value of \texttt{QuotientSemigroupCongruence} (\ref{QuotientSemigroupCongruence}). 

 It is probably most useful for calculating the elements of the equivalence
classes by using \texttt{Elements} (\ref{Elements}) or by looking at the images of elements of \texttt{QuotientSemigroupPreimage} (\ref{QuotientSemigroupPreimage}) under the map returned by \texttt{QuotientSemigroupHomomorphism} (\ref{QuotientSemigroupHomomorphism}), which maps the \texttt{QuotientSemigroupPreimage} (\ref{QuotientSemigroupPreimage}) value to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. 

 For intensive computations in a quotient semigroup, it is probably worthwhile
finding another representation as the equality test could involve enumeration
of the elements of the congruence classes being compared.

\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Green's Relations}}\label{Green's Relations}
\logpage{[ 51, 8, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X80C6C718801855E9}{}
{
  Green's equivalence relations play a very important role in semigroup theory.
In this section we describe how they can be used in \textsf{GAP}. 

 The five Green's relations are $R$, $L$, $J$, $H$, $D$: two elements $x$, $y$ from a semigroup $S$ are $R$\texttt{\symbol{45}}related if and only if $xS^1 = yS^1$, $L$\texttt{\symbol{45}}related if and only if $S^1 x = S^1 y$ and $J$\texttt{\symbol{45}}related if and only if $S^1 xS^1 = S^1 yS^1$; finally, $H = R \wedge L$, and $D = R \circ L$. 

 Recall that relations $R$, $L$ and $J$ induce a partial order among the elements of the semigroup $S$: for two elements $x$, $y$ from $S$, we say that $x$ is less than or equal to $y$ in the order on $R$ if $xS^1 \subseteq yS^1$; similarly, $x$ is less than or equal to $y$ under $L$ if $S^1x \subseteq S^1y$; finally $x$ is less than or equal to $y$ under $J$ if $S^1 xS^1 \subseteq S^1 tS^1$. We extend this preorder to a partial order on equivalence classes in the
natural way.
