\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Rees Matrix Semigroups}}\label{Rees Matrix Semigroups}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8225A9EC87A255E6}{}
{
  In this section, we describe the functions in \textsf{GAP} for Rees matrix and 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroups and their
subsemigroups. The importance of these semigroups lies in the fact that Rees
matrix semigroups over groups are exactly the completely simple semigroups,
and Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroups over groups are the completely
0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple semigroups. 

 Let $I$ and $J$ be sets, let $S$ be a semigroup, and let $P=(p_{ji})_{j\in J, i\in I}$ be a $|J|\times |I|$ matrix with entries in $S$. Then the \emph{Rees matrix semigroup} with underlying semigroup $S$ and matrix $P$ is just the direct product $I\times S \times J$ with multiplication defined by 
\[(i, s, j)(k, t, l)=(i,s\cdot p_{j,k}\cdot t, l).\]
 Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroups are defined as follows. If $I$, $J$, $S$, and $P$ are as above and $0$ denotes a new element, then the \emph{Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup} with underlying semigroup $S$ and matrix $P$ is $(I\times S\times J)\cup \{0\}$ with multiplication defined by 
\[(i, s, j)(k, t, l)=(i, s\cdot p_{j,k}\cdot t, l)\]
 when $p_{j,k}$ is not $0$ and $0$ if $p_{j,k}$ is 0.

 If $R$ is a Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup, then the \emph{rows} of $R$ is the index set $I$, the \emph{columns} of $R$ is the index set $J$, the semigroup $S$ is the \emph{underlying semigroup} of $R$, and the \emph{matrix} $P$ is the matrix of $S$. 

 Thoroughout this section, wherever the distinction is unimportant, we will
refer to Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroups collectively as
Rees matrix semigroups.

 Multiplication of elements of a Rees matrix semigroup obviously depends on the
matrix used to create the semigroup. Hence elements of a Rees matrix semigroup
can only be created with reference to the semigroup to which they belong. More
specifically, every collection or semigroup of Rees matrix semigroup elements
is created from a specific Rees matrix semigroup, which contains the whole
family of its elements. So, it is not possible to multiply or compare elements
belonging to distinct Rees matrix semigroups, since they belong to different
families. For example, this situation is similar to free groups, but it is
different to permutations, which belong to a single family, and where
arbitrary permutations can be compared and multiplied without reference to any
group containing them. 

 A subsemigroup of a Rees matrix semigroup is not necessarily a Rees matrix
semigroup. Every semigroup consisting of elements of a Rees matrix semigroup
satisfies the property \texttt{IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup} (\ref{IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup}) and every semigroup of Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup elements
satisfies \texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup} (\ref{IsReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup}). 

 Rees matrix and 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroups can be created using
the operations \texttt{ReesMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{ReesMatrixSemigroup}) and \texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}), respectively, from an underlying semigroup and a matrix. Rees matrix
semigroups created in this way contain the whole family of their elements.
Every element of a Rees matrix semigroup belongs to a unique semigroup created
in this way; every subsemigroup of a Rees matrix semigroup is a subsemigroup
of a unique semigroup created in this way.

 Subsemigroups of Rees matrix semigroups can also be created by specifying
generators. A subsemigroup of a Rees matrix semigroup $I\times U\times J$ satisfies \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}) if and only if it is equal to $I'\times U'\times J'$ where $I'\subseteq I$, $J'\subseteq J$, and $U'$ is a subsemigroup of $U$. The analogous statements holds for Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix
semigroups. 

 It is not necessarily the case that a simple subsemigroups of Rees matrix
semigroups satisfies \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}). A Rees matrix semigroup is simple if and only if its underlying semigroup is
simple. A finite semigroup is simple if and only if it is isomorphic to a Rees
matrix semigroup over a group; this isomorphism can be obtained explicitly
using \texttt{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup}).

 Similarly, 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple subsemigroups of Rees
0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroups do not have to satisfy \texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}). A Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup with more than 2 elements is
0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple if and only if every row and every column of its
matrix contains a non\texttt{\symbol{45}}zero entry, and its underlying
semigroup is simple. A finite semigroup is 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple if and
only if it is isomorphic to a Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup over
a group; again this isomorphism can be found by using \texttt{IsomorphismReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsomorphismReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}).

 Elements of a Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup belong to
the categories \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement} (\ref{IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement}) and \texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement} (\ref{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement}), respectively. Such elements can be created directly using the functions \texttt{ReesMatrixSemigroupElement} (\ref{ReesMatrixSemigroupElement}) and \texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement} (\ref{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement}). 

 A semigroup in \textsf{GAP} can either satisfies \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}) or \texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}) but not both. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ReesMatrixSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8526AA557CDF6C49}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ReesMatrixSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S, mat})\index{ReesMatrixSemigroup@\texttt{ReesMatrixSemigroup}}
\label{ReesMatrixSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S, mat})\index{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup@\texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}}
\label{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup.



 When \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is a semigroup and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mat}} is an \texttt{m} by \texttt{n} matrix with entries in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}, the function \texttt{ReesMatrixSemigroup} returns the \texttt{n} by \texttt{m} Rees matrix semigroup over \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} with multiplication defined by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mat}}. 

 The arguments of \texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} should be a semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} and an \texttt{m} by \texttt{n} matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mat}} with entries in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} or equal to the integer \texttt{0}. \texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} returns the \texttt{n} by \texttt{m} Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup over \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} with multiplication defined by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mat}}. In \textsf{GAP} a Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup always contains a multiplicative
zero element, regardless of whether there are any entries in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mat}} which are equal to \texttt{0}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:=Random(AllSmallGroups(Size, 32));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=List([1..5], x-> List([1..3], y-> Random(G)));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S:=ReesMatrixSemigroup(G, mat);|
  <Rees matrix semigroup 3x5 over <pc group of size 32 with
   5 generators>>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=[[(), 0, (), ()], [0, 0, 0, 0]];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S:=ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(DihedralGroup(IsPermGroup, 8), mat);|
  <Rees 0-matrix semigroup 4x2 over Group([ (1,2,3,4), (2,4) ])>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ReesMatrixSubsemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78D2A48C87FC8E38}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ReesMatrixSubsemigroup({\mdseries\slshape R, I, U, J})\index{ReesMatrixSubsemigroup@\texttt{ReesMatrixSubsemigroup}}
\label{ReesMatrixSubsemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup({\mdseries\slshape R, I, U, J})\index{ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup@\texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup}}
\label{ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix subsemigroup.



 The arguments of \texttt{ReesMatrixSubsemigroup} should be a Rees matrix semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, subsets \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape I}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape J}} of the rows and columns of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, respectively, and a subsemigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}} of the underlying semigroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. \texttt{ReesMatrixSubsemigroup} returns the subsemigroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} generated by the direct product of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape I}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape U}}, and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape J}}. 

 The usage and returned value of \texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup} is analogous when \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is a Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:=CyclicGroup(IsPermGroup, 1007);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=[[(), 0, 0], [0, (), 0], [0, 0, ()],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@[(), (), ()], [0, 0, ()]];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(G, mat);|
  <Rees 0-matrix semigroup 3x5 over
    <permutation group of size 1007 with 1 generator>>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup(R, [1,3], G, [1..5]);|
  <Rees 0-matrix semigroup 2x5 over
    <permutation group of size 1007 with 1 generator>>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7964B5C97FB9C07D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup@\texttt{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup}}
\label{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsomorphismReesZeroMatrixSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{IsomorphismReesZeroMatrixSemigroup@\texttt{IsomorphismReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}}
\label{IsomorphismReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
An isomorphism.



 Every finite simple semigroup is isomorphic to a Rees matrix semigroup over a
group, and every finite 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple semigroup is isomorphic to
a Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup over a group. 

 If the argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is a simple semigroup, then \texttt{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup} returns an isomorphism to a Rees matrix semigroup over a group. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is not simple, then \texttt{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup} returns an error. 

 If the argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is a 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple semigroup, then \texttt{IsomorphismReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} returns an isomorphism to a Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup over a
group. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is not 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple, then \texttt{IsomorphismReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} returns an error. 

 See \texttt{IsSimpleSemigroup} (\ref{IsSimpleSemigroup}) and \texttt{IsZeroSimpleSemigroup} (\ref{IsZeroSimpleSemigroup}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := Semigroup(Transformation([2, 1, 1, 2, 1]),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@                  Transformation([3, 4, 3, 4, 4]),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@                  Transformation([3, 4, 3, 4, 3]),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@                  Transformation([4, 3, 3, 4, 4]));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsSimpleSemigroup(S);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Range(IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup(S));|
  <Rees matrix semigroup 4x2 over Group([ (1,2) ])>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat := [[(), 0, 0],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@           [0, (), 0],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@           [0, 0, ()]];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R := ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(Group((1,2,4,5,6)), mat);|
  <Rees 0-matrix semigroup 3x3 over Group([ (1,2,4,5,6) ])>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@U := ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup(R, [1, 2], Group(()), [2, 3]);|
  <subsemigroup of 3x3 Rees 0-matrix semigroup with 4 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsZeroSimpleSemigroup(U);|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@U := ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup(R, [2, 3], Group(()), [2, 3]);|
  <subsemigroup of 3x3 Rees 0-matrix semigroup with 3 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsZeroSimpleSemigroup(U);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Rows(U); Columns(U);|
  [ 2, 3 ]
  [ 2, 3 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V := Range(IsomorphismReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(U));|
  <Rees 0-matrix semigroup 2x2 over Group(())>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Rows(V); Columns(V);|
  [ 1, 2 ]
  [ 1, 2 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement}}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F6B852B81488C86}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement({\mdseries\slshape elt})\index{IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement@\texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement}}
\label{IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement({\mdseries\slshape elt})\index{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement@\texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement}}
\label{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
\texttt{true} or \texttt{false}.



 Every element of a Rees matrix semigroup belongs to the category \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement}, and every element of a Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup belongs to
the category \texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:=Group((1,2,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=[ [ (), (1,3,2) ], [ (1,3,2), () ] ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=ReesMatrixSemigroup(G, mat);|
  <Rees matrix semigroup 2x2 over Group([ (1,2,3) ])>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfSemigroup(R);|
  [ (1,(1,2,3),1), (2,(),2) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReesMatrixSemigroupElement(last[1]);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement(last2[1]);|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ReesMatrixSemigroupElement}}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A0DE1F28470295E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ReesMatrixSemigroupElement({\mdseries\slshape R, i, x, j})\index{ReesMatrixSemigroupElement@\texttt{ReesMatrixSemigroupElement}}
\label{ReesMatrixSemigroupElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement({\mdseries\slshape R, i, x, j})\index{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement@\texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement}}
\label{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
An element of a Rees matrix or \texttt{0}\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup.



 The arguments of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape ReesMatrixSemigroupElement}} should be a Rees matrix subsemigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape j}} of the the rows and columns of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, respectively, and an element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} of the underlying semigroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. \texttt{ReesMatrixSemigroupElement} returns the element of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} with row index \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}, underlying element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} in the underlying semigroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, and column index \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape j}}, if such an element exist, if such an element exists.

 The usage of \texttt{ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement} is analogous to that of \texttt{ReesMatrixSemigroupElement}, when \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is a Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup. 

 The row \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}, underlying element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}}, and column \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape j}} of an element \texttt{y} of a Rees matrix (or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix) semigroup can be recovered
from \texttt{y} using \texttt{y[1]}, \texttt{y[2]}, and \texttt{y[3]}, respectively.

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:=Group((1,2,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=[ [ 0, () ], [ (1,3,2), (1,3,2) ] ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(G, mat);|
  <Rees 0-matrix semigroup 2x2 over Group([ (1,2,3) ])>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement(R, 1, (1,2,3), 2);|
  (1,(1,2,3),2)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MultiplicativeZero(R);|
  0
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F03BE707AC7F8A0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup@\texttt{IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup}}
\label{IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Synonym)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup@\texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup}}
\label{IsReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Synonym)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
\texttt{true} or \texttt{false}.



 Every semigroup consisting of elements of a Rees matrix semigroup satisfies
the property \texttt{IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup} and every semigroup of Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup elements
satisfies \texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup}. 

 Note that a subsemigroup of a Rees matrix semigroup is not necessarily a Rees
matrix semigroup. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:=DihedralGroup(32);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=List([1..2], x-> List([1..10], x-> Random(G)));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=ReesMatrixSemigroup(G, mat);|
  <Rees matrix semigroup 10x2 over <pc group of size 32 with
   5 generators>>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S:=Semigroup(GeneratorsOfSemigroup(R));|
  <subsemigroup of 10x2 Rees matrix semigroup with 14 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup(S);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S:=Semigroup(GeneratorsOfSemigroup(R)[1]);|
  <subsemigroup of 10x2 Rees matrix semigroup with 1 generator>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReesMatrixSubsemigroup(S);|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X780BB78A79275244}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsReesMatrixSemigroup@\texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}}
\label{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup@\texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}}
\label{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
\texttt{true} or \texttt{false}.



 A subsemigroup of a Rees matrix semigroup $I\times U\times J$ satisfies \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup} if and only if it is equal to $I'\times U'\times J'$ where $I'\subseteq I$, $J'\subseteq J$, and $U'$ is a subsemigroup of $U$. It can be costly to check that a subsemigroup defined by generators
satisfies \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}. The analogous statements holds for Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix
semigroups. 

 It is not necessarily the case that a simple subsemigroups of Rees matrix
semigroups satisfies \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}. A Rees matrix semigroup is simple if and only if its underlying semigroup is
simple. A finite semigroup is simple if and only if it is isomorphic to a Rees
matrix semigroup over a group; this isomorphism can be obtained explicitly
using \texttt{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup}).

 Similarly, 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple subsemigroups of Rees
0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroups do not have to satisfy \texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}. A Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup with more than 2 elements is
0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple if and only if every row and every column of its
matrix contains a non\texttt{\symbol{45}}zero entry, and its underlying
semigroup is simple. A finite semigroup is 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple if and
only if it is isomorphic to a Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup over
a group; again this isomorphism can be found by using \texttt{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:=PSL(2,5);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=[ [ 0, (), 0, (2,6,3,5,4) ],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@[ (), 0, (), 0 ], [ 0, 0, 0, () ] ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(G, mat);|
  <Rees 0-matrix semigroup 4x3 over Group([ (3,5)(4,6), (1,2,5)
  (3,4,6) ])>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(R);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@U:=ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup(R, [1..3], Group(()), [1..2]);|
  <subsemigroup of 4x3 Rees 0-matrix semigroup with 4 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(U);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:=Semigroup(GeneratorsOfSemigroup(U));|
  <subsemigroup of 4x3 Rees 0-matrix semigroup with 4 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(V);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S:=Semigroup(Transformation([1,1]), Transformation([1,2]));|
  <commutative transformation monoid of degree 2 with 1 generator>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsSimpleSemigroup(S);|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=[[0, One(S), 0, One(S)], [One(S), 0, One(S), 0],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@[0, 0, 0, One(S)]];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(S, mat);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@U:=ReesZeroMatrixSubsemigroup(R, [1..3],|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@Semigroup(Transformation([1,1])), [1..2]);|
  <subsemigroup of 4x3 Rees 0-matrix semigroup with 6 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:=Semigroup(GeneratorsOfSemigroup(U));|
  <subsemigroup of 4x3 Rees 0-matrix semigroup with 6 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(V);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@T:=Semigroup(|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement(R, 3, Transformation( [ 1, 1 ] ), 3),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@ReesZeroMatrixSemigroupElement(R, 2, Transformation( [ 1, 1 ] ), 2));|
  <subsemigroup of 4x3 Rees 0-matrix semigroup with 2 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(T);|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Matrix (for Rees matrix semigroups)}}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7CACF4D686AF1D19}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Matrix({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{Matrix@\texttt{Matrix}!for Rees matrix semigroups}
\label{Matrix:for Rees matrix semigroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MatrixOfReesMatrixSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{MatrixOfReesMatrixSemigroup@\texttt{MatrixOfReesMatrixSemigroup}}
\label{MatrixOfReesMatrixSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MatrixOfReesZeroMatrixSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{MatrixOfReesZeroMatrixSemigroup@\texttt{MatrixOfReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}}
\label{MatrixOfReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A matrix.



 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is a Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup, then \texttt{MatrixOfReesMatrixSemigroup} respectively \texttt{MatrixOfReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} return the matrix used to define multiplication in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. For convenience, one may also abbreviate either to \texttt{Matrix}. 

 More specifically, if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is a Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup, which is a proper
subsemigroup of another such semigroup, then \texttt{Matrix} returns the matrix used to define the Rees matrix (or
0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix) semigroup consisting of the whole family to which
the elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} belong. Thus, for example, a \texttt{1} by \texttt{1} Rees matrix semigroup can have a \texttt{65} by \texttt{15} matrix. 

 Arbitrary subsemigroups of Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix
semigroups do not have a matrix. Such a subsemigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} has a matrix if and only if it satisfies \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}) or \texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:=AlternatingGroup(5);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=[[(), (), ()], [(), (), ()]];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=ReesMatrixSemigroup(G, mat);|
  <Rees matrix semigroup 3x2 over Alt( [ 1 .. 5 ] )>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Matrix(R);|
  [ [ (), (), () ], [ (), (), () ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=ReesMatrixSubsemigroup(R, [1,2], Group(()), [2]);|
  <subsemigroup of 3x2 Rees matrix semigroup with 2 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Matrix(R);|
  [ [ (), (), () ], [ (), (), () ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Rows and columns}}\logpage{[ 51, 9, 9 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X82FC5D6980C66AC4}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Rows({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{Rows@\texttt{Rows}}
\label{Rows}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Columns({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{Columns@\texttt{Columns}}
\label{Columns}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
The rows or columns of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}.



 \texttt{Rows} returns the rows of the Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. Note that the rows of the semigroup correspond to the columns of the matrix
used to define multiplication in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}.

 \texttt{Columns} returns the columns of the Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix
semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. Note that the columns of the semigroup correspond to the rows of the matrix
used to define multiplication in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}.

 Arbitrary subsemigroups of Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix
semigroups do not have rows or columns. Such a subsemigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} has rows and columns if and only if it satisfies \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}) or \texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@G:=Group((1,2,3));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:=List([1..100], x-> List([1..200], x->Random(G)));;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=ReesZeroMatrixSemigroup(G, mat);|
  <Rees 0-matrix semigroup 200x100 over Group([ (1,2,3) ])>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Rows(R);|
  [ 1 .. 200 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Columns(R);|
  [ 1 .. 100 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{UnderlyingSemigroup (for a Rees matrix semigroup)}}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D9719F887AFCF8F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{UnderlyingSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{UnderlyingSemigroup@\texttt{UnderlyingSemigroup}!for a Rees matrix semigroup}
\label{UnderlyingSemigroup:for a Rees matrix semigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{UnderlyingSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{UnderlyingSemigroup@\texttt{UnderlyingSemigroup}!for a Rees 0-matrix semigroup}
\label{UnderlyingSemigroup:for a Rees 0-matrix semigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A semigroup.



 \texttt{UnderlyingSemigroup} returns the underlying semigroup of the Rees matrix or
0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 

 Arbitrary subsemigroups of Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix
semigroups do not have an underlying semigroup. Such a subsemigroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} has an underlying semigroup if and only if it satisfies \texttt{IsReesMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesMatrixSemigroup}) or \texttt{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup} (\ref{IsReesZeroMatrixSemigroup}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S:=Semigroup(Transformation( [ 2, 1, 1, 2, 1 ] ),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@Transformation( [ 3, 4, 3, 4, 4 ] ), Transformation([ 3, 4, 3, 4, 3 ] ),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@Transformation([ 4, 3, 3, 4, 4 ] ) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=Range(IsomorphismReesMatrixSemigroup(S));|
  <Rees matrix semigroup 4x2 over Group([ (1,2) ])>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@UnderlyingSemigroup(R);|
  Group([ (1,2) ])
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AssociatedReesMatrixSemigroupOfDClass}}
\logpage{[ 51, 9, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D1D9A0382064B8F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AssociatedReesMatrixSemigroupOfDClass({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{AssociatedReesMatrixSemigroupOfDClass@\texttt{Associated}\-\texttt{Rees}\-\texttt{Matrix}\-\texttt{Semigroup}\-\texttt{Of}\-\texttt{D}\-\texttt{Class}}
\label{AssociatedReesMatrixSemigroupOfDClass}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\textbf{\indent Returns:\ }
A Rees matrix or 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup.



 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} is a regular $\mathcal{D}$\texttt{\symbol{45}}class of a finite semigroup \texttt{S}, then there is a standard way of associating a Rees matrix semigroup to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} is a subsemigroup of \texttt{S}, then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} is simple and hence is isomorphic to a Rees matrix semigroup. In this case,
the associated Rees matrix semigroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} is just the Rees matrix semigroup isomorphic to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} is not a subsemigroup of \texttt{S}, then we define a semigroup with elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} and a new element \texttt{0} with multiplication of $x,y\in D$ defined by:  
\[ xy=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} x*y\ (\textrm{in }S)&\textrm{if }x*y\in D\\
0&\textrm{if }xy\not\in D. \end{array}\right. \]
   The semigroup thus defined is 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}simple and hence is
isomorphic to a Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup. This semigroup can
also be described as the Rees quotient of the ideal generated by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} by it maximal subideal. The associated Rees matrix semigroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} is just the Rees 0\texttt{\symbol{45}}matrix semigroup isomorphic to the
semigroup defined above. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S:=FullTransformationSemigroup(5);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@D:=GreensDClasses(S)[3];|
  {Transformation( [ 1, 1, 1, 2, 3 ] )}
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AssociatedReesMatrixSemigroupOfDClass(D);|
  <Rees 0-matrix semigroup 25x10 over Group([ (1,2)(3,5)(4,6), (1,3)
  (2,4)(5,6) ])>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  }

            
\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Finitely Presented Semigroups and Monoids}}\label{Finitely Presented Semigroups and Monoids}
\logpage{[ 52, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7DE7C52A7C4BDADE}{}
{
  A \emph{finitely presented semigroup} (resp. \emph{finitely presented monoid}) is a quotient of a free semigroup (resp. free monoid) on a finite number of
generators over a finitely generated congruence on the free semigroup (resp.
free monoid). 

 Finitely presented semigroups are obtained by factoring a free semigroup by a
set of relations (a generating set for the congruence), i.e., a set of pairs
of words in the free semigroup. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := FreeSemigroup( "a", "b" );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x := GeneratorsOfSemigroup( f );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@s := f / [ [ x[1] * x[2], x[2] * x[1] ] ];|
  <fp semigroup on the generators [ a, b ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfSemigroup( s );|
  [ a, b ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RelationsOfFpSemigroup( s );|
  [ [ a*b, b*a ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

 Finitely presented monoids are obtained by factoring a free monoid by a set of
relations, i.e. a set of pairs of words in the free monoid. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := FreeMonoid( "a", "b" );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x := GeneratorsOfMonoid( f );|
  [ a, b ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@e := Identity( f );|
  <identity ...>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@m := f / [ [ x[1] * x[2], e ] ];|
  <fp monoid on the generators [ a, b ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RelationsOfFpMonoid( m );|
  [ [ a*b, <identity ...> ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

 Notice that for \textsf{GAP} a finitely presented monoid is not a finitely presented semigroup. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsFpSemigroup( m );|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 

 However, one can build a finitely presented semigroup isomorphic to that
finitely presented monoid (see \texttt{IsomorphismFpSemigroup} (\ref{IsomorphismFpSemigroup})). 

 Also note that is not possible to refer to the generators by their names.
These names are not variables, but just display figures. So, if one wants to
access the generators by their names, one first has to introduce the
respective variables and to assign the generators to them. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Unbind( a );|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := FreeSemigroup( "a", "b" );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@s := f / [ [ f.1 * f.2, f.2 * f.1 ] ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a;|
  Error, Variable: 'a' must have a value
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a := s.1;|
  a
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a in f;|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a in s;|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 

 The generators of the free semigroup (resp. free monoid) are different from
the generators of the finitely presented semigroup (resp. finitely presented
monoid) (even though they are displayed by the same names). This means that
words in the generators of the free semigroup (resp. free monoid) are not
elements of the finitely presented semigroup (resp. finitely presented
monoid). Conversely elements of the finitely presented semigroup (resp.
finitely presented monoid) are not words of the free semigroup (resp. free
monoid). 

 Calculations comparing elements of a finitely presented semigroup may run into
problems: there are finitely presented semigroups for which no algorithm
exists (it is known that no such algorithm can exist) that will tell for two
arbitrary words in the generators whether the corresponding elements in the
finitely presented semigroup are equal. Therefore the methods used by \textsf{GAP} to compute in finitely presented semigroups may run into warning errors, run
out of memory or run forever. If the finitely presented semigroup is (by
theory) known to be finite the algorithms are guaranteed to terminate (if
there is sufficient memory available), but the time needed for the calculation
cannot be bounded a priori. The same can be said for monoids. (See \ref{Rewriting Systems and the Knuth-Bendix Procedure}.) 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@b := s.2;;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a*b = a^5;|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a^5 * b^2 * a = a^6 * b^2;|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 

 Note that elements of a finitely presented semigroup (or monoid) are not
printed in a unique way: 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a^5 * b^2 * a;|
  a^5*b^2*a
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a^6 * b^2;|
  a^6*b^2
\end{Verbatim}
  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup (Filter)}}\label{sect:IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup}
\logpage{[ 52, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X78C80F1A84C58E1E}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 52, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8496E23C80453C33}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape t})\index{IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup@\texttt{IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup}}
\label{IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSubmonoidFpMonoid({\mdseries\slshape t})\index{IsSubmonoidFpMonoid@\texttt{IsSubmonoidFpMonoid}}
\label{IsSubmonoidFpMonoid}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 The first function returns true if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape t}} is a finitely presented semigroup or a subsemigroup of a finitely presented
semigroup. The second function does the equivalent thing for monoids.
(Generally speaking, such a subsemigroup or monoid can be constructed with \texttt{Semigroup(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}})} or \texttt{Monoid(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}})}, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} is a list of elements of a finitely presented semigroup or monoid.) 

 A submonoid of a monoid has the same identity as the monoid. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsFpSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 52, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8239EF2B853411E9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFpSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape s})\index{IsFpSemigroup@\texttt{IsFpSemigroup}}
\label{IsFpSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFpMonoid({\mdseries\slshape m})\index{IsFpMonoid@\texttt{IsFpMonoid}}
\label{IsFpMonoid}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 The first function is a synonym for \texttt{IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}})} and \texttt{IsWholeFamily(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}})} (this is because a subsemigroup of a finitely presented semigroup is not
necessarily finitely presented). 

 Similarly, the second function is a synonym for \texttt{IsSubmonoidFpMonoid(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}})} and \texttt{IsWholeFamily(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}})}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsElementOfFpSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 52, 1, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81ABBE997A4C19B7}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsElementOfFpSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape elm})\index{IsElementOfFpSemigroup@\texttt{IsElementOfFpSemigroup}}
\label{IsElementOfFpSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsElementOfFpMonoid({\mdseries\slshape elm})\index{IsElementOfFpMonoid@\texttt{IsElementOfFpMonoid}}
\label{IsElementOfFpMonoid}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 returns true if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is an element of a finitely presented semigroup or monoid. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := FreeSemigroup( "a", "b" );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsFpSemigroup( f );|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@s := f / [ [ f.1^2, f.2^2 ] ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsFpSemigroup( s );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@t := Semigroup( [ s.1^2 ] );|
  <commutative semigroup with 1 generator>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup( t );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup( s );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsSubsemigroupFpSemigroup( f );|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsElementOfFpSemigroup( t.1^3 );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement}}
\logpage{[ 52, 1, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DC8A5D380AFE5DB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement({\mdseries\slshape elm})\index{FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement@\texttt{FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement}}
\label{FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns the finitely presented group, monoid or semigroup to which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} belongs. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@s = FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement( s.1 );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@s = FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement( t.1 );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f := FreeMonoid( 2 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@m := f / [ [ f.1^2, f.2^2 ] ];|
  <fp monoid on the generators [ m1, m2 ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@m = FpGrpMonSmgOfFpGrpMonSmgElement( m.1 * m.2 );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Creating Finitely Presented Semigroups and Monoids}}\label{Creating Finitely Presented Semigroups and Monoids}
\logpage{[ 52, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X865E230B83982E66}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/ (for a free semigroup or monoid and a list of pairs of elements)}}
\logpage{[ 52, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X84745EC6789FEB4C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/({\mdseries\slshape F, rels})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/}!for a free semigroup or monoid and a list of pairs of elements}
\label{bSlash/:for a free semigroup or monoid and a list of pairs of elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\


 \index{quotient!of free semigroup} \index{quotient!of free monoid} creates a finitely presented semigroup or monoid given by the presentation $\langle \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} \mid \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rels}} \rangle$ where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} are the generators of the free semigroup or free monoid \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}, and the relations \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rels}} are entered as pairs of words in the generators of the free semigroup or free
monoid. 

 The same result is obtained with the infix operator \texttt{/}, i.e. as \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} \texttt{/} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rels}}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@fs := FreeSemigroup( 3 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x := GeneratorsOfSemigroup( fs );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@s := fs / [ [ x[1] * x[2] * x[1], x[1] ], [ x[2]^4, x[1] ] ];|
  <fp semigroup on the generators [ s1, s2, s3 ]>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FactorFreeSemigroupByRelations}}
\logpage{[ 52, 2, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X822F04B2833BE254}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FactorFreeSemigroupByRelations({\mdseries\slshape f, rels})\index{FactorFreeSemigroupByRelations@\texttt{FactorFreeSemigroupByRelations}}
\label{FactorFreeSemigroupByRelations}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FactorFreeMonoidByRelations({\mdseries\slshape f, rels})\index{FactorFreeMonoidByRelations@\texttt{FactorFreeMonoidByRelations}}
\label{FactorFreeMonoidByRelations}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 for a free semigroup or free monoid \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape f}} and a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rels}} of pairs of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape f}}. Returns the finitely presented semigroup or monoid which is the quotient of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape f}} by the least congruence on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape f}} generated by the pairs in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape rels}}. 

 Users should be aware that much of the code described in this chapter is in
need of substantial revision. In particular, the two functions described here
are \emph{not} called by the operation \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}/} of the previous subsection, and so are liable to be removed in due course. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@fm := FreeMonoid( 3 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@y := GeneratorsOfMonoid( fm );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@m := FactorFreeMonoidByRelations( fm,|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@          [ [ y[1] * y[2] * y[1], y[1] ],[ y[2]^4, y[1] ] ] );|
  <fp monoid on the generators [ m1, m2, m3 ]>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsomorphismFpSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 52, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X869F966B8196F28C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsomorphismFpSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape m})\index{IsomorphismFpSemigroup@\texttt{IsomorphismFpSemigroup}}
\label{IsomorphismFpSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsomorphismFpMonoid({\mdseries\slshape g})\index{IsomorphismFpMonoid@\texttt{IsomorphismFpMonoid}}
\label{IsomorphismFpMonoid}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 for a finitely presented monoid \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} or a finitely presented group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}}. Returns an isomorphism from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} or \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape g}} to a finitely presented semigroup or monoid. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@phis := IsomorphismFpSemigroup( m );|
  MappingByFunction( <fp monoid on the generators
  [ m1, m2, m3 ]>, <fp semigroup on the generators [ <identity ...>, m1, m2, m3
   ]>, function( x ) ... end, function( x ) ... end )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@fg := FreeGroup( 2 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g := fg / [ fg.1^4, fg.2^5 ];|
  <fp group on the generators [ f1, f2 ]>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@phim := IsomorphismFpMonoid( g );|
  MappingByFunction( <fp group on the generators
  [ f1, f2 ]>, <fp monoid on the generators [ f1, f1^-1, f2, f2^-1
   ]>, function( x ) ... end, function( x ) ... end )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Comparison of Elements of Finitely Presented Semigroups}}\label{Comparison of Elements of Finitely Presented Semigroups}
\logpage{[ 52, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X85E7C8407C9D5FBE}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{\texttt{\symbol{92}}= (for two elements in a f.p. semigroup)}}
\logpage{[ 52, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DD9D81F863EBE31}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}=({\mdseries\slshape a, b})\index{\texttt{\symbol{92}}=@\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}=}!for two elements in a f.p. semigroup}
\label{bSlash=:for two elements in a f.p. semigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\


 \index{comparison!fp semigroup elements} Two elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape a}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape b}} of a finitely presented semigroup are equal if they are equal in the
semigroup. Nevertheless they may be represented as different words in the
generators. Because of the fundamental problems mentioned in the introduction
to this chapter such a test may take a very long time and cannot be guaranteed
to finish (see \ref{Rewriting Systems and the Knuth-Bendix Procedure}). }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Preimages in the Free Semigroup or Monoid}}\label{Preimages in the Free Semigroup or Monoid}
\logpage{[ 52, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7CD806CA7E0A1438}{}
{
  Elements of a finitely presented semigroup or monoid are not words, but are
represented using a word from the free semigroup or free monoid as
representative. 

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{UnderlyingElement (of an element in a fp semigroup or monoid)}}
\logpage{[ 52, 4, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X784B3DB686E7080C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{UnderlyingElement({\mdseries\slshape elm})\index{UnderlyingElement@\texttt{UnderlyingElement}!of an element in a fp semigroup or monoid}
\label{UnderlyingElement:of an element in a fp semigroup or monoid}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 for an element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} of a finitely presented semigroup or monoid. Returns the word from the free
semigroup or free monoid that is used as a representative for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@genm := GeneratorsOfMonoid( m );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@e := genm[2]^4;|
  m2^4
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsWord( e );|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ue := UnderlyingElement( e );|
  m2^4
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsWord( ue );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ElementOfFpSemigroup}}
\logpage{[ 52, 4, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X847012347856C55E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ElementOfFpSemigroup({\mdseries\slshape fam, word})\index{ElementOfFpSemigroup@\texttt{ElementOfFpSemigroup}}
\label{ElementOfFpSemigroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ElementOfFpMonoid({\mdseries\slshape fam, word})\index{ElementOfFpMonoid@\texttt{ElementOfFpMonoid}}
\label{ElementOfFpMonoid}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 for a family \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape fam}} of elements of a finitely presented semigroup or monoid and a word \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape word}} in the free generators underlying this finitely presented semigroup or monoid.
Returns the element of the finitely presented semigroup or monoid with the
representative \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape word}} in the free semigroup or free monoid. These operations are inverse to \texttt{UnderlyingElement}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@fam := FamilyObj( genm[1] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@w := y[1]^3 * y[2]^4 * y[3]^5;|
  m1^3*m2^4*m3^5
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ew := ElementOfFpMonoid( fam, w );|
  m1^3*m2^4*m3^5
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ew in fm;|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ew in m;|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@w = UnderlyingElement( ew );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }
