{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsAdditivelyCommutative}}
\logpage{[ 55, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82D471327A9CA960}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAdditivelyCommutative({\mdseries\slshape A})\index{IsAdditivelyCommutative@\texttt{IsAdditivelyCommutative}}
\label{IsAdditivelyCommutative}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive magma \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} in \textsf{GAP} is \emph{additively commutative} if for all elements $a, b \in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}}$ the equality $a + b = b + a$ holds. 

 Note that the commutativity of the \emph{multiplication} \texttt{*} in a multiplicative structure can be tested with \texttt{IsCommutative} (\ref{IsCommutative}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagma}}
\logpage{[ 55, 3, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X804B178884002A40}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagma({\mdseries\slshape A})\index{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagma@\texttt{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagma}}
\label{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagma}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfAdditiveMagma({\mdseries\slshape A})\index{GeneratorsOfAdditiveMagma@\texttt{GeneratorsOfAdditiveMagma}}
\label{GeneratorsOfAdditiveMagma}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is a list of elements of the near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive magma \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} that generates \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} as a near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive magma, that is, the closure of this list
under addition is \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagmaWithZero}}
\logpage{[ 55, 3, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EB9ABF880DCAE01}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagmaWithZero({\mdseries\slshape A})\index{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagmaWithZero@\texttt{Generators}\-\texttt{Of}\-\texttt{Near}\-\texttt{Additive}\-\texttt{Magma}\-\texttt{With}\-\texttt{Zero}}
\label{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveMagmaWithZero}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfAdditiveMagmaWithZero({\mdseries\slshape A})\index{GeneratorsOfAdditiveMagmaWithZero@\texttt{GeneratorsOfAdditiveMagmaWithZero}}
\label{GeneratorsOfAdditiveMagmaWithZero}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is a list of elements of the near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive
magma\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}zero \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} that generates \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} as a near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive
magma\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}zero, that is, the closure of
this list under addition and \texttt{Zero} (\ref{Zero}) is \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveGroup}}
\logpage{[ 55, 3, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EA15714795D71CF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveGroup({\mdseries\slshape A})\index{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveGroup@\texttt{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveGroup}}
\label{GeneratorsOfNearAdditiveGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfAdditiveGroup({\mdseries\slshape A})\index{GeneratorsOfAdditiveGroup@\texttt{GeneratorsOfAdditiveGroup}}
\label{GeneratorsOfAdditiveGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is a list of elements of the near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} that generates \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} as a near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive group, that is, the closure of this list
under addition, taking the zero element, and taking additive inverses
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{AdditiveInverse} (\ref{AdditiveInverse})) is \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AdditiveNeutralElement}}
\logpage{[ 55, 3, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X851EA2E67F0C9A75}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AdditiveNeutralElement({\mdseries\slshape A})\index{AdditiveNeutralElement@\texttt{AdditiveNeutralElement}}
\label{AdditiveNeutralElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns the element $z$ in the near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive magma \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} with the property that $z + a = a = a + z$ holds for all $a \in$ \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}}, if such an element exists. Otherwise \texttt{fail} is returned. 

 A near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive magma that is not a
near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive
magma\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}zero can have an additive
neutral element $z$; in this case, $z$ \emph{cannot} be obtained as \texttt{Zero( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} )} or as \texttt{0*}$a$ for an element $a$ in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}}, see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Zero} (\ref{Zero}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TrivialSubnearAdditiveMagmaWithZero}}
\logpage{[ 55, 3, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78FB0A5C86DC86F9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TrivialSubnearAdditiveMagmaWithZero({\mdseries\slshape A})\index{TrivialSubnearAdditiveMagmaWithZero@\texttt{TrivialSubnearAdditiveMagmaWithZero}}
\label{TrivialSubnearAdditiveMagmaWithZero}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the additive magma\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}zero that has
the zero of the near\texttt{\symbol{45}}additive
magma\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}zero \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} as its only element. }

 }

}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ShowAdditionTable}}
\logpage{[ 55, 4, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8142D994794B700A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ShowAdditionTable({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{ShowAdditionTable@\texttt{ShowAdditionTable}}
\label{ShowAdditionTable}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ShowMultiplicationTable({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{ShowMultiplicationTable@\texttt{ShowMultiplicationTable}}
\label{ShowMultiplicationTable}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For a structure \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} with an addition given by \texttt{+}, respectively a structure \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} with a multiplication given by \texttt{*}, this command displays the addition (multiplication) table of the structure
in a pretty way. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@B,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>B !gapinput@ShowAdditionTable(GF(4));B
  +        | 0*Z(2)   Z(2)^0   Z(2^2)   Z(2^2)^2
  ---------+------------------------------------
  0*Z(2)   | 0*Z(2)   Z(2)^0   Z(2^2)   Z(2^2)^2
  Z(2)^0   | Z(2)^0   0*Z(2)   Z(2^2)^2 Z(2^2)
  Z(2^2)   | Z(2^2)   Z(2^2)^2 0*Z(2)   Z(2)^0
  Z(2^2)^2 | Z(2^2)^2 Z(2^2)   Z(2)^0   0*Z(2)
  
  !gapprompt@gap>B !gapinput@ShowMultiplicationTable(GF(4));B
  *        | 0*Z(2)   Z(2)^0   Z(2^2)   Z(2^2)^2
  ---------+------------------------------------
  0*Z(2)   | 0*Z(2)   0*Z(2)   0*Z(2)   0*Z(2)
  Z(2)^0   | 0*Z(2)   Z(2)^0   Z(2^2)   Z(2^2)^2
  Z(2^2)   | 0*Z(2)   Z(2^2)   Z(2^2)^2 Z(2)^0
  Z(2^2)^2 | 0*Z(2)   Z(2^2)^2 Z(2)^0   Z(2^2)
  
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

 }

            
\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Rings}}\label{Rings}
\logpage{[ 56, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X81897F6082CACB59}{}
{
  This chapter deals with domains that are additive groups (see \texttt{IsAdditiveGroup} (\ref{IsAdditiveGroup}) closed under multiplication \texttt{*}. Such a domain, if \texttt{*} and \texttt{+} are distributive, is called a \emph{ring} in \textsf{GAP}. Each division ring, field (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Fields and Division Rings}), or algebra (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Algebras}) is a ring. Important examples of rings are the integers (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Integers}) and matrix rings.   

 In the case of a \emph{ring\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one}, additional multiplicative structure is present, see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsRingWithOne} (\ref{IsRingWithOne}). There is a little support in \textsf{GAP} for rings that have no additional structure: it is possible to perform some
computations for small finite rings; infinite rings are handled by \textsf{GAP} in an acceptable way in the case that they are algebras. 

 Also, the \textsf{SONATA} package provides support for near\texttt{\symbol{45}}rings, and a related
functionality for multiplicative semigroups of near\texttt{\symbol{45}}rings
is available in the \textsf{Smallsemi} package. 

 Several functions for ring elements, such as \texttt{IsPrime} (\ref{IsPrime}) and \texttt{Factors} (\ref{Factors}), are defined only relative to a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, which can be entered as an optional argument; if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is omitted then a \emph{default ring} is formed from the ring elements given as arguments, see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements}).  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Generating Rings}}\label{Generating Rings}
\logpage{[ 56, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X839FC48687C25FCD}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRing}}
\logpage{[ 56, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80FD843C8221DAC9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRing({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsRing@\texttt{IsRing}}
\label{IsRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 A \emph{ring} in \textsf{GAP} is an additive group (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsAdditiveGroup} (\ref{IsAdditiveGroup})) that is also a magma (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsMagma} (\ref{IsMagma})), such that addition \texttt{+} and multiplication \texttt{*} are distributive, see \texttt{IsDistributive} (\ref{IsDistributive}). 

 The multiplication need \emph{not} be associative (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsAssociative} (\ref{IsAssociative})). For example, a Lie algebra (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Lie Algebras}) is regarded as a ring in \textsf{GAP}. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Ring}}\logpage{[ 56, 1, 2 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X820B172A860A5B1A}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Ring({\mdseries\slshape r, s, ...})\index{Ring@\texttt{Ring}!for ring elements}
\label{Ring:for ring elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Ring({\mdseries\slshape coll})\index{Ring@\texttt{Ring}!for a collection}
\label{Ring:for a collection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 In the first form \texttt{Ring} returns the smallest ring that contains all the elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}}, $\ldots$ In the second form \texttt{Ring} returns the smallest ring that contains all the elements in the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}}. If any element is not an element of a ring or if the elements lie in no
common ring an error is raised. 

 \texttt{Ring} differs from \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements}) in that it returns the smallest ring in which the elements lie, while \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements}) may return a larger ring if that makes sense. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Ring( 2, E(4) );|
  <ring with 2 generators>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DefaultRing}}\logpage{[ 56, 1, 3 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X83AFFCC77DE6ABDA}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DefaultRing({\mdseries\slshape r, s, ...})\index{DefaultRing@\texttt{DefaultRing}!for ring elements}
\label{DefaultRing:for ring elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DefaultRing({\mdseries\slshape coll})\index{DefaultRing@\texttt{DefaultRing}!for a collection}
\label{DefaultRing:for a collection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 In the first form \texttt{DefaultRing} returns a ring that contains all the elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}}, $\ldots$ etc. In the second form \texttt{DefaultRing} returns a ring that contains all the elements in the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}}. If any element is not an element of a ring or if the elements lie in no
common ring an error is raised. 

 The ring returned by \texttt{DefaultRing} need not be the smallest ring in which the elements lie. For example for
elements from cyclotomic fields, \texttt{DefaultRing} may return the ring of integers of the smallest cyclotomic field in which the
elements lie, which need not be the smallest ring overall, because the
elements may in fact lie in a smaller number field which is itself not a
cyclotomic field. 

 (For the exact definition of the default ring of a certain type of elements,
look at the corresponding method installation.) 

 \texttt{DefaultRing} is used by ring functions such as \texttt{Quotient} (\ref{Quotient}), \texttt{IsPrime} (\ref{IsPrime}), \texttt{Factors} (\ref{Factors}), or \texttt{Gcd} (\ref{Gcd:for (a ring and) several elements}) if no explicit ring is given. 

 \texttt{Ring} (\ref{Ring:for ring elements}) differs from \texttt{DefaultRing} in that it returns the smallest ring in which the elements lie, while \texttt{DefaultRing} may return a larger ring if that makes sense. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DefaultRing( 2, E(4) );|
  GaussianIntegers
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RingByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 56, 1, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D736E027DFD8961}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RingByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape C})\index{RingByGenerators@\texttt{RingByGenerators}}
\label{RingByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{RingByGenerators} returns the ring generated by the elements in the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}}, i.{\nobreakspace}e., the closure of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}} under addition, multiplication, and taking additive inverses. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RingByGenerators([ 2, E(4) ]);|
  <ring with 2 generators>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DefaultRingByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 56, 1, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X839E609480495E27}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DefaultRingByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape coll})\index{DefaultRingByGenerators@\texttt{DefaultRingByGenerators}}
\label{DefaultRingByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 For a collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}}, returns a default ring in which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} is contained. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DefaultRingByGenerators([ 2, E(4) ]);|
  GaussianIntegers
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfRing}}
\logpage{[ 56, 1, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D0428D87E63288C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfRing({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{GeneratorsOfRing@\texttt{GeneratorsOfRing}}
\label{GeneratorsOfRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 \texttt{GeneratorsOfRing} returns a list of elements such that the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is the closure of these elements under addition, multiplication, and taking
additive inverses. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=Ring( 2, 1/2 );|
  <ring with 2 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfRing( R );|
  [ 2, 1/2 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Subring}}
\logpage{[ 56, 1, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X860E4AC78520D27E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Subring({\mdseries\slshape R, gens})\index{Subring@\texttt{Subring}}
\label{Subring}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SubringNC({\mdseries\slshape R, gens})\index{SubringNC@\texttt{SubringNC}}
\label{SubringNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the ring with parent \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} generated by the elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. When the second form, \texttt{SubringNC} is used, it is \emph{not} checked whether all elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} lie in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:= Integers;|
  Integers
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S:= Subring( R, [ 4, 6 ] );|
  <ring with 1 generator>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Parent( S );|
  Integers
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ClosureRing}}\logpage{[ 56, 1, 8 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X819B0AFE79C78C34}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ClosureRing({\mdseries\slshape R, r})\index{ClosureRing@\texttt{ClosureRing}!for a ring and a ring element}
\label{ClosureRing:for a ring and a ring element}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ClosureRing({\mdseries\slshape R, S})\index{ClosureRing@\texttt{ClosureRing}!for two rings}
\label{ClosureRing:for two rings}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 For a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} and either an element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} of its elements family or a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}, \texttt{ClosureRing} returns the ring generated by both arguments. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ClosureRing( Integers, E(4) );|
  <ring-with-one, with 2 generators>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Quotient}}
\logpage{[ 56, 1, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8350500B8576F833}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Quotient({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r, s})\index{Quotient@\texttt{Quotient}}
\label{Quotient}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{Quotient} returns a (right) quotient of the two ring elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in their default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). More specifically, it returns a ring element $q$ such that $r = q * s$ holds, or \texttt{fail} if no such elements exists in the respective ring. 

 The result may not be unique if the ring contains zero divisors. 

 (To perform the division in the quotient field of a ring, use the quotient
operator \texttt{/}.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Quotient( 2, 3 );|
  fail
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Quotient( 6, 3 );|
  2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Ideals of Rings}}\label{Ideals of Rings}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8776C3F97A731E70}{}
{
  A \emph{left ideal} in a ring $R$ is a subring of $R$ that is closed under multiplication with elements of $R$ from the left. 

 A \emph{right ideal} in a ring $R$ is a subring of $R$ that is closed under multiplication with elements of $R$ from the right. 

 A \emph{two\texttt{\symbol{45}}sided ideal} or simply \emph{ideal} in a ring $R$ is both a left ideal and a right ideal in $R$. 

 So being a (left/right/two\texttt{\symbol{45}}sided) ideal is not a property
of a domain but refers to the acting ring(s). Hence we must ask,
e.{\nobreakspace}g., \texttt{IsIdeal( }$R, I$\texttt{ )} if we want to know whether the ring $I$ is an ideal in the ring $R$. The property \texttt{IsTwoSidedIdealInParent} (\ref{IsTwoSidedIdealInParent}) can be used to store whether a ring is an ideal in its parent. 

 (Whenever the term \texttt{"Ideal"} occurs in an identifier without a specifying prefix \texttt{"Left"} or \texttt{"Right"}, this means the same as \texttt{"TwoSidedIdeal"}. Conversely, any occurrence of \texttt{"TwoSidedIdeal"} can be substituted by \texttt{"Ideal"}.) 

 For any of the above kinds of ideals, there is a notion of generators, namely \texttt{GeneratorsOfLeftIdeal} (\ref{GeneratorsOfLeftIdeal}), \texttt{GeneratorsOfRightIdeal} (\ref{GeneratorsOfRightIdeal}), and \texttt{GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal} (\ref{GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal}). The acting rings can be accessed as \texttt{LeftActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{LeftActingRingOfIdeal}) and \texttt{RightActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{RightActingRingOfIdeal}), respectively. Note that ideals are detected from known values of these
attributes, especially it is assumed that whenever a domain has both a left
and a right acting ring then these two are equal. 

 Note that we cannot use \texttt{LeftActingDomain} (\ref{LeftActingDomain}) and \texttt{RightActingDomain} here, since ideals in algebras are themselves vector spaces, and such a space
can of course also be a module for an action from the right. In order to make
the usual vector space functionality automatically available for ideals, we
have to distinguish the left and right module structure from the additional
closure properties of the ideal. 

 Further note that the attributes denoting ideal generators and acting ring are
used to create ideals if this is explicitly wanted, but the ideal relation in
the sense of \texttt{IsTwoSidedIdeal} (\ref{IsTwoSidedIdeal}) is of course independent of the presence of the attribute values. 

 Ideals are constructed with \texttt{LeftIdeal} (\ref{LeftIdeal}), \texttt{RightIdeal} (\ref{RightIdeal}), \texttt{TwoSidedIdeal} (\ref{TwoSidedIdeal}). Principal ideals of the form $x * R$, $R * x$, $R * x * R$ can also be constructed with a simple multiplication. 

 Currently many methods for dealing with ideals need linear algebra to work, so
they are mainly applicable to ideals in algebras. 

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TwoSidedIdeal}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C486A7C821D79F0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TwoSidedIdeal({\mdseries\slshape R, gens[, "basis"]})\index{TwoSidedIdeal@\texttt{TwoSidedIdeal}}
\label{TwoSidedIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Ideal({\mdseries\slshape R, gens[, "basis"]})\index{Ideal@\texttt{Ideal}}
\label{Ideal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LeftIdeal({\mdseries\slshape R, gens[, "basis"]})\index{LeftIdeal@\texttt{LeftIdeal}}
\label{LeftIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RightIdeal({\mdseries\slshape R, gens[, "basis"]})\index{RightIdeal@\texttt{RightIdeal}}
\label{RightIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} be a ring, and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} a list of collection of elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. \texttt{TwoSidedIdeal}, \texttt{LeftIdeal}, and \texttt{RightIdeal} return the two\texttt{\symbol{45}}sided, left, or right ideal, respectively, $I$ in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} that is generated by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. The ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} can be accessed as \texttt{LeftActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{LeftActingRingOfIdeal}) or \texttt{RightActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{RightActingRingOfIdeal}) (or both) of $I$. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is a left $F$\texttt{\symbol{45}}module then also $I$ is a left $F$\texttt{\symbol{45}}module, in particular the \texttt{LeftActingDomain} (\ref{LeftActingDomain}) values of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} and $I$ are equal. 

 If the optional argument \texttt{"basis"} is given then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} are assumed to be a list of basis vectors of $I$ viewed as a free $F$\texttt{\symbol{45}}module. (This is mainly applicable to ideals in algebras.)
In this case, it is \emph{not} checked whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} really is linearly independent and whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} is a subset of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 

 \texttt{Ideal} is simply a synonym of \texttt{TwoSidedIdeal}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:= Integers;;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@I:= Ideal( R, [ 2 ] );|
  <two-sided ideal in Integers, (1 generator)>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TwoSidedIdealNC}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C8E196478C7431A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TwoSidedIdealNC({\mdseries\slshape R, gens[, "basis"]})\index{TwoSidedIdealNC@\texttt{TwoSidedIdealNC}}
\label{TwoSidedIdealNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IdealNC({\mdseries\slshape R, gens[, "basis"]})\index{IdealNC@\texttt{IdealNC}}
\label{IdealNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LeftIdealNC({\mdseries\slshape R, gens[, "basis"]})\index{LeftIdealNC@\texttt{LeftIdealNC}}
\label{LeftIdealNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RightIdealNC({\mdseries\slshape R, gens[, "basis"]})\index{RightIdealNC@\texttt{RightIdealNC}}
\label{RightIdealNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 The effects of \texttt{TwoSidedIdealNC}, \texttt{LeftIdealNC}, and \texttt{RightIdealNC} are the same as \texttt{TwoSidedIdeal} (\ref{TwoSidedIdeal}), \texttt{LeftIdeal} (\ref{LeftIdeal}), and \texttt{RightIdeal} (\ref{RightIdeal}), respectively, but they do not check whether all entries of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} lie in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsTwoSidedIdeal}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DF623847B338850}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsTwoSidedIdeal({\mdseries\slshape R, I})\index{IsTwoSidedIdeal@\texttt{IsTwoSidedIdeal}}
\label{IsTwoSidedIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLeftIdeal({\mdseries\slshape R, I})\index{IsLeftIdeal@\texttt{IsLeftIdeal}}
\label{IsLeftIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRightIdeal({\mdseries\slshape R, I})\index{IsRightIdeal@\texttt{IsRightIdeal}}
\label{IsRightIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsTwoSidedIdealInParent({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{IsTwoSidedIdealInParent@\texttt{IsTwoSidedIdealInParent}}
\label{IsTwoSidedIdealInParent}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLeftIdealInParent({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{IsLeftIdealInParent@\texttt{IsLeftIdealInParent}}
\label{IsLeftIdealInParent}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRightIdealInParent({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{IsRightIdealInParent@\texttt{IsRightIdealInParent}}
\label{IsRightIdealInParent}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 The properties \texttt{IsTwoSidedIdealInParent} etc., are attributes of the ideal, and once known they are stored in the
ideal. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@A:= FullMatrixAlgebra( Rationals, 3 );|
  ( Rationals^[ 3, 3 ] )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@I:= Ideal( A, [ Random( A ) ] );|
  <two-sided ideal in ( Rationals^[ 3, 3 ] ), (1 generator)>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsTwoSidedIdeal( A, I );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TwoSidedIdealByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86C998178690DAE0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TwoSidedIdealByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape R, gens})\index{TwoSidedIdealByGenerators@\texttt{TwoSidedIdealByGenerators}}
\label{TwoSidedIdealByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IdealByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape R, gens})\index{IdealByGenerators@\texttt{IdealByGenerators}}
\label{IdealByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{TwoSidedIdealByGenerators} returns the ring that is generated by the elements of the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} under addition, multiplication, and multiplication with elements of the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} from the left and from the right. 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} can be accessed by \texttt{LeftActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{LeftActingRingOfIdeal}) or \texttt{RightActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{RightActingRingOfIdeal}), \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} can be accessed by \texttt{GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal} (\ref{GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LeftIdealByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82D8B07281EB0AC7}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LeftIdealByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape R, gens})\index{LeftIdealByGenerators@\texttt{LeftIdealByGenerators}}
\label{LeftIdealByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{LeftIdealByGenerators} returns the ring that is generated by the elements of the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} under addition, multiplication, and multiplication with elements of the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} from the left. 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} can be accessed by \texttt{LeftActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{LeftActingRingOfIdeal}), \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} can be accessed by \texttt{GeneratorsOfLeftIdeal} (\ref{GeneratorsOfLeftIdeal}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RightIdealByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X858EAEAF87751428}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RightIdealByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape R, gens})\index{RightIdealByGenerators@\texttt{RightIdealByGenerators}}
\label{RightIdealByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{RightIdealByGenerators} returns the ring that is generated by the elements of the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} under addition, multiplication, and multiplication with elements of the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} from the right. 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} can be accessed by \texttt{RightActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{RightActingRingOfIdeal}), \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} can be accessed by \texttt{GeneratorsOfRightIdeal} (\ref{GeneratorsOfRightIdeal}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86AAF5F9800E97EE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal@\texttt{GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal}}
\label{GeneratorsOfTwoSidedIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfIdeal({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{GeneratorsOfIdeal@\texttt{GeneratorsOfIdeal}}
\label{GeneratorsOfIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is a list of generators for the ideal \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape I}}, with respect to the action of the rings that are stored as the values of \texttt{LeftActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{LeftActingRingOfIdeal}) and \texttt{RightActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{RightActingRingOfIdeal}), from the left and from the right, respectively. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@A:= FullMatrixAlgebra( Rationals, 3 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@I:= Ideal( A, [ One( A ) ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfIdeal( I );|
  [ [ [ 1, 0, 0 ], [ 0, 1, 0 ], [ 0, 0, 1 ] ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfLeftIdeal}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B20BD2B7FAFBD64}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfLeftIdeal({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{GeneratorsOfLeftIdeal@\texttt{GeneratorsOfLeftIdeal}}
\label{GeneratorsOfLeftIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is a list of generators for the left ideal \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape I}}, with respect to the action from the left of the ring that is stored as the
value of \texttt{LeftActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{LeftActingRingOfIdeal}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfRightIdeal}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80F2239F8653FF74}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfRightIdeal({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{GeneratorsOfRightIdeal@\texttt{GeneratorsOfRightIdeal}}
\label{GeneratorsOfRightIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is a list of generators for the right ideal \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape I}}, with respect to the action from the right of the ring that is stored as the
value of \texttt{RightActingRingOfIdeal} (\ref{RightActingRingOfIdeal}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LeftActingRingOfIdeal}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81D81D027C2F8D06}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LeftActingRingOfIdeal({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{LeftActingRingOfIdeal@\texttt{LeftActingRingOfIdeal}}
\label{LeftActingRingOfIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RightActingRingOfIdeal({\mdseries\slshape I})\index{RightActingRingOfIdeal@\texttt{RightActingRingOfIdeal}}
\label{RightActingRingOfIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns the left (resp. right) acting ring of an ideal \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape I}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AsLeftIdeal}}
\logpage{[ 56, 2, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83D9D7408706B69A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AsLeftIdeal({\mdseries\slshape R, S})\index{AsLeftIdeal@\texttt{AsLeftIdeal}}
\label{AsLeftIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AsRightIdeal({\mdseries\slshape R, S})\index{AsRightIdeal@\texttt{AsRightIdeal}}
\label{AsRightIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AsTwoSidedIdeal({\mdseries\slshape R, S})\index{AsTwoSidedIdeal@\texttt{AsTwoSidedIdeal}}
\label{AsTwoSidedIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} be a subring of the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is a left ideal in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} then \texttt{AsLeftIdeal} returns this left ideal, otherwise \texttt{fail} is returned. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is a right ideal in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} then \texttt{AsRightIdeal} returns this right ideal, otherwise \texttt{fail} is returned. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} is a two\texttt{\symbol{45}}sided ideal in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} then \texttt{AsTwoSidedIdeal} returns this two\texttt{\symbol{45}}sided ideal, otherwise \texttt{fail} is returned. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@A:= FullMatrixAlgebra( Rationals, 3 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@B:= DirectSumOfAlgebras( A, A );|
  <algebra over Rationals, with 6 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@C:= Subalgebra( B, Basis( B ){[1..9]} );|
  <algebra over Rationals, with 9 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@I:= AsTwoSidedIdeal( B, C );|
  <two-sided ideal in <algebra of dimension 18 over Rationals>,
    (9 generators)>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Rings With One}}\label{Rings With One}
\logpage{[ 56, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X790DD00586F9B8B8}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRingWithOne}}
\logpage{[ 56, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E601FBD8020A0F3}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRingWithOne({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsRingWithOne@\texttt{IsRingWithOne}}
\label{IsRingWithOne}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 A \emph{ring\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one} in \textsf{GAP} is a ring (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsRing} (\ref{IsRing})) that is also a magma\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsMagmaWithOne} (\ref{IsMagmaWithOne})). 

 Note that the identity and the zero of a
ring\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one need \emph{not} be distinct. This means that a ring that consists only of its zero element can
be regarded as a ring\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one.   

 This is especially useful in the case of finitely presented rings, in the
sense that each factor of a
ring\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one is again a
ring\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RingWithOne}}\logpage{[ 56, 3, 2 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X80942A318417366E}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RingWithOne({\mdseries\slshape r, s, ...})\index{RingWithOne@\texttt{RingWithOne}!for ring elements}
\label{RingWithOne:for ring elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RingWithOne({\mdseries\slshape coll})\index{RingWithOne@\texttt{RingWithOne}!for a collection}
\label{RingWithOne:for a collection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 In the first form \texttt{RingWithOne} returns the smallest ring with one that contains all the elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}}, $\ldots$ In the second form \texttt{RingWithOne} returns the smallest ring with one that contains all the elements in the
collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}}. If any element is not an element of a ring or if the elements lie in no
common ring an error is raised. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@RingWithOne( [ 4, 6 ] );|
  Integers
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RingWithOneByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 56, 3, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X851115EC79B8C393}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RingWithOneByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape coll})\index{RingWithOneByGenerators@\texttt{RingWithOneByGenerators}}
\label{RingWithOneByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{RingWithOneByGenerators} returns the ring\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one generated by
the elements in the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}}, i.{\nobreakspace}e., the closure of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape coll}} under addition, multiplication, taking additive inverses, and taking the
identity of an element. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfRingWithOne}}
\logpage{[ 56, 3, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F9F122C831BCDD1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfRingWithOne({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{GeneratorsOfRingWithOne@\texttt{GeneratorsOfRingWithOne}}
\label{GeneratorsOfRingWithOne}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 \texttt{GeneratorsOfRingWithOne} returns a list of elements such that the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is the closure of these elements under addition, multiplication, taking
additive inverses, and taking the identity element \texttt{One( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} )}. 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} itself need \emph{not} be known to be a ring\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:= RingWithOne( [ 4, 6 ] );|
  Integers
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfRingWithOne( R );|
  [ 1 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SubringWithOne}}
\logpage{[ 56, 3, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D0BADF178D4DDF8}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SubringWithOne({\mdseries\slshape R, gens})\index{SubringWithOne@\texttt{SubringWithOne}}
\label{SubringWithOne}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SubringWithOneNC({\mdseries\slshape R, gens})\index{SubringWithOneNC@\texttt{SubringWithOneNC}}
\label{SubringWithOneNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the ring with one with parent \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} generated by the elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. When the second form, \texttt{SubringWithOneNC} is used, it is \emph{not} checked whether all elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} lie in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:= SubringWithOne( Integers, [ 4, 6 ] );|
  Integers
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Parent( R );|
  Integers
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Properties of Rings}}\label{Properties of Rings}
\logpage{[ 56, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X797F5869874BDBFB}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsIntegralRing}}
\logpage{[ 56, 4, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87A7D5B584713B52}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsIntegralRing({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsIntegralRing@\texttt{IsIntegralRing}}
\label{IsIntegralRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A ring\texttt{\symbol{45}}with\texttt{\symbol{45}}one \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is integral if it is commutative, contains no nontrivial zero divisors, and if
its identity is distinct from its zero. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsIntegralRing( Integers );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsUniqueFactorizationRing}}
\logpage{[ 56, 4, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X789A917085DB7527}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsUniqueFactorizationRing({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsUniqueFactorizationRing@\texttt{IsUniqueFactorizationRing}}
\label{IsUniqueFactorizationRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 A ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is called a \emph{unique factorization ring} if every nonzero element has a unique factorization into irreducible elements,
i.e., a unique representation as product of irreducibles (see \texttt{IsIrreducibleRingElement} (\ref{IsIrreducibleRingElement})). Unique in this context means unique up to permutations of the factors and
up to multiplication of the factors by units (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Units} (\ref{Units})). 

 (Note that we cannot install a subset maintained method for this filter since
the factorization of an element needs not exist in a subring. As an example,
consider the subring $4 {\ensuremath{\mathbb N}} + 1$ of the ring $4 {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} + 1$; in the subring, the element $3 \cdot 3 \cdot 11 \cdot 7$ has the two factorizations $33 \cdot 21 = 9 \cdot 77$, but in the large ring there is the unique factorization $(-3) \cdot (-3) \cdot (-11) \cdot (-7)$, and it is easy to see that every element in $4 {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} + 1$ has a unique factorization.) 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsUniqueFactorizationRing( PolynomialRing( Rationals, 1 ) );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLDistributive}}
\logpage{[ 56, 4, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D4BB44187C55BF2}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLDistributive({\mdseries\slshape C})\index{IsLDistributive@\texttt{IsLDistributive}}
\label{IsLDistributive}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if the relation $a * ( b + c ) = ( a * b ) + ( a * c )$ holds for all elements $a$, $b$, $c$ in the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}}, and \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRDistributive}}
\logpage{[ 56, 4, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79A5AEE786AED315}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRDistributive({\mdseries\slshape C})\index{IsRDistributive@\texttt{IsRDistributive}}
\label{IsRDistributive}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if the relation $( a + b ) * c = ( a * c ) + ( b * c )$ holds for all elements $a$, $b$, $c$ in the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}}, and \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsDistributive}}
\logpage{[ 56, 4, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86716D4F7B968604}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsDistributive({\mdseries\slshape C})\index{IsDistributive@\texttt{IsDistributive}}
\label{IsDistributive}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}} is both left and right distributive (see \texttt{IsLDistributive} (\ref{IsLDistributive}), \texttt{IsRDistributive} (\ref{IsRDistributive})), and \texttt{false} otherwise. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsDistributive( Integers );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsAnticommutative}}
\logpage{[ 56, 4, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82DECD237D49D937}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAnticommutative({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsAnticommutative@\texttt{IsAnticommutative}}
\label{IsAnticommutative}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if the relation $a * b = - b * a$ holds for all elements $a$, $b$ in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, and \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsZeroSquaredRing}}
\logpage{[ 56, 4, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EC0FEC88535E8CC}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsZeroSquaredRing({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsZeroSquaredRing@\texttt{IsZeroSquaredRing}}
\label{IsZeroSquaredRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if $a * a$ is the zero element of the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} for all $a$ in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, and \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsJacobianRing}}
\logpage{[ 56, 4, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X799BEF8581971A13}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsJacobianRing({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsJacobianRing@\texttt{IsJacobianRing}}
\label{IsJacobianRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if the Jacobi identity holds in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, and \texttt{false} otherwise. The Jacobi identity means that $x * (y * z) + z * (x * y) + y * (z * x)$ is the zero element of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, for all elements $x$, $y$, $z$ in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@L:= FullMatrixLieAlgebra( GF( 5 ), 7 );|
  <Lie algebra over GF(5), with 13 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsJacobianRing( L );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Units and Factorizations}}\label{Units and Factorizations}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8130085978A9B3C4}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsUnit}}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85CBFBAE78DE72E8}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsUnit({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r})\index{IsUnit@\texttt{IsUnit}}
\label{IsUnit}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{IsUnit} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is a unit in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in its default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is not a unit then \texttt{false} is returned. 

 An element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is called a \emph{unit} in a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} has an inverse in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 

 \texttt{IsUnit} may call \texttt{Quotient} (\ref{Quotient}).  }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Units}}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X853C045B7BA6A580}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Units({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{Units@\texttt{Units}}
\label{Units}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 \texttt{Units} returns the group of units of the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. This may either be returned as a list or as a group. 

 An element $r$ is called a \emph{unit} of a ring $R$ if $r$ has an inverse in $R$. It is easy to see that the set of units forms a multiplicative group. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Units( GaussianIntegers );|
  [ -1, 1, -E(4), E(4) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Units( GF( 16 ) );|
  <group of size 15 with 1 generator>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsAssociated}}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B307F217DDC7E20}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsAssociated({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r, s})\index{IsAssociated@\texttt{IsAssociated}}
\label{IsAssociated}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{IsAssociated} returns \texttt{true} if the two ring elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} are associated in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in their default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). If the two elements are not associated then \texttt{false} is returned. 

 Two elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} of a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} are called \emph{associated} if there is a unit $u$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} such that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} $u = $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Associates}}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A69C9097E17D161}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Associates({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r})\index{Associates@\texttt{Associates}}
\label{Associates}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{Associates} returns the set of associates of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in its default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). 

 Two elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} and $s$ of a ring $R$ are called \emph{associated} if there is a unit $u$ of $R$ such that $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} u = s$. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Associates( Integers, 2 );|
  [ -2, 2 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Associates( GaussianIntegers, 2 );|
  [ -2, 2, -2*E(4), 2*E(4) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{StandardAssociate}}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B1A9A4C7C59FB36}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StandardAssociate({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r})\index{StandardAssociate@\texttt{StandardAssociate}}
\label{StandardAssociate}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{StandardAssociate} returns the standard associate of the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in its default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). 

 The \emph{standard associate} of a ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is an associated element of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} which is, in a ring dependent way, distinguished among the set of associates
of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}. For example, in the ring of integers the standard associate is the absolute
value. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x:= Indeterminate( Rationals, "x" );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StandardAssociate( -x^2-x+1 );|
  x^2+x-1
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{StandardAssociateUnit}}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EB6803C789E027D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{StandardAssociateUnit({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r})\index{StandardAssociateUnit@\texttt{StandardAssociateUnit}}
\label{StandardAssociateUnit}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{StandardAssociateUnit} returns a unit in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} such that the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} times this unit equals the standard associate of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is not given, the default ring of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is used instead. (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). 

 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@y:= Indeterminate( Rationals, "y" );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@r:= -y^2-y+1;|
  -y^2-y+1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StandardAssociateUnit( r );|
  -1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@StandardAssociateUnit( r ) * r = StandardAssociate( r );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsIrreducibleRingElement}}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7CD7C64A7D961A18}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsIrreducibleRingElement({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r})\index{IsIrreducibleRingElement@\texttt{IsIrreducibleRingElement}}
\label{IsIrreducibleRingElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{IsIrreducibleRingElement} returns \texttt{true} if the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is irreducible in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in its default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is not irreducible then \texttt{false} is returned. 

 An element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} of a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is called \emph{irreducible} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is not a unit in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} and if there is no nontrivial factorization of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, i.e., if there is no representation of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} as product $s t$ such that neither $s$ nor $t$ is a unit (see \texttt{IsUnit} (\ref{IsUnit})). Each prime element (see \texttt{IsPrime} (\ref{IsPrime})) is irreducible. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsIrreducibleRingElement( Integers, 2 );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPrime}}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AA107AE7F79C6D8}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPrime({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r})\index{IsPrime@\texttt{IsPrime}}
\label{IsPrime}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{IsPrime} returns \texttt{true} if the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is a prime in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in its default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is not a prime then \texttt{false} is returned. 

 An element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} of a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} is called \emph{prime} if for each pair $s$ and $t$ such that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} divides $s t$ the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} divides either $s$ or $t$. Note that there are rings where not every irreducible element (see \texttt{IsIrreducibleRingElement} (\ref{IsIrreducibleRingElement})) is a prime. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Factors}}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82D6EDC685D12AE2}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Factors({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r})\index{Factors@\texttt{Factors}}
\label{Factors}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{Factors} returns the factorization of the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in its default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). The factorization is returned as a list of primes (see \texttt{IsPrime} (\ref{IsPrime})). Each element in the list is a standard associate (see \texttt{StandardAssociate} (\ref{StandardAssociate})) except the first one, which is multiplied by a unit as necessary to have \texttt{Product( Factors( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} ) ) = \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}}. This list is usually also sorted, thus smallest prime factors come first. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is a unit or zero, \texttt{Factors( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} ) = [ \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} ]}. 

  
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@x:= Indeterminate( GF(2), "x" );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@pol:= x^2+x+1;|
  x^2+x+Z(2)^0
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Factors( pol );|
  [ x^2+x+Z(2)^0 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Factors( PolynomialRing( GF(4) ), pol );|
  [ x+Z(2^2), x+Z(2^2)^2 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PadicValuation}}
\logpage{[ 56, 5, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8559CC7B80C479F1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PadicValuation({\mdseries\slshape r, p})\index{PadicValuation@\texttt{PadicValuation}}
\label{PadicValuation}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{PadicValuation} is the operation to compute the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}adic valuation of a ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Euclidean Rings}}\label{Euclidean Rings}
\logpage{[ 56, 6, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7F12BB99865EB7BF}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsEuclideanRing}}
\logpage{[ 56, 6, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X808B8E8E80D48E4A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsEuclideanRing({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{IsEuclideanRing@\texttt{IsEuclideanRing}}
\label{IsEuclideanRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 A ring $R$ is called a Euclidean ring if it is a non\texttt{\symbol{45}}trivial
commutative ring and there exists a function $\delta$, called the Euclidean degree, from $R-\{0_R\}$ into a well\texttt{\symbol{45}}ordered set (such as the nonnegative integers),
such that for every pair $r \in R$ and $s \in R-\{0_R\}$ there exists an element $q$ such that either $r - q s = 0_R$ or $\delta(r - q s) < \delta( s )$. In \textsf{GAP} the Euclidean degree $\delta$ is implicitly built into a ring and cannot be changed. The existence of this
division with remainder implies that the Euclidean algorithm can be applied to
compute a greatest common divisor of two elements, which in turn implies that $R$ is a unique factorization ring. 

  
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsEuclideanRing( GaussianIntegers );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EuclideanDegree}}
\logpage{[ 56, 6, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X784234088350D4E4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EuclideanDegree({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r})\index{EuclideanDegree@\texttt{EuclideanDegree}}
\label{EuclideanDegree}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{EuclideanDegree} returns the Euclidean degree of the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in its default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). 

 The ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} must be a Euclidean ring (see \texttt{IsEuclideanRing} (\ref{IsEuclideanRing})). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@EuclideanDegree( GaussianIntegers, 3 );|
  9
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EuclideanQuotient}}
\logpage{[ 56, 6, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A93FA788318B147}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EuclideanQuotient({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r, m})\index{EuclideanQuotient@\texttt{EuclideanQuotient}}
\label{EuclideanQuotient}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{EuclideanQuotient} returns the Euclidean quotient of the ring elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in their default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). 

 The ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} must be a Euclidean ring (see \texttt{IsEuclideanRing} (\ref{IsEuclideanRing})), otherwise an error is signalled. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@EuclideanQuotient( 8, 3 );|
  2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{EuclideanRemainder}}
\logpage{[ 56, 6, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B5E9639865E91BA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{EuclideanRemainder({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r, m})\index{EuclideanRemainder@\texttt{EuclideanRemainder}}
\label{EuclideanRemainder}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{EuclideanRemainder} returns the Euclidean remainder of the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} modulo the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in their default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). 

 The ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} must be a Euclidean ring (see \texttt{IsEuclideanRing} (\ref{IsEuclideanRing})), otherwise an error is signalled. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@EuclideanRemainder( 8, 3 );|
  2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{QuotientRemainder}}
\logpage{[ 56, 6, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X876B7532801A1B35}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{QuotientRemainder({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r, m})\index{QuotientRemainder@\texttt{QuotientRemainder}}
\label{QuotientRemainder}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{QuotientRemainder} returns the Euclidean quotient and the Euclidean remainder of the ring
elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in their default ring (see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements})). The result is a pair of ring elements. 

 The ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} must be a Euclidean ring (see \texttt{IsEuclideanRing} (\ref{IsEuclideanRing})), otherwise an error is signalled. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@QuotientRemainder( GaussianIntegers, 8, 3 );|
  [ 3, -1 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Gcd and Lcm}}\label{Gcd and Lcm}
\logpage{[ 56, 7, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7E9CF2C07C4A6CEE}{}
{
  
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Gcd}}\logpage{[ 56, 7, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7DE207718456F98F}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Gcd({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r1, r2, ...})\index{Gcd@\texttt{Gcd}!for (a ring and) several elements}
\label{Gcd:for (a ring and) several elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Gcd({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]list})\index{Gcd@\texttt{Gcd}!for (a ring and) a list of elements}
\label{Gcd:for (a ring and) a list of elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{Gcd} returns the greatest common divisor of the ring elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r2}}, $\ldots$ resp. of the ring elements in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in their default ring, see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements}). 

 \texttt{Gcd} returns the standard associate (see \texttt{StandardAssociate} (\ref{StandardAssociate})) of the greatest common divisors. 

 A divisor of an element $r$ in the ring $R$ is an element $d\in R$ such that $r$ is a multiple of $d$. A common divisor of the elements $r_1, r_2, \ldots$ in the ring $R$ is an element $d\in R$ which is a divisor of each $r_1, r_2, \ldots$. A greatest common divisor $d$ in addition has the property that every other common divisor of $r_1, r_2, \ldots$ is a divisor of $d$. 

 Note that this in particular implies the following: For the zero element $z$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, we have \texttt{Gcd( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}, }$z$\texttt{ ) = Gcd( }$z$\texttt{, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} ) = StandardAssociate( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} )} and \texttt{Gcd( }$z$\texttt{, }$z$\texttt{ ) = }$z$. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Gcd( Integers, [ 10, 15 ] );|
  5
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GcdOp}}
\logpage{[ 56, 7, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7836D50F8341D6E1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GcdOp({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r, s})\index{GcdOp@\texttt{GcdOp}}
\label{GcdOp}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{GcdOp} is the operation to compute the greatest common divisor of two ring elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} or in their default ring. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GcdRepresentation}}\logpage{[ 56, 7, 3 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7ABB91EF838075EF}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GcdRepresentation({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r1, r2, ...})\index{GcdRepresentation@\texttt{GcdRepresentation}!for (a ring and) several elements}
\label{GcdRepresentation:for (a ring and) several elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GcdRepresentation({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]list})\index{GcdRepresentation@\texttt{GcdRepresentation}!for (a ring and) a list of elements}
\label{GcdRepresentation:for (a ring and) a list of elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{GcdRepresentation} returns a representation of the greatest common divisor of the ring elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r2}}, $\ldots$ resp. of the ring elements in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} in the Euclidean ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in their default ring, see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements}). 

 A representation of the gcd $g$ of the elements $r_1, r_2, \ldots$ of a ring $R$ is a list of ring elements $s_1, s_2, \ldots$ of $R$, such that $g = s_1 r_1 + s_2 r_2 + \cdots$. Such representations do not exist in all rings, but they do exist in
Euclidean rings (see \texttt{IsEuclideanRing} (\ref{IsEuclideanRing})), which can be shown using the Euclidean algorithm, which in fact can compute
those coefficients. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a:= Indeterminate( Rationals, "a" );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GcdRepresentation( a^2+1, a^3+1 );|
  [ -1/2*a^2-1/2*a+1/2, 1/2*a+1/2 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

 \texttt{Gcdex} (\ref{Gcdex}) provides similar functionality over the integers. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GcdRepresentationOp}}
\logpage{[ 56, 7, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81392E7F84956341}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GcdRepresentationOp({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r, s})\index{GcdRepresentationOp@\texttt{GcdRepresentationOp}}
\label{GcdRepresentationOp}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{GcdRepresentationOp} is the operation to compute the representation of the greatest common divisor
of two ring elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} in the Euclidean ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} or in their default ring, respectively. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ShowGcd}}
\logpage{[ 56, 7, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X836DB8B47A0219FB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ShowGcd({\mdseries\slshape a, b})\index{ShowGcd@\texttt{ShowGcd}}
\label{ShowGcd}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 This function takes two elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape a}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape b}} of an Euclidean ring and returns their greatest common divisor. It will print
out the steps performed by the Euclidean algorithm, as well as the
rearrangement of these steps to express the gcd as a ring combination of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape a}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape b}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ShowGcd(192,42);|
  192=4*42 + 24
  42=1*24 + 18
  24=1*18 + 6
  18=3*6 + 0
  The Gcd is 6
   = 1*24 -1*18
   = -1*42 + 2*24
   = 2*192 -9*42
  6
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Lcm}}\logpage{[ 56, 7, 6 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7ABA92057DD6C7AF}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Lcm({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r1, r2, ...})\index{Lcm@\texttt{Lcm}!for (a ring and) several elements}
\label{Lcm:for (a ring and) several elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Lcm({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]list})\index{Lcm@\texttt{Lcm}!for (a ring and) a list of elements}
\label{Lcm:for (a ring and) a list of elements}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{Lcm} returns the least common multiple of the ring elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r1}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r2}}, $\ldots$ resp. of the ring elements in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in their default ring, see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements}). 

 \texttt{Lcm} returns the standard associate (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{StandardAssociate} (\ref{StandardAssociate})) of the least common multiples. 

 A least common multiple of the elements $r_1, r_2, \ldots$ of the ring $R$ is an element $m$ that is a multiple of $r_1, r_2, \ldots$, and every other multiple of these elements is a multiple of $m$. 

 Note that this in particular implies the following: For the zero element $z$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, we have \texttt{Lcm( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}, }$z$\texttt{ ) = Lcm( }$z$\texttt{, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} ) = StandardAssociate( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} )} and \texttt{Lcm( }$z$\texttt{, }$z$\texttt{ ) = }$z$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LcmOp}}
\logpage{[ 56, 7, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7FB6C5A67AC1E8C1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LcmOp({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r, s})\index{LcmOp@\texttt{LcmOp}}
\label{LcmOp}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{LcmOp} is the operation to compute the least common multiple of two ring elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} or in their default ring, respectively. 

 The default methods for this uses the equality $lcm( m, n ) = m*n / gcd( m, n )$ (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{GcdOp} (\ref{GcdOp})). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{QuotientMod}}
\logpage{[ 56, 7, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8555913A83D716A4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{QuotientMod({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r, s, m})\index{QuotientMod@\texttt{QuotientMod}}
\label{QuotientMod}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{QuotientMod} returns a quotient of the ring elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} modulo the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in their default ring, see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements}). 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} must be a Euclidean ring (see \texttt{IsEuclideanRing} (\ref{IsEuclideanRing})) so that \texttt{EuclideanRemainder} (\ref{EuclideanRemainder}) can be applied. If no modular quotient exists, \texttt{fail} is returned. 

 A quotient $q$ of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} modulo \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} is an element of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} such that $q \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} = \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}$ modulo $m$, i.e., such that $q \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape s}} - \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}$ is divisible by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} and that $q$ is either zero (if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is divisible by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}}) or the Euclidean degree of $q$ is strictly smaller than the Euclidean degree of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@QuotientMod( 7, 2, 3 );|
  2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PowerMod}}
\logpage{[ 56, 7, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X805A35D684B7A952}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PowerMod({\mdseries\slshape [R, ]r, e, m})\index{PowerMod@\texttt{PowerMod}}
\label{PowerMod}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{PowerMod} returns the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}th power of the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} modulo the ring element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} in the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, if given, and otherwise in their default ring, see \texttt{DefaultRing} (\ref{DefaultRing:for ring elements}). \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} must be an integer. 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} must be a Euclidean ring (see \texttt{IsEuclideanRing} (\ref{IsEuclideanRing})) so that \texttt{EuclideanRemainder} (\ref{EuclideanRemainder}) can be applied to its elements. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} is positive the result is \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}\texttt{\texttt{\symbol{94}}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} modulo \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} is negative then \texttt{PowerMod} first tries to find the inverse of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} modulo \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}}, i.e., $i$ such that $i \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} = 1$ modulo \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}}. If the inverse does not exist an error is signalled. If the inverse does
exist \texttt{PowerMod} returns \texttt{PowerMod( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape i}}, \texttt{\symbol{45}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} )}. 

 \texttt{PowerMod} reduces the intermediate values modulo \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}}, improving performance drastically when \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape e}} is large and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} small. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@PowerMod( 12, 100000, 7 );|
  2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{InterpolatedPolynomial}}
\logpage{[ 56, 7, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87711E6F8024A358}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InterpolatedPolynomial({\mdseries\slshape R, x, y})\index{InterpolatedPolynomial@\texttt{InterpolatedPolynomial}}
\label{InterpolatedPolynomial}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{InterpolatedPolynomial} returns, for given lists \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape y}} of elements in a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} of the same length $n$ the unique polynomial of degree less than $n$ which has value \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape y}}[$i$] at \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}}$[i]$, for all $i \in \{ 1, \ldots, n \}$. Note that the elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape x}} must be distinct. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@InterpolatedPolynomial( Integers, [ 1, 2, 3 ], [ 5, 7, 0 ] );|
  -9/2*x^2+31/2*x-6
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Homomorphisms of Rings}}\label{Homomorphisms of Rings}
\logpage{[ 56, 8, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7B13484581169439}{}
{
  A \emph{ring homomorphism} is a mapping between two rings that respects addition and multiplication. 

 Currently \textsf{GAP} supports ring homomorphisms between finite rings (using straightforward
methods) and ring homomorphisms with additional structures, where source and
range are in fact algebras and where also the linear structure is respected,
see \ref{Homomorphisms of Algebras}. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RingGeneralMappingByImages}}
\logpage{[ 56, 8, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DE9CC5B877C91DA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RingGeneralMappingByImages({\mdseries\slshape R, S, gens, imgs})\index{RingGeneralMappingByImages@\texttt{RingGeneralMappingByImages}}
\label{RingGeneralMappingByImages}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 is a general mapping from the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape A}} to the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. This general mapping is defined by mapping the entries in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} (elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}) to the entries in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape imgs}} (elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}), and taking the additive and multiplicative closure. 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} need not generate \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} as a ring, and if the specification does not define an additive and
multiplicative mapping then the result will be multivalued. Hence, in general
it is not a mapping. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RingHomomorphismByImages}}
\logpage{[ 56, 8, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78C1016284F08026}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RingHomomorphismByImages({\mdseries\slshape R, S, gens, imgs})\index{RingHomomorphismByImages@\texttt{RingHomomorphismByImages}}
\label{RingHomomorphismByImages}
