}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{RingHomomorphismByImages} returns the ring homomorphism with source \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} and range \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} that is defined by mapping the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} of generators of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} to the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape imgs}} of images in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} does not generate \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} or if the homomorphism does not exist (i.e., if mapping the generators
describes only a multi\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued mapping) then \texttt{fail} is returned. 

 One can avoid the checks by calling \texttt{RingHomomorphismByImagesNC} (\ref{RingHomomorphismByImagesNC}), and one can construct multi\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued mappings with \texttt{RingGeneralMappingByImages} (\ref{RingGeneralMappingByImages}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RingHomomorphismByImagesNC}}
\logpage{[ 56, 8, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D01646A7CCBEDBB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RingHomomorphismByImagesNC({\mdseries\slshape R, S, gens, imgs})\index{RingHomomorphismByImagesNC@\texttt{RingHomomorphismByImagesNC}}
\label{RingHomomorphismByImagesNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{RingHomomorphismByImagesNC} is the operation that is called by the function \texttt{RingHomomorphismByImages} (\ref{RingHomomorphismByImages}). Its methods may assume that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} generates \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} as a ring and that the mapping of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape imgs}} defines a ring homomorphism. Results are unpredictable if these conditions do
not hold. 

 For creating a possibly multi\texttt{\symbol{45}}valued mapping from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} that respects addition and multiplication, \texttt{RingGeneralMappingByImages} (\ref{RingGeneralMappingByImages}) can be used. }

  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NaturalHomomorphismByIdeal}}
\logpage{[ 56, 8, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83D53D98809EC461}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NaturalHomomorphismByIdeal({\mdseries\slshape R, I})\index{NaturalHomomorphismByIdeal@\texttt{NaturalHomomorphismByIdeal}}
\label{NaturalHomomorphismByIdeal}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 is the homomorphism of rings provided by the natural projection map of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} onto the quotient ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}/\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape I}}. This map can be used to take pre\texttt{\symbol{45}}images in the original
ring from elements in the quotient. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Small Rings}}\label{Small Rings}
\logpage{[ 56, 9, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X81D526A57B375AAD}{}
{
  \textsf{GAP} contains a library of small (order up to 15) rings. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SmallRing}}
\logpage{[ 56, 9, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E86DCB7812DF04C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SmallRing({\mdseries\slshape s, n})\index{SmallRing@\texttt{SmallRing}}
\label{SmallRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the $n$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th ring of order $s$ from a library of rings of small order (up to isomorphism). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@A,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>A !gapinput@R:=SmallRing(8,37);A
  <ring with 3 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>A !gapinput@ShowMultiplicationTable(R);A
  *     | 0*a   c     b     b+c   a     a+c   a+b   a+b+c
  ------+------------------------------------------------
  0*a   | 0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a
  c     | 0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a
  b     | 0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a   b     b     b     b
  b+c   | 0*a   0*a   0*a   0*a   b     b     b     b
  a     | 0*a   c     b     b+c   a+b   a+b+c a     a+c
  a+c   | 0*a   c     b     b+c   a+b   a+b+c a     a+c
  a+b   | 0*a   c     b     b+c   a     a+c   a+b   a+b+c
  a+b+c | 0*a   c     b     b+c   a     a+c   a+b   a+b+c
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NumberSmallRings}}
\logpage{[ 56, 9, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F2EE9AF83DCE641}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NumberSmallRings({\mdseries\slshape s})\index{NumberSmallRings@\texttt{NumberSmallRings}}
\label{NumberSmallRings}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the number of (nonisomorphic) rings of order $s$ stored in the library of small rings. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List([1..15],NumberSmallRings);|
  [ 1, 2, 2, 11, 2, 4, 2, 52, 11, 4, 2, 22, 2, 4, 4 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Subrings}}
\logpage{[ 56, 9, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8070D20B86148929}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Subrings({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{Subrings@\texttt{Subrings}}
\label{Subrings}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 for a finite ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} this function returns a list of all subrings of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Subrings(SmallRing(8,37));|
  [ <ring with 1 generator>, <ring with 1 generator>,
    <ring with 1 generator>, <ring with 1 generator>,
    <ring with 1 generator>, <ring with 1 generator>,
    <ring with 2 generators>, <ring with 2 generators>,
    <ring with 2 generators>, <ring with 2 generators>,
    <ring with 3 generators> ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Ideals}}
\logpage{[ 56, 9, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83629803819C4A6F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Ideals({\mdseries\slshape R})\index{Ideals@\texttt{Ideals}}
\label{Ideals}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 for a finite ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} this function returns a list of all ideals of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Ideals(SmallRing(8,37));|
  [ <ring with 1 generator>, <ring with 1 generator>,
    <ring with 1 generator>, <ring with 2 generators>,
    <ring with 3 generators> ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DirectSum}}
\logpage{[ 56, 9, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82AD6F187B550060}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DirectSum({\mdseries\slshape R\texttt{\symbol{123}}, S\texttt{\symbol{125}}})\index{DirectSum@\texttt{DirectSum}}
\label{DirectSum}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DirectSumOp({\mdseries\slshape list, expl})\index{DirectSumOp@\texttt{DirectSumOp}}
\label{DirectSumOp}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 These functions construct the direct sum of the rings given as arguments. \texttt{DirectSum} takes an arbitrary positive number of arguments and calls the operation \texttt{DirectSumOp}, which takes exactly two arguments, namely a nonempty list of rings and one
of these rings. (This somewhat strange syntax allows the method selection to
choose a reasonable method for special cases.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DirectSum(SmallRing(5,1),SmallRing(5,1));|
  <ring with 2 generators>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RingByStructureConstants}}
\logpage{[ 56, 9, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E7B1B727EA434CF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RingByStructureConstants({\mdseries\slshape moduli, sctable[, nameinfo]})\index{RingByStructureConstants@\texttt{RingByStructureConstants}}
\label{RingByStructureConstants}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns a ring $R$ whose additive group is described by the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape moduli}}, with multiplication defined by the structure constants table \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape sctable}}. The optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape nameinfo}} can be used to prescribe names for the elements of the canonical generators of $R$; it can be either a string \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} (then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}\texttt{1}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}\texttt{2} etc. are chosen) or a list of strings which are then chosen. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@T:=EmptySCTable( 1, 0 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SetEntrySCTable( T, 1, 1, [ 1, 1 ] );|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@R:=RingByStructureConstants([9], T);   # Z/9Z|
  <ring with 1 generator>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Elements(R);|
  [ 0*r.1, r.1, 2*r.1, 3*r.1, 4*r.1, 5*r.1, 6*r.1, 7*r.1, -r.1 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

 }

            
\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Modules}}\label{Modules}
\logpage{[ 57, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8183A6857B0C3633}{}
{
   
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Generating modules}}\label{Generating modules}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X87A33EFD7CC179C1}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C62FE5282E9C505}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{IsLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup@\texttt{IsLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup}}
\label{IsLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 A domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} lies in \texttt{IsLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup} if it is an additive group that is closed under scalar multiplication from the
left, and such that $\lambda * ( x + y ) = \lambda * x + \lambda * y$ for all scalars $\lambda$ and elements $x, y \in D$ (here and below by scalars we mean elements of a domain acting on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} from left or right as appropriate). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLeftModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7ED323027B291BDF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLeftModule({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{IsLeftModule@\texttt{IsLeftModule}}
\label{IsLeftModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 A domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} lies in \texttt{IsLeftModule} if it lies in \texttt{IsLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup}, \emph{and} the set of scalars forms a ring, \emph{and} $(\lambda + \mu) * x = \lambda * x + \mu * x$ for scalars $\lambda, \mu$ and $x \in M$, \emph{and} scalar multiplication satisfies $\lambda * (\mu * x) = (\lambda * \mu) * x$ for scalars $\lambda, \mu$ and $x \in M$. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= FullRowSpace( Rationals, 3 );|
  ( Rationals^3 )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsLeftModule( V );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F76B1FD84775025}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{GeneratorsOfLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup@\texttt{Generators}\-\texttt{Of}\-\texttt{Left}\-\texttt{Operator}\-\texttt{Additive}\-\texttt{Group}}
\label{GeneratorsOfLeftOperatorAdditiveGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a list of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} that generates \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} as a left operator additive group. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfLeftModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C7684EF867323C2}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfLeftModule({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{GeneratorsOfLeftModule@\texttt{GeneratorsOfLeftModule}}
\label{GeneratorsOfLeftModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a list of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} that generate \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} as a left module. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= FullRowSpace( Rationals, 3 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@GeneratorsOfLeftModule( V );|
  [ [ 1, 0, 0 ], [ 0, 1, 0 ], [ 0, 0, 1 ] ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AsLeftModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EB3E46D7BC4A35C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AsLeftModule({\mdseries\slshape R, D})\index{AsLeftModule@\texttt{AsLeftModule}}
\label{AsLeftModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 if the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} forms an additive group and is closed under left multiplication by the
elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, then \texttt{AsLeftModule( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} )} returns the domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} viewed as a left module. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@coll:= [[0*Z(2),0*Z(2)], [Z(2),0*Z(2)], [0*Z(2),Z(2)], [Z(2),Z(2)]];|
  [ [ 0*Z(2), 0*Z(2) ], [ Z(2)^0, 0*Z(2) ], [ 0*Z(2), Z(2)^0 ],
    [ Z(2)^0, Z(2)^0 ] ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@AsLeftModule( GF(2), coll );|
  <vector space of dimension 2 over GF(2)>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRightOperatorAdditiveGroup}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F19AD3D799D0469}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRightOperatorAdditiveGroup({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{IsRightOperatorAdditiveGroup@\texttt{IsRightOperatorAdditiveGroup}}
\label{IsRightOperatorAdditiveGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 A domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} lies in \texttt{IsRightOperatorAdditiveGroup} if it is an additive group that is closed under scalar multiplication from the
right, and such that $( x + y ) * \lambda = x * \lambda + y * \lambda$ for all scalars $\lambda$ and elements $x, y \in D$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRightModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8479A5AA7DF25F50}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRightModule({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{IsRightModule@\texttt{IsRightModule}}
\label{IsRightModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 A domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} lies in \texttt{IsRightModule} if it lies in \texttt{IsRightOperatorAdditiveGroup}, \emph{and} the set of scalars forms a ring, \emph{and} $x * (\lambda + \mu) = x * \lambda + x * \mu$ for scalars $\lambda, \mu$ and $x \in M$, \emph{and} scalar multiplication satisfies $(x * \mu) * \lambda = x * (\mu * \lambda)$ for scalars $\lambda, \mu$ and $x \in M$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfRightOperatorAdditiveGroup}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DBC4BCB876EEE1C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfRightOperatorAdditiveGroup({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{GeneratorsOfRightOperatorAdditiveGroup@\texttt{Generators}\-\texttt{Of}\-\texttt{Right}\-\texttt{Operator}\-\texttt{Additive}\-\texttt{Group}}
\label{GeneratorsOfRightOperatorAdditiveGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a list of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} that generates \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} as a right operator additive group. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfRightModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8586A83B85F176F6}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfRightModule({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{GeneratorsOfRightModule@\texttt{GeneratorsOfRightModule}}
\label{GeneratorsOfRightModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns a list of elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} that generate \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} as a left module. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LeftModuleByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79ED1D7D7F0AE59A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LeftModuleByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape R, gens[, zero]})\index{LeftModuleByGenerators@\texttt{LeftModuleByGenerators}}
\label{LeftModuleByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns the left module over \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} generated by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@coll:= [ [Z(2),0*Z(2)], [0*Z(2),Z(2)], [Z(2),Z(2)] ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= LeftModuleByGenerators( GF(16), coll );|
  <vector space over GF(2^4), with 3 generators>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LeftActingDomain}}
\logpage{[ 57, 1, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86F070E0807DC34E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LeftActingDomain({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{LeftActingDomain@\texttt{LeftActingDomain}}
\label{LeftActingDomain}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} be an external left set, that is, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} is closed under the action of a domain $L$ by multiplication from the left. Then $L$ can be accessed as value of \texttt{LeftActingDomain} for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Submodules}}\label{Submodules}
\logpage{[ 57, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7934FAE97B6D2AD8}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Submodule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8465103F874BC07B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Submodule({\mdseries\slshape M, gens[, "basis"]})\index{Submodule@\texttt{Submodule}}
\label{Submodule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 is the left module generated by the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}, with parent module \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. If the string \texttt{"basis"} is entered as the third argument then the submodule of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} is created for which the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} is known to be a list of basis vectors; in this case, it is \emph{not} checked whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} really is linearly independent and whether all in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} lie in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@coll:= [ [Z(2),0*Z(2)], [0*Z(2),Z(2)], [Z(2),Z(2)] ];;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= LeftModuleByGenerators( GF(16), coll );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@W:= Submodule( V, [ coll[1], coll[2] ] );|
  <vector space over GF(2^4), with 2 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Parent( W ) = V;|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SubmoduleNC}}
\logpage{[ 57, 2, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83CF3AD18050C982}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SubmoduleNC({\mdseries\slshape M, gens[, "basis"]})\index{SubmoduleNC@\texttt{SubmoduleNC}}
\label{SubmoduleNC}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{SubmoduleNC} does the same as \texttt{Submodule} (\ref{Submodule}), except that it does not check whether all in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} lie in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ClosureLeftModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C68C4E287481EC0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ClosureLeftModule({\mdseries\slshape M, m})\index{ClosureLeftModule@\texttt{ClosureLeftModule}}
\label{ClosureLeftModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 is the left module generated by the left module generators of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} and the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= LeftModuleByGenerators(Rationals, [ [ 1, 0, 0 ], [ 0, 1, 0 ] ]);|
  <vector space over Rationals, with 2 generators>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ClosureLeftModule( V, [ 1, 1, 1 ] );|
  <vector space over Rationals, with 3 generators>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TrivialSubmodule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 2, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7980BC20856B2B7D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TrivialSubmodule({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{TrivialSubmodule@\texttt{TrivialSubmodule}}
\label{TrivialSubmodule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 returns the zero submodule of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= LeftModuleByGenerators(Rationals, [[ 1, 0, 0 ], [ 0, 1, 0 ]]);;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TrivialSubmodule( V );|
  <vector space of dimension 0 over Rationals>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Free Modules}}\label{Free Modules}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X85BD57F27F513D3E}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsFreeLeftModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C4832187F3D9228}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFreeLeftModule({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{IsFreeLeftModule@\texttt{IsFreeLeftModule}}
\label{IsFreeLeftModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 A left module is free as module if it is isomorphic to a direct sum of copies
of its left acting domain. 

 Free left modules can have bases. 

 The characteristic (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Characteristic} (\ref{Characteristic})) of a free left module is defined as the characteristic of its left acting
domain (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{LeftActingDomain} (\ref{LeftActingDomain})). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FreeLeftModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C043E307E344AEE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FreeLeftModule({\mdseries\slshape R, gens[, zero][, "basis"]})\index{FreeLeftModule@\texttt{FreeLeftModule}}
\label{FreeLeftModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{FreeLeftModule( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} )} is the free left module over the ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, generated by the vectors in the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. 

 If there are three arguments, a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} and a collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} and an element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape zero}}, then \texttt{FreeLeftModule( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape zero}} )} is the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}\texttt{\symbol{45}}free left module generated by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}, with zero element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape zero}}. 

 If the last argument is the string \texttt{"basis"} then the vectors in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} are known to form a basis of the free module. 

 It should be noted that the generators \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} must be vectors, that is, they must support an addition and a scalar action of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} via left multiplication. (See also Section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Constructing Domains} for the general meaning of ``generators'' in \textsf{GAP}.) In particular, \texttt{FreeLeftModule} is \emph{not} an equivalent of commands such as \texttt{FreeGroup} (\ref{FreeGroup:for given rank}) in the sense of a constructor of a free group on abstract generators. Such a
construction seems to be unnecessary for vector spaces, for that one can use
for example row spaces (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{FullRowSpace} (\ref{FullRowSpace})) in the finite dimensional case and polynomial rings (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{PolynomialRing} (\ref{PolynomialRing:for a ring and a rank (and an exclusion list)})) in the infinite dimensional case. Moreover, the definition of a ``natural'' addition for elements of a given magma (for example a permutation group) is
possible via the construction of magma rings (see Chapter \ref{Magma Rings}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= FreeLeftModule(Rationals, [[ 1, 0, 0 ], [ 0, 1, 0 ]], "basis");|
  <vector space of dimension 2 over Rationals>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Dimension}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7E6926C6850E7C4E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Dimension({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{Dimension@\texttt{Dimension}}
\label{Dimension}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 A free left module has dimension $n$ if it is isomorphic to a direct sum of $n$ copies of its left acting domain. 

 (We do \emph{not} mark \texttt{Dimension} as invariant under isomorphisms since we want to call \texttt{UseIsomorphismRelation} (\ref{UseIsomorphismRelation}) also for free left modules over different left acting domains.) 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= FreeLeftModule( Rationals, [ [ 1, 0 ], [ 0, 1 ], [ 1, 1 ] ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Dimension( V );|
  2
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsFiniteDimensional}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X802DB9FB824B0167}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFiniteDimensional({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{IsFiniteDimensional@\texttt{IsFiniteDimensional}}
\label{IsFiniteDimensional}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 is \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape M}} is a free left module that is finite dimensional over its left acting domain,
and \texttt{false} otherwise. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= FreeLeftModule( Rationals, [ [ 1, 0 ], [ 0, 1 ], [ 1, 1 ] ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsFiniteDimensional( V );|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{UseBasis}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7909E8E785420F0E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{UseBasis({\mdseries\slshape V, gens})\index{UseBasis@\texttt{UseBasis}}
\label{UseBasis}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 The vectors in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} are known to form a basis of the free left module \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape V}}. \texttt{UseBasis} stores information in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape V}} that can be derived form this fact, namely 
\begin{itemize}
\item  \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} are stored as left module generators if no such generators were bound (this is
useful especially if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape V}} is an algebra), 
\item  the dimension of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape V}} is stored. 
\end{itemize}
 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= FreeLeftModule( Rationals, [ [ 1, 0 ], [ 0, 1 ], [ 1, 1 ] ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@UseBasis( V, [ [ 1, 0 ], [ 1, 1 ] ] );|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V;  # now V knows its dimension|
  <vector space of dimension 2 over Rationals>
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsRowModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C8F844783F4FA09}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRowModule({\mdseries\slshape V})\index{IsRowModule@\texttt{IsRowModule}}
\label{IsRowModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A \emph{row module} is a free left module whose elements are row vectors. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsMatrixModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81FCC1D780435CF1}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsMatrixModule({\mdseries\slshape V})\index{IsMatrixModule@\texttt{IsMatrixModule}}
\label{IsMatrixModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A \emph{matrix module} is a free left module whose elements are matrices. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsFullRowModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X853E085C868196EF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFullRowModule({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{IsFullRowModule@\texttt{IsFullRowModule}}
\label{IsFullRowModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A \emph{full row module} is a module $R^n$, for a ring $R$ and a nonnegative integer $n$. 

 More precisely, a full row module is a free left module over a ring $R$ such that the elements are row vectors of the same length $n$ and with entries in $R$ and such that the dimension is equal to $n$. 

 Several functions delegate their tasks to full row modules, for example \texttt{Iterator} (\ref{Iterator}) and \texttt{Enumerator} (\ref{Enumerator}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FullRowModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X848041A47BC4B038}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FullRowModule({\mdseries\slshape R, n})\index{FullRowModule@\texttt{FullRowModule}}
\label{FullRowModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 is the row module \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}}, for a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} and a nonnegative integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@V:= FullRowModule( Integers, 5 );|
  ( Integers^5 )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsFullMatrixModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X814CEA62842CF5BB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFullMatrixModule({\mdseries\slshape M})\index{IsFullMatrixModule@\texttt{IsFullMatrixModule}}
\label{IsFullMatrixModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A \emph{full matrix module} is a module $R^{{[m,n]}}$, for a ring $R$ and two nonnegative integers $m$, $n$. 

 More precisely, a full matrix module is a free left module over a ring $R$ such that the elements are $m$ by $n$ matrices with entries in $R$ and such that the dimension is equal to $m n$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FullMatrixModule}}
\logpage{[ 57, 3, 11 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A0C871B7C446F1F}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FullMatrixModule({\mdseries\slshape R, m, n})\index{FullMatrixModule@\texttt{FullMatrixModule}}
\label{FullMatrixModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 is the matrix module \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}[\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}},\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}]}, for a ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape R}} and nonnegative integers \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape m}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FullMatrixModule( GaussianIntegers, 3, 6 );|
  ( GaussianIntegers^[ 3, 6 ] )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

 }

         
\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Fields and Division Rings}}\label{Fields and Division Rings}
\logpage{[ 58, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X80A8E676814A19FD}{}
{
  \index{fields} \index{division rings} A \emph{division ring} is a ring (see Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Rings}) in which every non\texttt{\symbol{45}}zero element has an inverse. The most
important class of division rings are the commutative ones, which are called \emph{fields}. 

 \textsf{GAP} supports finite fields (see Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Finite Fields}) and abelian number fields (see Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Abelian Number Fields}), in particular the field of rationals (see Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Rational Numbers}). 

 This chapter describes the general \textsf{GAP} functions for fields and division rings. 

 If a field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} is a subfield of a commutative ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}} can be considered as a vector space over the (left) acting domain \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} (see Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Vector Spaces}). In this situation, we call \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} the \emph{field of definition} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}}. 

 Each field in \textsf{GAP} is represented as a vector space over a subfield (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsField} (\ref{IsField})), thus each field is in fact a field extension in a natural way, which is
used by functions such as \texttt{Norm} (\ref{Norm}) and \texttt{Trace} (\ref{Trace:for a field element}) (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Galois Action}).  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Generating Fields}}\label{Generating Fields}
\logpage{[ 58, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X82B74B458705B3CE}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsDivisionRing}}
\logpage{[ 58, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7F2CAA9E7A16913D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsDivisionRing({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{IsDivisionRing@\texttt{IsDivisionRing}}
\label{IsDivisionRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 A \emph{division ring} in \textsf{GAP} is a nontrivial associative algebra \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} with a multiplicative inverse for each nonzero element. In \textsf{GAP} every division ring is a vector space over a division ring (possibly over
itself). Note that being a division ring is thus not a property that a ring
can get, because a ring is usually not represented as a vector space. 

 The field of coefficients is stored as the value of the attribute \texttt{LeftActingDomain} (\ref{LeftActingDomain}) of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsField}}
\logpage{[ 58, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A5AE30E7C0F457C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsField({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{IsField@\texttt{IsField}}
\label{IsField}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (filter)}}\\


 A \emph{field} is a commutative division ring (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsDivisionRing} (\ref{IsDivisionRing}) and{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsCommutative} (\ref{IsCommutative})). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsField( GaloisField(16) );           # the field with 16 elements|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsField( Rationals );                 # the field of rationals|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@q:= QuaternionAlgebra( Rationals );;  # noncommutative division ring|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsField( q );  IsDivisionRing( q );|
  false
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@mat:= [ [ 1 ] ];;  a:= Algebra( Rationals, [ mat ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsDivisionRing( a );   # algebra not constructed as a division ring|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Field (for several generators)}}
\logpage{[ 58, 1, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X871AA7D58263E9AC}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Field({\mdseries\slshape z, ...})\index{Field@\texttt{Field}!for several generators}
\label{Field:for several generators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Field({\mdseries\slshape [F, ]list})\index{Field@\texttt{Field}!for (a field and) a list of generators}
\label{Field:for (a field and) a list of generators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{Field} returns the smallest field $K$ that contains all the elements $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}, \ldots$, or the smallest field $K$ that contains all elements in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}}. If no subfield \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} is given, $K$ is constructed as a field over itself, i.e. the left acting domain of $K$ is $K$. Called with a field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} and a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}}, \texttt{Field} constructs the field generated by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} and the elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}}, as a vector space over \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DefaultField (for several generators)}}
\logpage{[ 58, 1, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D9F7FD4786691EE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DefaultField({\mdseries\slshape z, ...})\index{DefaultField@\texttt{DefaultField}!for several generators}
\label{DefaultField:for several generators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DefaultField({\mdseries\slshape list})\index{DefaultField@\texttt{DefaultField}!for a list of generators}
\label{DefaultField:for a list of generators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \texttt{DefaultField} returns a field $K$ that contains all the elements $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}, \ldots$, or a field $K$ that contains all elements in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape list}}. 

 This field need not be the smallest field in which the elements lie,
cf.{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Field} (\ref{Field:for several generators}). For example, for elements from cyclotomic fields \texttt{DefaultField} returns the smallest cyclotomic field in which the elements lie, but the
elements may lie in a smaller number field which is not a cyclotomic field. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Field( Z(4) );  Field( [ Z(4), Z(8) ] );  # finite fields|
  GF(2^2)
  GF(2^6)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Field( E(9) );  Field( CF(4), [ E(9) ] ); # abelian number fields|
  CF(9)
  AsField( GaussianRationals, CF(36) )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f1:= Field( EB(5) );  f2:= DefaultField( EB(5) );|
  NF(5,[ 1, 4 ])
  CF(5)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@f1 = f2;  IsSubset( f2, f1 );|
  false
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DefaultFieldByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 58, 1, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C298A40852C2AFF}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DefaultFieldByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape [z, ...]})\index{DefaultFieldByGenerators@\texttt{DefaultFieldByGenerators}}
\label{DefaultFieldByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns the default field containing the elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}, $\ldots$. This field may be bigger than the smallest field containing these elements. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfDivisionRing}}
\logpage{[ 58, 1, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7EF624958648D0FA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfDivisionRing({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{GeneratorsOfDivisionRing@\texttt{GeneratorsOfDivisionRing}}
\label{GeneratorsOfDivisionRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 generators with respect to addition, multiplication, and taking inverses (the
identity cannot be omitted ...) }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GeneratorsOfField}}
\logpage{[ 58, 1, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AA715317A81261B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GeneratorsOfField({\mdseries\slshape F})\index{GeneratorsOfField@\texttt{GeneratorsOfField}}
\label{GeneratorsOfField}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 generators with respect to addition, multiplication, and taking inverses. This
attribute is the same as \texttt{GeneratorsOfDivisionRing} (\ref{GeneratorsOfDivisionRing}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DivisionRingByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 58, 1, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8641861A8550F8BE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DivisionRingByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape [F, ]gens})\index{DivisionRingByGenerators@\texttt{DivisionRingByGenerators}}
\label{DivisionRingByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FieldByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape [F, ]gens})\index{FieldByGenerators@\texttt{FieldByGenerators}}
\label{FieldByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Called with a field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} and a list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} of scalars, \texttt{DivisionRingByGenerators} returns the division ring over \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} generated by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. The unary version returns the division ring as vector space over \texttt{FieldOverItselfByGenerators( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}} )}. 

 \texttt{FieldByGenerators} is just a synonym for \texttt{DivisionRingByGenerators}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AsDivisionRing}}
\logpage{[ 58, 1, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C193B7D7AFB29BE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AsDivisionRing({\mdseries\slshape [F, ]C})\index{AsDivisionRing@\texttt{AsDivisionRing}}
\label{AsDivisionRing}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AsField({\mdseries\slshape [F, ]C})\index{AsField@\texttt{AsField}}
\label{AsField}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 If the collection \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}} can be regarded as a division ring then \texttt{AsDivisionRing( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}} )} is the division ring that consists of the elements of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}}, viewed as a vector space over its prime field; otherwise \texttt{fail} is returned. 

 In the second form, if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} is a division ring contained in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape C}} then the returned division ring is viewed as a vector space over \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}. 

 \texttt{AsField} is just a synonym for \texttt{AsDivisionRing}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Subfields of Fields}}\label{Subfields of Fields}
\logpage{[ 58, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7C53566A839B57F6}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Subfield}}
\logpage{[ 58, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7FE1FA217A08DCE5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Subfield({\mdseries\slshape F, gens})\index{Subfield@\texttt{Subfield}}
\label{Subfield}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SubfieldNC({\mdseries\slshape F, gens})\index{SubfieldNC@\texttt{SubfieldNC}}

}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Constructs the subfield of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} generated by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape gens}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FieldOverItselfByGenerators}}
\logpage{[ 58, 2, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82A0E79A7B9799E0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FieldOverItselfByGenerators({\mdseries\slshape [z, ...]})\index{FieldOverItselfByGenerators@\texttt{FieldOverItselfByGenerators}}
\label{FieldOverItselfByGenerators}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 This operation is needed for the call of \texttt{Field} (\ref{Field:for several generators}) or \texttt{FieldByGenerators} (\ref{FieldByGenerators}) without explicitly given subfield, in order to construct a left acting domain
for such a field. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PrimitiveElement}}
\logpage{[ 58, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X86DB31B57FB4F570}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PrimitiveElement({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{PrimitiveElement@\texttt{PrimitiveElement}}
\label{PrimitiveElement}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is an element of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} that generates \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} as a division ring together with the left acting domain. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{PrimeField}}
\logpage{[ 58, 2, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DD27F927BD57FDE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PrimeField({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{PrimeField@\texttt{PrimeField}}
\label{PrimeField}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The \emph{prime field} of a division ring \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}} is the smallest field which is contained in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape D}}. For example, the prime field of any field in characteristic zero is
isomorphic to the field of rational numbers. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPrimeField}}
\logpage{[ 58, 2, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X84B6F1E67AD0E33D}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPrimeField({\mdseries\slshape D})\index{IsPrimeField@\texttt{IsPrimeField}}
\label{IsPrimeField}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A division ring is a prime field if it is equal to its prime field
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{PrimeField} (\ref{PrimeField})). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DegreeOverPrimeField}}

\hyperdef{L}{X7845CECE86A83219}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DegreeOverPrimeField({\mdseries\slshape F})\index{DegreeOverPrimeField@\texttt{DegreeOverPrimeField}}
\label{DegreeOverPrimeField}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the degree of the field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} over its prime field (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{PrimeField} (\ref{PrimeField})). }

\logpage{[ 58, 2, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7ADDCBF47E2ED3D4}{}

\label{DefiningPolynomial}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the defining polynomial of the field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} as a field extension over the left acting domain of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}. A root of the defining polynomial can be computed with \texttt{RootOfDefiningPolynomial} (\ref{RootOfDefiningPolynomial}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RootOfDefiningPolynomial}}
\logpage{[ 58, 2, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8173DA4982DB1E8A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RootOfDefiningPolynomial({\mdseries\slshape F})\index{RootOfDefiningPolynomial@\texttt{RootOfDefiningPolynomial}}
\label{RootOfDefiningPolynomial}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is a root in the field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} of its defining polynomial as a field extension over the left acting domain of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}. The defining polynomial can be computed with \texttt{DefiningPolynomial} (\ref{DefiningPolynomial}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FieldExtension}}
\logpage{[ 58, 2, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82718B3B818DC699}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FieldExtension({\mdseries\slshape F, poly})\index{FieldExtension@\texttt{FieldExtension}}
\label{FieldExtension}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 is the field obtained on adjoining a root of the irreducible polynomial \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape poly}} to the field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Subfields}}
\logpage{[ 58, 2, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83490C65819D85FE}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Subfields({\mdseries\slshape F})\index{Subfields@\texttt{Subfields}}
\label{Subfields}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 is the set of all subfields of the field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}.  }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Galois Action}}\label{Galois Action}
\logpage{[ 58, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7D9A02B07D08FA40}{}
{
  Let $L > K$ be a field extension of finite degree. Then to each element $\alpha \in L$, we can associate a $K$\texttt{\symbol{45}}linear mapping $\varphi_{\alpha}$ on $L$, and for a fixed $K$\texttt{\symbol{45}}basis of $L$, we can associate to $\alpha$ the matrix $M_{\alpha}$ (over $K$) of this mapping. 

 The \emph{norm} of $\alpha$ is defined as the determinant of $M_{\alpha}$, the \emph{trace} of $\alpha$ is defined as the trace of $M_{\alpha}$, the \emph{minimal polynomial} $\mu_{\alpha}$ and the \emph{trace polynomial} $\chi_{\alpha}$ of $\alpha$ are defined as the minimal polynomial (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{MinimalPolynomial}) and the characteristic polynomial (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{CharacteristicPolynomial} (\ref{CharacteristicPolynomial}) and \texttt{TracePolynomial} (\ref{TracePolynomial})) of $M_{\alpha}$. (Note that $\mu_{\alpha}$ depends only on $K$ whereas $\chi_{\alpha}$ depends on both $L$ and $K$.) 

 Thus norm and trace of $\alpha$ are elements of $K$, and $\mu_{\alpha}$ and $\chi_{\alpha}$ are polynomials over $K$, $\chi_{\alpha}$ being a power of $\mu_{\alpha}$, and the degree of $\chi_{\alpha}$ equals the degree of the field extension $L > K$. 

 The \emph{conjugates} of $\alpha$ in $L$ are those roots of $\chi_{\alpha}$ (with multiplicity) that lie in $L$; note that if only $L$ is given, there is in general no way to access the roots outside $L$. 

 Analogously, the \emph{Galois group} of the extension $L > K$ is defined as the group of all those field automorphisms of $L$ that fix $K$ pointwise. 

 If $L > K$ is a Galois extension then the conjugates of $\alpha$ are all roots of $\chi_{\alpha}$ (with multiplicity), the set of conjugates equals the roots of $\mu_{\alpha}$, the norm of $\alpha$ equals the product and the trace of $\alpha$ equals the sum of the conjugates of $\alpha$, and the Galois group in the sense of the above definition equals the usual
Galois group, 

 Note that \texttt{MinimalPolynomial( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} )} is a polynomial \emph{over} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}, whereas \texttt{Norm( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}, \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} )} is the norm of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} \emph{in} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} w.r.t.{\nobreakspace}the field extension \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} {\textgreater} LeftActingDomain( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} )}. 

 The default methods for field elements are as follows. \texttt{MinimalPolynomial} (\ref{MinimalPolynomial}) solves a system of linear equations, \texttt{TracePolynomial} (\ref{TracePolynomial}) computes the appropriate power of the minimal polynomial, \texttt{Norm} (\ref{Norm}) and \texttt{Trace} (\ref{Trace:for a field element}) values are obtained as coefficients of the characteristic polynomial, and \texttt{Conjugates} (\ref{Conjugates}) uses the factorization of the characteristic polynomial. 

 For elements in finite fields and cyclotomic fields, one wants to do the
computations in a different way since the field extensions in question are
Galois extensions, and the Galois groups are well\texttt{\symbol{45}}known in
these cases. More general, if a field is in the category \texttt{IsFieldControlledByGaloisGroup} then the default methods are the following. \texttt{Conjugates} (\ref{Conjugates}) returns the sorted list of images (with multiplicity) of the element under the
Galois group, \texttt{Norm} (\ref{Norm}) computes the product of the conjugates, \texttt{Trace} (\ref{Trace:for a field element}) computes the sum of the conjugates, \texttt{TracePolynomial} (\ref{TracePolynomial}) and \texttt{MinimalPolynomial} (\ref{MinimalPolynomial}) compute the product of linear factors $x - c$ with $c$ ranging over the conjugates and the set of conjugates, respectively. \index{IsFieldControlledByGaloisGroup@\texttt{IsFieldControlledByGaloisGroup}} 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GaloisGroup (of field)}}
\logpage{[ 58, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80CAA5BA82F09ED2}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GaloisGroup({\mdseries\slshape F})\index{GaloisGroup@\texttt{GaloisGroup}!of field}
\label{GaloisGroup:of field}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 The \emph{Galois group} of a field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} is the group of all field automorphisms of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} that fix the subfield $K = $\texttt{LeftActingDomain( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} )} pointwise. 

 Note that the field extension $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} > K$ need \emph{not} be a Galois extension. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@g:= GaloisGroup( AsField( GF(2^2), GF(2^12) ) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size( g );  IsCyclic( g );|
  6
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@h:= GaloisGroup( CF(60) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Size( h );  IsAbelian( h );|
  16
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MinimalPolynomial (over a field)}}
\logpage{[ 58, 3, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8738C6687D784BB5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MinimalPolynomial({\mdseries\slshape F, z[, ind]})\index{MinimalPolynomial@\texttt{MinimalPolynomial}!over a field}
\label{MinimalPolynomial:over a field}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 returns the minimal polynomial of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} over the field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}. This is a generator of the ideal in $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}[x]$ of all polynomials which vanish on \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}. (This definition is consistent with the general definition of \texttt{MinimalPolynomial} (\ref{MinimalPolynomial}) for rings.) 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MinimalPolynomial( Rationals, E(8) );|
  x_1^4+1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MinimalPolynomial( CF(4), E(8) );|
  x_1^2+(-E(4))
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MinimalPolynomial( CF(8), E(8) );|
  x_1+(-E(8))
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TracePolynomial}}
\logpage{[ 58, 3, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X80FE7E017C2D255C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TracePolynomial({\mdseries\slshape L, K, z[, inum]})\index{TracePolynomial@\texttt{TracePolynomial}}
\label{TracePolynomial}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \index{characteristic polynomial!for field elements} returns the polynomial that is the product of $(X - c)$ where $c$ runs over the conjugates of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} in the field extension \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} over \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}}. The polynomial is returned as a univariate polynomial over \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}} in the indeterminate number \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape inum}} (defaulting to 1). 

 This polynomial is sometimes also called the \emph{characteristic polynomial} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} w.r.t.{\nobreakspace}the field extension $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} > \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}}$. Therefore methods are installed for \texttt{CharacteristicPolynomial} (\ref{CharacteristicPolynomial}) that call \texttt{TracePolynomial} in the case of field extensions. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TracePolynomial( CF(8), Rationals, E(8) );|
  x_1^4+1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TracePolynomial( CF(16), Rationals, E(8) );|
  x_1^8+2*x_1^4+1
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Norm}}
\logpage{[ 58, 3, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X838515278587FF01}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Norm({\mdseries\slshape [L, [K, ]]z})\index{Norm@\texttt{Norm}}
\label{Norm}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 \texttt{Norm} returns the norm of the field element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}. If two fields \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}} are given then the norm is computed w.r.t.{\nobreakspace}the field extension \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}}$ > $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}}, if only one field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} is given then \texttt{LeftActingDomain( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} )} is taken as default for the subfield \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}}, and if no field is given then \texttt{DefaultField( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} )} is taken as default for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}}. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Traces of field elements and matrices}}\logpage{[ 58, 3, 5 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7DD17EB581200AD6}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Trace({\mdseries\slshape [L, [K, ]]z})\index{Trace@\texttt{Trace}!for a field element}
\label{Trace:for a field element}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Trace({\mdseries\slshape mat})\index{Trace@\texttt{Trace}!for a matrix}
\label{Trace:for a matrix}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 \texttt{Trace} returns the trace of the field element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}. If two fields \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}} are given then the trace is computed w.r.t.{\nobreakspace}the field extension $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} > \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}}$, if only one field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} is given then \texttt{LeftActingDomain( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} )} is taken as default for the subfield \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}}, and if no field is given then \texttt{DefaultField( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} )} is taken as default for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}}. 

 The \emph{trace of a matrix} is the sum of its diagonal entries. Note that this is \emph{not} compatible with the definition of \texttt{Trace} for field elements, so the one\texttt{\symbol{45}}argument version is not
suitable when matrices shall be regarded as field elements.   }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Conjugates}}
\logpage{[ 58, 3, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X837A4A5781F8EE92}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Conjugates({\mdseries\slshape [L, [K, ]]z})\index{Conjugates@\texttt{Conjugates}}
\label{Conjugates}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 \texttt{Conjugates} returns the list of \emph{conjugates} of the field element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}. If two fields \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}} are given then the conjugates are computed w.r.t.{\nobreakspace}the field
extension \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}}$ > $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}}, if only one field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} is given then \texttt{LeftActingDomain( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}} )} is taken as default for the subfield \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape K}}, and if no field is given then \texttt{DefaultField( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} )} is taken as default for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}}. 

 The result list will contain duplicates if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} lies in a proper subfield of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape L}}, or of the default field of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}, respectively. The result list need not be sorted. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Norm( E(8) );  Norm( CF(8), E(8) );|
  1
  1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Norm( CF(8), CF(4), E(8) );|
  -E(4)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Norm( AsField( CF(4), CF(8) ), E(8) );|
  -E(4)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Trace( E(8) );  Trace( CF(8), CF(8), E(8) );|
  0
  E(8)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Conjugates( CF(8), E(8) );|
  [ E(8), E(8)^3, -E(8), -E(8)^3 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Conjugates( CF(8), CF(4), E(8) );|
  [ E(8), -E(8) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Conjugates( CF(16), E(8) );|
  [ E(8), E(8)^3, -E(8), -E(8)^3, E(8), E(8)^3, -E(8), -E(8)^3 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{NormalBase}}
\logpage{[ 58, 3, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8236A8B47E6AAD93}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{NormalBase({\mdseries\slshape F[, elm]})\index{NormalBase@\texttt{NormalBase}}
\label{NormalBase}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} be a field that is a Galois extension of its subfield \texttt{LeftActingDomain( \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} )}. Then \texttt{NormalBase} returns a list of elements in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} that form a normal basis of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}, that is, a vector space basis that is closed under the action of the Galois
group (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{GaloisGroup} (\ref{GaloisGroup:of field})) of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}}. 

 If a second argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape elm}} is given, it is used as a hint for the algorithm to find a normal basis with
the algorithm described in{\nobreakspace}\cite{Art68}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NormalBase( CF(5) );|
  [ -E(5), -E(5)^2, -E(5)^3, -E(5)^4 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NormalBase( CF(4) );|
  [ 1/2-1/2*E(4), 1/2+1/2*E(4) ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NormalBase( GF(3^6) );|
  [ Z(3^6)^2, Z(3^6)^6, Z(3^6)^18, Z(3^6)^54, Z(3^6)^162, Z(3^6)^486 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@NormalBase( GF( GF(8), 2 ) );|
  [ Z(2^6), Z(2^6)^8 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

     }

            
\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Finite Fields}}\label{Finite Fields}
\logpage{[ 59, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7893ABF67A028802}{}
{
  This chapter describes the special functionality which exists in \textsf{GAP} for finite fields and their elements. Of course the general functionality for
fields (see Chapter{\nobreakspace}\ref{Fields and Division Rings}) also applies to finite fields. 

 In the following, the term \emph{finite field element} is used to denote \textsf{GAP} objects in the category \texttt{IsFFE} (\ref{IsFFE}), and \emph{finite field} means a field consisting of such elements. Note that in principle we must
distinguish these fields from (abstract) finite fields. For example, the image
of the embedding of a finite field into a field of rational functions in the
same characteristic is of course a finite field but its elements are not in \texttt{IsFFE} (\ref{IsFFE}), and in fact \textsf{GAP} does currently not support such fields. 

 Special representations exist for row vectors and matrices over small finite
fields (see sections{\nobreakspace}\ref{Row Vectors over Finite Fields} and{\nobreakspace}\ref{Matrices over Finite Fields}).  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Finite Field Elements}}\label{Finite Field Elements}
\logpage{[ 59, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7B9DCCCC83400B47}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsFFE}}
\logpage{[ 59, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D3DF32C84FEBD25}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFFE({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsFFE@\texttt{IsFFE}}
\label{IsFFE}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFFECollection({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsFFECollection@\texttt{IsFFECollection}}
\label{IsFFECollection}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFFECollColl({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsFFECollColl@\texttt{IsFFECollColl}}
\label{IsFFECollColl}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsFFECollCollColl({\mdseries\slshape obj})\index{IsFFECollCollColl@\texttt{IsFFECollCollColl}}
\label{IsFFECollCollColl}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 Objects in the category \texttt{IsFFE} are used to implement elements of finite fields. In this manual, the term \emph{finite field element} always means an object in \texttt{IsFFE}. All finite field elements of the same characteristic form a family in \textsf{GAP} (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Families}). Any collection of finite field elements of the same characteristic
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsCollection} (\ref{IsCollection})) lies in \texttt{IsFFECollection}, and a collection of such collections (e.g., a matrix of finite field
elements) lies in \texttt{IsFFECollColl}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Z (for field size)}}
\logpage{[ 59, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7AA52FAF7EDEDD56}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Z({\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}d})\index{Z@\texttt{Z}!for field size}
\label{Z:for field size}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Z({\mdseries\slshape p, d})\index{Z@\texttt{Z}!for prime and degree}
\label{Z:for prime and degree}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For creating elements of a finite field, the function \texttt{Z} can be used. The call \texttt{Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}},\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}})} (alternatively \texttt{Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}\texttt{\symbol{94}}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}})}) returns the designated generator of the multiplicative group of the finite
field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}d}} elements. \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}} must be a prime integer. 

 \textsf{GAP} can represent elements of all finite fields \texttt{GF(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}d}})} such that either (1) \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}d}} $<= 65536$ (in which case an extremely efficient internal representation is used); (2) d
= 1, (in which case, for large \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}, the field is represented using the machinery of residue class rings (see
section{\nobreakspace}\ref{Residue Class Rings}) or (3) if the Conway polynomial of degree \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} over the field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}} elements is known, or can be computed (see \texttt{ConwayPolynomial} (\ref{ConwayPolynomial})). 

 If you attempt to construct an element of \texttt{GF(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}d}})} for which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape d}} $> 1$ and the relevant Conway polynomial is not known, and not necessarily easy to
find (see \texttt{IsCheapConwayPolynomial} (\ref{IsCheapConwayPolynomial})), then \textsf{GAP} will stop with an error and enter the break loop. If you leave this break loop
by entering \texttt{return;} \textsf{GAP} will attempt to compute the Conway polynomial, which may take a very long
time. 

 The root returned by \texttt{Z} is a generator of the multiplicative group of the finite field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}d}} elements, which is cyclic. The order of the element is of course \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}d}} $-1$. The \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}d}} $-1$ different powers of the root are exactly the nonzero elements of the finite
field. 

 Thus all nonzero elements of the finite field with \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}d}} elements can be entered as \texttt{Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}d}})\texttt{\symbol{94}}}$i$. Note that this is also the form that \textsf{GAP} uses to output those elements when they are stored in the internal
representation. In larger fields, it is more convenient to enter and print
elements as linear combinations of powers of the primitive element, see
section \ref{Printing, Viewing and Displaying Finite Field Elements}. 

 The additive neutral element is \texttt{0 * Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}})}. It is different from the integer \texttt{0} in subtle ways. First \texttt{IsInt( 0 * Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}) )} (see \texttt{IsInt} (\ref{IsInt})) is \texttt{false} and \texttt{IsFFE( 0 * Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}) )} (see \texttt{IsFFE} (\ref{IsFFE})) is \texttt{true}, whereas it is just the other way around for the integer \texttt{0}. 

 The multiplicative neutral element is \texttt{Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}})\texttt{\symbol{94}}0}. It is different from the integer \texttt{1} in subtle ways. First \texttt{IsInt( Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}})\texttt{\symbol{94}}0 )} (see \texttt{IsInt} (\ref{IsInt})) is \texttt{false} and \texttt{IsFFE( Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}})\texttt{\symbol{94}}0 )} (see \texttt{IsFFE} (\ref{IsFFE})) is \texttt{true}, whereas it is just the other way around for the integer \texttt{1}. Also \texttt{1+1} is \texttt{2}, whereas, e.g., \texttt{Z(2)\texttt{\symbol{94}}0 + Z(2)\texttt{\symbol{94}}0} is \texttt{0 * Z(2)}. 

 The various roots returned by \texttt{Z} for finite fields of the same characteristic are compatible in the following
sense. If the field \texttt{GF(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}},}$n$\texttt{)} is a subfield of the field \texttt{GF(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}},}$m$\texttt{)}, i.e., $n$ divides $m$, then \texttt{Z}$(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}^n) = $\texttt{Z}$(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}^m)^{{(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}^m-1)/(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}^n-1)}}$. Note that this is the simplest relation that may hold between a generator of \texttt{GF(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}},}$n$\texttt{)} and \texttt{GF(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}},}$m$\texttt{)}, since \texttt{Z}$(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}^n)$ is an element of order $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}^m-1$ and \texttt{Z}$(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}^m)$ is an element of order $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}^n-1$. This is achieved by choosing \texttt{Z(\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}})} as the smallest primitive root modulo \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}} and \texttt{Z(}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p\texttt{\symbol{94}}n}}\texttt{)} as a root of the $n$\texttt{\symbol{45}}th \emph{Conway polynomial} (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{ConwayPolynomial} (\ref{ConwayPolynomial})) of characteristic \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}. Those polynomials were defined by J.{\nobreakspace}H.{\nobreakspace}Conway,
and many of them were computed by R.{\nobreakspace}A.{\nobreakspace}Parker. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a:= Z( 32 );|
  Z(2^5)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a+a;|
  0*Z(2)
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@a*a;|
  Z(2^5)^2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@b := Z(3,12);|
  z
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@b*b;|
  z2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@b+b;|
  2z
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Print(b^100,"\n");|
  Z(3)^0+Z(3,12)^5+Z(3,12)^6+2*Z(3,12)^8+Z(3,12)^10+Z(3,12)^11
\end{Verbatim}
 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!|B,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt|gap>B !gapinput|Z(11,40);B
  Error, Conway Polynomial 11^40 will need to be computed and might be slow
  Stack trace:
  *[1] Error( "Conway Polynomial ", p, "^", d, " will need to be computed and might be slow" );
     @ GAPROOT/lib/ffeconway.gi:81
   [2] FFECONWAY.SetUpConwayStuff( p, d );
     @ GAPROOT/lib/ffeconway.gi:140
   [3] FFECONWAY.ZNC( p, d )
     @ GAPROOT/lib/ffeconway.gi:167
  <function "ZOp method">( <arguments> )
   called from read-eval loop at *stdin*:2
  you can enter 'quit;' to quit to outer loop, or
  you can enter 'return;' to continue
  !gapbrkprompt|brk>B !gapinput|B
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsLexOrderedFFE}}
\logpage{[ 59, 1, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8612BCEA816CF1B9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLexOrderedFFE({\mdseries\slshape ffe})\index{IsLexOrderedFFE@\texttt{IsLexOrderedFFE}}
\label{IsLexOrderedFFE}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsLogOrderedFFE({\mdseries\slshape ffe})\index{IsLogOrderedFFE@\texttt{IsLogOrderedFFE}}
\label{IsLogOrderedFFE}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (Category)}}\\


 Elements of finite fields can be compared using the operators \texttt{=} and \texttt{{\textless}}. The call \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape a}} = \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape b}}} returns \texttt{true} if and only if the finite field elements \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape a}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape b}} are equal. Furthermore \texttt{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape a}} {\textless} \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape b}}} tests whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape a}} is smaller than \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape b}}. The exact behaviour of this comparison depends on which of two categories
the field elements belong to: 

 Finite field elements are ordered in \textsf{GAP} (by \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}{\textless}} (\ref{bSlash<})) first by characteristic and then by their degree (i.e. the sizes of the
smallest fields containing them). Amongst irreducible elements of a given
field, the ordering depends on which of these categories the elements of the
field belong to (all irreducible elements of a given field should belong to
the same one) 

 Elements in \texttt{IsLexOrderedFFE} are ordered lexicographically by their coefficients with respect to the
canonical basis of the field. 

 Elements in \texttt{IsLogOrderedFFE} are ordered according to their discrete logarithms with respect to the \texttt{PrimitiveRoot} (\ref{PrimitiveRoot}) attribute of the field. For the comparison of finite field elements with other \textsf{GAP} objects, see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Comparisons}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Z( 16 )^10 = Z( 4 )^2;  # illustrates embedding of GF(4) in GF(16)|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@0 < 0*Z(101);|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Z(256) > Z(101);|
  false
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Z(2,20) < Z(2,20)^2; # this illustrates the lexicographic ordering|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Operations for Finite Field Elements}}\label{Operations for Finite Field Elements}
\logpage{[ 59, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7A79399283EF78D0}{}
{
  Since finite field elements are scalars, the operations \texttt{Characteristic} (\ref{Characteristic}), \texttt{One} (\ref{One}), \texttt{Zero} (\ref{Zero}), \texttt{Inverse} (\ref{Inverse}), \texttt{AdditiveInverse} (\ref{AdditiveInverse}), \texttt{Order} (\ref{Order}) can be applied to them (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Attributes and Properties of Elements}). Contrary to the situation with other scalars, \texttt{Order} (\ref{Order}) is defined also for the zero element in a finite field, with value \texttt{0}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Characteristic( Z( 16 )^10 );  Characteristic( Z( 9 )^2 );|
  2
  3
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Characteristic( [ Z(4), Z(8) ] );|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@One( Z(9) );  One( 0*Z(4) );|
  Z(3)^0
  Z(2)^0
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Inverse( Z(9) );  AdditiveInverse( Z(9) );|
  Z(3^2)^7
  Z(3^2)^5
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Order( Z(9)^7 );|
  8
\end{Verbatim}
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DegreeFFE (for a FFE)}}
\logpage{[ 59, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X828E846E7C1EA3DD}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DegreeFFE({\mdseries\slshape z})\index{DegreeFFE@\texttt{DegreeFFE}!for a FFE}
\label{DegreeFFE:for a FFE}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DegreeFFE({\mdseries\slshape vec})\index{DegreeFFE@\texttt{DegreeFFE}!for a vector of FFEs}
\label{DegreeFFE:for a vector of FFEs}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DegreeFFE({\mdseries\slshape mat})\index{DegreeFFE@\texttt{DegreeFFE}!for a matrix of FFEs}
\label{DegreeFFE:for a matrix of FFEs}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\


 \texttt{DegreeFFE} returns the degree of the smallest finite field \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} containing the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}, respectively all elements of the row vector \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape vec}} over a finite field (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Row Vectors}), or the matrix \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape mat}} over a finite field (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Matrices}). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DegreeFFE( Z( 16 )^10 );|
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DegreeFFE( Z( 16 )^11 );|
  4
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DegreeFFE( [ Z(2^13), Z(2^10) ] );|
  130
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LogFFE}}
\logpage{[ 59, 2, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B049A3478B369E4}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LogFFE({\mdseries\slshape z, r})\index{LogFFE@\texttt{LogFFE}}
\label{LogFFE}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 \texttt{LogFFE} returns the discrete logarithm of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} in a finite field with respect to the root \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}. An error is signalled if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} is zero. \texttt{fail} is returned if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} is not a power of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}. 

 The \emph{discrete logarithm} of the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}} with respect to the root \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}} is the smallest nonnegative integer $i$ such that $\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape r}}^i = \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}$ holds. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@LogFFE( Z(409)^116, Z(409) );  LogFFE( Z(409)^116, Z(409)^2 );|
  116
  58
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IntFFE}}
\logpage{[ 59, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79F48E337FC2746A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IntFFE({\mdseries\slshape z})\index{IntFFE@\texttt{IntFFE}}
\label{IntFFE}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{Int({\mdseries\slshape z})\index{Int@\texttt{Int}!for a FFE}
\label{Int:for a FFE}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (method)}}\\


 \texttt{IntFFE} returns the integer corresponding to the element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}, which must lie in a finite prime field. That is, \texttt{IntFFE} returns the smallest nonnegative integer $i$ such that $i$\texttt{ * One( }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}\texttt{ ) = }\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}. 

 The correspondence between elements from a finite prime field of
characteristic $p$ (for $p < 2^{16}$) and the integers between $0$ and $p-1$ is defined by choosing \texttt{Z(}$p$\texttt{)} the element corresponding to the smallest primitive root mod $p$ (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{PrimitiveRootMod} (\ref{PrimitiveRootMod})). 

 \texttt{IntFFE} is installed as a method for the operation \texttt{Int} (\ref{Int}) with argument a finite field element. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IntFFE( Z(13) );  PrimitiveRootMod( 13 );|
  2
  2
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IntFFE( Z(409) );|
  21
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IntFFE( Z(409)^116 );  21^116 mod 409;|
  311
  311
\end{Verbatim}
 See also \texttt{IntFFESymm} (\ref{IntFFESymm:for a FFE}). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IntFFESymm (for a FFE)}}
\logpage{[ 59, 2, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DABD827848BCC2A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IntFFESymm({\mdseries\slshape z})\index{IntFFESymm@\texttt{IntFFESymm}!for a FFE}
\label{IntFFESymm:for a FFE}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IntFFESymm({\mdseries\slshape vec})\index{IntFFESymm@\texttt{IntFFESymm}!for a vector of FFEs}
\label{IntFFESymm:for a vector of FFEs}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 For a finite prime field element \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape z}}, \texttt{IntFFESymm} returns the corresponding integer of smallest absolute value.
