 For a group character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} of a group $G$ and a normal subgroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} of $G$, \texttt{TestHomogeneous} returns a record with information whether the restriction of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} is homogeneous, i.e., is a multiple of an irreducible character. 

 \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} may be given also as list of conjugacy class positions
w.r.t.{\nobreakspace}the character table of $G$. 

 The components of the result are 

 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{isHomogeneous}}]  \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}, 
\item[{\texttt{comment}}]  a string telling a reason for the value of the \texttt{isHomogeneous} component, 
\item[{\texttt{character}}]  irreducible constituent of the restriction, only bound if the restriction had
to be checked, 
\item[{\texttt{multiplicity}}]  multiplicity of the \texttt{character} component in the restriction of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}}. 
\end{description}
 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@n:= DerivedSubgroup( Sl23 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@chi:= Irr( Sl23 )[7];|
  Character( CharacterTable( SL(2,3) ), [ 3, 0, 0, 3, 0, 0, -1 ] )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@test:= TestHomogeneous( chi, n );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@test.isHomogeneous;  test.comment;  test.multiplicity;|
  false
  "restriction checked"
  1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Degree( test.character );|
  1
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@chi:= Irr( Sl23 )[4];|
  Character( CharacterTable( SL(2,3) ), [ 2, 1, 1, -2, -1, -1, 0 ] )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@cln:= ClassPositionsOfNormalSubgroup( CharacterTable( Sl23 ), n );|
  [ 1, 4, 7 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestHomogeneous( chi, cln );|
  rec( comment := "restricts irreducibly", isHomogeneous := true )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPrimitiveCharacter}}
\logpage{[ 75, 3, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7BC72ECE822D4245}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPrimitiveCharacter({\mdseries\slshape chi})\index{IsPrimitiveCharacter@\texttt{IsPrimitiveCharacter}}
\label{IsPrimitiveCharacter}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 For a character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} of a group $G$, \texttt{IsPrimitiveCharacter} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is not induced from any proper subgroup, and \texttt{false} otherwise. This currently only works for characters of soluble groups. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsPrimitiveCharacter( Irr( Sl23 )[4] );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsPrimitiveCharacter( Irr( Sl23 )[7] );|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TestQuasiPrimitive}}
\logpage{[ 75, 3, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X82BFA6968415F308}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestQuasiPrimitive({\mdseries\slshape chi})\index{TestQuasiPrimitive@\texttt{TestQuasiPrimitive}}
\label{TestQuasiPrimitive}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsQuasiPrimitive({\mdseries\slshape chi})\index{IsQuasiPrimitive@\texttt{IsQuasiPrimitive}}
\label{IsQuasiPrimitive}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 \texttt{TestQuasiPrimitive} returns a record with information about quasiprimitivity of the group
character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}}, i.e., whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} restricts homogeneously to every normal subgroup of its group. The result
record contains at least the components \texttt{isQuasiPrimitive} (with value either \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}) and \texttt{comment} (a string telling a reason for the value of the component \texttt{isQuasiPrimitive}). If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is not quasiprimitive then there is additionally a component \texttt{character}, with value an irreducible constituent of a nonhomogeneous restriction of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}}. 

 \texttt{IsQuasiPrimitive} returns \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}, depending on whether the character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is quasiprimitive. 

 Note that for solvable groups, quasiprimitivity is the same as primitivity
(see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{IsPrimitiveCharacter} (\ref{IsPrimitiveCharacter})). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@chi:= Irr( Sl23 )[4];|
  Character( CharacterTable( SL(2,3) ), [ 2, 1, 1, -2, -1, -1, 0 ] )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestQuasiPrimitive( chi );|
  rec( comment := "all restrictions checked", isQuasiPrimitive := true )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@chi:= Irr( Sl23 )[7];|
  Character( CharacterTable( SL(2,3) ), [ 3, 0, 0, 3, 0, 0, -1 ] )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@test:= TestQuasiPrimitive( chi );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@test.isQuasiPrimitive;  test.comment;|
  false
  "restriction checked"
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Degree( test.character );|
  1
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TestInducedFromNormalSubgroup}}
\logpage{[ 75, 3, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X84860E3A7FECDBA3}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestInducedFromNormalSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape chi[, N]})\index{TestInducedFromNormalSubgroup@\texttt{TestInducedFromNormalSubgroup}}
\label{TestInducedFromNormalSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsInducedFromNormalSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape chi})\index{IsInducedFromNormalSubgroup@\texttt{IsInducedFromNormalSubgroup}}
\label{IsInducedFromNormalSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 \texttt{TestInducedFromNormalSubgroup} returns a record with information whether the irreducible character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} of the group $G$ is induced from a proper normal subgroup of $G$. If the second argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} is present, which must be a normal subgroup of $G$ or the list of class positions of a normal subgroup of $G$, it is checked whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is induced from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}}. 

 The result contains always the components \texttt{isInduced} (either \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}) and \texttt{comment} (a string telling a reason for the value of the component \texttt{isInduced}). In the \texttt{true} case there is a component \texttt{character} which contains a character of a maximal normal subgroup from which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is induced. 

 \texttt{IsInducedFromNormalSubgroup} returns \texttt{true} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is induced from a proper normal subgroup of $G$, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List( Irr( Sl23 ), IsInducedFromNormalSubgroup );|
  [ false, false, false, false, false, false, true ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List( Irr( S4 ){ [ 1, 3, 4 ] },|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@         TestInducedFromNormalSubgroup );|
  [ rec( comment := "linear character", isInduced := false ),
    rec( character := Character( CharacterTable( Alt( [ 1 .. 4 ] ) ),
          [ 1, 1, E(3), E(3)^2 ] ),
        comment := "induced from component '.character'",
        isInduced := true ),
    rec( comment := "all maximal normal subgroups checked",
        isInduced := false ) ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Testing Monomiality}}\label{Testing Monomiality}
\logpage{[ 75, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X86567D7F781BBCAE}{}
{
  A character $\chi$ of a finite group $G$ is called \emph{monomial} if $\chi$ is induced from a linear character of a subgroup of $G$. A finite group $G$ is called \emph{monomial} (or \emph{$M$\texttt{\symbol{45}}group}) if each ordinary irreducible character of $G$ is monomial. 

  
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TestMonomial}}\logpage{[ 75, 4, 1 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X84EB92B57DAF5C93}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestMonomial({\mdseries\slshape chi})\index{TestMonomial@\texttt{TestMonomial}!for a character}
\label{TestMonomial:for a character}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestMonomial({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{TestMonomial@\texttt{TestMonomial}!for a group}
\label{TestMonomial:for a group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestMonomial({\mdseries\slshape chi, uselattice})\index{TestMonomial@\texttt{TestMonomial}!for a character and a Boolean}
\label{TestMonomial:for a character and a Boolean}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestMonomial({\mdseries\slshape G, uselattice})\index{TestMonomial@\texttt{TestMonomial}!for a group and a Boolean}
\label{TestMonomial:for a group and a Boolean}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 Called with a group character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} of a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, \texttt{TestMonomial} returns a record containing information about monomiality of the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} or the group character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}}, respectively. 

 If \texttt{TestMonomial} proves the character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} to be monomial then the result contains components \texttt{isMonomial} (with value \texttt{true}), \texttt{comment} (a string telling a reason for monomiality), and if it was necessary to
compute a linear character from which \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is induced, also a component \texttt{character}. 

 If \texttt{TestMonomial} proves \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} or \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} to be nonmonomial then the value of the component \texttt{isMonomial} is \texttt{false}, and in the case of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} a nonmonomial character is the value of the component \texttt{character} if it had been necessary to compute it. 

 A Boolean can be entered as the second argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape uselattice}}; if the value is \texttt{true} then the subgroup lattice of the underlying group is used if necessary, if the
value is \texttt{false} then the subgroup lattice is used only for groups of order at most \texttt{TestMonomialUseLattice} (\ref{TestMonomialUseLattice}). The default value of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape uselattice}} is \texttt{false}. 

 For a group whose lattice must not be used, it may happen that \texttt{TestMonomial} cannot prove or disprove monomiality; then the result record contains the
component \texttt{isMonomial} with value \texttt{"?"}. This case occurs in the call for a character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} if and only if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is not induced from the inertia subgroup of a component of any reducible
restriction to a normal subgroup. It can happen that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is monomial in this situation. For a group, this case occurs if no irreducible
character can be proved to be nonmonomial, and if no decision is possible for
at least one irreducible character. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestMonomial( S4 );|
  rec( comment := "abelian by supersolvable group", isMonomial := true )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestMonomial( Sl23 );|
  rec( comment := "list Delta( G ) contains entry > 1",
    isMonomial := false )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TestMonomialUseLattice}}
\logpage{[ 75, 4, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X787CCCBB7FC17F5E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestMonomialUseLattice\index{TestMonomialUseLattice@\texttt{TestMonomialUseLattice}}
\label{TestMonomialUseLattice}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (global variable)}}\\


 This global variable controls for which groups the operation \texttt{TestMonomial} (\ref{TestMonomial:for a group and a Boolean}) may compute the subgroup lattice. The value can be set to a positive integer
or \texttt{infinity} (\ref{infinity}), the default is $1000$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsMonomialNumber}}
\logpage{[ 75, 4, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8261B5AA7BCFFCC2}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsMonomialNumber({\mdseries\slshape n})\index{IsMonomialNumber@\texttt{IsMonomialNumber}}
\label{IsMonomialNumber}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 For a positive integer \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}, \texttt{IsMonomialNumber} returns \texttt{true} if every solvable group of order \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}} is monomial, and \texttt{false} otherwise. One can also use \texttt{IsMonomial} instead. \index{IsMonomial@\texttt{IsMonomial}!for positive integers} 

 Let $\nu_p(n)$ denote the multiplicity of the prime $p$ as factor of $n$, and $ord(p,q)$ the multiplicative order of $p \pmod{q}$. 

 Then there exists a solvable nonmonomial group of order $n$ if and only if one of the following conditions is satisfied. 

 
\begin{description}
\item[{1.}]  $\nu_2(n) \geq 2$ and there is a $p$ such that $\nu_p(n) \geq 3$ and $p \equiv -1 \pmod{4}$, 
\item[{2.}]  $\nu_2(n) \geq 3$ and there is a $p$ such that $\nu_p(n) \geq 3$ and $p \equiv 1 \pmod{4}$, 
\item[{3.}]  there are odd prime divisors $p$ and $q$ of $n$ such that $ord(p,q)$ is even and $ord(p,q) < \nu_p(n)$ (especially $\nu_p(n) \geq 3$), 
\item[{4.}]  there is a prime divisor $q$ of $n$ such that $\nu_2(n) \geq 2 ord(2,q) + 2$ (especially $\nu_2(n) \geq 4$), 
\item[{5.}]  $\nu_2(n) \geq 2$ and there is a $p$ such that $p \equiv 1 \pmod{4}$, $ord(p,q)$ is odd, and $2 ord(p,q) < \nu_p(n)$ (especially $\nu_p(n) \geq 3$). 
\end{description}
 

 These five possibilities correspond to the five types of solvable minimal
nonmonomial groups (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{MinimalNonmonomialGroup} (\ref{MinimalNonmonomialGroup})) that can occur as subgroups and factor groups of groups of order \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape n}}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Filtered( [ 1 .. 111 ], x -> not IsMonomial( x ) );|
  [ 24, 48, 72, 96, 108 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TestMonomialQuick}}\logpage{[ 75, 4, 4 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X822E03EF7B8F92D3}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestMonomialQuick({\mdseries\slshape chi})\index{TestMonomialQuick@\texttt{TestMonomialQuick}!for a character}
\label{TestMonomialQuick:for a character}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestMonomialQuick({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{TestMonomialQuick@\texttt{TestMonomialQuick}!for a group}
\label{TestMonomialQuick:for a group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\


 \texttt{TestMonomialQuick} does some cheap tests whether the irreducible character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} or the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, respectively, is monomial. Here ``cheap'' means in particular that no computations of character tables are involved, and
it is \emph{not} checked whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is a character and irreducible. The return value is a record with components 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{isMonomial}}]  either \texttt{true} or \texttt{false} or the string \texttt{"?"}, depending on whether (non)monomiality could be proved, and 
\item[{\texttt{comment}}]  a string telling the reason for the value of the \texttt{isMonomial} component. 
\end{description}
 

 A group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is proved to be monomial by \texttt{TestMonomialQuick} if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is nilpotent or Sylow abelian by supersolvable, or if \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is solvable and its order is not divisible by the third power of a prime,
Nonsolvable groups are proved to be nonmonomial by \texttt{TestMonomialQuick}. 

 An irreducible character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is proved to be monomial if it is linear, or if its codegree is a prime power,
or if its group knows to be monomial, or if the factor group modulo the kernel
can be proved to be monomial by \texttt{TestMonomialQuick}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestMonomialQuick( Irr( S4 )[3] );|
  rec( comment := "whole group is monomial", isMonomial := true )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestMonomialQuick( S4 );|
  rec( comment := "abelian by supersolvable group", isMonomial := true )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestMonomialQuick( Sl23 );|
  rec( comment := "no decision by cheap tests", isMonomial := "?" )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TestSubnormallyMonomial}}\logpage{[ 75, 4, 5 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7E56A0EA868CC34A}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestSubnormallyMonomial({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{TestSubnormallyMonomial@\texttt{TestSubnormallyMonomial}!for a group}
\label{TestSubnormallyMonomial:for a group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestSubnormallyMonomial({\mdseries\slshape chi})\index{TestSubnormallyMonomial@\texttt{TestSubnormallyMonomial}!for a character}
\label{TestSubnormallyMonomial:for a character}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSubnormallyMonomial({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsSubnormallyMonomial@\texttt{IsSubnormallyMonomial}!for a group}
\label{IsSubnormallyMonomial:for a group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSubnormallyMonomial({\mdseries\slshape chi})\index{IsSubnormallyMonomial@\texttt{IsSubnormallyMonomial}!for a character}
\label{IsSubnormallyMonomial:for a character}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 An irreducible character of the group $G$ is called \emph{subnormally monomial} (\emph{SM} for short) if it is induced from a linear character of a subnormal subgroup of $G$. A group $G$ is called SM if all its irreducible characters are SM. 

 \texttt{TestSubnormallyMonomial} returns a record with information whether the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} or the irreducible character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is SM. 

 The result has the components \texttt{isSubnormallyMonomial} (either \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}) and \texttt{comment} (a string telling a reason for the value of the component \texttt{isSubnormallyMonomial}); in the case that the \texttt{isSubnormallyMonomial} component has value \texttt{false} there is also a component \texttt{character}, with value an irreducible character of $G$ that is not SM. 

 \texttt{IsSubnormallyMonomial} returns \texttt{true} if the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} or the group character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} is subnormally monomial, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestSubnormallyMonomial( S4 );|
  rec( character := Character( CharacterTable( S4 ), [ 3, -1, -1, 0, 1
       ] ), comment := "found non-SM character",
    isSubnormallyMonomial := false )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestSubnormallyMonomial( Irr( S4 )[4] );|
  rec( comment := "all subnormal subgroups checked",
    isSubnormallyMonomial := false )
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestSubnormallyMonomial( DerivedSubgroup( S4 ) );|
  rec( comment := "all irreducibles checked",
    isSubnormallyMonomial := true )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TestRelativelySM}}\logpage{[ 75, 4, 6 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X83EF7B8D7C1C2CA3}{}
{
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestRelativelySM({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{TestRelativelySM@\texttt{TestRelativelySM}!for a group}
\label{TestRelativelySM:for a group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestRelativelySM({\mdseries\slshape chi})\index{TestRelativelySM@\texttt{TestRelativelySM}!for a character}
\label{TestRelativelySM:for a character}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (attribute)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestRelativelySM({\mdseries\slshape G, N})\index{TestRelativelySM@\texttt{TestRelativelySM}!for a group and a normal subgroup}
\label{TestRelativelySM:for a group and a normal subgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestRelativelySM({\mdseries\slshape chi, N})\index{TestRelativelySM@\texttt{TestRelativelySM}!for a character and a normal subgroup}
\label{TestRelativelySM:for a character and a normal subgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRelativelySM({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsRelativelySM@\texttt{IsRelativelySM}!for a group}
\label{IsRelativelySM:for a group}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsRelativelySM({\mdseries\slshape chi})\index{IsRelativelySM@\texttt{IsRelativelySM}!for a character}
\label{IsRelativelySM:for a character}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 In the first two cases, \texttt{TestRelativelySM} returns a record with information whether the argument, which must be a SM
group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} or an irreducible character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} of a SM group $G$, is relatively SM with respect to every normal subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}. 

 In the second two cases, a normal subgroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the second argument. Here \texttt{TestRelativelySM} returns a record with information whether the first argument is relatively SM
with respect to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}}, i.e, whether there is a subnormal subgroup $H$ of $G$ that contains \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} such that the character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} resp.{\nobreakspace}every irreducible character of $G$ is induced from a character $\psi$ of $H$ such that the restriction of $\psi$ to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape N}} is irreducible. 

 The result record has the components \texttt{isRelativelySM} (with value either \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}) and \texttt{comment} (a string that describes a reason). If the argument is a group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} that is not relatively SM with respect to a normal subgroup then additionally
the component \texttt{character} is bound, with value a not relatively SM character of such a normal subgroup. 

 \texttt{IsRelativelySM} returns \texttt{true} if the SM group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} or the irreducible character \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape chi}} of the SM group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is relatively SM with respect to every normal subgroup of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}}, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 \emph{Note} that it is \emph{not} checked whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is SM. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsSubnormallyMonomial( DerivedSubgroup( S4 ) );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@TestRelativelySM( DerivedSubgroup( S4 ) );|
  rec(
    comment := "normal subgroups are abelian or have nilpotent factor gr\
  oup", isRelativelySM := true )
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Minimal Nonmonomial Groups}}\label{Minimal Nonmonomial Groups}
\logpage{[ 75, 5, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7B5735897DE29BCB}{}
{
  

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsMinimalNonmonomial}}
\logpage{[ 75, 5, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D7E2667821A23CD}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsMinimalNonmonomial({\mdseries\slshape G})\index{IsMinimalNonmonomial@\texttt{IsMinimalNonmonomial}}
\label{IsMinimalNonmonomial}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 A group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is called \emph{minimal nonmonomial} if it is nonmonomial, and all proper subgroups and factor groups are monomial. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsMinimalNonmonomial( Sl23 );  IsMinimalNonmonomial( S4 );|
  true
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{MinimalNonmonomialGroup}}
\logpage{[ 75, 5, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B416BBD80072079}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{MinimalNonmonomialGroup({\mdseries\slshape p, factsize})\index{MinimalNonmonomialGroup@\texttt{MinimalNonmonomialGroup}}
\label{MinimalNonmonomialGroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 is a solvable minimal nonmonomial group described by the parameters \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape factsize}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}} if such a group exists, and \texttt{false} otherwise. 

 Suppose that the required group $K$ exists. Then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape factsize}} is the size of the Fitting factor $K / F(K)$, and this value is 4, 8, an odd prime, twice an odd prime, or four times an
odd prime. In the case that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape factsize}} is twice an odd prime, the centre $Z(K)$ is cyclic of order $2^{{\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}+1}}$. In all other cases \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}} is the (unique) prime that divides the order of $F(K)$. 

 The solvable minimal nonmonomial groups were classified by van der Waall,
see{\nobreakspace}\cite{vdW76}. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MinimalNonmonomialGroup(  2,  3 ); # the group SL(2,3)|
  2^(1+2):3
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MinimalNonmonomialGroup(  3,  4 );|
  3^(1+2):4
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MinimalNonmonomialGroup(  5,  8 );|
  5^(1+2):Q8
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MinimalNonmonomialGroup( 13, 12 );|
  13^(1+2):2.D6
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MinimalNonmonomialGroup(  1, 14 );|
  2^(1+6):D14
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@MinimalNonmonomialGroup(  2, 14 );|
  (2^(1+6)Y4):D14
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

 }

    
\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Using and Developing \textsf{GAP} Packages}}\label{Using and Developing GAP Packages}
\logpage{[ 76, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X79F76C1E834BFDCC}{}
{
  \index{package} The functionality of \textsf{GAP} can be extended by loading \textsf{GAP} packages. The \textsf{GAP} distribution already contains all currently redistributed \textsf{GAP} packages in the \texttt{gap\texttt{\symbol{45}}4.17dev/pkg} directory. 

 \textsf{GAP} packages are written by (groups of) \textsf{GAP} users who may not necessarily be members of the \textsf{GAP} developer team. The responsibility and copyright of a \textsf{GAP} package remains with the original author(s). 

 \textsf{GAP} packages have their own documentation which is smoothly integrated into the \textsf{GAP} help system. (When \textsf{GAP} is started, \texttt{LoadPackageDocumentation} is called for all packages.) 

 All \textsf{GAP} users who develop new code are invited to share the results of their efforts
with other \textsf{GAP} users by making the code and its documentation available in form of a package.
Guidance on how to do this is available from the \textsf{GAP} website (\href{https://www.gap-system.org} {\texttt{https://www.gap\texttt{\symbol{45}}system.org}}) and in the \textsf{GAP} package \textsf{Example} (see \href{https://www.gap-system.org/Packages/example.html} {\texttt{https://www.gap\texttt{\symbol{45}}system.org/Packages/example.html}}). 

 The \textsf{GAP} development team will assist in making any new package suitable for
distribution with \textsf{GAP}. It is also possible to submit a package to a formal refereeing process. 

 In this chapter we first describe how to use existing packages, and then
provide guidelines for writing a \textsf{GAP} package.  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Installing a \textsf{GAP} Package}}\label{Installing a GAP Package}
\logpage{[ 76, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X82473E4B8756C6CD}{}
{
  Before a package can be used it must be installed. A standard distribution of \textsf{GAP} already contains all the packages currently redistributed with \textsf{GAP}. This set of packages has been checked for compatibility with the system and
with each other during release preparation. Most of the packages can be used
immediately, but some of them may require further installation steps (see
below). 

 Also, since \textsf{GAP} packages are released independently of the main \textsf{GAP} system, it may sometimes be useful to upgrade or install new packages between
upgrades of your \textsf{GAP} installation, e.g. if a new version of a package adds new capabilities or bug
fixes that you need. 

 A package consists of a collection of files within a single directory that
must be a subdirectory of the \texttt{pkg} directory in one of the \textsf{GAP} root directories (see \ref{GAP Root Directories}). If you don't have access to the \texttt{pkg} directory in your main \textsf{GAP} installation you can add private root directories as explained in section \ref{GAP Root Directories}. 

 Whenever you download or clone an archive of a \textsf{GAP} package, it will contain a \texttt{README} file (or \texttt{README.md} etc.) that explains how it should be installed. Some packages just consist of \textsf{GAP} code and the installation is done by unpacking the archive in one of the
places described above. There are also packages that need further installation
steps, such as compilation or installing additional software to satisfy their
dependencies. If there are some external programs which have to be compiled,
this is often done by executing \texttt{./configure; make} inside the unpacked package directory (but check the individual \texttt{README} files). 

 Most of the packages that require compilation can be compiled in a single step
by changing to the \texttt{pkg} directory of your \textsf{GAP} installation and calling the \texttt{../bin/BuildPackages.sh} script. 

 Note that if you use Windows you may not be able to use some or all external
binaries. }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Loading a \textsf{GAP} Package}}\label{Loading a GAP Package}
\logpage{[ 76, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X825CBC5B86F8F811}{}
{
  If a package is not already loaded, it may be loaded using the function \texttt{LoadPackage} (\ref{LoadPackage}). 

 Some \textsf{GAP} packages are prepared for automatic loading, that is they will be loaded
automatically when \textsf{GAP} starts (see \ref{LoadPackageAutomatic}). 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LoadPackage}}
\logpage{[ 76, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79B373A77B29D1F5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LoadPackage({\mdseries\slshape name[, version][, banner]})\index{LoadPackage@\texttt{LoadPackage}}
\label{LoadPackage}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 loads the \textsf{GAP} package with name \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}. 

 As an example, the following loads the \textsf{GAP} package \textsf{SONATA} (case insensitive) which provides methods for the construction and analysis of
finite nearrings: 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@LoadPackage("sonata");|
  ... some more lines with package banner(s) ...
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 

 The package name is case insensitive and may be appropriately abbreviated. At
the time of writing, for example, \texttt{LoadPackage("semi");} will load the \textsf{Semigroups} package, and \texttt{LoadPackage("js");} will load the \textsf{json} package. If the abbreviation cannot be uniquely completed, a list of available
completions will be offered, and \texttt{LoadPackage} returns \texttt{fail}. Thus the names of \emph{all} installed packages can be shown by calling \texttt{LoadPackage("");}. 

 When the optional argument string \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}} is present, the package will only be loaded in a version number equal to or
greater than \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}} (see{\nobreakspace}\texttt{CompareVersionNumbers} (\ref{CompareVersionNumbers})). If the first character of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}} is \texttt{=} then only that version will be loaded. 

 \texttt{LoadPackage} will return \texttt{true} if the package has been successfully loaded, and will return \texttt{fail} if the package could not be loaded. The latter may be the case if the package
is not installed, if necessary binaries have not been compiled, or if the
version number of the available version is too small. If the package cannot be
loaded, \texttt{TestPackageAvailability} (\ref{TestPackageAvailability}) can be used to find the reasons. Also, \texttt{DisplayPackageLoadingLog} (\ref{DisplayPackageLoadingLog}) can be used to find out more about the failure. To see the problems directly,
one can change the verbosity using the user preference \texttt{InfoPackageLoadingLevel}, see \texttt{InfoPackageLoading} (\ref{InfoPackageLoading}) for details. 

 If the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} has already been loaded in a version number equal to or greater than \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}}, \texttt{LoadPackage} returns \texttt{true} without doing anything else. 

 If the optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape banner}} is present then it must be either \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}; in the latter case, the effect is that no package banner is printed. 

 After a package has been loaded, all its code becomes available to use with
the rest of the \textsf{GAP} library. }

 \index{automatic loading of GAP packages@automatic loading of \textsf{GAP} packages} \index{disable automatic loading} 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Automatic loading of \textsf{GAP} packages}}\label{LoadPackageAutomatic}
\logpage{[ 76, 2, 2 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7E6767B485F23BFC}{}
{
  When \textsf{GAP} is started some packages are loaded automatically, and these belong to two
categories. The first are those packages which are needed to start \textsf{GAP} (at the present time, the only such package is \textsf{GAPDoc}). Their list is contained in \texttt{GAPInfo.Dependencies.NeededOtherPackages}. The second are packages which are loaded during \textsf{GAP} startup by default. The latter list may be obtained by calling \texttt{UserPreference("PackagesToLoad")} and is customisable as described in Section  (\textbf{Reference: Configuring User preferences}). 

 While \textsf{GAP} will not start if any of the packages from the former group is missing,
loading of the packages from the latter group may be suppressed by using the \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{45}}A} command line option (see \ref{Command Line Options}). 

 If for some reason you don't want certain packages to be automatically loaded, \textsf{GAP} provides three levels for disabling autoloading. 

 \index{NOAUTO@\texttt{NOAUTO}} The autoloading of specific packages can be overwritten \emph{for the whole \textsf{GAP} installation} by putting a file \texttt{NOAUTO} into a \texttt{pkg} directory that contains lines with the names of packages which should not be
automatically loaded. 

 Furthermore, \emph{individual users} can disable the autoloading of specific packages by putting the names of these
packages into the list that is assigned to the user preference ``ExcludeFromAutoload'', for example in the user's \texttt{gap.ini} file (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{subsect:gap.ini file}). 

 Using the \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{45}}A} command line option when starting \textsf{GAP} (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{Command Line Options}), automatic loading of packages is switched off \emph{for this \textsf{GAP} session}. 

 In any of the above three cases, the packages listed in \texttt{GAPInfo.Dependencies.NeededOtherPackages} are still loaded automatically, and an error is signalled if any of these
packages is unavailable. 

 See \texttt{SetPackagePath} (\ref{SetPackagePath}) for a way to force the loading of a prescribed package version. See also \texttt{ExtendRootDirectories} (\ref{ExtendRootDirectories}) and \texttt{ExtendPackageDirectories} (\ref{ExtendPackageDirectories}) for methods of adding directories containing packages \emph{after} \textsf{GAP} has been started. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{SetPackagePath}}
\logpage{[ 76, 2, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X858E8985840BFA72}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{SetPackagePath({\mdseries\slshape pkgname, pkgpath})\index{SetPackagePath@\texttt{SetPackagePath}}
\label{SetPackagePath}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 This function can be used to force \textsf{GAP} to load a particular version of a package, even though newer versions of the
package are available. 

 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgpath}} be strings denoting the name of a \textsf{GAP} package and the path to a directory where a version of this package can be
found (i.{\nobreakspace}e., calling \texttt{Directory} (\ref{Directory}) with the argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgpath}} will yield a directory that contains the file \texttt{PackageInfo.g} of the package). 

 If the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} is already loaded with an installation path different from \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgpath}} then \texttt{SetPackagePath} signals an error. If the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} is not yet loaded then \texttt{SetPackagePath} erases the information about available versions of the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}}, and stores the record that is contained in the \texttt{PackageInfo.g} file at \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgpath}} instead, such that only the version installed at \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgpath}} can be loaded with \texttt{LoadPackage} (\ref{LoadPackage}). 

 One should call \texttt{SetPackagePath} immediately before loading the package in question. Note that calling \texttt{ExtendPackageDirectories} (\ref{ExtendPackageDirectories}) or \texttt{ExtendRootDirectories} (\ref{ExtendRootDirectories}) may change the available versions of the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ExtendRootDirectories}}
\logpage{[ 76, 2, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7CD0A2F27D19BA03}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ExtendRootDirectories({\mdseries\slshape paths})\index{ExtendRootDirectories@\texttt{ExtendRootDirectories}}
\label{ExtendRootDirectories}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape paths}} be a list of strings that denote paths to intended \textsf{GAP} root directories (see \ref{GAP Root Directories}). The function \texttt{ExtendRootDirectories} adds these paths to the global list \texttt{GAPInfo.RootPaths} and calls the initialization of available \textsf{GAP} packages, such that later calls to \texttt{LoadPackage} (\ref{LoadPackage}) will find the \textsf{GAP} packages that are contained in \texttt{pkg} subdirectories of the directories given by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape paths}}. 

 Note that the purpose of this function is to make \textsf{GAP} packages in the given directories available. It cannot be used to influence
the start of \textsf{GAP}, because the \textsf{GAP} library is loaded before \texttt{ExtendRootDirectories} can be called (and because \texttt{GAPInfo.RootPaths} is not used for reading the \textsf{GAP} library). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ExtendPackageDirectories}}
\logpage{[ 76, 2, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81BFC5C87EE2E02A}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ExtendPackageDirectories({\mdseries\slshape paths})\index{ExtendPackageDirectories@\texttt{ExtendPackageDirectories}}
\label{ExtendPackageDirectories}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape paths}} be a list of strings that denote paths to intended \textsf{GAP} package directories (see \ref{GAP Package Directories}). The function \texttt{ExtendPackageDirectories} adds these paths to the global list \texttt{GAPInfo.PackageDirectories} and calls the initialization of available \textsf{GAP} packages, such that later calls to \texttt{LoadPackage} (\ref{LoadPackage}) will find the \textsf{GAP} packages that are contained in the directories given by \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape paths}}. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DisplayPackageLoadingLog}}
\logpage{[ 76, 2, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D162DDF813D2BBA}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DisplayPackageLoadingLog({\mdseries\slshape [severity]})\index{DisplayPackageLoadingLog@\texttt{DisplayPackageLoadingLog}}
\label{DisplayPackageLoadingLog}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InfoPackageLoading\index{InfoPackageLoading@\texttt{InfoPackageLoading}}
\label{InfoPackageLoading}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (info class)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}ERROR\index{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}ERROR@\texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}ERROR}}
\label{PACKAGEuScoreERROR}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (global variable)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}WARNING\index{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}WARNING@\texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}WARNING}}
\label{PACKAGEuScoreWARNING}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (global variable)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}INFO\index{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}INFO@\texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}INFO}}
\label{PACKAGEuScoreINFO}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (global variable)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}DEBUG\index{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}DEBUG@\texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}DEBUG}}
\label{PACKAGEuScoreDEBUG}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (global variable)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LogPackageLoadingMessage({\mdseries\slshape severity, message[, name]})\index{LogPackageLoadingMessage@\texttt{LogPackageLoadingMessage}}
\label{LogPackageLoadingMessage}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Whenever \textsf{GAP} considers loading a package, log messages are collected in a global list. The
messages for the current \textsf{GAP} session can be displayed with \texttt{DisplayPackageLoadingLog}. To each message, a ``severity'' is assigned, which is one of \texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}ERROR}, \texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}WARNING}, \texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}INFO}, \texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}DEBUG}, in increasing order. The function \texttt{DisplayPackageLoadingLog} shows only the messages whose severity is at most \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape severity}}, the default for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape severity}} is \texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}WARNING}. 

 The intended meaning of the severity levels is as follows. 

 
\begin{description}
\item[{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}ERROR}]  should be used whenever \textsf{GAP} will run into an error during package loading, where the reason of the error
shall be documented in the global list. 
\item[{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}WARNING}]  should be used whenever \textsf{GAP} has detected a reason why a package cannot be loaded, and where the message
describes how to solve this problem, for example if a package binary is
missing. 
\item[{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}INFO}]  should be used whenever \textsf{GAP} has detected a reason why a package cannot be loaded, and where it is not
clear how to solve this problem, for example if the package is not compatible
with other installed packages. 
\item[{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}DEBUG}]  should be used for other messages reporting what \textsf{GAP} does when it loads packages (checking dependencies, reading files, etc.). One
purpose is to record in which order packages have been considered for loading
or have actually been loaded. 
\end{description}
 

 The log messages are created either by the functions of \textsf{GAP}'s package loading mechanism or in the code of your package, for example in
the \texttt{AvailabilityTest} function of the package's \texttt{PackageInfo.g} file (see \ref{The PackageInfo.g File}), using \texttt{LogPackageLoadingMessage}. The arguments of this function are \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape severity}} (which must be one of the above severity levels), \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape message}} (which must be either a string or a list of strings), and optionally \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} (which must be the name of the package to which the message belongs). The
argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is not needed if the function is called from a call of a package's \texttt{AvailabilityTest} function (see \ref{The PackageInfo.g File}) or is called from a package file that is read from \texttt{init.g} or \texttt{read.g}; in these cases, the name of the current package (stored in the record \texttt{GAPInfo.PackageCurrent}) is taken. According to the above list, the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape severity}} argument of \texttt{LogPackageLoadingMessage} calls in a package's \texttt{AvailabilityTest} function is either \texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}WARNING} or \texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}INFO}. 

 If you want to see the log messages already during the package loading
process, you can set the level of the info class \texttt{InfoPackageLoading} to one of the severity values listed above; afterwards the messages with at
most this severity are shown immediately when they arise. In order to make
this work already for autoloaded packages, you can call \texttt{SetUserPreference("InfoPackageLoadingLevel", \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lev}});} to set the desired severity level \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape lev}}. This can for example be done in your \texttt{gap.ini} file, see Section \ref{subsect:gap.ini file}. }

 }

  
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Functions for \textsf{GAP} Packages}}\label{Functions for GAP Packages}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7C6CE28B7E142804}{}
{
  The following functions are mainly used in files contained in a package and
not by users of a package. They are needed to organise reading package files
into \textsf{GAP} in the right order, performing maintenance tasks like building documentation
and running package tests, checking package dependencies, etc. You will find
further information about their use in Section \ref{Guidelines for Writing a GAP Package} and subsequent sections. 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ReadPackage}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X870954577B27DCAB}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ReadPackage({\mdseries\slshape [name, ]file})\index{ReadPackage@\texttt{ReadPackage}}
\label{ReadPackage}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RereadPackage({\mdseries\slshape [name, ]file})\index{RereadPackage@\texttt{RereadPackage}}
\label{RereadPackage}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Called with two strings \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape file}}, \texttt{ReadPackage} reads the file \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape file}} of the \textsf{GAP} package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape file}} is given as a path relative to the home directory of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}. Note that \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape file}} is read in the namespace of the package, see Section \ref{Namespaces} for details. 

 If only one argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape file}} is given, this should be the path of a file relative to the \texttt{pkg} subdirectory of \textsf{GAP} root paths (see{\nobreakspace}\ref{GAP Root Directories}). Note that in this case, the package name is assumed to be equal to the
first part of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape file}}, \emph{so the one argument form is not recommended}. 

 The absolute path is determined as follows. If the package in question has
already been loaded then the file in the directory of the loaded version is
read. If the package is available but not yet loaded then the directory given
by \texttt{TestPackageAvailability} (\ref{TestPackageAvailability}) is used, without prescribed version number. (Note that the \texttt{ReadPackage} call does \emph{not} force the package to be loaded.) 

 If the file is readable then \texttt{true} is returned, otherwise a warning is displayed (for \texttt{ReadPackage}) or \texttt{false} is returned (for \texttt{RereadPackage}). 

 Each of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape file}} should be a string. The \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} argument is case insensitive. 

 \texttt{RereadPackage} does the same as \texttt{ReadPackage}, except that also read\texttt{\symbol{45}}only global variables are
overwritten (cf.{\nobreakspace}\texttt{Reread} (\ref{Reread})). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TestPackageAvailability}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8580DF257E4D7046}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestPackageAvailability({\mdseries\slshape name[, version][, checkall]})\index{TestPackageAvailability@\texttt{TestPackageAvailability}}
\label{TestPackageAvailability}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For strings \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}}, this function tests whether the \textsf{GAP} package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is available for loading in a version that is at least \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}}, or equal to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}} if the first character of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}} is \texttt{=} (see \texttt{CompareVersionNumbers} (\ref{CompareVersionNumbers}) for further details about version numbers). 

 The result is \texttt{true} if the package is already loaded, \texttt{fail} if it is not available, and the string denoting the \textsf{GAP} root path where the package resides if it is available, but not yet loaded. So
the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is available if the result of \texttt{TestPackageAvailability} is not equal to \texttt{fail}. 

 If the optional argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape checkall}} is \texttt{true} then all dependencies are checked, even if some have turned out to be not
satisfied. This is useful when one is interested in the reasons why the
package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} cannot be loaded. In this situation, calling first \texttt{TestPackageAvailability} and then \texttt{DisplayPackageLoadingLog} (\ref{DisplayPackageLoadingLog}) with argument \texttt{PACKAGE{\textunderscore}INFO} (\ref{PACKAGEuScoreINFO}) will give an overview of these reasons. 

 You should \emph{not} call \texttt{TestPackageAvailability} in the test function of a package (the value of the component \texttt{AvailabilityTest} in the \texttt{PackageInfo.g} file of the package, see \ref{The PackageInfo.g File}), because \texttt{TestPackageAvailability} calls this test function.  

 The argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is case insensitive. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPackageLoaded}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C8724C183E24665}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPackageLoaded({\mdseries\slshape name[, version]})\index{IsPackageLoaded@\texttt{IsPackageLoaded}}
\label{IsPackageLoaded}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For strings \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}}, this function tests whether the \textsf{GAP} package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is already loaded in a version that is at least \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}}, or equal to \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}} if the first character of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}} is \texttt{=} (see \texttt{CompareVersionNumbers} (\ref{CompareVersionNumbers}) for further details about version numbers). 

 The result is \texttt{true} if the package is already loaded, \texttt{false} otherwise. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsPackageMarkedForLoading}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8067348B836BAF37}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsPackageMarkedForLoading({\mdseries\slshape name, version})\index{IsPackageMarkedForLoading@\texttt{IsPackageMarkedForLoading}}
\label{IsPackageMarkedForLoading}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 This function can be used in the code of a package $A$ for testing whether the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} in version \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}} will be loaded after the \texttt{LoadPackage} (\ref{LoadPackage}) call for the package $A$ has been executed. This means that the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} had been loaded before, or has been (directly or indirectly) requested as a
needed or suggested package of the package $A$ or of a package whose loading requested that $A$ was loaded. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{TestPackage}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X866ADD4E814A54F0}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{TestPackage({\mdseries\slshape pkgname})\index{TestPackage@\texttt{TestPackage}}
\label{TestPackage}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 It is recommended that a \textsf{GAP} package specifies a standard test in its \texttt{PackageInfo.g} file. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} is a string with the name of a \textsf{GAP} package, then \texttt{TestPackage(pkgname)} will check if this package is loadable and has the standard test, and will run
this test in the current \textsf{GAP} session.

 The output of the test depends on the particular package, and it also may
depend on the current \textsf{GAP} session (loaded packages, state of the random sources, defined global
variables etc.). }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{InstalledPackageVersion}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 6 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B79FEE57DBDBD71}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{InstalledPackageVersion({\mdseries\slshape name})\index{InstalledPackageVersion@\texttt{InstalledPackageVersion}}
\label{InstalledPackageVersion}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 If the \textsf{GAP} package with name \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} has already been loaded then \texttt{InstalledPackageVersion} returns the string denoting the version number of this version of the package.
If the package is available but has not yet been loaded then the version
number string for that version of the package that currently would be loaded.
(Note that loading \emph{another} package might force loading another version of the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}, so the result of \texttt{InstalledPackageVersion} will be different afterwards.) If the package is not available then \texttt{fail} is returned. 

 The argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is case insensitive. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DirectoriesPackageLibrary}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 7 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X807D835C7B032D4E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DirectoriesPackageLibrary({\mdseries\slshape name[, path]})\index{DirectoriesPackageLibrary@\texttt{DirectoriesPackageLibrary}}
\label{DirectoriesPackageLibrary}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 takes the string \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}}, a name of a \textsf{GAP} package, and returns a list that is either empty or contains one directory
object \texttt{dir} that describes the place where the library functions of this \textsf{GAP} package should be located. 

 In the latter case, \texttt{dir} is the \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape path}} subdirectory of a directory where the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is installed, where the default for \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape path}} is \texttt{"lib"}, and where the package directory belongs to the version of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} that is already loaded or is currently going to be loaded or would be the
first version \textsf{GAP} would try to load if no other version is explicitly prescribed. (If the
package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is not yet loaded then we cannot guarantee that the directory belongs to a
version that really can be loaded.) 

 Note that \texttt{DirectoriesPackageLibrary} is likely to be called in the \texttt{AvailabilityTest} function in the package's \texttt{PackageInfo.g} file (see \ref{The PackageInfo.g File}). 

 As an example, the following returns a directory object for the library
functions of the \textsf{GAP} package \textsf{Example}: 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DirectoriesPackageLibrary( "Example", "gap" );|
  [ dir("/home/werner/gap/4.0/pkg/example/gap/") ]
\end{Verbatim}
 

 Observe that we needed the second argument \texttt{"gap"} here, since \textsf{Example}'s library functions are in the subdirectory \texttt{gap} rather than \texttt{lib}. 

 In order to find a subdirectory deeper than one level in a package directory,
the second argument is again necessary whether or not the desired subdirectory
relative to the package's directory begins with \texttt{lib}. The directories in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape path}} should be separated by \texttt{/} (even on systems, like Windows, which use \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{92}}} as the directory separator). For example, suppose there is a package \texttt{somepackage} with a subdirectory \texttt{m11} in the directory \texttt{data}, then we might expect the following: 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DirectoriesPackageLibrary( "somepackage", "data/m11" );|
  [ dir("/home/werner/gap/4.0/pkg/somepackage/data/m11") ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DirectoriesPackagePrograms}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 8 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X794508E5811D3BC9}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DirectoriesPackagePrograms({\mdseries\slshape name})\index{DirectoriesPackagePrograms@\texttt{DirectoriesPackagePrograms}}
\label{DirectoriesPackagePrograms}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 \index{GAPInfo.Architecture@\texttt{GAPInfo.Architecture}} returns a list that is either empty or contains one directory object \texttt{dir} that describes the place where external binaries of the \textsf{GAP} package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} should be located. 

 In the latter case, \texttt{dir} is the \texttt{bin/}\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape architecture}} subdirectory of a directory where the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is installed, where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape architecture}} is the architecture on which \textsf{GAP} has been compiled (this can be accessed as \texttt{GAPInfo.Architecture}, see \texttt{GAPInfo} (\ref{GAPInfo})), and where the package directory belongs to the version of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} that is already loaded or is currently going to be loaded or would be the
first version \textsf{GAP} would try to load if no other version is explicitly prescribed. (If the
package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape name}} is not yet loaded then we cannot guarantee that the directory belongs to a
version that really can be loaded.) 

 Note that \texttt{DirectoriesPackagePrograms} is likely to be called in the \texttt{AvailabilityTest} function in the package's \texttt{PackageInfo.g} file (see \ref{The PackageInfo.g File}). 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@DirectoriesPackagePrograms( "nq" );|
  [ dir("/home/gap/4.0/pkg/nq/bin/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-default64-kv3/") ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{CompareVersionNumbers}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 9 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X787DFEB383545A49}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CompareVersionNumbers({\mdseries\slshape supplied, required[, "equal"]})\index{CompareVersionNumbers@\texttt{CompareVersionNumbers}}
\label{CompareVersionNumbers}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 A version number is a string which contains nonnegative integers separated by
non\texttt{\symbol{45}}numeric characters. Examples of valid version numbers
are for example: 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  "1.0"   "3.141.59"  "2-7-8.3" "5 release 2 patchlevel 666"
\end{Verbatim}
 

 \texttt{CompareVersionNumbers} compares two version numbers, given as strings. They are split at
non\texttt{\symbol{45}}digit characters, the resulting integer lists are
compared lexicographically. The routine tests whether \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape supplied}} is at least as large as \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape required}}, and returns \texttt{true} or \texttt{false} accordingly. A version number ending in \texttt{dev} is considered to be infinite. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{DeclareAutoreadableVariables}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 10 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X8495E5327D563AC3}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{DeclareAutoreadableVariables({\mdseries\slshape pkgname, filename, varlist})\index{DeclareAutoreadableVariables@\texttt{DeclareAutoreadableVariables}}
\label{DeclareAutoreadableVariables}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} be the name of a package, let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filename}} be the name of a file relative to the home directory of this package, and let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape varlist}} be a list of strings that are the names of global variables which get bound
when the file is read. \texttt{DeclareAutoreadableVariables} notifies the names in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape varlist}} such that the first attempt to access one of the variables causes the file to
be read. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{Kernel modules in \textsf{GAP} packages}}\label{Kernel modules}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 11 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X85672DDD7D34D5F0}{}
{
  \index{gac@\texttt{gac}} If the package has a kernel module, then it can be compiled using the \textsf{gac} script. A kernel module is implemented in C and follows certain conventions to
comply with the \textsf{GAP} kernel interface, which we plan to document later. In the meantime, we advice
to get in touch with \textsf{GAP} developers if you plan to develop such a package. 

 To use the \textsf{gac} script to produce dynamically loadable modules, call it with the \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{45}}d} option, for example: 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  $ gap4/gac -d test.c
\end{Verbatim}
 

 This will produce a file \texttt{test.so}, which then can be loaded into \textsf{GAP} with \texttt{LoadKernelExtension} (\ref{LoadKernelExtension}). If the kernel module is required for the package to work, then its \texttt{PackageInfo.g} should define a \texttt{AvailabilityTest} which calls \texttt{IsKernelExtensionAvailable} (\ref{IsKernelExtensionAvailable}), see \ref{Test for the Existence of GAP Package Binaries} for details. 

 Note that before \textsf{GAP} 4.12, \texttt{LoadDynamicModule} (\ref{LoadDynamicModule}) was used for this. It is still available and in fact \texttt{LoadKernelExtension} (\ref{LoadKernelExtension}) call it; but the latter provides a higher level abstraction and is more
convenient to use. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsKernelExtensionAvailable}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 12 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D23646086F33A9E}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsKernelExtensionAvailable({\mdseries\slshape pkgname[, modname]})\index{IsKernelExtensionAvailable@\texttt{IsKernelExtensionAvailable}}
\label{IsKernelExtensionAvailable}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For use by packages: Search for a loadable kernel module inside package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} with name \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape modname}} and return \texttt{true} if found, otherwise \texttt{false}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape modname}} is omitted, then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} is used instead. Note that package names are case insensitive, but \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape modname}} is not. 

 This function first appeared in GAP 4.12. It is typically called in the \texttt{AvailabilityTest} function of a package (see \ref{Test for the Existence of GAP Package Binaries}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsKernelExtensionAvailable("myPackageWithKernelExtension");|
  true
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LoadKernelExtension}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 13 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85F1B83079A11F89}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LoadKernelExtension({\mdseries\slshape pkgname[, modname]})\index{LoadKernelExtension@\texttt{LoadKernelExtension}}
\label{LoadKernelExtension}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 For use by packages: Search for a loadable kernel module inside package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} with name \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape modname}}, and load it if found. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape modname}} is omitted, then \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} is used instead. Note that package names are case insensitive, but \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape modname}} is not. 

 This function first appeared in GAP 4.12. It is typically called in the \texttt{init.g} file of a package. 

 Previously, packages with a kernel module typically used code like this: 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=]
  path := Filename(DirectoriesPackagePrograms("SomePackage"), "SomePackage.so");
  if path <> fail then
    LoadDynamicModule(path);
  fi;
\end{Verbatim}
 That can now be replaced by the following, which also produces more helpful
error messages for the user: 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=]
  LoadKernelExtension("SomePackage");
\end{Verbatim}
 For packages where the name of the kernel extension is not identical to that
of the package, you can either rename the kernel extension to have a matching
name (recommended if you only have a single kernel extension in your package,
which is how we recommend to set up things anyway), or else use the two
argument version: 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  LoadKernelExtension("SomePackage", "kext"); # this will look for kext.so
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{LoadDynamicModule}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 14 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7C99782886B18C77}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{LoadDynamicModule({\mdseries\slshape filename})\index{LoadDynamicModule@\texttt{LoadDynamicModule}}
\label{LoadDynamicModule}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 To load a compiled file, the command \texttt{LoadDynamicModule} is used. This command loads \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape filename}} as module. 

 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@LoadDynamicModule("./test.so");|
\end{Verbatim}
 

 On some operating systems, once you have loaded a dynamic module with a
certain filename, loading another with the same filename will have no effect,
even if the file on disk has changed. }

 
\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{The PackageInfo.g File}}\label{The PackageInfo.g File}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 15 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X85C8DE357EE424D8}{}
{
  Each package has the file \texttt{PackageInfo.g} which contains meta\texttt{\symbol{45}}information about the package (package
name, version, author(s), relations to other packages, homepage, download
archives, etc.). This file is used by the package loading mechanism, by the \textsf{GAP} webpages about packages, and also for the redistribution of a package with \textsf{GAP}. 

 A \texttt{PackageInfo.g} file contains a call to the function \texttt{SetPackageInfo}, with argument a record. The following components of this record are \emph{mandatory}. 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{PackageName}}]  a nonempty string denoting the name of the package, 
\item[{\texttt{Subtitle}}]  a string that describes the package's contents, may be used by a default
banner or on a web page, should fit on one line, 
\item[{\texttt{Version}}]  a nonempty string that does not start with \texttt{=}, denoting the version number of the package (see Section \ref{Version Numbers}), 
\item[{\texttt{Date}}]  a string of the form \texttt{yyyy\texttt{\symbol{45}}mm\texttt{\symbol{45}}dd}  denoting the release date of the current version of the package (a date since
1999, when \textsf{GAP}{\nobreakspace}4 appeared), 
\item[{\texttt{License}}]  a nonempty string containing an SPDX ID (see Section \ref{Selecting a license for a GAP Package}), 
\item[{\texttt{ArchiveURL}}]  a string started with \texttt{http://}, \texttt{https://}, or \texttt{ftp://}, denoting an URL from where the current package archive can be downloaded,
but without the suffix describing the format (see the \texttt{ArchiveFormats} component), 
\item[{\texttt{ArchiveFormats}}]  a string that lists the supported formats (among \texttt{.tar.gz}, \texttt{.tar.bz2}, \texttt{\texttt{\symbol{45}}win.zip}), separated by whitespace or commas, 
\item[{\texttt{README{\textunderscore}URL}}]  a string started with \texttt{http://}, \texttt{https://}, or \texttt{ftp://}, denoting an URL from where the current \texttt{README.md} or \texttt{README} file of the package can be downloaded, 
\item[{\texttt{PackageInfoURL}}]  a string started with \texttt{http://}, \texttt{https://}, or \texttt{ftp://}, denoting an URL from where the current \texttt{PackageInfo.g} file of the package can be downloaded, 
\item[{\texttt{AbstractHTML}}]  a string that describes the package's contents in a few lines, in HTML format;
this text will be displayed on the package overview web page of \textsf{GAP}, 
\item[{\texttt{PackageWWWHome}}]  a string started with \texttt{http://}, \texttt{https://}, or \texttt{ftp://}, denoting the address of the package's home page, 
\item[{\texttt{PackageDoc}}]  a record or a list of records; each record describes a book of the package
documentation, with the following components 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{BookName}}]  a string, the name of the book, 
\item[{\texttt{LongTitle}}]  a string shown by \texttt{?books}, 
\item[{\texttt{SixFile}}]  a string denoting a relative path to the \texttt{manual.six} file of the book, 
\item[{\texttt{HTMLStart}}]  a string denoting a relative path to the start file of the HTML version of the
book, 
\item[{\texttt{PDFFile}}]  a string denoting a relative path to the \texttt{.pdf} file of the book, 
\item[{\texttt{ArchiveURLSubset}}]  a list of strings denoting relative paths to those files and directories from
the archive that are needed for the online manual; typically, \texttt{[ "doc" ]} suffices, 
\end{description}
 
\end{description}
 The following components of the record are \emph{optional}. 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{TextFiles} or \texttt{BinaryFiles} or \texttt{TextBinaryFilesPatterns}}]  a list of strings that specify which files in the archive are text files or
binary files (at most one of the three components can be available, each
string in \texttt{TextBinaryFilesPatterns} must start with \texttt{T} for text files and by \texttt{B} for binary files), 
\item[{\texttt{Persons}}]  a list of records, each with the mandatory components 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{LastName}}]  a string, 
\item[{at least one of \texttt{IsAuthor} or \texttt{IsMaintainer}}]  \texttt{true} or \texttt{false}, 
\end{description}
 and optional components 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{FirstNames}}]  a string (was mandatory before \textsf{GAP} 4.14), 
\item[{\texttt{Place}}]  a string, 
\item[{\texttt{Institution}}]  a string, 
\end{description}
 If the \texttt{IsMaintainer} value is \texttt{true} then also one of the following components is mandatory, otherwise these
components are optional. 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{Email}}]  a string, 
\item[{\texttt{WWWHome}}]  a string denoting an URL, or 
\item[{\texttt{PostalAddress}}]  a string. 
\end{description}
 
\item[{\texttt{SourceRepository}}]  a record with the components \texttt{Type} (the version control system, e.g. \texttt{"git"} or \texttt{"hg"}) and \texttt{URL} (the URL of the repository), both strings, 
\item[{\texttt{IssueTrackerURL}}]  a string started with \texttt{http://}, \texttt{https://}, or \texttt{ftp://}, 
\item[{\texttt{SupportEmail}}]  a string denoting an e\texttt{\symbol{45}}mail address, 
\item[{\texttt{Dependencies}}]  a record describing the dependencies of the package (see Section \ref{Package dependencies}), with the following optional components 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{GAP}}]  a string denoting the needed version of \textsf{GAP}, 
\item[{\texttt{NeededOtherPackages}}]  a list of pairs \texttt{[ pkgname, pkgversion ]} of strings, denoting the other packages which must be available if the current
package shall be loadable, 
\item[{\texttt{SuggestedOtherPackages}}]  a list of pairs \texttt{[ pkgname, pkgversion ]} of strings, denoting the other packages which shall be loaded together with
the current package if they are available, 
\item[{\texttt{TestPackages}}]  a list of pairs \texttt{[ pkgname, pkgversion ]} of strings, denoting packages that are needed only to test the package, but
not to load the package, 
\item[{\texttt{NeededSystemPackages}}]  a record whose contents describe external dependencies of the package in a
machine\texttt{\symbol{45}}readable form (see \ref{External dependencies} for more information), 
\item[{\texttt{ExternalConditions}}]  a list of strings or of pairs \texttt{[ text, URL ]} of strings, denoting conditions on external programs in a
human\texttt{\symbol{45}}readable form (see \ref{External dependencies} for more information), 
\end{description}
 
\item[{\texttt{AvailabilityTest}}]  a function with no arguments that returns \texttt{true} if the package is available, and \texttt{false} otherwise (can be \texttt{ReturnTrue} (\ref{ReturnTrue}) if the package consists only of \textsf{GAP} code; this is also the default value), 
\item[{\texttt{BannerString} or \texttt{BannerFunction}}]  a string or a function, respectively, that is used to create a package banner
different from the default banner (see Section \ref{The Banner}), 
\item[{\texttt{TestFile}}]  a string denoting a relative path to a readable file which contains tests of
the package's functionality (see Section \ref{Testing a GAP package}), 
\item[{\texttt{Keywords}}]  a list of strings that are keywords related to the topic of the package, 
\item[{\texttt{Extensions}}]  a list of records that describe conditional extensions of the package (see
Section \ref{Extensions Provided by a Package}). 
\end{description}
 Other components of the record can be supported; for example, \texttt{AutoDoc} is used by the \textsf{AutoDoc} package if applicable. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ValidatePackageInfo}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 16 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X79767C2482FF6F55}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ValidatePackageInfo({\mdseries\slshape info})\index{ValidatePackageInfo@\texttt{ValidatePackageInfo}}
\label{ValidatePackageInfo}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 This function is intended to support package authors who create or modify \texttt{PackageInfo.g} files. (It is \emph{not} called when these files are read during the startup of \textsf{GAP} or when packages are actually loaded.) 

 The argument \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape info}} must be either a record as is contained in a \texttt{PackageInfo.g} file or a string which describes the path to such a file. The result is \texttt{true} if the record or the contents of the file, respectively, has correct format,
and \texttt{false} otherwise; in the latter case information about the incorrect components is
printed. These diagnostic messages can be suppressed by setting the global
option \texttt{quiet} to \texttt{true}. 

 Note that the components used for package loading are checked as well as the
components that are needed for composing the package overview web page or for
updating the package archives. 

 If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape info}} is a string then \texttt{ValidatePackageInfo} checks additionally whether those package files exist that are mentioned in
the file \texttt{info}, for example the \texttt{manual.six} file of the package documentation. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ShowPackageVariables}}
\logpage{[ 76, 3, 17 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7D34AC3287611B15}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ShowPackageVariables({\mdseries\slshape pkgname[, version][, arec]})\index{ShowPackageVariables@\texttt{ShowPackageVariables}}
\label{ShowPackageVariables}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{PackageVariablesInfo({\mdseries\slshape pkgname, version})\index{PackageVariablesInfo@\texttt{PackageVariablesInfo}}
\label{PackageVariablesInfo}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 Let \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} be the name of a \textsf{GAP} package. If the package \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape pkgname}} is available but not yet loaded then \texttt{ShowPackageVariables} prints a list of global variables that become bound and of methods that become
installed when the package is loaded. (For that, \textsf{GAP} actually loads the package.) 

 If a version number \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape version}} is given (see Section{\nobreakspace} (\textbf{Reference: Version Numbers})) then this version of the package is considered. 

 An error message is printed if (the given version of) the package is not
available or already loaded. 

 Information is printed about new and redeclared global variables, and about
names of global variables introduced in the package that differ from existing
globals only by case; note that the \textsf{GAP} help system is case insensitive, so it is difficult to document identifiers
that differ only by case. 

 Info lines for undocumented variables are marked with an asterisk \texttt{*}. 

 The following entries are omitted from the list: default setter methods for
attributes and properties that are declared in the package, and \texttt{Set\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape attr}}} and \texttt{Has\mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape attr}}} type variables where \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape attr}} is an attribute or property. 

 The output can be customized using the optional record \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape arec}}, the following components of this record are supported. 
\begin{description}
\item[{\texttt{show}}]  a list of strings describing those kinds of variables which shall be shown,
such as \texttt{"new global functions"}; the default are all kinds that appear in the package, 
\item[{\texttt{showDocumented}}]  \texttt{true} (the default) if documented variables shall be shown, and \texttt{false} otherwise, 
\item[{\texttt{showUndocumented}}]  \texttt{true} (the default) if undocumented variables shall be shown, and \texttt{false} otherwise,
